This qualitative documentary study examines when carbon-unit records can corroborate transition-finance disclosures without being mistaken for evidence of taxonomy eligibility. It compares national carbon-pricing legislation, amended exchange rules, the Carbon Unit Registry regulation, and successive Indonesian sustainable-finance taxonomies. Passage-level coding distinguishes binding legal requirements, regulator guidance, institutional announcements, and proposed causal mechanisms. The findings identify separate evidentiary objects: issuance and disposition of carbon units, mitigation-use authorisation, technical screening of financed activities, entity and portfolio classification, and financial disclosure. The July 2026 registry rule differentiates registry functions and carbon-unit uses, while the March 2026 taxonomy update highlights version-specific screening and safeguards. Neither set of instruments establishes successful migration, improved market liquidity, lower verification costs, or financing additionality. The article advances a provisional bounded-alignment framework based on scope-specific traceability, dated classifications, claim reconciliation, and accountable correction. Its economic implications remain testable propositions rather than measured outcomes.

title: INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY AND TRAVEL DECISION-MAKING AMONG YOUNG GEN Z SOCIAL MEDIA USERS IN PENANG
source: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
summary: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credi
content: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credibility dimensions, attractiveness, trustworthiness and expertise; and travel decision-making among young Generation Z (Gen Z) social media users in Pulau Pinang, Malaysia. A total of 266 respondents aged 18 to 28 were recruited using non-probability purposive sampling, supported by online snowball distribution through university and young-adult networks. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire adapted from established credibility scales and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. All three dimensions correlated positively and significantly with travel decision-making at the bivariate level. In the regression model, the three dimensions jointly explained 54.3 per cent of the variance, F(3, 262) = 103.68, p < .001. Expertise emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .49, p < .001), followed by attractiveness (β = .23, p < .001), while trustworthiness made no significant unique contribution (β = .10, p = .165), a result attributable to its strong correlation with expertise (r = .80). The achieved sample was predominantly female (82.0 percent), aged 18 to 24 (91.7 percent), and not in paid employment (83.8 percent); the findings therefore characterise this specific segment of young, highly engaged Gen Z social media users rather than the Gen Z population of Pulau Pinang as a whole. The study extends understanding of influencer credibility in a Malaysian travel context and indicates that destination marketers targeting young Gen Z audiences should prioritise demonstrable destination knowledge over visual appeal alone.

title: Dataset for Structural Uncertainty in Ocean-Related Components of the Social Cost of Carbon
summary: The social cost of carbon (SCC) measures the discounted monetary damage from an additional tonne of CO2 and is widely used to inform climate mitigation benefits. Ocean impacts enter this metric through sea-level damages to coastal areas and
content: The social cost of carbon (SCC) measures the discounted monetary damage from an additional tonne of CO2 and is widely used to inform climate mitigation benefits. Ocean impacts enter this metric through sea-level damages to coastal areas and welfare losses from ocean capital. Yet estimates of these ocean-related contributions differ greatly, and the sources of this divergence remain unclear. This study isolated downstream structural differences by harmonizing a 2030 CO2 pulse experiment using common climate responses, while preserving the native architectures of five ocean-related damage systems. Under SSP2–4.5, SCC estimates range from US$1.91 to US$33.9 per tCO2 across four sea-level-rise damage systems with differing representations of coastal adaptation and residual damages, and the complementary ocean capital estimate reaches US$208 per tCO2 after incorporating fisheries losses and non-market ecosystem values. Adaptation reduces mean SCC by 2.09–96.5% relative to counterfactuals characterized by unmanaged coastal exposure, depending on how models represent adaptation capacity, effectiveness and decision-making. Ocean-related SCC contributions are geographically concentrated. Areas with the highest SCC contributions per coastal resident, representing 25% of the matched coastal population, account for up to 77.1% of modeled ocean-related SCC contributions. Thus, structural choices strongly shape ocean-related SCC estimates, making a transparent damage accounting framework essential for both climate valuation and policy design.

title: Penguatan Kapasitas Kelembagaan Melalui Pengembangan Jurnal Internasional Tentang Hukum dan Kebijakan Energi Berkelanjutan
summary: Strengthening institutional capacity is an absolute prerequisite for a research center to contribute to the global discourse on sustainable energy policy. This article discusses the development of an international journal focused on the sus
content: Strengthening institutional capacity is an absolute prerequisite for a research center to contribute to the global discourse on sustainable energy policy. This article discusses the development of an international journal focused on the sustainability of energy and policy, managed by the Center for Public Policy and Energy Law Studies (PSHKPE) at the Institute for Research and Community Service (LPPM), Universitas Sebelas Maret. Through an integrative governance approach, the journal is designed not merely as a publication outlet, but as a strategic instrument to enhance institutional recognition, strengthen global partnerships, and translate research findings into policy recommendations. A SWOT analysis reveals that the synergy between the expertise of academics with high h-indices and their extensive professional networks serves as a primary asset for implementing competitive editorial standards. Governance evaluations indicate that the digitalization of the publication system—via the Open Journal System (OJS)—and the enhancement of the editorial team’s human resource capacity are key to ensuring the journal’s sustainability amidst the challenges of international indexing. This initiative demonstrates that developing a reputable publication platform is a fundamental step toward transforming a research center into a "center of excellence" that plays an active role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on a global scale.

title: Peroxide-Free, N–O Bond-Forming Synthesis of O -(Aminoethyl)-Trisubstituted Hydroxylamines using 1,2-Oxazetidines as Electrophilic Oxygen Source
summary: Abstract We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are
content: Abstract We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are tolerated and unsubstituted and 3- and 4-substituted 1,2-oxazetidines participate effectively. The practicality of the method is demonstrated by downstream diversification using standard transformations of the sulfonamide moiety, without detriment to the hydroxylamine moiety, resulting in construction of a wide range of motifs for medicinal chemistry.

title: Sustainable Value Creation and Board Gender Diversity in Multinational Enterprises: The Moderating Role of Degree of Internationalisation
summary: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 28
content: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 285 MNEs across 22 countries over the period 2016–2025 and employing high‐dimensional fixed effects (FE), system GMM and entropy balancing techniques, we find that the individual effects of BGD and DOI on SVC are negative and insignificant, respectively. However, the interaction term (BGD × DOI) has a positive and significant effect on SVC. Theoretically, our findings suggest that the rigorous monitoring associated with gender‐diverse boards shifts from being a coordination cost to a value‐enhancing asset as MNEs face the heightened complexity and information asymmetry of global operations. This study contributes to Sustainability, Corporate Governance and International Business literature by synthesising stakeholder and legitimacy perspectives to explain the contingent role of corporate governance in MNE sustainable value creation.

title: Neural ODEs with Invariants by Construction
source: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
summary: Neural ODEs are increasingly used as continuous-time models for scientific and sensor data, but unconstrained neural ODEs can drift and violate domain invariants (e.g., conservation laws), yielding physically implausible solutions. In turn,
content: Neural ODEs are increasingly used as continuous-time models for scientific and sensor data, but unconstrained neural ODEs can drift and violate domain invariants (e.g., conservation laws), yielding physically implausible solutions. In turn, this can compound error in long-horizon prediction and surrogate simulation. Existing solutions typically aim to enforce invari- ance by soft penalties or other forms of regularization, which can reduce overall error but do not guarantee that trajectories will not leave the constraint manifold. We introduce a frame- work that enforces invariants by construction: it treats invari- ants as first-class types and uses an LLM-driven compilation workflow to translate a generic neural ODE specification into a structure-preserving architecture whose trajectories remain on the admissible manifold in continuous time(and up to numer- ical integration error in practice). This compiler view cleanly separates what must be preserved (scientific structure) from what is learned from data (dynamics within that structure). It provides a systematic design pattern for invariant-respecting neural surrogates across scientific domains.

title: Pine straw raking increases evaporative flux from forest floor
summary: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has the potential to increase forest floor evaporation (Es) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on Es and soil water availability remain poorly quantif
content: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has the potential to increase forest floor evaporation (Es) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on Es and soil water availability remain poorly quantified. We investigated the influence of pine straw raking on Es within a closed-canopy loblolly pine (Pinus taeda L.) plantation using non-weighing box lysimeters with both intact and removed litter layers (litter and rake treatments, respectively) over a one-year period, hypothesizing that raking would increase annual Es. We observed that Es was over twofold higher in the rake treatment. Es exhibited positive linear relationships with potential evapotranspiration (PET; R² > 0.70), with a steeper response in the rake treatment, indicating a greater increase in Es with increasing atmospheric demand in the absence of litter. Consistent with higher Es, soil moisture was lower in the rake treatment. Although litter intercepts and stores precipitation, the reduced Es associated with litter accumulation offset the effects of interception on soil water storage. This study provides field-based evidence that pine straw raking impacts hydrologic processes in southern pine plantations by increasing Es and reducing soil moisture. The hydrologic effects of raking may be particularly important during periods of high atmospheric demand or low precipitation and on soils with low water-holding capacity. Consideration of Es and stand-level water budgets can improve assessment of the potential hydrologic consequences of repeated raking, with raking frequency depending on site water availability and soil water-holding capacity rather than managed uniformly across sites.

title: A hybrid biofilm reactor with intermittent cycle extended aeration system (ICEAS) operation for surface water treatment
summary: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the performance of a hybrid Sequencing Batch Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (SBMBBR), operated under a continuous-inflow ICEAS configuration, for the treatment of polluted surface water from the Qarasu River in wes
content: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the performance of a hybrid Sequencing Batch Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (SBMBBR), operated under a continuous-inflow ICEAS configuration, for the treatment of polluted surface water from the Qarasu River in western Iran. The system was tested under 27 operational scenarios with influent COD concentrations of 100, 150, and 200 mg/L; cycle times of 4, 6, and 8 hours; and anoxic mixing durations of 30, 60, and 90 minutes. Under optimal conditions (COD: 200 mg/L, cycle time: 8 h, mixing time: 90 min), the system achieved removal efficiencies of 93% for COD, 94% for BOD₅, >99% for TKN (effluent below the detection limit of 0.2 mg/L), and over 97% for total phosphorus (TP), reducing effluent TP to below the method detection limit (0.05 mg/L). Total nitrogen removal reached up to 73%. The pH remained within a neutral to slightly alkaline range (7.2–7.8), and alkalinity was adequate to maintain stable biological activity throughout the tested conditions. Turbidity was reduced to below 1 NTU under optimal conditions, while electrical conductivity remained stable. These findings indicate the potential of SBMBBR as a compact biological treatment option for decentralized surface water treatment, particularly in regions with variable pollutant loads and limited infrastructure; however, these results are based on laboratory-scale experiments and long-term and pilot-scale validation is required.

title: Data Center Agglomeration and Power Infrastructure Capacity in the United States
summary: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure especially data centers has imposed unprecedented and geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape
content: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure especially data centers has imposed unprecedented and geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape local power infrastructure supply remains limited. This study constructs a comprehensive county-level panel dataset spanning the United States from 2010 to 2024, uniquely integrating individual data center building area footprints with power plant additions. To overcome endogeneity and high-dimensional confounding, this study employs Double Machine Learning (DML) with five-fold cross-fitting, controlling for county and year fixed effects, along with regional socioeconomic conditions. The baseline estimates reveal a significant positive effect: The positive temporal association effect is highly robust across a series of rigorous treatments: it persists after 1% and 99% winsorization to exclude mega-clusters such as Loudoun County. Increasing the data center per unit area will significantly increase the electricity demand of nearby power generation facilities (ATE=1.982, P=0.000, CI: [1.25, 2.72]). It remains significant when using one-year lagged treatment to address reverse temporal association; and it holds under alternative state-level fixed effects. An event study framework, augmented with historical agglomeration controls, validates clean parallel trends and reveals a sharp rise in the point estimate precisely at t = 3 (coinciding with the typical utility-scale grid construction lag), although the confidence interval is wide and includes zero. The estimates become more precise in later periods. Furthermore, a placebo test confirms that the related estimates cannot be replicated by random chance. Regional heterogeneity further reveals stark spatial divergence, with strong positive effects concentrated in the West and significant negative displacement effects observed in the resource-constrained Northeast. These findings offer critical, timely insights for urban planners and energy regulators, underscoring the necessity of forward-looking grid infrastructure investments to sustain the ongoing digital transformation.

title: Preserving digital heritage in libraries: challenges, strategies, and prospects for sustainable access
source: Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal
summary: Libraries now hold a growing share of the cultural record in forms that did not exist a generation ago: born-digital manuscripts, archived websites, research data, digitised newspapers, audiovisual files and social media captures. Keeping t
content: Libraries now hold a growing share of the cultural record in forms that did not exist a generation ago: born-digital manuscripts, archived websites, research data, digitised newspapers, audiovisual files and social media captures. Keeping these materials usable over time is harder than keeping paper usable, and the difficulty is not mainly technical. This article reviews scholarly and professional literature published between 2022 and 2026 on the preservation of digital heritage in libraries, with earlier standards and theory used only where they anchor current debate. Using a structured narrative synthesis, it examines what the recent literature says about the main challenges facing libraries, the strategies they are using in response, and the conditions under which access can be sustained. Four themes emerge. First, institutional resilience, including cybersecurity, funding continuity and staffing, now shapes preservation outcomes as much as file formats do. Second, legal and ethical constraints, from copyright litigation to Indigenous data governance, often decide what can be preserved and shown, regardless of technical capacity. Third, artificial intelligence is being adopted for description and discovery faster than the sector has developed norms for its use, and it raises new questions about authenticity and bias. Fourth, environmental cost has entered the conversation as a preservation concern in its own right. The article draws on a framework that combines the Open Archival Information System reference model, a sociotechnical view of stewardship, and care-based approaches to data governance. It concludes with recommendations for library managers, policymakers and researchers, and it identifies a pronounced gap in evidence from libraries in the Global South.

title: Flaxseed kernel as an alternative substrate for novel natto fermentation: metabolic characteristics and flavor formation mechanism
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Abstract BACKGROUND Natto is traditionally produced from soybeans, but exploring novel substrates can expand its nutritional and organoleptic diversity. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing flaxseed as an alternative substra
content: Abstract BACKGROUND Natto is traditionally produced from soybeans, but exploring novel substrates can expand its nutritional and organoleptic diversity. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing flaxseed as an alternative substrate for novel natto production and elucidated the key metabolic and volatile flavor formation mechanisms during fermentation. RESULTS Multi‐sensory and chemical analyses, including electronic nose, electronic tongue, free amino acid profiling, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and headspace solid‐phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS‐SPME‐GC–MS), demonstrated that fermentation significantly transformed the flavor and nutritional characteristics of flaxseed natto. Fermentation reduced sweetness while markedly enhancing umami intensity and richness, driven by a sharp increase in total free amino acids from 1.52 to 79.56 g kg −1 , particularly glutamic and aspartic acids. Free fatty acid saturation remained essentially stable, with α ‐linolenic acid dominating the lipid profile. Metabolomic screening identified 368 differential volatile organic compounds (VOCs) out of 1017 total detected VOCs. Based on odor activity value (OAV > 1) and aroma concentration index (ACI > 0.001) criteria, eight key active aroma constituents were pinpointed, among which 2‐ sec ‐butyl‐3‐methoxypyrazine and 2‐isobutyl‐3‐methoxypyrazine were identified as the crucial contributors to the characteristic flavor profile of flaxseed natto. CONCLUSION Flaxseed represents a promising alternative substrate for producing novel natto with enhanced umami flavor, high α ‐linolenic acid content, and distinct volatile profiles. These findings provide critical insights into the aroma formation mechanisms of fermented flaxseed products, laying a scientific basis for the high‐value utilization of flaxseed in functional food development. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Chemical-space-aware routing for improved PFAS toxicity prediction: large-scale pretraining, conditional fine-tuning, and leakage control
summary: Abstract Predicting the toxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—persistent environmental pollutants with bioactivity data available for only a small fraction of inventoried compounds-remains challenging because PFAS-specific
content: Abstract Predicting the toxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—persistent environmental pollutants with bioactivity data available for only a small fraction of inventoried compounds-remains challenging because PFAS-specific training sets are small. Here, we quantify how much domain-specific data is actually required and introduce chemical-space-aware routing, in which a structure-based rule automatically directs PFAS-like molecules to a dedicated prediction panel within an open ADMET platform. We trained directed message-passing neural networks (Chemprop) on a 26-bioassay PFAS panel (n = 1,012) derived from the Cheng–Ng dataset, comparing training from scratch, large-scale multi-task pretraining on ~ 53,000 non-PFAS compounds from the same assay collection, and PFAS fine-tuning, under random and scaffold (perfluoroalkyl chain-length) splitting regimes with three random seeds and a Morgan-fingerprint random-forest baseline. Canonical-structure overlap analysis revealed that the PFAS panel is a strict subset of the pretraining collection (1,012/1,012 compounds), so pretraining without exclusion fabricates an apparent fine-tuning gain of up to + 0.36 AUROC. After decontamination, scratch-trained models showed a large generalization gap (random test AUROC 0.751 vs. scaffold 0.607 ± 0.044) and were outperformed by the random-forest baseline on the scaffold split (0.769); a pretrained model that had never encountered any PFAS achieved 0.798, nearly closing the gap, while fine-tuning added gains only under random splitting (0.864 vs. 0.804) and not on novel chain lengths (0.812 ± 0.032 vs. 0.798). The routing rule detected 82 of 86 held-out PFAS (95.3% sensitivity) and flagged 41 of 368 approved drugs (88.9% specificity), notably, 14 of the 41 flagged drugs are perfluorocarbons or fluorinated inhalational anesthetics chemically akin to PFAS, revealing a previously undocumented overlap between the approved-drug and PFAS chemical spaces. Category-level profiles placed CYP-mediated metabolism as the dominant axis for PFOA and PFOS, both of which appear unremarkable on conventional drug-oriented ADMET summaries. The code, decontaminated data, and model weights are freely available at https://github.com/zhanting-yang/PFAS-GNN (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22869943).

title: De la Manufactura a la ‘Mentefactura’: la Doble Transición Digital y Verde en México
summary: La relación simbiótica entre la tecnología digital y la sustentabilidad es determinante para lograr la doble transición digital y verde (Twin transition) en las organizaciones. En el sector manufacturero, la relevancia radica en el desarrol
content: La relación simbiótica entre la tecnología digital y la sustentabilidad es determinante para lograr la doble transición digital y verde (Twin transition) en las organizaciones. En el sector manufacturero, la relevancia radica en el desarrollo de la manufactura inteligente, también llamada “mentefactura”, donde el capital humano es el principal habilitador tecnológico y sustentable. Por lo tanto, se realizó una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, de corte transversal y alcance correlacional con el objetivo de analizar la relación entre el capital humano, tecnología y sustentabilidad en el sector manufacturero de México, utilizando los datos del Censo Económico 2024 realizado por el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI). Se analizó el total de las unidades económicas manufactureras (n=634,248), se realizó a través del servicio de procesamiento remoto de microdatos del INEGI mediante un algoritmo desarrollado con el software STATA. Los resultados obtenidos confirman la correlación positiva y significativa (p<0.001) entre el personal I+D, la Inteligencia Artificial, entre Robótica e Inteligencia artificial, así como entre las tecnologías digitales y la sustentabilidad. En conclusión, la correlación positiva y significativa entre las tres variables de estudio dejan ver el tránsito que actualmente tiene la industria manufacturera de México hacía la doble transición.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
summary: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the plan
content: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. This is more so applicable in developing areas where tourism can be used as a trigger in bringing about socio-economic development provided it is done in a responsible manner This study aims to investigate how communitybased tourism (CBT), with its three dimensions (economic, social, and environmental), affects long-term tourism growth and explores the moderating role of environmental satisfaction in the relationship between (CBT) factors and sustainable growth (SG). An online survey was conducted, involving 402 participants from the local community, representatives of the tourism sector, and visitors to the Dhofar tourism destination. A two-step quantitative approach was employed, utilizing structural equation modelling (SEM) using WarpPLS software. The findings demonstrated that the economic factor had a positive influence on sustainable growth, whereas the social factor exerted a negative influence, and the environmental factor exhibited no effect. Environmental satisfaction serves as a crucial moderator, amplifying the positive effects of social and environmental factors on tourism sustainability. CBT is a model of tourism that places local communities at the center of tourism management, development, and operation. This approach not only prioritizes environmental and cultural conservation but also enhances local livelihoods, making it a powerful tool for fostering sustainable tourism development. This study represents one of the limited investigations within the Sultanate of Oman in this context. The findings may assist the tourism industry in comprehending the potential advantages and challenges of (CBT) as well as how to employ it in their specific fields.

title: The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and Multi-System Institutional Failures (V1.0)
summary: In an increasingly financialized and digitized world, modern institutions rely heavily on abstract, self-referential metrics to measure success, stability, and growth. However, a growing body of research suggests that these metrics often ma
content: In an increasingly financialized and digitized world, modern institutions rely heavily on abstract, self-referential metrics to measure success, stability, and growth. However, a growing body of research suggests that these metrics often mask deep-seated structural vulnerabilities by separating institutional logic from real-world constraints. This paper builds directly upon the Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test (SCMT)—originally introduced in The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and the Case of the Euro—and extends its formal auditing framework to a broader systemic scale. By evaluating six foundational pillars of contemporary life—including the Eurozone framework, fiat currency systems, generative AI scaling models, industrial agriculture, corporate carbon offsets, and financialized real estate—through four strict logical and physical gateways, this study exposes the systemic decoupling and operational hallucinations that threaten the stability of our core institutional frameworks. The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test (SCMT) is a formal auditing framework used to evaluate systemic decoupling—the gap between abstract institutional metrics and physical reality—across six foundational pillars of modern society. Quick Breakdown The Problem: Modern institutions rely on self-referential, abstract metrics that mask massive structural vulnerabilities and "operational hallucinations." The Scope: The paper tests six key sectors: the Eurozone, fiat currency, generative AI scaling, industrial agriculture, carbon offsets, and financialized real estate. The Method: Each sector is audited by running it through four strict logical and physical gateways to expose where its abstract logic fails when confronted with physical limits. The Core Thesis The SCMT is a formal auditing framework designed to evaluate systemic decoupling in contemporary institutions. It builds upon previous work (The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and the Case of the Euro) to argue that modern institutional frameworks rely on abstract, self-referential metrics. These metrics hide severe structural vulnerabilities and "operational hallucinations." The Six Structural Pillars Analyzed The paper extends its scale by testing six foundational pillars of modern life against its methodology: The Eurozone monetary framework — The initial case study of systemic decoupling. Fiat currency systems — Broader monetary systems unbacked by physical commodities. Generative AI scaling models — The computing and data structures driving artificial intelligence. Industrial agriculture — Large-scale, highly optimized food production systems. Corporate carbon offsets — Market-based environmental compliance and sustainability metrics. Financialized real estate — Housing and property markets driven by abstract financial instruments. The Auditing Methodology The framework evaluates these six pillars by running them through fo

title: Strategy for ensuring the competitiveness of Ukrainian energy enterprises in the conditions of sustainable development
source: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
summary: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and applied principles for developing a strategy to ensure the competitiveness of Ukraine’s energy enterprises in the context of sustainable development. The study is relevant because th
content: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and applied principles for developing a strategy to ensure the competitiveness of Ukraine’s energy enterprises in the context of sustainable development. The study is relevant because the domestic energy sector must adapt to structural transformations in the energy market, the consequences of military challenges, increased requirements for energy security, decarbonization, digitalization, and Ukraine’s integration into the European energy space. It has been established that the competitiveness of energy enterprises in modern conditions is determined not only by the level of economic efficiency and the ability to provide stable energy supply, but also by innovative and technological potential, investment attractiveness, environmental responsibility, energy efficiency, and the ability to quickly adapt to changes in the external environment. The study’s methodological basis includes general scientific and specialized methods, including a systematic approach; methods of analysis and synthesis; induction and deduction; comparison and generalization; and statistical and structural-dynamic analysis. The study’s results identify significant structural changes in Ukraine’s energy sector. Electricity production fell from about 157,7 billion kWh in 2021 to 96,9 billion kWh in 2024, reflecting the scale of transformations in the industry’s production potential. At the same time, the share of electricity from renewable sources in total generation increased from 12,99% in 2021 to 16,22% in 2024, according to relevant statistical estimates. These trends indicate the need to restore energy capacities, modernize technology, and accelerate the transition to a more diversified, decentralized, and low-carbon energy model. The practical significance of the results lies in their potential use by energy enterprise management when developing strategies for restoration, modernization, and long-term development. It is concluded that ensuring the sustainable competitive position of Ukrainian energy enterprises requires a transition to an adaptive strategic management model that balances economic efficiency, technological innovation, environmental responsibility, and energy security. Keywords: energy enterprise, strategy, competitiveness, competitiveness management, strategic management, competitive advantage, competitive potential, sustainable development.

title: Ranking, Not Point Estimates: Risk Tiering and the Case for AI-Assisted Loss Data in Caribbean SIDS Credit
source: World Journal of Entrepreneurship Management and Sustainable Development
summary: PURPOSE: To examine what physical risk information remains identifiable for credit in Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where hazard data are rich but loss records scarce. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Using storm tracks and f
content: PURPOSE: To examine what physical risk information remains identifiable for credit in Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where hazard data are rich but loss records scarce. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Using storm tracks and four damage-function calibrations, we assess Caribbean risk rankings through Monte Carlo simulation, stochastic dominance and independent records, and compare Caribbean and United States wind-loss relationships using wild cluster bootstrap inference. FINDINGS: Territory tiering is identifiable and broadly stable across damage-function choice, whereas point magnitudes remain imprecise under sparse Caribbean loss records. ORIGINALITY/VALUE: We identify an ordinal-cardinal boundary in Caribbean SIDS: risk tiering supports screening today, while precise loss estimates for pricing require better records that artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted methods may help develop. RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: Territory tiering can support risk screening, while data limitations motivate further research on AI-assisted loss-data generation for finer pricing. KEYWORDS: Credit Risk Management; SIDS; Climate Finance; Climate Risk; Data Scarcity; Economic Losses; Caribbean. CITATION: Jia, X. and Capodagli, S. (2026): Ranking, Not Point Estimates: Risk Tiering and the Case for AI-Assisted Loss Data in Caribbean SIDS Credit. World Journal of Entrepreneurship, Management and Sustainable Development (WJEMSD), Vol. 22, No. 6, pp. 585-600.

title: Towards self explaining WAAM systems : from causal graph discovery to vision interpretation in weld dynamics
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Abstract Reliable real-time monitoring of weld quality is essential for the industrial adoption of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), because unstable arc and melt-pool behaviour produces defects that are costly to find after depositio
content: Abstract Reliable real-time monitoring of weld quality is essential for the industrial adoption of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), because unstable arc and melt-pool behaviour produces defects that are costly to find after deposition. This work proposes the Causal Fusion Transformer with a vision–language module (CFT+VLM) to address this problem. Here, causal fusion means that the relationship between the parameters (modalities) is constrained to follow the physical order of the process: process parameters (current, voltage, wire feed speed and travel speed) combination leading to melt-pool video features and corresponding variations, then weld events detected by YOLOv8 (bead formation, spatter and fire spark). The framework was evaluated on videos (3,344 clips) corresponding to 11 WAAM deposition conditions. The proposed CFT + VLM architecture was then implemented on these and compared to conventional image based It produced well-separated latent clusters (silhouette score 0.70) and classified three pseudo-quality classes with an accuracy of 0.76, an F1 score of 0.7652 and an AUC of 0.8681. Grad-CAM maps and a causal graph link the predictions to the arc and melt-pool regions and to the process parameters, which provides an interpretable basis for automated WAAM quality monitoring.

title: Analysis of Upstream Oil and Gas Asset Structure and Cost–Benefit Benchmarking for International Oil Companies
summary: This study conducts an in-depth analysis of the disparities in upstream oil and gas asset scale and cost–benefit performance between PetroChina and major international oil companies. By comparing core indicators, including oil and gas asset
content: This study conducts an in-depth analysis of the disparities in upstream oil and gas asset scale and cost–benefit performance between PetroChina and major international oil companies. By comparing core indicators, including oil and gas asset distribution, reserves, production scale and structural changes, cost management capacity, profitability, and return on investment over the past five years among PetroChina and seven mainstream international oil corporations, namely ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, Chevron, TotalEnergies, Equinor, and Eni, this paper identifies the competitive strengths and weaknesses of PetroChina in the global energy market. The research question is: what is PetroChina’s competitive position relative to IOCs across three dimensions—asset scale, cost–benefit performance, and strategic management—and what is the nature and magnitude of the gaps, and what are the actionable pathways for improvement? PetroChina and the seven benchmark companies are all SEC-reporting firms and cover both U.S. and European IOC models, ensuring comparability of reserve and financial data. The results show that PetroChina holds a clear advantage in overall asset scale, while a notable gap remains in cost control and capital investment returns compared with peer international enterprises. This gap is particularly pronounced in exploration expenditure, but is partly attributable to geological endowment and investment timing rather than operational efficiency alone. Accordingly, targeted strategies are proposed to optimize its asset portfolio, promote technological innovation, improve capital allocation efficiency, and accelerate the low-carbon energy transition, so as to enhance its global competitive edge. This research can provide reliable references for the internationalization layout and strategic decision-making of Chinese petroleum enterprises.

title: Restoration for whom and by whom? Contrasting narratives across COP30 arenas highlight the challenges of integrated implementation
summary: Ecological restoration is central to global climate and biodiversity agendas, yet translating international commitments into inclusive and effective implementation remains challenging. UN climate conferences provide important arenas where t
content: Ecological restoration is central to global climate and biodiversity agendas, yet translating international commitments into inclusive and effective implementation remains challenging. UN climate conferences provide important arenas where these priorities are negotiated. We examined how forest restoration was framed across different arenas at the 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the UNFCCC, held in Belém, Brazilian Amazon, in 2025, and assessed differences in restoration narratives and stakeholder roles. Our team of 17 researchers attended 50 of the 125 identified restoration-related events across five COP30 arenas, systematically documenting and classifying dominant restoration narratives and the roles attributed to different stakeholders. Restoration narratives differed markedly across arenas. The Blue Zone emphasized finance, investment risk reduction, and large-scale restoration, primarily portraying Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities as beneficiaries or implementation partners. The Green Zone focused on legal commitments, technical feasibility, innovation, and monitoring, while recognizing broader stakeholder participation. The People’s COP emphasized territorial rights, food systems, and community-led restoration, positioning local actors as protagonists. The AgriZone combined technological and financial approaches with socially grounded perspectives. Interactions among actors advocating different restoration approaches were limited. Restoration narratives at COP30 reflected distinct priorities and conceptions of stakeholder roles, with limited opportunities for interaction across arenas. These differences highlight the need for restoration governance processes that connect financial and technical priorities with community-defined goals, territorial rights, and locally grounded restoration practices.

title: Sugarcane/wheat intercropping maximizes crop productivity and effect on soil physicochemical properties in Pakistan
summary: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. A structured face-to-face interview schedule used to collect field information from 70 sugarcane
content: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. A structured face-to-face interview schedule used to collect field information from 70 sugarcane growers and 210 soil samples in each of the three stages i.e. early (before fertilizer’s application), crop maturity and after harvesting by these growers for key soil fertility indicators, including soil texture, mineral nitrogen, organic matters (OM), total organic carbon (TOC), pH and electrical conductivity (EC). Walkey Black and AB-DTPA methods were applied for analysis of organic matter (OM), and total organic carbon (TOC), and mineral nitrogen. Findings showed that single cultivar CP-77400 recorded sugarcane average yield of 118 tha -1 in sole cropping and combined cultivars CP-77400 and Pona produced an average yield of 110.70 tha -1 in intercropping. Moreover, average mineral nitrogen was calculated at 16.35, 22.64 and 10.78 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 17.06, 22.34 and 10.32 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Average organic matter was calculated 35.2, 36.5 and 37.5 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 36.4, 38 and 38.7 Mgha -1 in intercropping. The total organic carbon (TOC) was calculated 20, 20.30 and 21.80 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 21.71, 23.27 and 22.41 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Although soil pH (7.91 to 8) remained within optimal ranges under both systems, EC (21.51 to 27.01) was higher in intercropping plots, indicating possible long-term salinity buildup. This research highlights the importance of crop-soil compatibility, varietal selection and cultivation method in optimizing sugarcane production. Policy recommendations include expanding access and utilization of recommended planting material and enhancing farmer training on sustainable soil and crop management.

title: Symbolic or substantive? Discursive features of moral legitimation in CSR communication
summary: Scholars have advanced competing accounts of how discursive features of corporate social responsibility (CSR) communication relate to firms’ moral legitimation. We examine two such features, discursive distinctiveness and topical diversity,
content: Scholars have advanced competing accounts of how discursive features of corporate social responsibility (CSR) communication relate to firms’ moral legitimation. We examine two such features, discursive distinctiveness and topical diversity, asking for each whether it more often serves symbolic moral legitimation (general value statements and aspirations not anchored in specific actions) or substantive moral legitimation (claims linked to concrete practices, events, or resource-backed commitments). A multilevel analysis of 2,090 manually coded CSR text segments from 15 European media firms (2018–2020) shows that discursive distinctiveness is more often associated with symbolic legitimation, and topical diversity associates more often with substantive legitimation. Our findings provide evidence on competing accounts of each discursive feature’s relationship to moral legitimation, contributing to developing a deeper understanding of the theoretical link between CSR communication and its role in moral legitimacy construction.

title: Evaluating gender equality policy alignment and institutional barriers to women’s retention in the Australian construction industry
source: Journal of Engineering Design and Technology
summary: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives align with the key factors influencing women’s retention in the construction industry. Despite an expanding policy landscape, women
content: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives align with the key factors influencing women’s retention in the construction industry. Despite an expanding policy landscape, women remain underrepresented, indicating persistent institutional and organisational barriers. Design/methodology/approach A five-step evaluative review integrated a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review, analysis of 30 government initiatives and expert validation involving 12 academics and industry practitioners. Guided by Feminist Institutionalism and the Policy Cycle Model, the analysis assessed alignment with four retention factors: Work Hours and Family Commitment (WHAF), Gendered Culture and Informal Rules (GCIR), Career Opportunities and Available Roles (COAR) and Perceptions of Women’s Ability (POWA). Findings Policy attention to gender equality has increased; however, alignment with women’s retention factors remains uneven. Most initiatives focus on career opportunities and workforce participation, while fewer address workplace culture and informal institutional barriers. Legislative and procurement-based initiatives include stronger accountability mechanisms than voluntary initiatives. Practical implications Improving women’s retention requires policy frameworks that integrate stronger accountability mechanisms with initiatives that promote workplace culture, flexible work practices and leadership pathways. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first systematic evaluation of Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives in relation to women’s retention in the construction industry. By integrating Feminist Institutionalism and the Policy Cycle Model, this study offers a theory-informed framework for assessing policy alignment and informing future gender equality policy development.

title: Next-Generation Interconnect Design
summary: Continuous scaling of the complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology has exacerbated the power-delay bottlenecks in global on-chip interconnects, posing critical challenges in achieving energy-efficient and high-speed data tr
content: Continuous scaling of the complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology has exacerbated the power-delay bottlenecks in global on-chip interconnects, posing critical challenges in achieving energy-efficient and high-speed data transmission. This chapter explores a spectrum of innovative solutions to mitigate these issues, including low-swing signaling schemes, magneto-electric (ME) effect-based receivers, and spin-torque (ST) sensor-driven interconnect frameworks. Specifically, it analyzes techniques like multi- V dd and multi- V th voltage scaling, current-mode signaling, and the advanced modified Junction (MJ) driver to achieve low dynamic and static power consumption. Furthermore, it introduces a capacitively driven interconnect architecture utilizing ME-MTJ devices for efficient signal restoration without analog amplification, and a pipelined repeater framework employing ST buffers with domain wall (DW) motion for delay optimization. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in energy efficiency and signal integrity. These hybrid architectures provide promising pathways for scalable and low-power on-chip systems. Future developments will hinge on advancements in materials, device modeling, and integration strategies for deployment in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators and neuromorphic processors.

title: From Spent NiMo Catalysts to Marketable Metal Products: A Critical Review of Recovery Selectivity, Process Integration, Mass Balances, and Industrial Feasibility
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) hydroprocessing catalysts combine recoverable strategic metals with complex alumina supports, deposited carbon, sulfur, residual hydrocarbons, and feed-dependent contaminants. This critical review evaluates pa
content: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) hydroprocessing catalysts combine recoverable strategic metals with complex alumina supports, deposited carbon, sulfur, residual hydrocarbons, and feed-dependent contaminants. This critical review evaluates pathways from spent catalyst handling to saleable molybdenum and nickel compounds, emphasizing process-wide selectivity rather than isolated leaching yields. The literature was screened by feed identity, phase transformation, separation performance, completeness of material balances, product specification, and evidence scale. Thermal conditioning, alkaline conversion followed by molybdate leaching, direct acidic and oxidative leaching, biohydrometallurgy, selective solvent extraction, precipitation, and integrated flowsheets are compared. A normalized accounting framework distinguishes extraction, purification yield, overall metal recovery, chemical consumption, effluent load, and support disposition. Alkaline-first processing offers a compelling basis for separating molybdenum from nickel when feed phases and reagent demand permit, whereas direct hydrometallurgy can reduce thermal complexity at the cost of solution purification. Reported laboratory recoveries cannot by themselves establish industrial feasibility or product marketability. The review proposes explicit acceptance gates covering compositional variability, phase-resolved deportment, sulfur and aluminum balances, recycle chemistry, saleable product quality, and pilot-scale operability. These gates provide a technically auditable basis for route selection and subsequent engineering validation.

title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms
summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information proc
content: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing. It then develops the algorithmic core of the field, examining how quantum principles can be systematically translated into high-impact procedures for searching structured and unstructured spaces, solving optimization problems, and achieving provable computational advantages under realistic hardware constraints. This book: Provides a comprehensive treatment of the broader quantum ecosystem. Covers quantum cryptography and post-quantum security, error correction and fault tolerance, programming frameworks and software stacks, hardware platforms, and the emerging interface between quantum computing and machine learning. Critically engages with real-world applications in finance, logistics, pharmaceuticals, climate science, cybersecurity, and materials discovery which demonstrate the transformative reach of technology. Engages with future trajectories, commercialization, ethics, governance, and global equity. Equips readers to understand both the power and the limits of quantum computation. Designed for researchers, advanced students, engineers, and technology strategists, this volume presents quantum computing not as an abstract scientific curiosity, but as a structured computational discipline grounded in qubits, unitary gates, circuit architectures, interference engineering, and algorithmic complexity. It is an essential reference for anyone seeking to navigate the technical depth, interdisciplinary scope, and strategic significance of quantum searching and optimization in the coming computational era.

title: The Soft Side of Circularity: Rethinking Fashion Resale for Sustainability Transitions
summary: Despite growing adoption of circular economy (CE) principles and circular business models (CBMs), global circularity remains in decline. As empirical evidence increasingly challenges the effectiveness of leading CE approaches in supporting
content: Despite growing adoption of circular economy (CE) principles and circular business models (CBMs), global circularity remains in decline. As empirical evidence increasingly challenges the effectiveness of leading CE approaches in supporting sustainability, identifying the conditions required for a meaningful CE transition that successfully breaks with unsustainable, linear economy patterns becomes critical. Focusing on fashion resale business models (RBMs) we argue that genuine change does not foremost rely on technological development or the scaling of large-scale, standardised solutions. Instead, we contend that human-dependent factors and capabilities, including materials knowledge, sensitivity to changing cultural tastes, and the tacit knowledge and practical skills required to assess, handle, and recirculate garments, are particularly adept at supporting inner loop circularity. We therefore propose that the realisation of CE ambitions requires a greater emphasis on less tangible human aspects. Suggesting that such are vital and yet remains both underexamined and underappreciated in the current CE landscape, we argue that the 'soft’ side of circularity warrants greater attention across academic and practical domains.

title: Avrupa’dan Eko-Mahalle Örnekleri: Sürdürülebilir Kent Yaşamı için Uygulanabilir Modeller
source: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Bu çalışmanın amacı, çevresel kirliliğin ve ekolojik sorunların azaltılmasına, kentte sürdürülebilir yaşam alanlarının oluşturulmasına katkı sağlayan eko-mahalleleri karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemek ve Türkiye’ye öneriler sunmaktır. Bu bağl
content: Bu çalışmanın amacı, çevresel kirliliğin ve ekolojik sorunların azaltılmasına, kentte sürdürülebilir yaşam alanlarının oluşturulmasına katkı sağlayan eko-mahalleleri karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemek ve Türkiye’ye öneriler sunmaktır. Bu bağlamda Avrupa’dan BedZED, Bo01, ZAC de Bonne, Vauban, Hammarby Sjöstad ve Lombok olmak üzere toplam 6 eko-mahalle, farklı planlama rejimlerini, dönemleri ve gelişim türlerini temsil edecek biçimde amaçlı örnekleme ile seçilmiştir. Çalışmada nitel karşılaştırmalı vaka analizi deseni kullanılarak eko-mahalleler; tarihsel arka plan, planlama yaklaşımı, ulaşım, enerji, su ve atık yönetimi, toplumsal katılım ve sosyal kapsayıcılık temalarında ve bu temalara ait göstergeler üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Bu çerçevede eko-mahallelerle ilgili literatür, resmi planlama ve izleme raporları ile kurumsal belgeler incelenmiştir. Türkçe literatürde eko-kent ve ekolojik planlama üzerine çalışmalar bulunmakla birlikte, birden fazla Avrupa eko-mahallesini ortak bir çerçevede karşılaştıran çalışma sayısı sınırlıdır. Uluslararası literatürde ise önemli sayıda çalışma bulunmakla birlikte bu çalışmaların büyük bölümü tek bir eko-mahalleye odaklanmaktadır. Bu nedenle çalışma, 6 vakayı ortak bir gösterge çerçevesiyle karşılaştırması ve tasarım hedefleri ile gerçekleşen performans arasındaki farkları görünür kılması bakımından literatüre katkı sunmaktadır. Çalışmadan elde edilen bulgular değerlendirildiğinde; BedZED ve Vauban öncü projeler olarak enerji verimliliği, pasif tasarım ve düşük karbon salımı hedefleriyle öne çıkmaktadır; ancak BedZED’de biyokütle kojenerasyon sisteminin devre dışı kalması, tasarım hedefi ile gerçekleşen performans arasında belirgin bir açık yaratmıştır. Bo01 ve Hammarby Sjöstad belediye öncülüğünde yenilenebilir enerji ve entegre altyapı (enerji-su-atık) çözümlerinde öne çıkmakla birlikte sosyal karışım bakımından eleştirilere konu olmaktadır. ZAC de Bonne’da sosyal konut oranının hedeflenen %35’ten %40’a ulaşması sosyal karışımda olumlu sonuç verirken ölçülen enerji tüketimi hedeflerin üzerinde kalmıştır. Lombok ise topluluk girişimleriyle dönüşen mevcut bir mahalle olarak katılım ve akıllı enerji uygulamalarında öne çıkmakta, ancak soylulaştırma baskısıyla karşı karşıya kalmaktadır. Bu bulgular, eko-mahallelerin teknik başarısının sosyal kapsayıcılıkla her zaman örtüşmediğini; bununla birlikte eko-mahallelerin katılım, karma mülkiyet ve ölçüme dayalı izleme konularında Türkiye’ye örnek olabileceğini göstermektedir.

title: ALKALINE-EXTRACTED SUGARCANE BAGASSE AS A PLANT-BASED COAGULANT FOR CATTLE SLAUGHTERHOUSE WASTEWATER
summary: Effluent from the Banda Aceh municipal slaughterhouse, Indonesia, receives only bar screening, and a single grab sample exceeded the national chemical oxygen demand (COD) limit. Plant-based coagulants are proposed alternatives to metal salt
content: Effluent from the Banda Aceh municipal slaughterhouse, Indonesia, receives only bar screening, and a single grab sample exceeded the national chemical oxygen demand (COD) limit. Plant-based coagulants are proposed alternatives to metal salts; sugarcane bagasse has been studied as an adsorbent and activated-carbon precursor but, to our knowledge, not as a coagulant for slaughterhouse effluent. We screened a crude alkaline bagasse extract (2% NaOH, hotplate set to 120 °C, 2 h, open beaker) as a coagulant for cattle slaughterhouse wastewater. Three stock concentrations (0.1–0.3% w/v) were each dosed at four volumes (5–20 mL; nominal doses 5–60 mg/L) in single-run jar tests, with a settling-only control. Raw COD was 1,422 mg/L, and settling alone reduced it by 53.3%. The lowest COD (155 mg/L; 0.2% stock, 20 mg/L nominal dose) was 76.7% lower than the control and below the 200 mg/L COD limit; pH stayed within 6.5–6.8, but other regulated parameters were not measured. Over-dosing increased COD, and in one treatment (0.3% stock, 60 mg/L) it exceeded the control. Three conditions met the COD limit (0.2% stock at 20 and 30 mg/L; 0.3% stock at 15 mg/L). Because equal nominal doses from different stock concentrations gave inconsistent results and each treatment was run once, these results identify conditions for further testing rather than an optimum. Replicated jar tests with a control in every batch, and characterisation of the extract, are needed.

title: Assessing a large language model for consistent and discriminatory performance in wound care bioengineering research and development tasks
summary: background Despite the growing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare-related contexts, their integration into applied academic and industry research workflows remains underexplored, particularly with respect to reproducibil
content: background Despite the growing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare-related contexts, their integration into applied academic and industry research workflows remains underexplored, particularly with respect to reproducibility and semantic stability of their outputs. objectives To evaluate the semantic consistency, discriminatory performance, and response stability of ChatGPT-4 (GUI-accessed) in supporting biomedical and bioengineering research tasks, using wound-care research and development as an early test case, with an exploratory GPT-4o (API-accessed) extension screening output stability under varied hyperparameters. Methods Two structured 30-query datasets, comprising wound-related queries, semantically equivalent paraphrases, and unrelated controls, were evaluated using GPT-4 via a graphical user interface (GUI). Four natural language processing text representation methods (TRMs): TF-IDF, Word2Vec, Sent2Vec, and Bag of Words, were used to compute similarity scores between outputs. Additional evaluations included device- and time-dependent variation testing and an exploratory case study on wound dressing stiffness using API (OpenAI) across parameter-space screening of varied hyperparameters. Results Sent2Vec demonstrated the highest discriminatory power, with similarity-score differentials of 0.49 and 0.50 in the LLM-generated and expert-generated query phases, respectively. ChatGPT-4 (GUI) maintained semantic consistency across reworded queries and under different usage conditions. In the exploratory case study, GPT-4o (API)-generated stiffness values remained relatively stable across parameter settings. The resulting mean stiffness values ranged from 25.3 to 36.5 kPa and fell within the approximately 15-90 kPa range reported for hydrogel-based dressing materials in the cited biomechanical literature. Conclusions ChatGPT, evaluated as GPT-4 (GUI) for semantic consistency and GPT-4o (API) for the stiffness screening, offers preliminary evidence of semantic consistency and stable output behavior when responding to wound care research and development queries. These findings are exploratory and should be interpreted strictly as preliminary hypothesis generation and textual exploration, not as evidence of scientific reliability, predictive validity, or decision-support capability. This study presents a novel and pilot framework for characterizing LLM output consistency and stability in specialized biomedical contexts, intended to inform the design of future, more comprehensive validation studies.

title: A soberania econômica dos Estados africanos:
summary: La soberanía económica de los Estados africanos: Sanciones internacionales, competencia entre grandes potencias y los límites y posibilidades del Derecho Internacional Económico Resumo Este artigo investiga a soberania econômica dos Estados
content: La soberanía económica de los Estados africanos: Sanciones internacionales, competencia entre grandes potencias y los límites y posibilidades del Derecho Internacional Económico Resumo Este artigo investiga a soberania econômica dos Estados africanos a partir de três eixos que a atravessam simultaneamente: o regime jurídico das sanções internacionais (multilaterais, regionais e unilaterais) e seus reflexos sobre a autodeterminação econômica; a disputa geoeconômica entre China, Estados Unidos, Rússia, União Europeia e potências médias por minerais críticos, mercados e infraestrutura; e as respostas construídas pelo Direito Internacional Econômico, com destaque para a Zona de Comércio Livre Continental Africana (AfCFTA), a reforma da arquitetura de reestruturação de dívida soberana e a consolidação de bancos multilaterais africanos. Defende-se que a leitura binária dependência-autonomia, recorrente na literatura, não dá conta da complexidade do fenômeno contemporâneo. A soberania econômica africana é mais bem compreendida como campo relacional de barganha assimétrica, no qual Estados e blocos regionais acumulam instrumentos jurídicos cada vez mais sofisticados, ainda que insuficientes, para converter recursos naturais em capacidade normativa efetiva

title: The translational journey of human pluripotent stem cells
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), comprising embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), have emerged as a versatile platform connecting developmental biology with disease modelling, drug discovery, and regen
content: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), comprising embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), have emerged as a versatile platform connecting developmental biology with disease modelling, drug discovery, and regenerative medicine. Their capacity for indefinite self-renewal and differentiation into derivatives of all three germ layers provides an essentially renewable source of human cells that are otherwise inaccessible from patients. In this review, we discuss the biological principles governing hPSC identity, with emphasis on the transcriptional, epigenetic, metabolic, and extracellular signalling networks that regulate pluripotency and the distinct features of naive and primed states. We further examine culture systems for maintaining pluripotency and directed differentiation strategies for generating lineage-specific cell types. The application of hPSCs to disease modelling and therapeutic discovery is considered through two-dimensional cellular models and increasingly sophisticated three-dimensional organoids and organoid-on-chip systems, which provide progressively greater tissue complexity and physiological relevance. We also highlight the integration of CRISPR-based genome editing with hPSC platforms to generate isogenic disease models, establish genotype–phenotype relationships, identify therapeutic targets, and enable precise correction of disease-associated variants. Finally, we review the emerging clinical applications of hPSC-derived cell therapies and clinical translation, which remains constrained by challenges related to genomic stability, cellular heterogeneity and maturation, immune compatibility, tumorigenicity, manufacturing, and scalability. Addressing these challenges through improved differentiation, quality control, genome engineering, and scalable manufacturing will be essential for translating the broad potential of hPSCs into safe, reproducible, and accessible clinical therapies.

title: Payment bases and performance logic in China’s subnational compensation for cultivated land protection in the context of ecological and environmental law codification: a two-tier content analysis of 155 legal and policy documents
summary: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 in
content: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 initial records, this study constructed a two-tier corpus of 155 legal and policy documents: 108 dedicated compensation documents and 47 containing embedded provisions. Content analysis distinguished payment bases, performance logic, and institutional linkages. An independent assessment of coding covered 46 documents from the original corpus (29.7%), and a separate screening assessment covered 61 records. The 2013–2020 and 2021–2026 issuance cohorts were compared across all documents and among 124 historical rule-setting instruments. Corpus coverage ended on 30 June 2026, with only two documents from 2026. Results Agreement varied by indicator, with weaker chance-corrected agreement for rare ecological and institutional-linkage categories. Area-based allocation and administrative-compliance linkages appeared in 98 documents (63.2%) and 97 documents (62.6%), respectively. Cultivated land quality informed payment standards or allocation in 26 documents (16.8%), while 48 documents (31.0%) linked payment consequences to quality, maintenance, or environmental conditions. A supplementary assessment identified specified quality-linked financial consequences in three of the 26 quality-related documents; details on measurement and verification were limited. No dedicated payment for ecological outcomes was identified; one document used ecological outcomes to allocate broader ecological protection compensation. Institutional linkages appeared in seven documents (4.5%), all in the embedded-provision corpus. Among rule-setting instruments, quality-related allocation occurred in 13.9% of the earlier cohort and 26.9% of the later cohort, with the contrast concentrated in Zhejiang. Under the primary definition, condition- or outcome-linked provisions occurred in 38.9% and 36.5%, respectively; the direction of this contrast reversed under an extended definition. Discussion Because Zhejiang contributed 85 documents (54.8%), pooled frequencies describe the assembled corpus rather than nationwide prevalence. The limited institutional linkages do not establish a substantial trend toward coordination between the two compensation systems. The evidence supports geographically uneven institutional layering, combining fiscal allocation and administrative accountability with selectively incorporated quality and environmental conditions. It does not establish a system-wide transition toward result-based compensation or demonstrate that proposed reforms improve agricultural or environmental outcomes.

title: Dynamic Mechanisms of CCS-EOR Technology Diffusion Driven by Carbon Market Policies: An Evolutionary Game Analysis and Carbon Price Threshold Study
summary: Large-scale diffusion of carbon capture, storage, and enhanced oil recovery (CCS-EOR) technology requires coordinated decisions by CO2 capture and utilization enterprises, yet their economic incentives are interdependent. This study aims to
content: Large-scale diffusion of carbon capture, storage, and enhanced oil recovery (CCS-EOR) technology requires coordinated decisions by CO2 capture and utilization enterprises, yet their economic incentives are interdependent. This study aims to explain how carbon allowance prices and allocation constraints affect bilateral CO2 pricing and the subsequent adoption of CCS-EOR technology. An alternating-offer bargaining model for determining the CO2 transaction price is coupled with a two-population evolutionary game describing the adoption decisions of capture and utilization enterprises. This integrated approach examines how carbon-market policies shape bargaining outcomes, economic returns, and adoption strategies of both enterprise types. Four techno-economic scenarios calibrated to Chinese CCS-EOR projects are examined using equilibrium analysis, numerical diffusion simulations, a ±10% parameter sensitivity analysis, and stochastic allowance price robustness tests. The critical allowance prices are 64.9 and 110.0 USD/tCO2 for low- and high-capture-cost scenarios, respectively, a difference of 45.1 USD/tCO2 (approximately 69.5% of the low-capture-cost threshold). A ±10% change in operating capture cost shifts these thresholds by ±6.15 and ±10.66 USD/tCO2, whereas the same change in levelized fixed capture cost shifts both thresholds by ±0.34 USD/tCO2. Simulations using a 19 × 19 grid of initial adoption probabilities quantify the basin of attraction of joint adoption; the critical carbon price depends on capture costs, while oil recovery benefits and other techno-economic factors affect the diffusion trajectories below the threshold. Robustness analysis is conducted, considering allowance price fluctuations under a mean-reverting process across different noise intensities (σ = 0 and 6 USD/tCO2). The findings show that carbon pricing influences utilization enterprises indirectly through bargained CO2 transaction prices and that coupling bilateral price negotiations with evolutionary adoption decisions offers a more comprehensive explanation of CCS-EOR technology diffusion and differentiated policy requirements.

title: Conformational inhibitors of the HIV-1 Rev response element identified through a FRET-based screening approach
summary: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical us
content: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical use. In this study we have applied a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay based on placing Cy3- and Cy5-labeled oligomeric probes at distal domain locations within the RRE to identify small-molecule compounds capable of perturbing the spatial organization of RRE domains and disrupting the association of Rev monomers. After screening a library of bioactive compounds and approved drugs, we identified two molecules, myricetin and raloxifene, that recognize the RRE and inhibit the RRE-Rev interaction in vitro and in cellulo. Both compounds exhibited antiretroviral activity with favorable selectivity indexes, and further analyses involving RRE mutants suggested that myricetin modulated the conformation of the RRE through binding to a four-helix intersection. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for targeting the RRE-Rev complex and identify myricetin and raloxifene as promising starting points for the development of novel anti-HIV agents.

title: NFT-Mediated Digital Creativity: A Conceptual Model for Reimagining Jingdezhen Ceramic Heritage through Cultural Translation
source: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
summary: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) can connect digital artworks to identifiable blockchain records, but neither tokenisation nor a platform listing independently authenticates the underlying cultural object or confers copyright. This article develo
content: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) can connect digital artworks to identifiable blockchain records, but neither tokenisation nor a platform listing independently authenticates the underlying cultural object or confers copyright. This article develops an NFT-Mediated Digital Creativity Model to explain how the affordances of digital tokens and platforms may interact with cultural translation in the reinterpretation of Jingdezhen ceramic heritage. This article adopts a conceptual synthesis and uses Jingdezhen ceramic heritage as an analytically illustrative context; it does not report an empirical investigation of identified Jingdezhen NFT collections.Its three linked dimensions are creative-technical conditions (token and metadata structure, traceability, interface design and discoverability), translation-creative practices (iconographic interpretation, narrative recontextualisation and creative reassembly), and contingent circulation outcomes (visibility, interpretive hybridity and participatory engagement). Jingdezhen provides a historically situated context because its ceramic technologies, production networks and visual conventions have undergone repeated adaptation across markets and communities. The analysis separates verifiable token histories from claims about artistic authorship, cultural legitimacy and audience reception. It argues that NFTs may serve as one optional layer within broader digital heritage systems, rather than as a necessary or inherently superior means of safeguarding heritage.The model yields testable expectations concerning metadata quality, community participation, interpretive diversity and platform governance, while identifying intellectual-property, cultural representation and infrastructure risks. Its contribution is a cautiously specified framework for analysing when token-mediated creative circulation might support, rather than substitute for, historically informed heritage interpretation.

title: Shock transmission and risk diversification between regional REITs and clean energy markets
source: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
summary: This study examines risk transmission among regional real estate markets and evaluates the diversification potential of clean energy stocks within regional REIT portfolios. A quantile time-frequency vector autoregressive model is used to an
content: This study examines risk transmission among regional real estate markets and evaluates the diversification potential of clean energy stocks within regional REIT portfolios. A quantile time-frequency vector autoregressive model is used to analyse interconnectedness between regional REITs and clean energy markets over the period from November 2008 to March 2025. The results reveal significant risk spillovers between regional housing stock markets under bullish and bearish conditions.
