An ALA–Stacking–ARIMA model combines hyperparameter optimization, multivariate prediction, and time-series adjustment, while Monte Carlo simulations propagate uncertainty in future drivers under business-as-usual, mitigation, and high-growth scenarios. Compared with basic Stacking, the proposed model reduces RMSLE by 22.7%–33.3% across the four clusters and achieves a maximum R 2 of 0.9912. The scenario projections show substantial differences in provincial peak timing and emission levels. Mitigation-oriented assumptions generally lead to earlier peaking and lower peak emissions, whereas faster economic expansion tends to increase peak levels and delay peaking. Scenario rankings also vary across provinces, indicating the need to consider regional growth patterns and emission characteristics when developing mitigation strategies. The framework provides conditional projections of provincial carbon-peaking pathways to inform planning under alternative economic and energy-development assumptions.

title: SUSTAINABILITY MANAGEMENT IN CHALLENGING TIMES: REBRANDING, GREENHUSHING, AND CLIMATE SEVERITY
summary: This article examines the hypothesis that the central concepts of the climate debate and corporate responsibility, such as “social responsibility”, “sustainability”, “ESG” and “global warming”, evolve according to a logic of conceptual bran
content: This article examines the hypothesis that the central concepts of the climate debate and corporate responsibility, such as “social responsibility”, “sustainability”, “ESG” and “global warming”, evolve according to a logic of conceptual branding and rebranding. In a context of geopolitical tensions, regulatory uncertainty, and pressure on compliance costs, this process has direct consequences for the management of communication and organizational legitimacy. The analysis rests on an integrative review and a triangulation of secondary sources (research interest, frequency of terms in business reports, news coverage, and physical climate indicators), compared and interpreted descriptively in light of Downs’s issue-attention cycle, media agenda-setting and framing, and institutional isomorphism. Four arenas are compared: the United States, the European Union, China, and Global South countries in the UN negotiations. Documented findings are kept apart from interpretation, and no causal claims are made. Five conclusions emerge. First, the transition from “social responsibility” to “sustainability” and then to “ESG” reveals acceleration followed by semantic wear, with no synchrony across jurisdictions. Second, Anglophone climate discourse follows a similar path, from “global warming” to “climate crisis”. Third, the Global South developed its own cycle, from “climate debt” to “loss and damage”, shaped by the North’s resistance to legal accountability. Fourth, China has built a competing vocabulary. Fifth, the popularity of terms appears decoupled from the physical severity of the problem and may give way to strategic silence (greenhushing) instead of lexical substitution. The study separates rebranding from greenhushing and suggests that organisations keep verifiable commitments stable while adapting their narrative to each jurisdiction. The main contribution is a conceptual distinction between rebranding and greenhushing, two outcomes of lexical decline that look alike but call for different managerial responses.

title: ENSURING MACROECONOMIC STABILITY AND NATIONAL SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF A GREEN ECONOMY: CHALLENGES AND SOLUTIONS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The study presents a comprehensive analysis of theoretical and practical issues of macroeconomic stability provision and the acceleration of national sustainable development in the transition to a green economy. It examines the effects of c
content: The study presents a comprehensive analysis of theoretical and practical issues of macroeconomic stability provision and the acceleration of national sustainable development in the transition to a green economy. It examines the effects of climate change, resource scarcity and environmental threats on macroeconomic variables such as GDP growth, inflation, public debt and investment flows. The study develops mechanisms of ensuring the economic growth with carbon neutrality by comparing the global experience with the green development strategies of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Furthermore, it covers a comprehensive analysis of the opinions of international and domestic scholars, as well as the author's critical and analytical standpoint. The study concludes with actionable recommendations based on science, including green budgeting, green bonds, carbon taxes, and the promotion of resource-efficient technologies

title: OPTIMIZING THE INSULATION LAYER FOR ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN BUILDING FACADES
source: Journal of Mathematics Mechanics and Computer Science
summary: This paper examines the role of shape optimization in improving the thermal performance of building facades. The study investigates whether modifying the internal interface between brick and expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation can enhance
content: This paper examines the role of shape optimization in improving the thermal performance of building facades. The study investigates whether modifying the internal interface between brick and expanded polystyrene (EPS) insulation can enhance seasonal thermal performance without increasing material usage. A two-dimensional steady-state heat diffusion model is solved using a finite-difference scheme. The interface is parameterized by a cubic polynomial under a strict volume-preservation constraint, and optimal shapes are determined through a discrete search. Results indicate that interface geometry affects heat transfer differently across seasons: redistribution of insulation changes thermal resistance under summer conditions, while in winter it alters conductive heat pathways. Overall, geometric redistribution can influence seasonal thermal response while keeping total material volume constant. Without insolation, however, the winter optimal geometry increases heat loss, so the winter result applies to peak-insolation conditions only.

title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
summary: ABSTRACT In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conv
content: ABSTRACT In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1 2 ‐Pt 3 Fe/TiO 2 intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1 2 ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm −2 , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

title: Half-hourly NEE simulation based on flux observations across China's grassland ecosystems: A machine learning fusion approach with interpretability analysis
summary: Accurate simulation of grassland carbon fluxes is critical for regional carbon budget assessment and for supporting China's carbon neutrality goals under climate change. However, high-temporal-resolution estimates of carbon fluxes across Ch
content: Accurate simulation of grassland carbon fluxes is critical for regional carbon budget assessment and for supporting China's carbon neutrality goals under climate change. However, high-temporal-resolution estimates of carbon fluxes across China's heterogeneous grassland ecosystems remain largely limited, and single machine-learning models often show inconsistent predictive performance among ecosystem types. Here, we developed a Random Forest–eXtreme Gradient Boosting (RF-XGB) fusion model to simulate half-hourly net ecosystem CO₂ exchange (NEE) based on eddy covariance observations and concurrent environmental variables from 15 grassland flux sites across China. The fusion model achieved an overall R 2 of 0.6425 across all sites and outperformed standalone base models at 80% of monitoring sites with higher R 2 and lower RMSE. Model performance varied significantly across different grassland types, with alpine steppe (AS, R 2 = 0.7394) and temperate typical steppe (TTS, R 2 = 0.7354) showing relatively high prediction accuracy, alpine meadow (AM, R 2 = 0.6145) exhibiting slightly lower accuracy, and temperate desert steppe (TDS, R 2 = 0.5558) showing the lowest prediction accuracy. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed a hierarchical driver structure for half-hourly NEE, where radiation acts as the primary driver, temperature serves as the secondary regulator, and water-related factors shift from atmospheric dryness (VPD) in mesic grasslands to soil moisture (SWC) in arid systems. This study provides a systematic, type-differentiated evaluation of half-hourly NEE simulation across China's grasslands, demonstrating that multi-algorithm fusion combined with ecosystem-specific parameterization can improve high-resolution carbon flux modeling in heterogeneous landscapes.

title: ECP-YOLO11n: a lightweight insulator defect detection algorithm
summary: Facing the dual carbon goal and the demands of power grid intelligent upgrading, UAV-based inspection technology has been widely adopted for power equipment operation and maintenance. However, restricted by UAV load capacity and the complex
content: Facing the dual carbon goal and the demands of power grid intelligent upgrading, UAV-based inspection technology has been widely adopted for power equipment operation and maintenance. However, restricted by UAV load capacity and the complexity of insulator defect detection, existing methods struggle to balance real-time performance and reliable inspection for small defective targets. We improved the recognition performance of small defective targets by embedding an efficient multi-scale attention mechanism. A lightweight C3Ghost-based feature fusion layer was constructed to eliminate redundant computational overhead. For the backbone network, a progressive channel compression strategy was designed to cut network parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the YOLO11n baseline, the proposed ECP-YOLO11n reduces the parameter count by 59.7% and computational cost by 23.8%. Meanwhile, it retains 99.5% and 95.1% of the original model’s mAP50 on the CPLID-2000 and IDID datasets respectively, satisfying the requirements of real-time and high-reliability detection.

title: Evaluating how restoration frameworks bridge social and ecological dimensions: A mixed‐methods literature review
summary: Abstract Nature restoration has evolved from focussing mostly on ecology to include societal aspects, yet it is unclear how this is reflected in the academic literature. In this article, we investigate the social and ecological dimensions o
content: Abstract Nature restoration has evolved from focussing mostly on ecology to include societal aspects, yet it is unclear how this is reflected in the academic literature. In this article, we investigate the social and ecological dimensions of published frameworks and principles that guide nature restoration. We further assess how socio‐ecological concepts can be used to broaden and strengthen the discipline of nature restoration through an interdisciplinary analysis. We carried out a mixed‐methods literature review on socio‐ecological restoration frameworks based on 8142 articles published 2010–2024. We first classified the occurrence of words in the abstract and title as social or ecological based on the Society for Ecological Restoration's (SER) Ecological Recovery and Social Benefits wheels for tracking restoration progress. For the in‐depth analysis, we shortlisted the most relevant articles based on their citation rank and relevance. We assessed how social and ecological concepts in the SER principles were interlinked and identified emerging dimensions. We found that the frequency of ecological and social words has increased equally. We identify that concepts integrating ecological and social dimensions have become more popular, including ecological words such as landscape restoration, ecosystem function, spatial planning and functional diversity, and social words such as nature‐based solutions, agroforestry, agroecology, carbon sink, cultural heritage and restoration governance. Other concepts have become less commonly mentioned in literature, such as endangered species, invasive species and novel ecosystems . The in‐depth analysis of the nature restoration framework literature identifies emerging dimensions that strengthen and broaden the SER's existing principles including landscape‐scale restoration, governance, climate change, restoration for social benefits and cost‐effectiveness. We find that although ecological dimensions remain important in restoration, interdisciplinary and social dimensions are increasing, thereby increasing awareness of nature restoration as a socio‐ecological process. We discuss ways of integrating these in future restoration guidelines. While social science perspectives in nature restoration research are growing, ecology remains the dominant paradigm and interdisciplinarity is largely aspirational rather than embedded in practice. Better integrating social and ecological dimensions will be essential to achieving effective, just and context‐sensitive restoration outcomes for both people and nature. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
summary: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infra
content: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

title: Towards an Updated National Hydrogen Strategy: Spatially and Temporally Resolved Hydrogen Demand Estimation in Japan
summary: Governments worldwide have adopted hydrogen strategies to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, yet Japan lacks a comprehensive assessment of domestic hydrogen demand. This study estimates hydrogen demand and associated carbon requirements in
content: Governments worldwide have adopted hydrogen strategies to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, yet Japan lacks a comprehensive assessment of domestic hydrogen demand. This study estimates hydrogen demand and associated carbon requirements in industry and transportation using a stoichiometric approach and analyses their spatial and temporal distributions. Estimated hydrogen demand reaches 42.4–47.0 Mt-H 2 yr −1 for industry and 12.2–24.8 Mt-H 2 yr −1 for transportation. The results reveal pronounced spatial mismatches between hydrogen production potential, demand, and carbon capture opportunities, highlighting challenges for infrastructure planning. Moreover, Japan's current national hydrogen strategy would satisfy only 42.6–47.2% of the estimated industrial hydrogen demand in 2050. These findings highlight the importance of revising Japan's national hydrogen strategy based on quantitative spatial and temporal demand assessments to support hydrogen infrastructure planning and improve energy security.

title: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane via charge-symmetry-breaking
summary: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane into C2+ chemicals represents a sustainable route towards carbon-neutral management, yet faces critical challenges including narrow solar spectrum utilization, inefficient charge carrier dynamics,
content: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane into C2+ chemicals represents a sustainable route towards carbon-neutral management, yet faces critical challenges including narrow solar spectrum utilization, inefficient charge carrier dynamics, and tricky C − C coupling. Herein, we achieve highly active and selective light-driven methane conversion to C2+ chemicals over multi-interfacial CuO/ZnO heterojunction. Mechanistic investigations reveal that charge redistribution at CuO/ZnO interface creates interfacial sites with unbalanced electronic states, which promote methane dissociation, alleviate coupling energy of methyl intermediates, and suppress electrostatic repulsion, thereby facilitating C − C coupling. Additionally, Z-Scheme charge transfer spatially decouples oxygen reduction on CuO and methane oxidation on ZnO, respectively. Consequently, CuO/ZnO delivers an ethane yield of 30.87 mmol g−1 h−1 with a C2+ selectivity up to 97.8%, an apparent quantum yield of 3.9% at 420 nm and a durability of 124 h. Here, we show that charge symmetry breaking provides a feasible strategy for converting methane to high-value C2+ chemicals. The successful construction of multiple CuO/ZnO interfaces with charge symmetry breaking achieves a high POCM performance with a C2H6 yield of 30.87 mmol g − 1 h − 1 and C2+ selectivity of 97.8% under ambient conditions in flowing reactor.

title: Revealing the generation characteristics of China’s household food waste by provinces by year
summary: Household food waste (HFW) lies at the intersection of food security, resource efficiency, and climate mitigation, yet robust regional-scale generation data remain scarce in rapidly urbanizing developing countries. We compiled 274 data poin
content: Household food waste (HFW) lies at the intersection of food security, resource efficiency, and climate mitigation, yet robust regional-scale generation data remain scarce in rapidly urbanizing developing countries. We compiled 274 data points covering 38 cities to quantify the proportion of HFW in total municipal solid waste (PHFW_MSW) and the HFW across 31 Chinese provinces during 2001–2024. A socioeconomic-driven backpropagation neural network model is constructed to project HFW trajectories up to 2050 under three scenarios, and facility operational data are adopted to assess economic and carbon reduction benefits of large-scale anaerobic digestion. Our analysis reveals substantial spatial heterogeneity in PHFW_MSW, ranging from 14 to 76% across provinces, with East China generating nearly half of national HFW. National HFW rose from 62.12 ± 8.34 to 139.11 ± 19.39 Mt yr -1 and its projects to peak at 150–160 Mt around 2030 before declining. Scenario analysis indicates that, under the optimistic scenario, cumulative carbon reductions can reach 738.05–828.05 Mt CO 2 -eq by 2050, and that anaerobic digestion can yield cumulative economic benefits of 177.30–219.86 billion USD by 2040. This study provides baseline data for differentiated regional HFW governance (e.g., the formulation of future regional coordinated waste reduction strategies), and the modelling framework is globally applicable.

title: Competing attention and linked emotions coexist in Reddit climate and pandemic discussions
summary: The temporal overlap between the COVID-19 pandemic and the climate crisis provides a real-world setting for examining how public attention and emotional expression shift when societies face multiple concurrent threats. Here we examine publi
content: The temporal overlap between the COVID-19 pandemic and the climate crisis provides a real-world setting for examining how public attention and emotional expression shift when societies face multiple concurrent threats. Here we examine public discourse during overlapping global crises using nearly 26 million Reddit comments posted in 2020-2021. Higher COVID-19 mortality was associated with a modest reduction in climate-focused comment volume, consistent with aggregate attention displacement. Dynamic models revealed selective short- and long-run emotional-language associations, concentrated mainly in negative sentiment and observed more often in the COVID-19-to-climate orientation. Comments mentioning both crises connected them through competing attention, shared root causes, expert knowledge, governance, inequality, and expectations of social change. These findings show that reduced visibility for climate discussion can coexist with selective cross-topic emotional coupling during overlapping societal crises. Climate discussions received less attention during peaks in pandemic mortality while emotional responses remained linked across topics, according to analyses of 26 million Reddit comments.

title: The intellectual structure and evolution of regenerative hospitality research: A bibliometric analysis
summary: Regenerative thinking has emerged as a transformative extension of sustainability within hospitality, shifting the field’s orientation from impact mitigation toward active socio-ecological renewal. Hospitality – defined by the immersive man
content: Regenerative thinking has emerged as a transformative extension of sustainability within hospitality, shifting the field’s orientation from impact mitigation toward active socio-ecological renewal. Hospitality – defined by the immersive management of place-based guest experiences, community relations and built environments – provides a uniquely appropriate and analytically distinct site for regenerative inquiry. Despite growing prominence, rapid expansion of the discourse has produced conceptual ambiguity and fragmented knowledge production. This study addresses these gaps through a systematic bibliometric analysis of 128 records (PRISMA-screened, 2016–2025), mapping the field’s intellectual structure via co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence networks and thematic mapping using R Studio’s Biblioshiny package. Findings reveal a significant publication surge since 2019, strong conceptual anchoring in place-based relational discourse and intellectual foundations centred on living systems theory and critical sustainability scholarship. Co-citation clusters identify a tripartite but fragmented theoretical structure spanning regenerative design, community-based development and post-growth economics. Geographic mapping exposes an asymmetric concentration of knowledge production in the Global North – a structural tension given the field’s deep roots in indigenous and Global South traditions. This study advances theoretical understanding of an emergent, conceptually under-consolidated field and provides an evidence-based agenda for future empirical inquiry.

title: Integrating Biotechnology and Artificial Intelligence for Circular Food Systems: A Critical Review of Evidence, Trade‐offs, and Research Priorities
summary: ABSTRACT Food systems remain largely linear, generating large amounts of food loss and waste and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while being increasingly exposed to climatic, geopolitical, and economic shocks. Biotechnology and artificial in
content: ABSTRACT Food systems remain largely linear, generating large amounts of food loss and waste and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while being increasingly exposed to climatic, geopolitical, and economic shocks. Biotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI) are supported circular food systems (CFS), but their combined benefits remain unclear. This narrative review, based on a structured search of five bibliographic databases, examines how biotechnological conversion routes (fermentation, enzyme‐assisted extraction, engineered microbial cell factories, crop biotechnology, and bio‐based packaging) and AI tools (machine learning, computer vision, soft sensors, and predictive models) interact across production, processing, packaging, and distribution. A four‐level integration framework is proposed, covering organism and enzyme design, bioprocess operation, feedstock and supply‐chain logistics, and product quality and traceability, and the maturity of the supporting evidence is assessed for each level. Most reported gains derive from laboratory‐ or pilot‐scale studies and from AI models validated on limited, single‐site datasets; techno‐economic and life‐cycle evidence for integrated bio‐digital systems is scarce, and trade‐offs in energy, water, cost and food safety are rarely quantified. Research priorities include open and representative datasets, externally validated and interpretable models, harmonized circularity indicators coupled with life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno‐economic analysis (TEA), and pilot‐scale demonstrations under realistic regulatory conditions.

title: Heterogeneity in carbon emission efficiency across global marine capture fisheries: a metafrontier analysis of technology gaps and reduction potentials
summary: Improving the carbon emission efficiency of marine capture fisheries is important for the sustainable development of fisheries under climate change. Using 66 major marine fishing countries over 1995–2017 as the sample, we divided the countr
content: Improving the carbon emission efficiency of marine capture fisheries is important for the sustainable development of fisheries under climate change. Using 66 major marine fishing countries over 1995–2017 as the sample, we divided the countries into three groups by fishing structure: high-input predatory fish-dominated, mixed, and small pelagic and other finfish-dominated. We measured carbon emission efficiency with a slacks-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs and a metafrontier approach, and decomposed the potential emission reduction into managerial inefficiency and the technology gap. The results show the following. (1) Carbon emission efficiency was generally low, with a mean metafrontier efficiency of 0.331, and the differences between groups were closely related to catch value. (2) The technology gap was concentrated in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group and the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, and its causes differed across countries: in Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia it was associated with fuel-intensive fishing operations, whereas in Peru and Chile it stemmed from the low value of the catch. (3) The mean annual potential carbon emission reduction of the sample countries was 85.4 Mt CO 2 -eq, about 53% of their total emissions, and was concentrated in countries such as Indonesia, India and Vietnam. (4) Managerial inefficiency was the main source of the reduction potential, accounting for 69%. In the mixed group, almost all of the potential came from managerial inefficiency; in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group, the technology gap dominated; and in the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, both sources contributed. Countries should therefore choose different pathways according to the source of their reduction potential. For most countries, catching up with the best practice of similar countries could release most of the potential with existing technology, especially in countries where the potential is concentrated, such as Indonesia and India. Countries whose technology gap is accompanied by high fuel intensity should focus on promoting energy-saving fishing gear and propulsion technology, while countries that mainly land low-value catch should increase the value of their catch.

title: Magnetoplasmons in N-layer structures
summary: Abstract We provide a systematic framework to investigate magnetoplasmons in multilayer two-dimensional electron systems using the the Kac-Murdock-Szegő (KMS) Toeplitz matrix to describe interlayer Coulomb interactions. In the absence of in
content: Abstract We provide a systematic framework to investigate magnetoplasmons in multilayer two-dimensional electron systems using the the Kac-Murdock-Szegő (KMS) Toeplitz matrix to describe interlayer Coulomb interactions. In the absence of interlayer tunneling, we show that the single-layer magnetoplasmon branch splits into N collective modes-one in-phase mode and N-1 out-of-phase modes-and derive their asymptotic behaviors in the long-wavelength limit, as well as in the large layer separation and weak magnetic-field limit. When interlayer tunneling is present, we clarify the magnetoplasmon dispersion, both qualitatively and quantitatively, by identifying the magnetoplasmon mode associated with each interband transition, including tunneling magnetoplasmons arising from interband transitions with the same Landau level index. Our study reveals the symmetry-governed hybridization between the identified modes, along with an enhanced tunneling magnetoplasmon gap exceeding the associated interband gap. The KMS-based analytic formalism thus provides a comprehensive physical understanding of magnetoplasmons in multilayer structures.

title: An early-stage, multi-lifecycle assessment framework for sustainable material selection in automotive industry
summary: The transition toward low-carbon mobility requires material-selection approaches that account for extended use cycles and cross-sector reuse pathways. However, early-stage automotive design decisions are typically informed by single-life cr
content: The transition toward low-carbon mobility requires material-selection approaches that account for extended use cycles and cross-sector reuse pathways. However, early-stage automotive design decisions are typically informed by single-life cradle-to-grave assessments, which do not explicitly integrate reuse-induced substitution effects or multi-stage emission accounting within development timelines. This study operationalizes an integrated cradle-to-reuse-to-grave (C2R2G) assessment approach by combining established life cycle assessment (LCA), system expansion, and substitution modeling principles into an automotive-specific decision-support structure. The framework formalizes emission accounting across primary use, reuse preparation, secondary application, and end-of-life treatment, including explicit system expansion, substitution, and circular scenario modeling parameters. A bio-based laminated veneer lumber (LVL) seat-shell is evaluated as a demonstrative case within passenger vehicle applications. Scenario modeling compares single-life, recycling, and open-loop reuse pathways under varying lifetime and energy-intensity assumptions. Results indicate that reuse-driven substitution effects can significantly alter cumulative carbon footprints compared to single-life configurations, though outcomes remain highly sensitive to assumed service lifetimes, displaced material emission factors, and energy mixes in second-life sectors. Sensitivity analysis highlights key parameters influencing ranking stability and identifies boundary conditions under which reuse advantages diminish. Rather than proposing a new LCA methodology, this work demonstrates how established analytical components can be systematically integrated to support early-stage automotive material pathway evaluation. The approach enhances transparency in allocation choices and trade-off identification, contributing to more informed low-carbon design decisions in circular mobility systems. Graphical Abstract

title: Using cellulose nanofibers as the sole binder for cement-free construction materials
summary: Abstract Cellulose nanofibers (CNF), fibrils extracted from wood, bind through hydrogen bonding and have served as the sole binder in wood-based panels, but to the authors’ knowledge they have not been used as the sole binder for un-sintere
content: Abstract Cellulose nanofibers (CNF), fibrils extracted from wood, bind through hydrogen bonding and have served as the sole binder in wood-based panels, but to the authors’ knowledge they have not been used as the sole binder for un-sintered mineral sand without any hydraulic cement. Here we report an exploratory, proof-of-concept study in which an aqueous CNF gel (3.00–5.87 wt% solids) was the only binder for sand. Twelve compositions combined four gel solids contents with three gel-to-sand mass ratios (25:75, 40:60, 50:50), corresponding to 1.0–5.5 wt% dry cellulose in the dried composite. Cohesive solids formed at about 1 wt% dry cellulose and above, with dry compressive strengths of 0.42–3.73 MPa, comparable to rammed earth and adobe. Strength increased with both the gel fraction and the gel solids content, which interacted, so dry cellulose content alone does not describe the behaviour. Water saturation reduced strength to about 6% of the dry value; re-drying restored it (110 ± 22%), which is consistent with, but does not prove, a reversible physical binding mechanism. The results provide a preliminary composition-property map of cement-free CNF-sand composites and identify moisture sensitivity and the energy cost of drying as the main barriers to practical application.

title: Effect of additives on physical characteristics, combustion behavior, and pollutant emission of co-pellets produced from torrefied-biomass and semi-dried sewage sludge
source: International Journal of Coal Science & Technology
summary: Abstract Co-pelletizing torrefied Camellia oleifera shell (TCOS) with semi-dried sewage sludge (SS) can improve pellet quality but may create new challenges in pollutant emissions and ash slagging. To address these challenges, single and bl
content: Abstract Co-pelletizing torrefied Camellia oleifera shell (TCOS) with semi-dried sewage sludge (SS) can improve pellet quality but may create new challenges in pollutant emissions and ash slagging. To address these challenges, single and blended CaO/kaolin additives were evaluated for their effects on the physical properties, combustion behavior, emissions, and ash fusion characteristics of the co-pellets. Additives increased compaction energy by 4.09% – 17.43% but had little effect on extrusion energy or pellet density. The single addition of kaolin reduced cumulative SO 2 from 1.17 to 0.97 mg and PM0.1 by 29.72%, while raising ash fusion temperatures (AFT) and lowering the slagging index. The single addition of CaO advanced the NO 2 emission peak, but reduced AFT by up to 118℃, increasing the slagging tendency. For blended additions, TCS-Ca3K1 gave the lowest cumulative NO 2 (3.31 mg), while TCS-Ca1K3 achieved the greatest PM 0.1 reduction (28.75%). XRD confirmed CaSO4 in CaO-added pellets and KAlSiO 4 in kaolin-containing pellets. These results indicate that CaO and kaolin target different pollutants and ash risks, and their ratio can be tailored to balance emission control and slagging mitigation.

title: The Impact of Public Data Openness on Urban Green Total Factor Productivity: A Quasi-Natural Experiment Based on the Establishment of Government Data Open Platforms
source: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
summary: The study treats the establishment of government data open platforms as a quasi-natural experiment and constructs a theoretical analysis framework of "public data openness—technological innovation, industrial structure upgrading and public
content: The study treats the establishment of government data open platforms as a quasi-natural experiment and constructs a theoretical analysis framework of "public data openness—technological innovation, industrial structure upgrading and public supervision—green total factor productivity". Based on 2011-2022 panel data of 282 prefecture-level and above cities in China, the study adopts the entropy method, the SBM-GML model, a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model and a mediating effect model to measure urban green total factor productivity (GTFP), identify the causal effect of public data openness, and test its transmission mechanisms. The results show that the establishment of a government data open platform significantly raises urban GTFP by 0.038, equivalent to about 3.2% of the sample mean, and the conclusion remains robust to the parallel trend test, placebo test, PSM-DID, alternative variable measurement, exclusion of concurrent policies and heterogeneity-robust estimators. Mechanism analysis indicates that green technology innovation, industrial structure upgrading and public environmental attention are three significant channels. The effect is stronger in eastern and large cities than in central-western and small and medium-sized cities. This study provides empirical support and policy reference for releasing the value of public data and promoting the high-quality green transformation of China's cities, also offer reference for other developing emerging economies.

title: Optimizing Container Drayage with Electric Tractors under a Separation Mode
source: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
summary: The global strategic imperatives of carbon dioxide emission reduction and carbon neutrality, together with the promotion of high-quality sustainable development, have led to a progressive decline in the reliance on fossil fuels across both
content: The global strategic imperatives of carbon dioxide emission reduction and carbon neutrality, together with the promotion of high-quality sustainable development, have led to a progressive decline in the reliance on fossil fuels across both commercial and passenger vehicle fleets. In response, a growing number of freight carriers are transitioning toward electric trucks as their primary delivery fleet. This study addresses the local container drayage problem with electric vehicles and conventional diesel vehicles, aiming to find out the gap between these two different types of vehicles within and outside the tractor-container separation mode. In this context, an electric tractor can be separated from the container during the process of (un)loading at customer nodes for the other tasks or recharging. This study also focuses on the different energy consumption rates of electric trucks under empty load, laden load, or separation mode to simulate a more realistic transportation scenario. Accordingly, a route planning and charging decision model for electric tractors is formulated with the objective of minimizing the total operation cost, including the fixed cost, energy cost, and labor cost. To efficiently solve this mathematical model, an adapted Clarke and Wright heuristic algorithm suitable for this problem is designed. We introduce the feasibility check functions for battery state and (un)loading time constraints into the adapted heuristic algorithm. Finally, a series of numerical experiments is conducted in real-world highway networks and transportation scenarios to assess the performance of the algorithm compared with Gurobi and to analyze the practicability of electric tractors for the separation mode under the influence of various objective terms.

title: Gallium–Nickel Subnano Clusters for Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
summary: Abstract The hydrogenation of CO2 into valuable products offers a promising approach for carbon neutral technologies, with gallium–nickel alloys emerging as effective catalysts. Structuring the catalyst on the nano or subnano scale can be u
content: Abstract The hydrogenation of CO2 into valuable products offers a promising approach for carbon neutral technologies, with gallium–nickel alloys emerging as effective catalysts. Structuring the catalyst on the nano or subnano scale can be used effectively for tuning the catalytic activity and selectivity. In this study, we investigated the geometry, stability, electronic structure, and reactivity of small gallium–nickel subnano clusters for electrochemical carbon dioxide hydrogenation. The stabilities were investigated by the generalization of the second differential energy to bimetallic clusters, that combined with cluster composition appears as a promising descriptor for reactivity with carbon monoxide. The electronic structures were extensively characterized using electronic structure analysis, including molecular orbitals, density of states, d-band center theory, as well as by Energy Decomposition Analysis. We systematically explored cluster reactivity with carbon monoxide, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide, identifying key trends and their potential impact on catalytic activity. Finally, we investigated the possible reaction pathways on Ni4, Ga2Ni3, and Ga4Ni2 clusters toward C1 products using Computational Hydrogen Electrode model-based computations. The results indicate that Ga2Ni3 exhibits enhanced product desorption and reduced catalyst poisoning, making it a promising candidate for further investigation. Our observations provide valuable insights into the catalytic activity of Ga–Ni alloy clusters, demonstrating that subnano structuring represents a promising approach for catalytic tuning.

title: Greenwashing in green bonds: a systematic literature review
summary: Purpose This study aims to explain how greenwashing emerges, persists and affects credibility in green bond markets. Rather than treating greenwashing as isolated misleading communication, it examines the interaction between financial incen
content: Purpose This study aims to explain how greenwashing emerges, persists and affects credibility in green bond markets. Rather than treating greenwashing as isolated misleading communication, it examines the interaction between financial incentives, governance structures, information asymmetries, institutional arrangements and market consequences. The study also identifies the main manifestations, drivers, consequences and mitigation mechanisms associated with greenwashing in sustainable debt instruments. Design/methodology/approach The study conducts a systematic literature review following the PRISMA protocol. Scopus and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies addressing greenwashing in sustainable debt markets, resulting in a final sample of 46 articles. The selected studies were analyzed through inductive thematic synthesis, involving iterative data reduction, thematic organization, relational interpretation and refinement of conclusions. Categories were developed from recurring patterns concerning governance dynamics, operational mechanisms, manifestations, consequences and mitigation strategies. Findings The findings show that greenwashing in green bond markets is driven by reputational incentives, lower financing costs, weak regulatory oversight, investor attraction and the relabeling of preexisting projects. It manifests through selective disclosure, weak additionality, symbolic certification, regulatory arbitrage, limited transparency and redirection of proceeds. These practices can erode investor trust, damage issuer reputation, widen credit spreads, increase financing costs and restrict market scalability. Institutional moderators may either mitigate or reproduce these dynamics depending on their effectiveness. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by the geographical concentration of the literature, particularly its strong focus on the Chinese green bond market, and by its reliance on published academic research, which may underrepresent enforcement actions and emerging regulatory developments. Future studies should conduct comparative cross-country analyses and empirically test the proposed framework through case studies, interviews, process tracing and document analysis, particularly in emerging markets and the Global South. Practical implications The findings suggest that issuers should incorporate environmental integrity before issuance through clear eligibility criteria, measurable targets, additionality and traceability of proceeds. Investors, auditors and external reviewers should assess discrepancies between ex ante commitments and post-issuance outcomes. Policymakers should strengthen harmonized taxonomies, standardized reporting, post-issuance verification, reviewer independence and enforcement mechanisms. However, regulatory requirements should remain proportionate to avoid restricting access to climate finance for smaller issuers and emerging markets. Social implications Greenwashing in green b

title: Strategic Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nakuru County, Kenya
source: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
summary: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms
content: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms, which operate in an increasingly uncertain environment characterised by economic instability, supply chain disruptions, climate variability and rising production costs. In Nakuru County, Kenya, many manufacturing firms still respond to such disruptions reactively, and evidence on how agility practices relate to their ability to sustain performance remains limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of strategic agility on sustainable performance of manufacturing firms in Nakuru County, Kenya. It explored four practices, namely environmental scanning, scenario planning, strategic flexibility and early warning systems. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Complexity Theory, the Resource-Based View and Organizational Learning Theory. The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design and targeted the 34 manufacturing firms in the county. A census of the firms was undertaken and four managers, comprising senior, operations and strategy managers, were purposively selected from each firm, giving 136 respondents, of whom 96 returned completed questionnaires. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 43.9% of the variation in sustainable performance. Environmental scanning was the strongest predictor of sustainable performance, followed by scenario planning and early warning systems, while strategic flexibility had a significant but comparatively weaker influence. The study, therefore, recommends that manufacturing firms institutionalise environmental scanning, regularly develop and review alternative scenarios, strengthen decision-making and resource reallocation mechanisms, and integrate predictive risk monitoring, clear reporting channels and predefined response thresholds into their early warning systems.

title: Transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy: Evidence from Japan
summary: Japan has pledged carbon neutrality by 2050, yet energy production still accounts for 84% of its greenhouse-gas emissions, and only 33.4% (328.48 TWh) of its 2023 electricity generation came from nuclear and renewable sources. This paper as
content: Japan has pledged carbon neutrality by 2050, yet energy production still accounts for 84% of its greenhouse-gas emissions, and only 33.4% (328.48 TWh) of its 2023 electricity generation came from nuclear and renewable sources. This paper asks how Japan's electricity generation can complete the transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy. Using annual data for 1980-2023 from the World Bank, IMF, and the Statistics Bureau of Japan, we estimate an autoregressive log-growth model of electricity consumption driven by GDP per capita, median age, and population change, and project Japan's 2050 electricity consumption at approximately 1,000 TWh (999 TWh; range 900-1,000 TWh across specifications, sample horizons, and population paths). Closing the resulting clean-energy gap of roughly 469 TWh would require the equivalent of about 56 additional nuclear reactors of average current capability (8.41 TWh each), rising to about 67 at the capacity factors Japan has realized since Fukushima. Applying machine-learning facility-location methods (genetic and NSGA-II algorithms) to a benchmark 21-plant configuration, we show that siting new plants on Japan's least-populated coastlines reduces the population inside their emergency planning zones by roughly two orders of magnitude relative to naive placement, at an additional transmission cost of a few hundred million US dollars per year. Public acceptance, rather than engineering capacity, is the binding constraint on Japan's nuclear future, and siting policy that takes safety over efficiency directly addresses it. Hydrogen-based generation, whose commercial viability at scale by 2050 remains unconfirmed, lies outside the scope of the quantitative analysis.

title: Li–B–Mg Composite Foils With a LiB 0.88 Microrod Array Enable Ultrathin Self‐Supporting Lithium Metal Anodes
summary: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting lithium foils (USSLFs, ≤50 µm) are highly desirable for high‐energy‐density batteries, as eliminating current collectors enhances energy density and reduces material costs. However, the intrinsic mechanica
content: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting lithium foils (USSLFs, ≤50 µm) are highly desirable for high‐energy‐density batteries, as eliminating current collectors enhances energy density and reduces material costs. However, the intrinsic mechanical vulnerability of metallic Li remains a critical barrier to both the fabrication and long‐term cycling of USSLFs. Herein, we develop a Li‐rich Li–B–Mg composite foil (LBM) through sequential melt alloying followed by post‐solidification thermomechanical processing, yielding a dense and interconnected LiB 0.88 microrod array with LiMg and MgB 2 lithiophilic phases within the Li‐rich matrix. This architecture enables large‐area (>170 cm 2 ) self‐supporting foils down to 15 µm while preserving a high Li content. During cycling, the microrod array redistributes local stress and restrains deformation, preserving the internal architecture and accessibility of lithiophilic sites. These sites, in turn, favor Li accommodation within the electrode interior, suppressing surface Li accumulation and alleviating local stress concentration. This self‐sustained coupling between stress regulation and lithiophilic guidance supports stable cycling for over 5000 h in symmetric cells using 50 µm LBM foils with about 10% thickness expansion, while 15 µm foils cycle for over 500 h at a depth of discharge of about 37.4%. This work advances the design of practical USSLFs for high‐energy lithium metal batteries.

title: A comprehensive benchmark and dual-encoder baseline for terraced field extraction in complex mountainous regions
summary: Terraces play a vital role in mitigating runoff and intercepting sediment. Large-scale, high-precision extraction of terraces from remote sensing imagery is essential for environmental monitoring and soil erosion control. However, accurate
content: Terraces play a vital role in mitigating runoff and intercepting sediment. Large-scale, high-precision extraction of terraces from remote sensing imagery is essential for environmental monitoring and soil erosion control. However, accurate spatial identification of terraces still presents significant challenges, including scale variability, shadow interference, and complex geometric configurations. To address these issues, we propose DETS-Net, a dual-encoder network that integrates CNN and Transformer architectures. The network employs ResNet-34 as the CNN encoder for local feature detail extraction, utilizes a Transformer encoder to strengthen long-range dependency modeling, and incorporates an adaptive feature fusion (AFF) module for the dynamic integration of the two feature branches. We develop the THDIR dataset, which covers four typical terrain types, namely, plateau mountains, hills, and mountain-basin transition zones, and contains 9,336 standardized 256 × 256 pixel images. We conduct systematic comparisons with eight representative deep learning models. Experimental results demonstrate that DETS-Net achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 89.91%, a mean intersection over union (MIoU) of 81.28%, and an F1-score of 87.99% on the THDIR dataset, outperforming current mainstream methods in segmentation precision. We apply the optimized model to 2023 remote sensing imagery of Luotian County in the Dabie Mountains, Hubei Province, and generate a high-precision county-level terrace spatial distribution map. This framework supports the assessment of soil and water conservation benefits through area statistics, slope distribution data, and high-precision boundary extraction and provides a reproducible technical pathway for automated terrace mapping using high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex mountainous regions.

title: From Instability to Design Principle: Rethinking Ir‐Free Catalysts for Acidic OER
summary: ABSTRACT The instability of non‐noble catalysts in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is not merely a materials limitation, but a fundamental consequence of thermodynamic constraints under highly oxidative conditions. Here, we prese
content: ABSTRACT The instability of non‐noble catalysts in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is not merely a materials limitation, but a fundamental consequence of thermodynamic constraints under highly oxidative conditions. Here, we present a unified perspective that reinterprets this instability as a thermodynamically driven and kinetically modulated process, rather than an intrinsic material deficiency. This review covers the fundamental origins of catalyst degradation in acidic OER, including the lack of thermodynamically stable phases and the activity‐stability trade‐off. We further discuss emerging strategies such as compositional engineering, entropy stabilization, and functional decoupling, which can expand stability windows and alleviate bulk instability while maintaining surface reactivity. Finally, we highlight insights from operando studies that uncover dynamic reconstruction, dissolution, and redeposition processes under operating conditions. By integrating thermodynamic design, kinetic control, and multiscale structural engineering, this perspective outlines emerging strategies to transform instability into a controllable feature, offering new directions for designing durable, earth‐abundant OER catalysts.

title: HEATING CHARACTERISTICS OF A SOLAR-CO₂ AIR SOURCE HEAT PUMP COUPLED SYSTEM WITH VALLEY-ELECTRICITY HEAT STORAGE
summary: Taking the heating system of a rural household in Yinchuan as the research object, a simulation model of a solar-CO₂ air source heat pump heating system was developed based on TRNSYS, and its operation from November to March of the followin
content: Taking the heating system of a rural household in Yinchuan as the research object, a simulation model of a solar-CO₂ air source heat pump heating system was developed based on TRNSYS, and its operation from November to March of the following year was simulated and analyzed. The results show that the system can reliably satisfy the indoor winter heating demand of rural households, with heating temperature fluctuating little and remaining stable at approximately 18.0 ℃. Regarding the electricity consumption of the coupled system, the energy use of the space-heating pump and the heating circulation pump rises in step with the extreme-cold heat load in winter, showing a pronounced negative correlation with outdoor temperature; in contrast, the energy consumption of the solar collector pump is governed solely by solar irradiation and remains stable throughout the entire heating season. Over the whole heating season, the collector harvested 6,276.26 kWh of heat and the air source heat pump delivered 6,359.19 kWh, the two contributions being nearly equal, with the total heat output of the heat pump slightly exceeding that of the solar collector. The carbon emissions of the solar-coupled heat pump heating system are only 1,433.94 kgCO₂, equivalent to 24.5% of those of a coal-fired boiler (the highest-emitting option), demonstrating remarkable energy-saving and emission-reduction effects. This study aims to refine the theoretical framework of solar-CO₂ heat pump coupled heating and to provide data support for the engineering design and operation-and-maintenance optimization of clean heating projects for residential and public buildings in cold regions.

title: SAE-MOGWO-PRS: A probability ranking strategy-based grey wolf optimizer for spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization
summary: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogene
content: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer. To validate the efficacy of the proposed SAE-MOGWO-PRS algorithm, we compared it against four state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization algorithms, including those that specifically handle heterogeneous evaluation times. The comparative analysis on four test problems demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed probabilistic ranking strategy-based algorithm, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the SAE-MOGWO-PRS method.

title: Dynamic Interfacial S–O Bonding Stabilizes Oxygen Redox Through Reversible Electron Confinement
summary: ABSTRACT The reversible activation of lattice oxygen represents a transformative opportunity for high‐energy battery electrodes but remains fundamentally limited by the instability of oxidized oxygen states. In layered oxide cathodes, oxyge
content: ABSTRACT The reversible activation of lattice oxygen represents a transformative opportunity for high‐energy battery electrodes but remains fundamentally limited by the instability of oxidized oxygen states. In layered oxide cathodes, oxygen oxidation generates oxygen‐centered hole states that become electronically unstable at particle surfaces, triggering oxygen loss, interfacial reconstruction, and irreversible electrochemical degradation. Here, we develop an interfacial electronic regulation strategy that stabilizes oxygen redox through reversible sulfur–oxygen (S–O) bonding. During charging, dynamic S–O bond formation at the cathode surface confines oxygen hole states and suppresses their delocalization and irreversible evolutions, whereas bond dissociation upon discharge restores the lattice oxygen electronic configuration and enables reversible oxygen redox. Applied to the Na 0.72 Li 0.24 Mn 0.76 O 2 layered oxide cathode, this strategy enables stable oxygen redox activity, mitigates voltage decay, and improves long‐term cycling stability. These findings establish reversible interfacial electron confinement as a general design principle for regulating unstable oxygen electronic states and advancing durable high‐energy‐storage materials.

title: An edge-conditioned convolution model for carbon flow rate prediction under source-load uncertainty
summary: Introduction The realization of China’s dual-carbon goals relies on accurate and fine-grained carbon emission modeling of the new-type power systems. Conventional carbon calculation methods are designed for traditional power systems and rel
content: Introduction The realization of China’s dual-carbon goals relies on accurate and fine-grained carbon emission modeling of the new-type power systems. Conventional carbon calculation methods are designed for traditional power systems and rely on deterministic power flow calculations. This makes it difficult to capture the impacts of source–load uncertainty on the carbon flow rate under high renewable penetration. Methods This paper proposes a carbon flow rate prediction model based on Edge Conditioned Convolution (ECC) to account for source–load uncertainty. First, a carbon flow rate calculation framework is established by incorporating the full lifecycle carbon emissions of renewable generators and a network loss allocation mechanism. This mechanism combines upstream and downstream power flow tracing to allocate network losses between the generation and consumption sides using an allocation coefficient. Second, an ECC-based carbon flow rate prediction model is developed to incorporate branch attributes into information aggregation through edge-conditioned convolution weights. A physics-informed loss function is adopted to encourage the conservation of the carbon flow rate. Furthermore, by using Sobol sequences and Inverse Transform Sampling (ITS) algorithms to generate multi-scenario data sets, the application scenarios of the prediction model are extended to power systems with high renewable-energy penetration. This also enhances the model’s generalization ability under uncertainty. Results Case studies show that the proposed model achieves a mean absolute error of approximately 0.144 tCO 2 /h, confirming practical prediction accuracy. Further analysis reveals that under different renewable penetration levels, the method more accurately characterizes carbon flow rate distributions and adapts better to source–load uncertainty than conventional carbon flow tracing methods. Discussion These results support the use of ECC to predict carbon flow rates under source–load uncertainty and the specified network-loss allocation scheme, providing a potential basis for low-carbon power system dispatch.

title: How and when do green HRM practices foster organizational citizenship behavior for the environment? A multilevel approach
summary: Purpose Organizational citizenship behavior for the environment (OCBE) is essential for sustainable development. This study aims to examine how and when green human resource management (GHRM) practices contribute to OCBE. Design/methodology
content: Purpose Organizational citizenship behavior for the environment (OCBE) is essential for sustainable development. This study aims to examine how and when green human resource management (GHRM) practices contribute to OCBE. Design/methodology/approach Two waves of multisource data were collected from 737 employees and 84 HR directors in the Chinese hospitality industry. Data were analyzed using robust maximum likelihood estimators in Mplus 7.4. Findings The results show that green organizational climate (GOC) and employee environmental commitment (EEC) serially mediate the GHRM practices–OCBE relationship. Moreover, line managers’ environmental support (LMES) moderates the GHRM practices–GOC relationship. Practical implications The current study suggests that organizations can improve OCBE by implementing GHRM practices and recognizing LMES’s significant role. Social implications Specifically, the authors’ findings offer actionable insights for Global South organizations to support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 12 and SDG 13) by fostering voluntary pro-environmental behaviors. Originality/value This study explains how and when GHRM practices contribute to OCBE.

title: Stellarator Plasma Start-up Model Based on Energy Confinement Time Scaling Laws, Experimental Verification and Numerical Simulation Results
summary: Abstract Based on the energy confinement time scaling law of stellarator in the low-confinement mode, combined with energy balance equation and the plasma propagation and power deposition equations of the electron cyclotron wave in the thre
content: Abstract Based on the energy confinement time scaling law of stellarator in the low-confinement mode, combined with energy balance equation and the plasma propagation and power deposition equations of the electron cyclotron wave in the three-dimensional magnetic field, a stellarator plasma start-up model including electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and impurity radiation power loss is established. Validation against W7-X experimental data demonstrates good agreement in the temporal evolution of electron temperature and radiation losses, which verified that the model can correctly give the plasma start-up results of the stellarator under ECRH. This model is applied to predict the results of plasma start-up under 28 GHz ECRH for China Helical Device 1 (CN-H1) stellarator. The effects of the initial electron-to-ion temperature ratio (Te/Ti), ECRH injection power (Pinj), deposition position and effective charge number Z_{\text{eff}} on start-up are systematically studied and analyzed. The results show that the initial Te/Ti ratio affects only the ramp-up rate, while the final steady-state electron and ion temperature remain unaffected. Higher Pinj accelerates electron temperature rise and increases flat-top electron temperature, whereas the ion temperature exhibits the opposite trend, decreasing with increasing Pinj. The deposition location has a decisive impact on the start-up outcome: only core deposition on the low-field side leads to a successful start-up, while high-field side and off-axis low-field side depositions fail owing to refractive deviation of the ray trajectory and insufficient absorption, respectively. The steady-state electron and ion temperatures are insensitive to {\mathrm{Z}}_{\text{eff}} within a reasonable range.

title: Enhancing regional ecological resilience through blue and green spaces in China
summary: Blue-green spaces (BGSs) are key material carriers for regional ecological resilience under accelerating climate change. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions over 2012-2024, this study constructs a three-dimensional ecol
content: Blue-green spaces (BGSs) are key material carriers for regional ecological resilience under accelerating climate change. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions over 2012-2024, this study constructs a three-dimensional ecological resilience index (resistance, adaptability and recoverability) and applies spatiotemporal econometric models to examine how BGSs affect ecological resilience, through which mechanisms, and with what spatial features. (1) BGSs significantly enhance ecological resilience. With the three BGS indicators standardized to z-scores, one-standard-deviation increases in per capita BGS area, blue-space share and green-space share raise the composite resilience score (0-1 scale) by 0.0625, 0.0096 and 0.0304 index points, equivalent to 0.86, 0.13 and 0.42 standard deviations of resilience (SD = 0.0724). The effect varies across geographic, institutional, resource-based and economic dimensions and follows a nonlinear, threshold-dependent pattern. (2) BGSs work through three parallel channels: carbon sinks, green technological innovation and external openness. For blue space, the indirect effect (+0.0178) is significantly positive while the direct effect (-0.0083) is significantly negative, a suppression configuration in which the indirect-to-total ratio (186.3%) is not a conventional mediation share; green space shows partial mediation (26.0%). (3) Under the inverse-distance matrix, spillover effects exceed local effects, with indirect-to-direct ratios of 9.59, 4.15 and 1.32 for blue space, green space and per capita BGS area; this ranking is matrix-dependent (the per capita BGS ratio falls to 0.54 under the K-nearest-neighbor matrix), and spillovers vary nonmonotonically with distance. The findings inform differentiated ecological governance and coordinated cross-regional protection.

title: Multi-Scenario Decarbonization Pathway Analysis for Energy-Intensive Industries Based on an Integrated LEAP Framework: Evidence from Shandong Province, China
summary: Against the backdrop of global carbon neutrality, energy-intensive industries represent the core source of carbon emissions in the industrial sector. Scientifically quantifying decarbonization pathways and evaluating the emission reduction
content: Against the backdrop of global carbon neutrality, energy-intensive industries represent the core source of carbon emissions in the industrial sector. Scientifically quantifying decarbonization pathways and evaluating the emission reduction effects of different policies are of great significance for delivering regional carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. This study proposes an integrated assessment framework based on the LEAP model, which integrates baseline accounting, scenario simulation, and emission reduction driver decomposition, incorporating both energy consumption-related and industrial process emissions. Combined with multi-source data integration to improve the reliability of emission accounting inputs, we conduct an empirical study on three typical energy-intensive sectors, namely iron and steel, cement, and chemicals, in Shandong Province, a major industrial province in China. Taking 2023 as the base year, three policy scenarios are set: the Business-as-Usual (BAU) scenario, the Low-Carbon Policy Scenario (CPS), and the Net-Zero Scenario (NZS), to quantitatively evaluate the evolution trajectory of carbon emissions, sector-specific decarbonization pathways, and emission reduction contributions from 2024 to 2060. The results show that total emissions of the three sectors increased from 325.93 million tonnes in 2022 to 344.17 million tonnes in the 2023 projection base year (+5.6%), with the chemical industry remaining the largest emission source. Under the BAU scenario, emissions rise to a broad high-level plateau of approximately 371 million tonnes around 2040–2050 and decline only slightly thereafter; although a shallow peak is formed, the post-peak reduction is insufficient to support deep decarbonization. Under the CPS and NZS scenarios, emission reductions of 74.1% and 97.1% can be achieved by 2060, respectively. Energy efficiency improvement is the core short-term driving force for emission reduction, while power decarbonization and CCUS technologies are key supports for deep decarbonization in the medium and long term. This study can provide methodological reference and empirical evidence for decarbonization pathway design and policy formulation of energy-intensive industries in similar regions.

title: Agroforestry enhances soil quality and carbon storage with carbon-credit potential across contrasting land-use systems in the Western Ghats
summary: Abstract Agroforestry systems can improve soil quality and carbon storage while generating additional economic value through carbon financing. This study evaluated forest, coffee agroforestry (Coffee AF), rubber agroforestry (Rubber AF), ma
content: Abstract Agroforestry systems can improve soil quality and carbon storage while generating additional economic value through carbon financing. This study evaluated forest, coffee agroforestry (Coffee AF), rubber agroforestry (Rubber AF), mango agroforestry (Mango AF), and sole-cropping systems for soil quality, soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, biomass carbon accumulation, and indicative carbon-finance potential in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India. SOC was assessed throughout the soil profile to capture both surface and subsurface carbon pools. Soil quality index (SQI) was higher under Coffee AF (0.655), Rubber AF (0.617), and Mango AF (0.550) than sole cropping (0.499) at 0–30 cm. Surface SOC stocks ranged from 16.6 to 88.3 Mg C ha⁻¹, with Coffee AF showing greater surface SOC storage, whereas Rubber AF recorded the highest deep-soil carbon storage. Relative to sole cropping, annual soil-C accumulation potential was 8.1, 3.8 and 0.76 t CO₂e ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ at 0–30 cm and 4.41, 5.17 and 4.12 t CO₂e ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ at 30–100 cm for Coffee AF, Rubber AF and Mango AF, respectively. Biomass carbon reached 68.9, 28.8 and 22.5 t C ha⁻¹ in Rubber AF, Coffee AF and Mango AF, with annual woody biomass removal potentials of 11.8, 4.6 and 3.7 t CO₂e ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹, respectively. Indicative gross carbon-finance value was highest for Rubber AF (USD 415.5 ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), followed by Coffee AF (USD 338.3) and Mango AF (USD 167.3). Overall, agroforestry provides combined soil, carbon-storage and economic benefits, with Rubber AF particularly promising for deep-soil carbon storage and carbon-finance potential.

title: Scenario-dependent projections of brown planthopper immigration intensity under CMIP6 climate pathways
summary: Abstract Climate change reshapes the dynamics of agricultural pests by altering temperature, wind, vertical airflows, precipitation and humidity. Brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens (Stål), is among the most destructive migratory pests in
content: Abstract Climate change reshapes the dynamics of agricultural pests by altering temperature, wind, vertical airflows, precipitation and humidity. Brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens (Stål), is among the most destructive migratory pests in Asian rice, and its dynamics are tightly coupled to climate. Clarifying how the different emission pathways affect this pest is essential for forward-looking management. We combined 2001–2023 light-trap records from 11 Chinese stations with the Norwegian Earth System Model version 2 low-resolution configuration (NorESM2-LM) from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Lower-tropospheric temperature showed the strongest marginal associations at most representative stations. Random forest (RF), k-nearest neighbors (KNN) and linear regression (LR) were compared using temporally ordered development and independent 2019–2023 validation. Source qualification retained 8,428 station-pentads. Development annual-log RMSE averaged 0.744 for LR, 0.758 for KNN and 0.807 for RF; RF300 remained the projection reference. Across 42 independent station-years, exact-grade accuracy was 92.9%, matching an always-Grade-1 baseline. Mann–Kendall tests with false-discovery-rate control identified nine significant station–scenario trends, six retained after trend-free pre-whitening; none was significant under SSP1-2.6. Projections from all 11 stations showed marked spatial heterogeneity rather than uniform northward expansion. These conditional projections support climate-adaptive monitoring.

title: Multi-field coupling response and storage efficiency of CO₂ sequestration in deep chambers considering capillary trapping and surrounding rock damage
summary: Abstract In the face of global climate change, geological sequestration of carbon dioxide (CO₂) using underground space is a key pathway to achieving carbon emission reduction. In such engineering practices, storage efficiency and long-term
content: Abstract In the face of global climate change, geological sequestration of carbon dioxide (CO₂) using underground space is a key pathway to achieving carbon emission reduction. In such engineering practices, storage efficiency and long-term safety directly constrain the technical feasibility of the project and its full life-cycle evolution. To investigate the safety, feasibility, and storage efficiency of CO₂ sequestration in deep chambers, this study combines physical experiments with numerical simulations to construct a thermal–hydraulic–mechanical (THM) three-field coupling model for CO₂ sequestration in abandoned mines, incorporating the dual effects of capillary pressure and surrounding rock damage. The storage safety and efficiency of CO₂ sequestration in deep chambers are then investigated. The results indicate that: (1) Under multi-field coupling, surrounding rock damage preferentially develops and propagates along the direction of higher initial in-situ stress, causing high-pressure CO₂ to preferentially form a dominant seepage pathway along this direction. (2) The seepage process of CO₂ is accompanied by significant heat exchange, leading to a marked temperature decrease in the surrounding rock of the chamber. This physical characteristic can serve as an important early warning indicator for monitoring concealed CO₂ leakage in practical engineering. (3) Storage depth has a significant nonlinear influence on CO₂ storage efficiency. As storage depth increases, the CO₂ storage efficiency of the chamber first increases and then decreases. When the depth increases from 500 m to 800 m, the storage efficiency increases by 0.76%; however, when the depth further increases from 800 m to 1200 m, the storage efficiency decreases by 0.24% due to factors such as high in-situ stress compaction. This study reveals the THM coupling mechanism of CO₂ sequestration in deep chambers under high-stress environments. It not only provides solid theoretical support for the large-scale resource utilization of underground space in abandoned mines, but also offers important scientific basis and engineering guidance for the scheme design and long-term safety evaluation of future deep geological carbon sequestration projects.

title: Rapid Cycling-Mediated Indirect Facilitation: A Formal Hypothesis on the Maintenance of Plankton Diversity
summary: Abstract The paradox of the plankton---that coexisting species vastly outnumber limiting resource types---has lacked a formal explanation that simultaneously embeds classical competition theory and niche theory since Hutchinson. This paper
