content: Abstract The paradox of the plankton---that coexisting species vastly outnumber limiting resource types---has lacked a formal explanation that simultaneously embeds classical competition theory and niche theory since Hutchinson. This paper proposes a hypothesis: in plankton communities, rapid material cycling transforms the resource pool from a passive sink assumed by competition theory into a cycling medium in which biomass temporarily hosts resources. When a species consumes a resource, the resource does not vanish; it merely transfers from the inorganic pool to the biomass pool. When that species dies and is remineralized, the resource immediately returns to the inorganic pool and becomes available to other species. This cycling feedback produces interspecific indirect facilitation at long time scales, with strength proportional to mortality rate $\delta_i$ and stoichiometric fraction $\mu_{ji}$, competing against consumption rate $V_{ji}f_i$. When $\mu_{ji}\delta_i > V_{ji}f_i$ for all resources, the net effect of niche overlap shifts from competition to facilitation, and the conclusions of classical competitive exclusion are revised. The criterion is a sufficient condition: if it holds for some resources but not others, the net effect may still be positive. At equilibrium, the criterion takes the form $\mu_{ji}r_i > V_{ji}$, and the two are limits of the same criterion at different time scales. We further situate this mechanism within the classical literature of the microbial loop, provide a strict mathematical definition of the ''unified coupled population'' concept and three testable emergent properties, distinguish it from the storage effect, viral lysis explanations, and the quasi-optimal resource mechanism, and address evolutionary stability. A simple evolutionary model is provided to show how Red Queen dynamics can sustain high mortality rates. Each testable prediction is accompanied by runnable Python code, available at \url{https://github.com/mldih/Planktion-1}. The value of this hypothesis does not lie in being proven, but in advancing the plankton paradox from a qualitative debate to a measurable, computable, and falsifiable formal framework.

title: The Proposed Structure of the Income Tax Base
summary: Abstract The proposed income tax base is developed and explained in this chapter. Income is the return to any type of capital. A distinction is made between human and nonhuman capital in order to facilitate administration and the use of adv
content: Abstract The proposed income tax base is developed and explained in this chapter. Income is the return to any type of capital. A distinction is made between human and nonhuman capital in order to facilitate administration and the use of advanced payments. Gross returns to capital are reduced by the deductions necessary to derive the net return to the taxpayer’s capital. Only individuals are taxpayers, so there is no tax on any entity. Deductions include full interest payments, expenses for maintaining human capital, and other related expenses. There are no deductions for contributions to pensions or to charitable organizations. The chapter contains two annexes supplying technical details, including proposed drafting instructions, and numerical examples.

title: Legitimation Manipulation in Political Argumentation: A Cognitive Critical Comparative Analysis on Energy Policy Discourse of the Democratic Party and the Republicn Party
summary: Abstract Energy has become a global issue and the U.S.’ energy policy remains volatile as the Democratic party and the Republican have different stances on energy. This article constructs a three-dimensional theoretical framework: strategy-
content: Abstract Energy has become a global issue and the U.S.’ energy policy remains volatile as the Democratic party and the Republican have different stances on energy. This article constructs a three-dimensional theoretical framework: strategy-argumentation-critique, which combines representation, action and critique together. The proximization and distanciation are integrated together into symbolic distance strategies which are used to adjust the distance between outside-deictic center and inside-deictic center. And the symbolic distance strategies are used to manipulate the public’s construal mechanism in the process of argumentation or deliberation leading to decision and action. Finally the critique of argumentation can disclose the rightfulness and wrongness which can contribute to the social development. Therefore, this article, taking the energy part of Economic Report of the President as data, analyzes how the two parties deliberate their own energy action in the practical argumentation, explores how they use symbolic distance strategies in the argumentation to achieve their rhetorical effects, and offers a critical analysis of the argumentation to reveal the ideologies and stances of the two party reflected in their discourse.

title: Plasmonic S‐Scheme Heterojunction‐Mediated Photocatalytic Cascade Reaction for Antibiotic Wastewater‐to‐Hydrocarbon Fuel Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic mineralization of organic pollutants has attracted considerable attention in antibiotic wastewater treatment. However, this process inevitably produces CO 2 , and the efficient treatment and utilization of this envir
content: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic mineralization of organic pollutants has attracted considerable attention in antibiotic wastewater treatment. However, this process inevitably produces CO 2 , and the efficient treatment and utilization of this environmentally detrimental substance remain a major challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a photocatalytic cascade reaction on a well‐designed plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunction, where plasmonic W 18 O 49 acts as the oxidative photocatalyst for antibiotic mineralization into CO 2 , and amino‐rich g‐C 3 N 4 serves as the reductive photocatalyst to capture the as‐produced CO 2 and hydrogenate it into CO and CH 4 . This cascade reaction directly converts antibiotic‐contaminated wastewater into hydrocarbon fuels, thereby reducing CO 2 emissions. We show that visible‐NIR‐driven hot electrons in W 18 O 49 transfer to g‐C 3 N 4 to boost CO 2 hydrogenation, while the remaining holes sufficiently oxidize water into · OH. Upon simulated sunlight irradiation, this process enhances the cascade reaction activity. With 5 mg of the S‑scheme heterojunction under 2 h irradiation, ∼86% tetracycline was degraded, lowering the initial wastewater toxicity. The carbon conversion efficiencies for tetracycline‐to‐CO/CH 4 and mineralization‑derived CO 2 ‐to‐CO/CH 4 reached ∼0.60% and ∼2.68%, respectively. This work provides a promising strategy for integrating pollutant degradation with CO 2 valorization via rational design of high‐performance photocatalysts, advancing sustainable wastewater treatment and carbon neutrality.

title: SiO₂-modified bacterial nanocellulose (BNC) for efficient COD removal from petrochemical wastewater: characterization, removal performance and mechanistic insights
summary: Petrochemical wastewater contains high concentrations of refractory organic pollutants, resulting in elevated chemical oxygen demand (COD) and serious environmental concerns. In this study, a SiO₂-modified bacterial nanocellulose (SiO₂–BNC)
content: Petrochemical wastewater contains high concentrations of refractory organic pollutants, resulting in elevated chemical oxygen demand (COD) and serious environmental concerns. In this study, a SiO₂-modified bacterial nanocellulose (SiO₂–BNC) nanocomposite was synthesized via the sol–gel method and evaluated for COD removal from petrochemical wastewater. Material characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of SiO₂ and the formation of a porous, high-surface-area architecture. Process evaluation using response surface methodology (RSM) identified temperature and adsorbent dosage as the most influential operating parameters. Under the optimized conditions (pH 6.5, adsorbent dosage of 250 mg/L and temperature of 30 °C), the nanocomposite achieved an exceptional COD removal efficiency of 98.2%, displaying reasonable correspondence with experimental trends, although quantitative model predictions should be interpreted cautiously due to the significant lack-of-fit. The superior adsorption performance was attributed to the synergistic effects of intraparticle diffusion, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic attraction, and surface complexation. Furthermore, the adsorbent retained 89.4% of its initial removal efficiency (preserving approximately 91.0% of its initial adsorption capacity) after five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. These findings demonstrate that the SiO₂–BNC nanocomposite represents an efficient, robust and recyclable adsorbent for advanced industrial wastewater remediation.

title: Electricity-Secure Sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chain Design at the Production-Land-Energy Nexus: A Data-Driven Co-Optimization Framework for the Steel Industry
summary: Abstract Energy shortages, resource scarcity, and limited industrial land can infeasible the attractive steelmaking locations. This study develops an integrated robust optimization framework for a sustainable closed-loop DRI-EAF steel suppl
content: Abstract Energy shortages, resource scarcity, and limited industrial land can infeasible the attractive steelmaking locations. This study develops an integrated robust optimization framework for a sustainable closed-loop DRI-EAF steel supply chain in which facility location, production-line selection, scrap recovery, wastewater reuse, on-site electricity generation, and industrial-land allocation are co-planned. The central modeling contribution is the endogenous competition for a common, finite land resource between steel production, photovoltaic systems, and diesel-fueled CHP units of different capacities. This coupling allows electricity-constrained candidate locations to remain feasible when the economic and operational value of the site justifies appropriately sized on-site generation. A data driven approach is used to model polynomial regression based on historical temperature, solar-irradiance, and energy-consumption data to estimate location- and period-specific electricity conditions, natural-gas availability, and solar-generation potential; bounded uncertainty is then handled through robust optimization. The multi-objective MILP model proposed to minimize total system cost and CO 2 emissions while maximizing surplus on-site electricity exported to the grid. In the case study, the selected design generates approximately 1.29E + 10 kWh of on-site electricity annually, including 6.94E + 9 kWh from solar PV, and exports 5.34E + 9 kWh to the grid. The associated circular-resource strategy avoids approximately 6.10E + 6 t of iron-ore extraction, mitigates approximately 2.80E + 9 kg of CO 2 emissions, reuses approximately 2.15E + 8 m of wastewater, and creates 7,415 jobs. The results show that industrial land is an active coupling resource between production expansion and energy security, rather than a passive siting parameter, and that coordinated energy-land-production planning can preserve technically constrained but strategically attractive steelmaking locations.

title: Measurements, spatial differences, and convergence analysis of carbon offset in the Yangtze River economic belt
summary: In the context of China’s dual carbon goals and the strategic positioning of the Yangtze River Economic Belt as a pilot zone for carbon-peak and carbon-neutrality policies, understanding the spatiotemporal evolution and convergence of regio
content: In the context of China’s dual carbon goals and the strategic positioning of the Yangtze River Economic Belt as a pilot zone for carbon-peak and carbon-neutrality policies, understanding the spatiotemporal evolution and convergence of regional carbon offset capacity is essential for designing differentiated low-carbon development pathways. This study utilizes panel data from 107 prefecture-level cities along the Yangtze River Economic Belt from 2006 to 2017 to investigate the “catch-up effect” in carbon offset capacity and trace the temporal and spatial evolution of carbon offset gaps. Employing spatial dependence analysis alongside absolute and conditional \( \beta \) -convergence testing, the study examines convergence trends in the carbon offset gap. The findings reveal that: (1) The carbon offset gap across the Yangtze River Economic Belt exhibited an overall upward trend, peaking around 2011–2012, with values declining progressively from downstream to midstream and upstream regions. (2) The carbon offset gap first increased and then decreased over the sample period; approximately 30% of the variation was attributed to intra-regional differences, a proportion that remained stable over time, while inter-regional disparities and density-related heterogeneity accounted for approximately 45% and 25%, respectively, with mild inverse fluctuations. (3) Convergence analysis identified significant absolute and conditional \( \beta \) -convergence across the belt, revealing a clear catch-up tendency; the coefficient of variation nevertheless increased over the full sample period, indicating \( \sigma \) -divergence, although its decline after 2014 signaled an emerging \( \sigma \) -convergence trend. The convergence rate was highest in the upstream section, followed by the midstream and downstream sections. Based on these results, the study proposes regionally differentiated policy recommendations: enhancing carbon sink capacity in the upstream section, transitioning the midstream section into a low-carbon transition hub, and achieving substantial carbon emission reduction in the downstream section. Additionally, a collaborative support system should be established, incorporating green finance mechanisms, evaluation frameworks, and an integrated carbon monitoring and accounting platform to facilitate coordinated low-carbon development across the Yangtze River Economic Belt.

title: Ex-Ante Product Carbon Footprint Forecasting in Electric Arc Furnace Stainless Steel Production: A Probabilistic Machine Learning Framework for Alloy Eco-design
summary: Abstract Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product Carbon Footprint (CFP) are robust tools for evaluating sustainability in hard-to-abate sectors like steelmaking, but their data-intensive and ex-post nature severely limits their use as proac
content: Abstract Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Product Carbon Footprint (CFP) are robust tools for evaluating sustainability in hard-to-abate sectors like steelmaking, but their data-intensive and ex-post nature severely limits their use as proactive eco-design tools. Highly granular LCA models mapping entire product portfolios remain exceptionally rare, as their development is labor-intensive and demands specialized expertise. To overcome this bottleneck and tackle the eco-design paradox, this work proposes an ex-ante Machine Learning (ML) framework to forecast the CFP of Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) stainless-steel production, directly during the alloy and charge design stage. The ML framework was developed by analyzing 2206 EAF heats. The target CFP for each heat was derived from a previous study and charge mix macro-categories (i.e., scrap, Cr, Ni, and Mo sources) were used as features. This study overcomes deterministic ML approaches by propagating the LCA model uncertainty via dataset augmentation, leveraging Monte Carlo simulations with 10,000 iterations per steel family. Algorithms including Linear Quantile Regression (LQR), XGBoost, Quantile Random Forest (QRF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Long Short-Term Memory neural networks (LSTM) and TabNet were evaluated. To ensure methodological robustness and industrial reliability, a time-series cross-validation (walk-forward) approach was employed to prevent look-ahead bias and data leakage, effectively handling temporal variations in process conditions (e.g., maintenance, refractory conditions) and scrap availability. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was used to interpret feature contributions, acting as a consistency check. QRF emerged as the most robust algorithm, outperforming other models due to its generalization capabilities and its ability to capture LCA parametric uncertainty. The model achieved an R2 of 97.4% and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 105.4 kg CO2,eq/ton (a 4.38% relative error against the full dataset average of 2404.65 kg CO2,eq/ton). Furthermore, the model successfully provided probabilistically calibrated prediction intervals that robustly account for the uncertainty stemming from the underlying LCA model, achieving a Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) of 95.3%. SHAP analysis confirmed the model's reliance on raw materials, accurately capturing the strong positive correlation between CFP and main alloying sources (i.e., Cr, Ni, and Mo). Conversely, a negative correlation was found with scrap. By linking raw material inputs to environmental performance, the proposed ML framework provides a robust, transferable, and scalable eco-design tool. This empowers steelmakers to optimize secondary raw material usage and improve alloy design, thereby accelerating the transition towards resource-efficient and sustainable metallurgy.

title: Applied versus faced trade protectionism and ecological sustainability: Evidence from a dynamic panel threshold and quantile regression analysis of 96 countries
summary: The question of the environmental consequences of protectionism has emerged as an urgent issue at the intersection of international political economy and sustainability studies, as the world economy becomes increasingly fragmented into comp
content: The question of the environmental consequences of protectionism has emerged as an urgent issue at the intersection of international political economy and sustainability studies, as the world economy becomes increasingly fragmented into competing trade blocs. The environmental cost of trade protectionism is often seen in the barriers a country puts up, but the barriers it faces from other countries may be more significant. What matters is which of the two determines where the ecological burden of a fragmenting trading system falls and which governments are in a position to act on it. This study disentangles applied protection (i.e., the restrictiveness of a country's own trade policy) and faced protection (i.e., the intensity with which a country is targeted by anti-dumping measures abroad) and tests their effects on ecological sustainability. Using a balanced panel of 96 countries over the period 2001-2022, environmental sustainability is measured by the load capacity factor (the ratio of biocapacity to ecological footprint), a supply-inclusive measure that goes beyond carbon emissions alone. We test the load capacity curve using static and dynamic panel threshold models, modelling faced protection as a targeting regime, employing second-generation methods robust to cross-sectional dependence, including the CIPS unit-root test, Westerlund cointegration, Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, and method-of-moments quantile regression. The results show a strong asymmetry. Applied protection has no detectable threshold effect on the load capacity factor, a result obtained with two independent measures. The load capacity factor declines monotonically with income over the income range spanned by the panel, so the recovery arm posited by the load capacity curve hypothesis is not detected in this global sample. Protection, by contrast, conditions the relationship: in heavily targeted countries the adverse association between growth and ecological sustainability is about twice as large as in never-targeted countries, a difference robust across the conditional distribution. Because targeting is not randomly assigned, this contrast is interpreted as a strong conditional association, not a fully identified causal effect. Importantly, this pattern works mainly through the biological ecological footprint (cropland, grazing land, forest, and fishing grounds) and not through carbon: decomposing the footprint reveals a regime gap several times larger in its biological than in its carbon component and none at all in aggregate carbon emissions, a channel largely missed by carbon-only analyses. Our results indicate that the ecological costs of trade fragmentation are borne by the countries targeted and that trade policy assessments—in economics, environmental governance, and development policy—need to look beyond carbon.

title: Hydrogen development in ASEAN: standards, carbon integrity and regional market readiness
summary: Hydrogen development in Southeast Asia is moving from strategy formation toward industrial projects, hub planning and emerging certification systems, yet deployment readiness remains uneven. This structured critical narrative review assesse
content: Hydrogen development in Southeast Asia is moving from strategy formation toward industrial projects, hub planning and emerging certification systems, yet deployment readiness remains uneven. This structured critical narrative review assesses Malaysia within the wider ASEAN market using evidence current to 17 August 2026. Southeast Asia consumed about 4 Mt of hydrogen in 2024, whereas the identified low-emissions production pipeline to 2030 was about 480 kt per year and only 6% had reached final investment decision in the 2025 IEA assessment. Malaysia is a useful focal case because it combines existing refining and methanol demand, renewable-resource potential, established oil-and-gas capabilities, and national and state hydrogen initiatives. The review integrates policy, project, standards, lifecycle-GHG, conformity-assessment and certification evidence through a four-layer readiness framework: technical conformity, carbon identity, MRV and assurance, and market eligibility. The synthesis argues that colour labels alone are too coarse for trade and climate claims. ASEAN readiness depends on traceable carbon attributes, interoperable chain-of-custody controls and competent verification linked to durable demand. Regional cooperation is therefore most useful when it makes evidence portable across schemes rather than imposing a single hydrogen label.

title: Strategic deployment of cross-border energy infrastructure investment for SDG 7: evaluating China’s role in electricity access along the Belt and Road
summary: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 requires a strategic integration of cross-border infrastructure investment to bridge persistent energy gaps and uneven development along the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). This study moves beyond tr
content: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 requires a strategic integration of cross-border infrastructure investment to bridge persistent energy gaps and uneven development along the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). This study moves beyond traditional financial analysis to evaluate the strategic impact of Chinese Outward Energy Investment (COEI) for expanding electricity access (EA). Using high-resolution satellite remote sensing data for EA indicators, we construct a panel dataset for 85 countries (2013–2020) and apply the Method of Moments Quantile Regression to analyze infrastructure efficacy across development stages. The findings offer three critical strategic insights: (1) COEI significantly enhances EA, with robust evidence across all quantiles. (2) There is a significant institutional threshold effect, where the strategic success of energy infrastructure in improving EA is contingent upon host-country governance reaching a baseline level of effectiveness. (3) Strategic alignment is most pronounced in nations characterized by high-renewable energy shares and advanced industrialization, particularly in Latin America and East Asia, whereas the impact remains constrained in Sub-Saharan Africa. This study enhances the understanding of heterogeneous energy development, providing a framework for differentiated BRI energy cooperation, and offers empirical evidence for transitioning from broad infrastructure funding toward projects for inclusive, resilient energy systems.

title: Income Tax Reform: A Novel Framework for Policy and Administration
summary: Abstract A proposed reform of the income tax in more advanced economies is developed in this book. The proposal is developed and discussed in Chapters 1 and 2. Administration is the basis for the discussion in Chapter 3. The income tax base
content: Abstract A proposed reform of the income tax in more advanced economies is developed in this book. The proposal is developed and discussed in Chapters 1 and 2. Administration is the basis for the discussion in Chapter 3. The income tax base is derived from a modification to Haig–Simons income developed in Chapter 4. Chapter 5 contains a brief discussion of transition rules, revenue estimates, and progressivity. The approach is based on the authors’ extensive experience over more than 40 years advising governments in emerging economies. Tax administration, simplicity, and clarity are the keys to implementing reasonable tax changes in such environments. The authors believe that advanced countries can learn much from the experience of emerging economies in terms of tax design that is based on reasonable economic foundations. Income is defined as returns to capital, either human or nonhuman. One feature of the proposal is that the costs of developing and maintaining human capital are recognized in the derivation of the tax base. Other features of the proposal include: (1) a method of taxing gains at the time of realization on capital items for which there is not an active market, such as equity shares of closely held corporations, that approximates mark-to-market valuation in established markets; (2) a different approach to transfer pricing; (3) the elimination of the corporate tax but replacing it with advanced payments that flow through to the shareholder; and (4) enhanced administration by expansive withholding via the use of private agents, called Advanced Payment Agents (APAs).

title: Fretting corrosion of nuclear materials: an overview on current understanding and emerging challenges
summary: Abstract Fretting corrosion is an important degradation mechanism in nuclear reactors, particularly at fuel rod-spacer grid interfaces where flow-induced vibration produces repeated relative motion in sustained contact. The coupled effects
content: Abstract Fretting corrosion is an important degradation mechanism in nuclear reactors, particularly at fuel rod-spacer grid interfaces where flow-induced vibration produces repeated relative motion in sustained contact. The coupled effects of wear and corrosion can accelerate material degradation and compromise component integrity. While fretting corrosion in aqueous environments has been extensively investigated, understanding remains limited in liquid metals, high-temperature helium (HTH), and molten salts. Existing liquid-metal studies have focused on simplified contacts and selected materials, with limited concerns of contact mode and the dynamic role of dissolved oxygen. Research in HTH is also scarce, where limited oxygen may suppress oxide formation and promote direct metal-to-metal contact. Notably, fretting corrosion in molten-salt conditions remains unexplored. This overview examines the current understanding of fretting corrosion across reactor-relevant environments, identifies key knowledge gaps and unresolved mechanistic issues, highlighting emerging research opportunities, with particular emphasis on molten-salt systems and their implications for advanced nuclear reactors.

title: Water-induced degradation and small-strain dynamic characteristics of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide treated loess
summary: The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainab
content: The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus (Gmax) and reference shear strain (γr) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, Gmax follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content. TFP treatment significantly bolsters the small-strain shear stiffness; at a 2% dosage (σc = 150 kPa, w = 13%), Gmax increases from 63.12 MPa to 139.93 MPa. TFP treatment enhances the initial shear stiffness while altering the reference shear strain, indicating changes in the strain-dependent modulus reduction characteristics. A unified multi-factor model was developed to characterize the variations in Gmax and γr, providing a quantitative description of the strain-dependent modulus reduction behavior. SEM observations reveal film-like and filament-like features around soil particles, suggesting microstructural changes associated with TFP treatment. These findings highlight the potential of TFP as a sustainable bio-based approach to enhance the small-strain shear stiffness of loess, particularly under high-water-content conditions.

title: Design for battery-cartridge longevity in cordless power tools: Modular standardization via LCA to end-of-life management and circularity
summary: Proprietary battery systems in cordless power tools cause premature obsolescence, resource inefficiency and barriers to end-of-life management. This study quantifies the benefits of standardization and modularization through a comparative l
content: Proprietary battery systems in cordless power tools cause premature obsolescence, resource inefficiency and barriers to end-of-life management. This study quantifies the benefits of standardization and modularization through a comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) of three representative cordless-drill battery designs (36 V, 18 V and 18 V nominal/20 V max) under three standardization scenarios: proprietary, partially standardized, and fully standardized modular. The attributional LCA follows ISO 14040/14044 (GWP100 of ReCiPe 2016 (H) and critical-metal demand), uses an energy-based functional unit (225 kWh of battery discharge energy over 10 years) that includes the tool body and charger, and applies Monte Carlo simulation to battery lifespan, failure rates and recycling efficiency. Full standardization with modular design reduces global warming potential by 13–26% (mean 20%) and net primary Ni–Co–Li demand by 48–51% relative to proprietary systems; replacement part availability explains about half of this reduction. Battery cycle life, material-related burdens and part availability are the most influential design-related parameters (a 20% improvement in cycle life or availability lowers GWP by 5–9% and 2–6%), whereas the electricity grid sets the use-phase share (−29% to +94% GWP). The benefit holds in 99.2–99.95% of paired Monte Carlo draws. Five design guidelines are proposed (Design for Replaceability, Modularity, Compatibility, Recyclability and Repair) and operationalized in a conceptual battery architecture. This research provides actionable insights for manufacturers, policymakers and standardization bodies, including the European Commission's ongoing common-charger assessment; economic feasibility and consumer acceptance require further research.

title: Chemical Weathering in Small Catchments with Contrasting Lithologies and the Influence of Exogenous Acids on CO2 Consumption in Headwater Catchments of South China
summary: Geological carbon sequestration is an important component of the global terrestrial carbon sink and plays a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and contributes to regional carbon-neutrality goals. However, acid deposition and exogenous
content: Geological carbon sequestration is an important component of the global terrestrial carbon sink and plays a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and contributes to regional carbon-neutrality goals. However, acid deposition and exogenous acid pollution can substantially modify the hydrochemical characteristics of surface runoff, thereby affecting the assessment of regional geological carbon sequestration. In this study, we investigated stream-water chemistry in two small headwater catchments in the Pearl River Basin, South China, with contrasting lithologies: the Dinghushan (DH) catchment, which is dominated by silicate rocks, and the Niudu stream (ND) catchment, which contains both silicate and carbonate rocks. We examined the effects of lithology and exogenous acid inputs on the solute composition of stream water and estimated CO2 consumption associated with chemical weathering. The results indicate that lithological composition, atmospheric precipitation, and human activities jointly influence mineral weathering and stream-water chemistry in both catchments. Under the humid and warm climate, the two catchments exhibited different chemical weathering rates, and the intensity of carbonate mineral weathering was substantially greater than that of silicate mineral weathering. After excluding the contribution of exogenous acids to rock and mineral weathering, the estimated carbon dioxide consumption for silicate weathering in the DH basin was 1.34 × 105 mol km−2 yr−1. In the ND basin, the corresponding estimated values for silicate and carbonate weathering were 1.30 × 105 and 8.93 × 105 mol km−2 yr−1, respectively. However, ignoring the influence of exogenous acids would lead to an overestimation of the silicate weathering estimate in the DH basin by approximately 167%, while for the ND basin, the silicate and carbonate weathering would be overestimated by 15.38% and 60.13%, respectively. Exogenous acid inputs have different effects on the enhancement of silicate and carbonate mineral weathering, but neglecting their effects leads to an overestimation of regional carbon sinks.

title: Ocean economy promotional legislation in China’s coastal provinces: progress, problems and prospects
summary: China’s ocean economy has reached a substantial scale, and the policy objective has consequently shifted from expanding output to improving the quality of development. In 2018, the central authorities called for high-quality development of
content: China’s ocean economy has reached a substantial scale, and the policy objective has consequently shifted from expanding output to improving the quality of development. In 2018, the central authorities called for high-quality development of the ocean economy. In response, China’s coastal provinces began exploring a governance model in which legislation serves as a driver of high-quality growth, giving rise to a distinct form of lawmaking: ocean economy promotion legislation. This form of legislation has since become an increasingly important governance tool in China’s coastal provinces. Nevertheless, existing enactments exhibit several shortcomings, including a tendency to prioritize economic growth over marine environmental protection, the limited binding force of statutory provisions, legislative homogenization, and the absence of a post-legislative evaluation system. To address these issues, the relationship between ocean economy development and marine environmental protection must be better balanced; the binding force of promotional legislation must be strengthened; legal institutions must be tailored to each province’s circumstances; and a system for post-legislative evaluation, together with a dynamic amendment mechanism, must be established. Looking ahead, China should draw on the experience and lessons of provincial ocean economy promotion legislation and, when conditions permit, develop a national-level legal framework to address regional disparities in ocean economy development and provide a sound legal foundation for the healthy, sustainable, and balanced development of the country’s ocean economy.

title: Thermal Response and Failure Characteristics of Water-Saturated Bituminous Coal after Microwave Irradiation
summary: Abstract Microwave-induced fracturing has potential for mitigating dynamic hazards in coal mines. In this study, initially water-saturated bituminous coal specimens were subjected to microwave irradiation for 0, 40, 80, 120, and 160 s, foll
content: Abstract Microwave-induced fracturing has potential for mitigating dynamic hazards in coal mines. In this study, initially water-saturated bituminous coal specimens were subjected to microwave irradiation for 0, 40, 80, 120, and 160 s, followed by uniaxial compression tests using an MTS 322 electro-hydraulic servo testing machine coupled with a PCI-2 acoustic emission system. Infrared thermography, stress–strain behavior, fracture morphology, failure mode, and energy evolution were analyzed to evaluate the effects of microwave heating duration on the subsequent mechanical failure of the coal specimens. The untreated specimens exhibited pronounced strong dynamic failure. With increasing microwave heating duration, progressive postpeak failure became evident at 80 s, while obvious strain-softening behavior occurred at 120 s. Meanwhile, the dominant failure mode gradually changed from mixed tensile–shear failure to predominantly tensile failure. The elastic energy-storage capacity decreased with increasing heating duration, whereas the proportion of dissipated energy increased. With increasing microwave treatment duration, the failure intensity of the specimens decreased and the failure process became progressively milder and more controllable. The experimental observations indicate that vapor-pressure buildup within the pore–fracture network during microwave heating is an important mechanism responsible for microwave-induced damage in initially water-saturated coal. The microwave penetration depth into the coal seam increases as water is removed. During the application of microwave-induced fracturing technology, attention should be paid to controlling the effective range of microwave energy to avoid additional damage.

title: Global insights and feasibility evaluation of incineration approach for sustainable waste-to-energy conversion
summary: The generation of municipal solid waste (MSW) is expected to rise from 2.01 billion tons in 2016–3.40 billion tons by 2050, mostly due to population expansion, urbanization, and industrialization in low- and middle-income nations. The techn
content: The generation of municipal solid waste (MSW) is expected to rise from 2.01 billion tons in 2016–3.40 billion tons by 2050, mostly due to population expansion, urbanization, and industrialization in low- and middle-income nations. The technical, economic, environmental, and social viability of incineration-based waste-to-energy (WTE) is still heavily reliant on local waste characteristics and institutional conditions. WTE offers simultaneous waste-volume reduction, energy recovery, and partial displacement of fossil-based electricity. Using literature in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar for the years 2015–2026, this study presents a comprehensive evaluation of incineration-based WTE development; 118 studies are kept after PRISMA-based screening. Successful WTE deployment depends not only on technological maturity but also on source segregation, regulatory enforcement, emission-control infrastructure, financial capacity, and public acceptance. Large-scale incineration is restricted in developing-city contexts due to high-moisture trash, low technical capacity, poor governance, and reliance on unofficial waste-recovery systems. These limitations and the promise of an integrated treatment pathway are further demonstrated by a case study of Gazipur, Bangladesh. Diverting the organic portion (∼2220 t day⁻¹) to anaerobic digestion results in a dry combustible residue of about 627 t day⁻¹ with a corrected net calorific value of 14.79 MJ kg⁻¹ from around 3000 t MSW day⁻¹ and an organic content of about 74%. The outcomes indicate that a phased hybrid process of thermal treatment of dry combustible fraction and anaerobic digestion of the wet organic fraction can improve the quality of feedstock and improve the energy recovery time. The review also highlights the importance of advanced flue-gas treatment systems as well as efforts to prevent waste-throughput lock-in and the replacement of informal waste-sector livelihoods. Overall, the study shows that rather than choosing technologies based only on energy-recovery capability, sustainable WTE deployment necessitates an integrated techno-economic, environmental, and institutional framework.

title: A Substitution Paradox in China’s Plastics Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on Energy-System Decarbonization
summary: Abstract Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce
content: Abstract Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China’s plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.

title: Development of Distributed Energy Resource Control Technology to Alleviate Congestion in Power Grids
source: IEEJ Transactions on Electrical and Electronic Engineering
summary: This paper provides an overview of the ‘Development of Flexible and Distributed Energy Resources Control Technology to Mitigate Congestion in Power Systems’ (FLEX DER Project), a demonstration project conducted by the New Energy and Industr
content: This paper provides an overview of the ‘Development of Flexible and Distributed Energy Resources Control Technology to Mitigate Congestion in Power Systems’ (FLEX DER Project), a demonstration project conducted by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) from 2022 to 2024. With the expected further advancement of photovoltaic systems into distribution systems, it is inevitable that local supply systems and distribution substations will experience periods of overload (grid congestion) due to reverse power flow. This project aims to alleviate grid congestion by utilizing distributed energy resources (DERs) as an alternative to facility reinforcement. It includes advanced use of DER, necessitating sophisticated information sharing between power system operators and aggregators. Considering existing DER utilization already in practical use, the requirements for the business flow, information sharing, and operational management systems necessary for realizing grid congestion mitigation were comprehensively investigated. Furthermore, field‐based demonstration tests were conducted to verify these elements. This paper describes the entire project, focusing on the considerations behind each part, the implications for practical application derived from the results, and outlines future prospects for maximizing the value of DERs based on a report prepared by NEDO and comparisons of the initiatives of other countries. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a
content: ABSTRACT Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor is proposed for rational electrolyte engineering. By investigating a series of C3 alcohol co‐solvents with tunable hydroxyl configurations, we reveal a volcano‐type relationship between MPI and electrochemical performance. Co‐solvents with intermediate MPI, exemplified by 1,3‐propanediol, reside at the apex of this volcano. This optimal polarity strikes a delicate balance between interfacial homogeneity and reaction kinetics, thereby promoting dendrite‐free deposition and suppressing side reactions. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables a symmetric battery to achieve a cumulative plating capacity of 5.2 A h cm −2 and a lifespan exceeding seven months. Furthermore, a high‐mass‐loading (∼30 mg cm −2 ) Zn//I 2 pouch cell (0.3 A h) maintains stable operation over 1200 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.057‰ per cycle. More importantly, this framework successfully identifies 1,2,4‐butanetriol as a new highly efficient co‐solvent, demonstrating the robust predictive power of MPI descriptor. This work translates the Sabatier principle into a predictive tool for electrolyte formulation, establishing a generalizable framework for co‐solvent screening that accelerates the development of high‐performance Zn batteries for large‐scale energy storage.

title: When Green Incentives Backfire: ESG‐Linked Compensation, Dual Accountability, and Corporate Greenwashing
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether executive pay that responds to ESG performance is associated with corporate greenwashing. Using 8634 firm‐year observations for 1286 Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2012 to 2022, we measure greenwashin
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether executive pay that responds to ESG performance is associated with corporate greenwashing. Using 8634 firm‐year observations for 1286 Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2012 to 2022, we measure greenwashing as the gap between Bloomberg ESG disclosure scores and Huazheng ESG performance scores. We estimate fixed‐effect models and check robustness with dynamic system GMM, propensity score matching, entropy balancing, and instrumental variable estimation. ESG pay sensitivity is positively associated with greenwashing. Dual accountability, where pay relates to both financial and ESG performance, is negatively associated with greenwashing. Female directors are associated with a weaker link between ESG pay sensitivity and greenwashing only when critical mass is accompanied by relatively higher female director pay, with this pattern appearing around the 40th percentile in an exploratory analysis. The associations appear stronger among small and less profitable firms, although most group differences are modest. Because contract‐level ESG targets are not observed and unobserved firm orientation may play a role, we interpret the results as associations rather than causal effects. The findings suggest that how pay is structured and who oversees it matter for whether ESG‐responsive pay is accompanied by symbolic reporting.

title: Boosting CO 2 Desorption via Al‐Pair‐Anchored Fe–Mo Dual Sites: A Bimetallic Lewis Acid Catalyst for Energy‐Efficient Amine Regeneration
summary: ABSTRACT High energy consumption poses a significant challenge in the application of CO 2 capture by amine absorption‐regeneration technology. Solid acid catalysts (SACs) exhibit limitations due to poor accessibility of active sites and low
content: ABSTRACT High energy consumption poses a significant challenge in the application of CO 2 capture by amine absorption‐regeneration technology. Solid acid catalysts (SACs) exhibit limitations due to poor accessibility of active sites and low stability. This study reports a Fe x Mo y ‐modified HAP‐ZSM‐5 zeolite catalyst with abundant high Al pairs (HAP). Fe and Mo species are incorporated into the HAP‐ZSM‐5 framework to generate metal‐associated Lewis acid sites (LAS). The Fe/Mo sites anchored by Al pairs exhibit high activity and stability. Compared to the uncatalyzed condition, the catalyst increases the CO 2 desorption capacity by 186 mmol L −1 within 800 s, reduces the relative heat duty by 41.7%, and doubles the reaction rate constant. In situ Raman and in situ attenuated total reflectance Fourier‐transform infrared (ATR‐FT‐IR) spectroscopy were employed to investigate how Brønsted acid sites (BAS) and LAS catalyze the regeneration of MEACOO − . The LAS formed by Fe and Mo facilitated the Lewis acid‐mediated stepwise decomposition mechanism. Notably, the framework‐anchored Fe‐O‐Mo dual sites significantly lower the activation energy for C─N bond dissociation to 0.31 eV, demonstrating a distinct bimetallic synergistic advantage over the isolated Al pair‐Fe (0.85 eV) and Al pair‐Mo (0.81 eV) sites. Faster desorption kinetics significantly shorten the time to reach equilibrium, thereby lowering energy consumption. This work provides strategic approaches and mechanistic insights for the preparation of highly efficient and stable catalysts, advancing the practical implementation of amine‐based CO 2 capture technology.

title: A Photo‐Charging Time Regulation Strategy for Enhancing the Solar‐to‐Electrochemical Energy Efficiency of Photo‐Rechargeable Devices
summary: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable devices (PRDs) that directly integrate photovoltaic and energy storage units have emerged as a promising solution for stable off‐grid power supply. Present efforts to improve PRD efficiency focus on parameter mat
content: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable devices (PRDs) that directly integrate photovoltaic and energy storage units have emerged as a promising solution for stable off‐grid power supply. Present efforts to improve PRD efficiency focus on parameter matching between the two units. Although static matching strategies, represented by voltage matching, are effective under ideal conditions, they exhibit significant limitations when applied to energy storage units that lack an obvious voltage plateau. Herein, a photo‐charging time regulation strategy is proposed as a universal optimization framework to enhance PRD efficiency, which is realized by maximizing the energy efficiency product of the photovoltaic and energy storage units via precise time control. Furthermore, this strategy reveals that when photo‐charging time is governed by a cut‐off voltage, the optimal value typically deviates from the maximum power point voltage of the photovoltaic units. To validate this strategy, PRDs were constructed by integrating passivated emitter and rear cell (PERC) solar cells with Co‐doped Ni(OH) 2 ‐based asymmetric supercapacitors. By controlling the photo‐charging time to 5.7 s, the PRDs deliver a maximum overall efficiency of 11.61% (under AM 1.5G photo‐charging and discharging at 2 A g −1 ). This work provides a viable and scalable strategy to maximize the solar‐to‐electrochemical energy efficiency, paving the way for high‐performance PRDs.

title: Defect‐Rich Ultrathin CuO Nanosheets Promote Electrocatalytic Coupling of CO 2 With Ethylene Glycol
summary: ABSTRACT Electrochemical upgrading of CO 2 is a promising strategy for carbon neutrality. Herein, we demonstrate that thickness‐modulated CuO nanosheets enable efficient electrocatalytic coupling of CO 2 and ethylene glycol (EG) to ethylene
content: ABSTRACT Electrochemical upgrading of CO 2 is a promising strategy for carbon neutrality. Herein, we demonstrate that thickness‐modulated CuO nanosheets enable efficient electrocatalytic coupling of CO 2 and ethylene glycol (EG) to ethylene carbonate (EC) under ambient conditions. Ultrathin CuO nanosheets with a thickness of approximately 1.6 nm and abundant coordinatively unsaturated Cu sites and oxygen vacancies are synthesized, which significantly modulate the electronic structure and CO 2 adsorption behavior without changing the monoclinic CuO phase. Spectroscopic and electrochemical characterizations reveal a decoupled activation mechanism: EG undergoes electrochemical deprotonation to form alkoxide intermediates, while CO 2 insertion occurs on vacancy‐rich Cu sites. The ultrathin CuO catalyst exhibits a significantly enhanced EC yield of 51%, outperforming thicker CuO nanosheets. This work highlights the key role of coordination‐environment engineering and defect‐mediated electronic regulation in interfacial coupling reactions, providing new insights for oxide catalyst design in non‐reductive CO 2 electrosynthesis.
