title: Fluctuation in China’s liquefied natural gas import prices and risk transmission mechanism: an empirical study from the perspective of the eco-environment-oriented development model
summary: Introduction This study is an exploratory analysis. From the perspective of the Eco-environment-oriented Development (EOD) model, this study constructs a three-dimensional transmission model of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–en
content: Introduction This study is an exploratory analysis. From the perspective of the Eco-environment-oriented Development (EOD) model, this study constructs a three-dimensional transmission model of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–environmental policy” to explore the drivers and risk transmission paths of China’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) import price fluctuations. Methods Using monthly data (September 2021 to September 2024) on China’s LNG import prices, international oil prices (Brent and WTI), the Geopolitical Risk (GPR) Index, and the Environmental Policy Index (EPI), we conduct a dynamic empirical analysis via a vector autoregression (VAR) model. Results The research findings indicate that, based on asymptotic standard error statistics, the bootstrap robustness check reveals that only the contribution of GPR (22.81%, 95% Bootstrap CI: 3.04%–42.59%) is statistically significant, making it the only robust driver of price fluctuations within the sample period. The contributions of international oil prices (Brent point estimate 13.54%, WTI point estimate 10.05%) and environmental policy (EPI point estimate 11.38%) do not reach statistical significance under bootstrap inference; their point estimates are provided only as directional references and require further validation with larger samples. Discussion The study suggests possible transmission pathways of “international oil prices–geopolitical risk–environmental policy” on China’s LNG import price fluctuations under the EOD model, providing directional policy implications for balancing energy security and low-carbon transition goals. We recommend carbon price-linked LNG long-term contracts, a diversified supply system, and enhanced geopolitical risk early warning and coordination.

title: Toward the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development: Integrating ESG Strategies, Green Dynamic Capability, and Institutional Alignment for Cleaner Production Performance
summary: ABSTRACT Accelerating cleaner production has become central to achieving sustainable development, particularly in emerging economies where industrial expansion must be balanced with environmental sustainability. Despite growing investments
content: ABSTRACT Accelerating cleaner production has become central to achieving sustainable development, particularly in emerging economies where industrial expansion must be balanced with environmental sustainability. Despite growing investments in ESG strategies, limited understanding exists of how firms translate these strategic commitments into cleaner production outcomes that support the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and Institutional Theory, this study examines how ESG strategies enhance cleaner production through the development of Green Dynamic Capability and the enabling role of institutional alignment. Using panel data from 475 manufacturing firms in Sub‐Saharan Africa over 2010–2025, the study applies the two‐step System Generalized Method of Moments estimator and conducts robustness checks using alternative measures and estimators. The findings reveal that environmental and governance strategies significantly improve cleaner production performance, whereas social strategies exhibit limited direct effects. Green Dynamic Capability partially mediates the relationship between ESG strategies and cleaner production, while institutional alignment strengthens the effectiveness of ESG strategies in achieving superior environmental outcomes. Robustness analyses using alternative measures, alternative estimators, and heterogeneity tests across regional and industrial contexts confirm the consistency of the findings. This study advances the sustainable development literature by demonstrating that cleaner production is accelerated not merely through ESG commitments, but through the strategic integration of organizational capabilities and supportive institutional environments. The findings offer important implications for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen sustainable manufacturing and contribute to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly in emerging economies.

title: Dynamic electrochemical modelling and parameter estimation of PEM electrolyzers across broad thermal and pressure envelopes using BO-LSBoost
summary: Abstract This paper investigates accurate electrochemical parameter identification in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems (PEMWES), which is essential for multiphysics digital twins and dynamic control. Conventional analytic
content: Abstract This paper investigates accurate electrochemical parameter identification in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems (PEMWES), which is essential for multiphysics digital twins and dynamic control. Conventional analytical and metaheuristic methods may suffer from numerical instability, parameter coupling, and high computational latency under coupled thermal and pressure variations. Purely data-driven models may lack physical interpretability and electrochemical consistency, motivating the proposed BO-LSBoost framework for parameter identification and residual correction. Five core parameters ( $$\:\varDelta\:G,\:J₀,\:\alpha\:,\:r,\:\:{J}_{L}$$ ) are identified for a 160 cm² single-cell electrolyzer operating at 50–80 ( $$\: {}^{ \circ }C $$ )and pressures up to 30 bars. Bayesian Optimization (BO) estimates global thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, while Least-Squares Gradient Boosting (LSBoost) compensates for unmodelled multiphysics residuals. The model achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 0.0006% and 0.0014% for thermal and pressure sweeps, respectively. Dynamic cycling yields an average absolute voltage error of 0.01 V. Increasing the sample size from N = 60 to 239 reduces MAPE from 0.0335% to 0.0028%, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy for real-time load emulation.

title: Soil moisture anomalies lead seasonal hydropower operator valuation stress
summary: Abstract Hydropower output depends on basin storage and reservoir operation. Climate finance studies rely primarily on firm-level scores, while the relationship between basin-scale hydrometeorological variables and the market valuation of h
content: Abstract Hydropower output depends on basin storage and reservoir operation. Climate finance studies rely primarily on firm-level scores, while the relationship between basin-scale hydrometeorological variables and the market valuation of hydropower operators is rarely tested. We screen Earth observation hydroclimate anomalies upstream of the Longtan Hydropower Station against its operator’s market-adjusted valuation over 2020 to 2026. Root-zone soil-moisture anomalies are associated with forward 20-day valuation stress, an idiosyncratic volatility measure, about 4.5 months later (Spearman ρ = 0.41 at a 90-trading-day lead, false discovery rate q = 0.012). Annualized, this volatility averages about 18% after anomalies in the driest quintile and 30% after the wettest. The association persists with all other basin variables held fixed and under a non-linear dependence measure. No precipitation association survives false discovery rate control. Basin storage indicators from satellite and reanalysis products are candidates for seasonal hydropower climate risk screening.

title: Must-Have or Nice-to-Have? Factors Influencing Chinese Travelers’ Intention to Use E-Boarding Passes: Using Mixed Methods Approaches
summary: Abstract Ranked as the world’s second largest airport system, China attaches great importance to sustainable travel. Travelers’ adoption of electronic boarding passes could promote green behavior and sustainability. Using mixed methods appr
content: Abstract Ranked as the world’s second largest airport system, China attaches great importance to sustainable travel. Travelers’ adoption of electronic boarding passes could promote green behavior and sustainability. Using mixed methods approaches, this study examines factors influencing Chinese travelers’ attitudes and intentions to adopt electronic boarding passes (E-boarding passes), based on the technology acceptance model (TAM) and the theory of reasoned action (TRA). In Study 1, 317 online data responses are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis (NCA) via SmartPLS 4.0 to identify sufficient and necessary conditions of proposed factors. In Study 2, semi-structured interviews are conducted to illuminate quantitative results. The findings indicate that emotional value and environmental concern are both sufficient and necessary conditions of travelers’ attitudes towards E-boarding pass adoption. Although environmental concern emerges as a necessary condition (must-have factor), while a certain level is required to achieve the desired outcome (i.e., behavioral intention). The study illustrates the triangulation of advanced mixed-method approaches can advance theory testing, offering useful insights for the air travel industry and policymakers to understand Chinese travelers’ technology adoption and sustainable behaviors.

title: A non-perturbative framework for ion stopping in partially ionized warm dense matter with a physics-informed neural-network solver
summary: Abstract Ion energy deposition in dense plasmas is of central importance to ion-beam-driven inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density physics. In the Bragg-peak regime, the stopping power governs the spatial distribution of deposi
content: Abstract Ion energy deposition in dense plasmas is of central importance to ion-beam-driven inertial confinement fusion and high-energy-density physics. In the Bragg-peak regime, the stopping power governs the spatial distribution of deposited energy and therefore strongly affects the formation of warm dense states and the efficiency of ion fast ignition. In this regime, the projectile velocity becomes comparable to the characteristic velocity of target electrons, and the beam–plasma interaction may enter a nonlinear, non-perturbative scattering regime in which Born-based perturbative treatments are no longer adequate. For partially ionized warm dense matter, additional complexity arises from charge-state distributions, bound-electron response and dynamic screening. Here, we develop a physically constrained, self-consistent non-perturbative framework for ion stopping in warm dense matter. The approach combines formal quantum-scattering relations, a charge-state-resolved collisional–radiative model and multiscale effective interaction potentials. In the strong-scattering regime, non-perturbative phase shifts are obtained from the Calogero equation using a variable-phase physics-informed neural-network solver, while the Born limit is recovered naturally in the weak-coupling asymptotic regime. This provides a unified description in which deviations from perturbative stopping can be quantified and the onset of perturbative breakdown can be identified. The framework is validated against time-resolved proton energy-loss measurements in a hydrogen discharge plasma and against FCDF benchmarks in the classical and strongly degenerate limits. For partially ionized warm dense carbon, the calculated stopping power remains close to TD-KS-DFT and TD-OF-DFT reference data, while conventional phenomenological and average-atom models tend to overestimate the Bragg-peak region. These results indicate that higher-order phase-shift corrections are essential in the strongly coupled regime and that the present framework provides a consistent non-perturbative description of ion energy loss in partially ionized warm dense plasmas.

title: China-Pakistan Bilateral Energy Investment Agreements in the Perspective of CPEC: Environmental Challenges, Legal Issues and Recommendations
source: NUST Journal of Social Sciences and Humannities
summary: The purpose of the following study is to conduct a critical and in-depth investigation of the coal-based electricity projects and investment under CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor), discussing their environmental impacts, legal issues
content: The purpose of the following study is to conduct a critical and in-depth investigation of the coal-based electricity projects and investment under CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor), discussing their environmental impacts, legal issues, and recommendations. This research uncovers various aspects of these projects, phases them out, and presents solutions to achieve sustainability. For this study, the researchers have chosen the qualitative research method with the help of secondary data sources and thematic analysis. Following the qualitative design, this research will uncover varied subjective data, such as the results of other studies on carbon pricing, the carbon power energy projects of CPEC, and the arbitration methods used for amicable solutions and their impacts. Additionally, using the qualitative design will allow offering more enriched and detailed outcomes, supporting a better understanding of the data. The data sources of the current research include but not limited to Acts, Statutes, International Conventions and Treaties, International Energy Reports and Statistics, Case laws as well as quality research articles, books and e-journals repositories. Through the findings of this study, it may be observed that coal-based electricity projects under the CPEC require further improvement to overcome environmental and legal issues. The solutions recommended within this study include emission trading system, significant development and work on renewable sources, carbon pricing policy and adopting best international arbitration practices. This study is significant because by examining Pakistan's coal-based energy infrastructure situation, revisiting applicable rules and regulations, and considering the bilateral investment regime, Pakistan can better manage the CPEC projects.

title: Influence of Mg doping on the structural, magnetic, optical, and electrical properties of Co–Zn spinel ferrites
summary: Abstract The effect of Mg substitution on the structural, vibrational, optical, magnetic, dielectric, and electrical properties of cobalt–zinc ferrite was systematically investigated using Co₀.₅Zn₀.₅₋ₓMgₓFe₂O₄ (x = 0.0–0.5) ceramics synthes
content: Abstract The effect of Mg substitution on the structural, vibrational, optical, magnetic, dielectric, and electrical properties of cobalt–zinc ferrite was systematically investigated using Co₀.₅Zn₀.₅₋ₓMgₓFe₂O₄ (x = 0.0–0.5) ceramics synthesized by the sol–gel method. X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement confirmed the formation of a single-phase cubic spinel structure (space group Fd3̅m) for all compositions. Structural parameters, including cation–cation and cation–anion distances, were systematically analyzed, revealing crystallite sizes in the range of 13.47–25.92 nm. FTIR spectra exhibited characteristic absorption bands near 650 and 460 cm⁻¹, corresponding to tetrahedral and octahedral metal–oxygen vibrations, accompanied by slight reductions in bond length, force constant, and Debye temperature. Optical analysis revealed a gradual decrease in the band gap from 1.72 to 1.43 eV with increasing Mg content, indicating modifications in the electronic structure. Magnetic measurements confirmed ferromagnetic behavior with a multidomain nature, while a single-peak switching field distribution indicated uniform magnetization reversal. The Co₀.₅Zn₀.₅Mg₀.₅Fe₂O₄ composition exhibited the highest saturation magnetization among all Mg-substituted samples. Dielectric studies demonstrated that this composition possessed a high dielectric constant with comparatively low dielectric loss. Impedance and modulus analyses revealed non-Debye relaxation behavior, whereas Nyquist plots confirmed the contributions of both grains and grain boundaries to the electrical conduction process. These findings demonstrate that Mg substitution effectively tailors the multifunctional properties of Co–Zn ferrites, making Co₀.₅Zn₀.₅Mg₀.₅Fe₂O₄ a promising material for high-frequency electronic and memory device applications.

title: Does Energy Quota Trading Alleviate Regional Carbon Distortion? Evidence from a Quasi-Natural Experiment in China
summary: Abstract Global climate action increasingly requires balancing ambitious decarbonization with sustained economic growth, in which carbon distortion—the misallocation of carbon-emission capacity across economic activities—is a key manifestat
content: Abstract Global climate action increasingly requires balancing ambitious decarbonization with sustained economic growth, in which carbon distortion—the misallocation of carbon-emission capacity across economic activities—is a key manifestation of this tension. This study asks whether market-based energy governance can alleviate regional carbon distortion. We exploit the 2016 launch of China's Energy Quota Trading (EQT) pilot as a quasi-natural experiment and apply a difference-in-differences design to provincial panel data for 2010–2022. The EQT policy significantly reduces carbon distortion, and the effect strengthens over time and survives instrumental-variable, synthetic-DID, double/debiased machine learning (DDML), placebo, and alternative-sample robustness checks. Mechanism analyses show that green technological innovation and industrial upgrading are two transmission channels. The moderating-effect analysis shows that better transportation infrastructure, higher human capital, and greater informatization strengthen the distortion-mitigating effect of EQT. These findings indicate that market-based environmental governance can improve carbon allocation efficiency at relatively low economic cost, offering implications for improving market-based energy governance during the low-carbon transition.

title: CEO environmental communication, speech acts, and firm value
source: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
summary: Abstract Signaling theory predicts that communication, such as by CEOs, might complement observable environmental engagement by a firm, by reducing information asymmetry. Yet it remains unclear whether firms with stronger environmental enga
content: Abstract Signaling theory predicts that communication, such as by CEOs, might complement observable environmental engagement by a firm, by reducing information asymmetry. Yet it remains unclear whether firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate more about these efforts and the potential implications for firm value. To analyze 14,523 firm-quarter earnings call Q&A sessions held by 364 publicly listed firms between 2007 and 2022, the current research measures CEO communication about firm environmental engagement and the communicative intent behind such communication by combining MSCI Environmental Pillar Scores, Compustat data, and a fine-tuned DeBERTa model. Firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate less, rather than more, about their efforts during earnings call Q&A sessions. Yet CEO communication about firm environmental engagement can be positively associated with firm value, depending on the communicative intent the CEO indicates, such that assertive and directive speech maintain this positive association, but expressive and commissive speech acts are negatively associated with firm value.

title: Beyond biomass yield: A conversion-aware framework for climate-resilient feedstocks and sustainable biofuel production
summary: Climate change increasingly threatens biofuel feedstocks through drought, salinity, temperature extremes, flooding and interacting stressors. However, feedstock resilience is commonly assessed from biomass survival or yield, with limited co
content: Climate change increasingly threatens biofuel feedstocks through drought, salinity, temperature extremes, flooding and interacting stressors. However, feedstock resilience is commonly assessed from biomass survival or yield, with limited consideration of how stress-induced changes in biomass quality affect downstream conversion and sustainability. This review examines the continuum from climate stress and physiological response to biomass quality, processability and conversion performance, focusing on changes in carbon allocation, structural carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, secondary metabolites, mineral accumulation and biomass recalcitrance. We define conversion-aware resilience as the capacity of a feedstock–conversion system to maintain acceptable biological productivity, biomass processability and conversion performance under climate stress while sustaining favourable environmental and economic outcomes. The framework further recognizes genotype or variety, soil conditions, irrigation regime, nutrient availability and harvest stage as contextual factors that modify stress responses, biomass characteristics and downstream conversion performance. Its assessment is therefore based on measurable indicators including stress-adjusted biomass productivity, water-use efficiency, carbohydrate or lipid accessibility, lignin and ash/mineral content, pretreatment requirements, conversion yield, fuel productivity and associated environmental and techno-economic performance. The review highlights critical resilience-conversion trade-offs, whereby traits that enhance stress tolerance may increase lignification, mineral accumulation or pretreatment requirements, while desirable biochemical enrichment may occur alongside reduced biomass productivity. A conversion-aware climate-resilience framework is proposed linking stress exposure, physiological resilience, biomass quality, processability, conversion compatibility, pathway selection, stress-adjusted fuel productivity and LCA-TEA/resource performance. The framework shifts assessment from feedstocks in isolation toward feedstock–conversion configurations and identifies research priorities including multi-stress factorial experiments, field and multi-location validation, pilot-scale conversion, integrated sustainability assessment and predictive modelling. This approach moves climate-resilient biofuel assessment beyond biomass yield toward measurable conversion-aware resilience and provides a basis for selecting feedstock–conversion configurations capable of maintaining productive and sustainable biofuel systems under future climate conditions.

title: Thematic evolution of green finance in the banking sector for environmental sustainability using bibliometric analysis
summary: The increased urgency of climate change and its implications to financial systems have gained intensified academic attention to green finance, especially in the banking domain. In spite of this growing body of literature, the studies that a
content: The increased urgency of climate change and its implications to financial systems have gained intensified academic attention to green finance, especially in the banking domain. In spite of this growing body of literature, the studies that are available are still fragmented and most of them focus on single dimensions without providing a complete synthesis of the discipline. To fill this gap, this paper will conduct a bibliometric review to map and assess the trends, contributors, major clusters and future prospects of the research on green finance in the banking institutions. The paper is based on a dataset of 640 articles, the analysis of which is carried out with 4 research questions including (RQ1) analysis of publication trends, relevant journals, and institutional affiliations; (RQ2) determining dominant keywords; (RQ3) identifying major thematic clusters; and (RQ4) identifying future research avenues. The results indicate that there had been a significant publication growth since 2015, with a shift from conceptual and exploratory studies to empirical and data-driven research. The number of publications is higher in the case of China, but the average citations per publication is higher in Nigeria, suggesting that publication volume and citation impact do not necessarily coincide. The thematic and factorial analysis identifies few major areas, including climate risk and the stability of financial systems, green banking and mitigation of carbon emissions, the banking industry under sustainability pressure, and digital transformation as the means of developing green financial innovation. These clusters demonstrate how green finance research is a multidimensional field and technological shifts in the financial industry. In general, the study is relevant to literature in that it offers a systematic and thorough overview of the research trends, intellectual grounding, and emergent trends of green finance in the banking institutions. The findings are relevant to interest to researchers, policymakers, and other practitioners interested in making financial practices more sustainable and facilitate the shift towards a greener banking system. Not applicable.

title: Database-driven divergence in carbon footprint estimates for Chinese refined copper supply chains
summary: Refined copper is critical to the global energy transition, yet carbon footprint estimates for Chinese primary production vary because background databases represent concentrate supply, electricity systems, and process conditions differentl
content: Refined copper is critical to the global energy transition, yet carbon footprint estimates for Chinese primary production vary because background databases represent concentrate supply, electricity systems, and process conditions differently. Using 2025 operational data from two Chinese smelters, this study developed cradle-to-gate inventories for Ausmelt-based and double-flash production systems and evaluated them across five software-database-modeling configurations. Across these configurations, the observed Ausmelt case yielded 5.9-7.1 t CO2e/t Cu, whereas the double-flash case yielded 4.6-6.3 t CO2e/t Cu. Because feed composition and operating conditions were not normalized, this contrast represents the sampled plant systems rather than an intrinsic technology effect. Upstream concentrate production was the main source of inter-configuration divergence. A controlled parameter-transfer check reproduced the SimaPro result in OpenLCA within 0.008%, indicating transfer fidelity rather than native cross-software equivalence; the estimated OpenLCA-ecoinvent 3.11 result was 1.31% lower than the reconstructed ecoinvent 3.10 case. Paired Monte Carlo analysis confirmed the case-level ordering and showed that inter-configuration dispersion exceeded within-configuration parameter uncertainty. After consistently rebasing the electricity-factor trajectory, combined process-efficiency improvement and grid decarbonization reduced modeled electricity-related emissions by approximately 19% in 2030 and 96% in 2060. Oxygen-production efficiency provided additional reductions, although long-term mitigation remained dominated by grid decarbonization. These findings identify low-carbon concentrate supply, efficient air separation, grid decarbonization, and regularly updated localized databases as priorities for comparable refined-copper carbon footprints.

title: Half-truths, misrepresentations, and exaggerations: why Fressoz’s rejection of transitions and transition studies is wrong and politically problematic
summary: Although Fressoz’s recent articles and book make some interesting points, this Forum Comment shows that his claims about transitions (which focus on energy inputs) and the academic field of transition studies (which focuses on changes in so
content: Although Fressoz’s recent articles and book make some interesting points, this Forum Comment shows that his claims about transitions (which focus on energy inputs) and the academic field of transition studies (which focuses on changes in socio-technical configurations that provide final services) are tainted by half-truths, misrepresentations, and exaggerations. In particular, we show that Fressoz’s analysis is embedded in half-truths about CO2 emission increases, makes distorted statements about transitions, misrepresents the field of transition studies, and exaggerates the rebound effect. Fressoz also advances flawed claims that resonate with storylines used by incumbent firms and right-wing populists to hamper and delegitimize low-carbon transitions, which is politically problematic. While rejecting transitions as a climate mitigation strategy, he casually proposes alternative solutions like degrowth, sufficiency and ‘energy amputation’ without discussing their (very low) socio-political feasibility or impacts on poverty, which is politically risky as it could leave society without a feasible emission reduction path.

title: SDG 11‐Aligned Sustainable Cities Under Environmental Pressure: Distributional Evidence on Green, Digital and Policy Transitions in OECD Countries
summary: ABSTRACT Urban air pollution remains a major challenge for sustainable urban development and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 11 (SDG 11). This study examines the heterogeneous associations between green technology diffusion,
content: ABSTRACT Urban air pollution remains a major challenge for sustainable urban development and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 11 (SDG 11). This study examines the heterogeneous associations between green technology diffusion, renewable energy consumption, digitalization, environmental policy stringency, income level, government effectiveness, and PM2.5 concentrations across 30 OECD countries during 2000–2023. The analysis employs Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) with country fixed effects, complemented by two‐way fixed‐effects estimation with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel Granger causality tests. The MMQR results reveal substantial distributional heterogeneity. Renewable energy consumption shows a consistently negative and statistically significant association across all conditional pollution quantiles, while digitalization is negatively associated with pollution primarily at higher quantiles. In contrast, patent‐based green technology diffusion and environmental policy stringency indicate positive associations over different parts of the conditional distribution. Income level and government effectiveness show no statistically significant quantile‐specific associations. The Driscoll–Kraay estimates provide complementary evidence on average relationships but do not directly validate quantile heterogeneity. Additional sensitivity analyses indicate that some associations vary across model specifications. These findings provide distributional evidence relevant to SDG 11, particularly Target 11.6, while highlighting the need for cautious interpretation of observational relationships and context‐sensitive urban sustainability policies.

title: COVID-19 impact on households’ energy poverty and clean energy transition in China
summary: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound yet understudied impact on energy poverty and clean energy transition among households. Using at least 6000 and up to 12,000 household longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies f
content: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound yet understudied impact on energy poverty and clean energy transition among households. Using at least 6000 and up to 12,000 household longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies from 2014 through 2022, this study implements multiple empirical strategies to assess these effects on urban and rural Chinese households. Our findings reveal that the pandemic disrupted the pre-existing trend of rising electricity usage and exacerbated energy inequality, as indicated by shifts in the Lorenz curves of household energy expenditure. In particular, the energy poverty of rural households increased more rapidly than that of their urban counterparts in the post-pandemic era. Moreover, the growth rates of energy poverty incidence, depth, and intensity decelerated following the outbreak, suggesting a partial regression of energy poverty alleviation interventions, particularly in western and certain central regions compared to the more developed eastern Chinese provinces. Finally, the pandemic shock further intensified household energy poverty, whereby structurally advantaged households demonstrated resilience, but marginalized households experienced deepened deprivation. These insights highlight the urgency of implementing affordable, equitable, and resilience-based clean energy policy interventions in and beyond China.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Non-Parametric Probabilistic Wind Power Forecasting under Regime-Dependent Uncertainty
summary: Abstract Reliable ultra-short-term probabilistic wind-power forecasting is important for renewable-energy integration, especially during ramps and extreme fluctuations. Existing deep probabilistic models typically encode historical operatin
content: Abstract Reliable ultra-short-term probabilistic wind-power forecasting is important for renewable-energy integration, especially during ramps and extreme fluctuations. Existing deep probabilistic models typically encode historical operating regimes only implicitly, while conventional non-parametric estimators rely on low-dimensional similarity measures and coarse sample weighting. This paper proposes a retrieval-augmented non-parametric framework that reconstructs the conditional distribution of wind power from physically relevant historical analogs. A physically informed BiLSTM–Attention network extracts regime features from meteorological and historical power inputs; candidate historical samples are then retrieved and weighted by combining deep-feature similarity, wind-speed proximity, and temporal continuity, and the weighted neighbors are passed to a diffusion-smoothed kernel density estimator that produces both point forecasts and prediction intervals. Experiments on two heterogeneous wind farms in Zhejiang and Inner Mongolia show that, on Dataset A at the 60-min horizon, the method lowers MAE and RMSE by 21.2% and 22.7% relative to a Transformer baseline and reduces the 80% Winkler score by 24.4% relative to CKDE. A retrieved-neighbor analysis further makes each forecast traceable to physically meaningful historical samples.

title: Beyond Material Footprints: A Function-Driven Framework for Assessing the Circularity and Sustainability of Food Packaging
summary: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) introduces design and recycling requirements while permitting exemptions for demonstrated, indispensable product protection, yet assessment of circularity and sustainability remains lar
content: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) introduces design and recycling requirements while permitting exemptions for demonstrated, indispensable product protection, yet assessment of circularity and sustainability remains largely material-centric. This study presents FunSusPack, a framework that grounds circularity and sustainability assessment in packaging’s functional role for protection, shelf life and logistics rather than material properties alone, enabling function-driven life cycle assessment. Applied to potato chips, the framework compares metallised PP, metallised paper, and transparent mono-PP designs. Key findings challenge prevailing narratives: transparent mono-PP bags provide sufficient moisture barrier for typical shelf-life duration for adapted supply-chain management, while metallised paper laminates have approximately 37 % higher climate impacts than the conventional PP reference. Headspace reductions by up to 30 % do not compromise mechanical protection and enabled secondary packaging redesign, reducing system-level climate impacts by approximately 33 % and increasing pallet utilisation by 22 %. The framework provides a methodological basis for PPWR compliance and future digital sustainability reporting.

title: Lewis Acid‐Activated High‐Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide for Superior Seawater Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corros
content: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corrosion. In this study, we introduce Zn 2+ as a Lewis acid site into high‐entropy layered double hydroxide (LDH) to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure. The resulting catalyst requires overpotentials of 35 and 160 mV for the hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions at 10 mA cm −2 , respectively, accompanied by small Tafel slopes. Furthermore, an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer demonstrates operational stability over a duration of 900 h at 1.5 A cm −2 . Theoretical and in situ analyses reveal that Zn 2+ exhibits a preference for adsorbing OH − , thereby repelling Cl − . Concurrently, this process induces oxygen vacancies and optimizes the d‑band centers of Fe/Co sites, establishing a interfacial/bulk dual regulation. This work offers a novel paradigm for the design of robust high‑entropy catalysts via Lewis acid doping for practical applications in harsh environments.

title: Reduced-rate controlled-release fertilizer combined with humic acid: responses of paddy soil properties and rice nitrogen-use performance
summary: Background To explore the regulatory mechanisms of humic acid (HA) combined with different fertilizer types and application rates on paddy soil structure, soil nitrogen supply, and rice yield formation, a two‑year field experiment was condu
content: Background To explore the regulatory mechanisms of humic acid (HA) combined with different fertilizer types and application rates on paddy soil structure, soil nitrogen supply, and rice yield formation, a two‑year field experiment was conducted with conventional bulk fertilizer (BBF) and controlled‑release fertilizer (CRF). Methods Treatments of single fertilizer application and HA co‑application were set up to systematically investigate soil aggregate composition, dynamic changes of soil NH 4 + -N and NO 3 – -N, rice tiller population, leaf area index, dry matter accumulation, yield components, and nitrogen use efficiency (NUE). Pearson correlation and principal component analysis (PCA) were employed to elucidate factor effects and variable associations. Results The results showed that HA significantly increased the proportion of > mm macro‑aggregates via organic cementation, optimized soil aggregate structure, and improved soil water and nutrient retention capacity. HA effectively retained soil NH 4 + -N, increased available nitrogen concentration during the critical tillering and panicle initiation stages, and avoided excessive NO 3 – -N accumulation, thereby reducing the risk of nitrate leaching in paddy fields. In addition, the combined application of HA and CRF achieved higher yield and NUE under reduced nitrogen application conditions. Conclusion In conclusion, the co‑application of controlled‑release fertilizer and HA can optimize paddy soil structure, regulate soil nitrogen transformation, improve rice productivity and nitrogen use efficiency, and balance grain yield improvement and soil quality amelioration. Further research is needed on the scientific dosage adjustment of these two materials.

title: Nitrogen Harmonized Fluoride Solid‐State Electrolytes With Modulus‐Mismatch‐Induced Interfacial Defects for Fast Li + Transport
summary: ABSTRACT Fluoride‐based solid electrolytes possess excellent air stability, strong oxidation stability and wide electrochemical windows, however their application potential is hindered by intrinsic poor ionic conductivity. Herein, a fused‐s
content: ABSTRACT Fluoride‐based solid electrolytes possess excellent air stability, strong oxidation stability and wide electrochemical windows, however their application potential is hindered by intrinsic poor ionic conductivity. Herein, a fused‐salt‐etched nitrogen‐modulated fluoride electrolyte (LAFN) is designed to improve conductivity performance via synergistic interfacial construction and lattice coordination regulation. The chloride softened grain boundaries and constructed K(Na)Cl/LAFN heterostructures optimize solid‐solid contact, while the Young modulus mismatch between K(Na)Cl and LAFN domains generates massive lattice distortion and defect regions, which can percolate to form continuous pathways for rapid Li + diffusion. Nitrogen doping mediates the generation of self‐limiting stable Li 3 N‐LiF composite layer on Li metal, effectively inhibiting the anode side reactions. It also enables the weakening of rigid Li‐F ionic bonding with the enrichment of lithium vacancies, and the moderate Li‐N coordination balances the activation of Li + migration and structural stability. As a result, the room‐temperature ionic conductivity of LAFN is elevated to 2.04 × 10 −4 S cm −1 , delivering outstanding rate capability and long‐cycle stability in both symmetric and full cells. The LiFePO 4 ‐based solid‐state full cells retain the 81.9% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. When paired with conversion‐type FeF 3 , the cells deliver a high reversible capacity of 233.24 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles.

title: Cooperative R&D contracts for power batteries under R&D outcome uncertainty and subsidies
summary: This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to ch
content: This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to characterize R&D outcome uncertainty. The impacts of R&D subsidies and R&D capability on R&D investment, supply chain members, and their expected profits are examined. A comparative analysis of cost-sharing (CS) and revenue-sharing (RS) contracts is conducted. The findings reveal that: (1) R&D investment exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with R&D capability and a positive relationship with R&D subsidies. (2) Under an RS contract, the expected profits of the supply chain and its members increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability. Under a CS contract, the expected profits of the PBS and the supply chain increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability; however, the NEVM's expected profit exhibits a U-shaped relationship with R&D subsidies and R&D capability. (3) Compared with centralized decision-making, neither contract achieves the centralized benchmark for the supply chain's expected profit. However, compared with decentralized decision-making, the CS contract increases the PBS's R&D investment and expected profit; the RS contract increases the PBS's R&D investment and expected profit as well as the supply chain's expected profit. Both contracts can only improve the NEVM's expected profit under certain conditions. These findings provide valuable theoretical insights and practical implications for decision-making by NEVMs, PBSs, and government agencies.

title: Spillover effect between oil prices, climate risks, and carbon prices in China: dynamic effects and key drivers
summary: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and volatile international oil markets, the interdependence among energy prices, climate-risk information, and carbon markets has become increasingly prominent. Clarifying their dynam
content: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and volatile international oil markets, the interdependence among energy prices, climate-risk information, and carbon markets has become increasingly prominent. Clarifying their dynamic spillover patterns is important for climate governance, energy security, and carbon-market risk management. This study examines the dynamic interactions among decomposed oil price shocks, physical and transition climate-risk indices, and China’s regional carbon price represented by the Guangdong pilot market. The research design is structured in three stages. First, oil price fluctuations are decomposed into supply, demand, and risk shocks following Ready (2018), and a time-varying parameter vector autoregressive (TVP-VAR) model is employed to capture evolving spillovers. Second, the Baruník–Křehlík (2018) frequency-domain spillover framework is used to distinguish short- and long-horizon connectedness. Third, the XGBoost–SHAP framework is used as a post-estimation predictive complement to identify nonlinear feature contributions to changes in spillover intensity; the resulting SHAP values are interpreted as feature-association evidence rather than structural causal estimates. The results show that: (1) oil price shocks, carbon prices, and climate risks exhibit substantial volatility spillovers, with short-term spillovers considerably stronger than long-term spillovers (baseline short-term TCI = 24.91 versus long-term TCI = 5.30, using a 1–10 trading-day short-term band); (2) physical and transition climate-risk information has strong bilateral spillover links with carbon prices, while oil-related risk shocks are more relevant in the short term and supply- and demand-related oil shocks display stronger long-horizon connections; and (3) SHAP-based variable-importance analysis indicates that exchange rate dynamics, China’s economic policy uncertainty, and market liquidity are important predictors of time-varying spillover intensity. Robustness checks using the Hubei pilot carbon market, together with additional frequency-domain evidence under the baseline 1–10 trading-day partition, confirm that the main conclusions remain qualitatively stable. The findings should be interpreted in light of the fact that regional pilots differ from the national ETS in liquidity, sector coverage, and allowance fungibility, and that the climate-risk indices are constructed from global media sources.

title: Fleet-level prospective life cycle assessment: a scoping review of methods and standards toward harmonized modelling
source: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
summary: Abstract Purpose Life cycle assessment (LCA) is increasingly applied to evaluate long-term decarbonization pathways, e.g., in the automotive sector. While life cycle-based approaches are well established at product level, methodological con
content: Abstract Purpose Life cycle assessment (LCA) is increasingly applied to evaluate long-term decarbonization pathways, e.g., in the automotive sector. While life cycle-based approaches are well established at product level, methodological concepts for prospective, fleet-level applications remain fragmented across scientific literature, standards, and policy frameworks. The purpose of this review is to systematically identify, structure, and synthesize methodological building blocks relevant to fleet-level prospective LCA (pLCA) of passenger vehicles and to assess existing gaps and harmonization potential. Methods A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR principles. Peer-reviewed literature from the period 2015–2025 was systematically identified through Scopus and Web of Science and supplemented by standards, methodological guidelines, and EU regulatory documents. In total, 44 documents were identified through the systematic search. An additional 19 applied assessments, policy studies, and corporate reports were included through purposive screening, resulting in a total of 63 documents. The documents were synthesized using a concept-driven clustering approach and organized into five methodological clusters: policy and normative frameworks, core methodological foundations, fleet- and system-level modelling, foreground technology modelling and upscaling, and scenario design with background system coupling. In addition, the 19 purposively selected sources and three sources from the systematic corpus were coded according to how they operationalize the fleet. Results and discussion Most methodological elements are individually well established, yet they are not integrated in a consistent manner. The coding indicates that quantitative fleet-level results are presented using a common terminology, although they refer to at least three reference quantities that cannot be converted into one another: cohort-lifetime, stock-period, and activity-based quantities. Of the eight applications examined, only three explicitly and unambiguously state which reference quantity is used. Moreover, three corporate reports covering the same financial year delimit the respective cohort by different entry events. Neither of the two harmonization frameworks requires fleet aggregation. Additional gaps result from inconsistent temporal representation and a lack of alignment between foreground technologies and scenario-based background systems. Based on these findings, the synthesis identifies four alignment conditions, each accompanied by an indicator for detecting violations. Conclusions Fleet-level pLCA is primarily constrained by methodological integration challenges rather than by the absence of suitable methods. Harmonization can be achieved by aligning existing approaches through clearer conceptual definitions, explicit temporal assumptions, and transparent documentation of scenario dependence, without introducing new assessment frameworks. title: The investment attraction effect of financial technology: evidence from China
summary: Frontier technologies, such as artificial intelligence, when deeply integrated with traditional finance, give rise to financial technology (Fintech), which continuously influences cross-regional capital flows. We examine the development of
content: Frontier technologies, such as artificial intelligence, when deeply integrated with traditional finance, give rise to financial technology (Fintech), which continuously influences cross-regional capital flows. We examine the development of Fintech in Chinese prefecture-level cities, using data on cross-regional investments by A-share listed firms, and empirically analyze the attraction effect and mechanisms of Fintech development. The results indicate that Fintech has a significant investment attraction effect, which can attract nonlocal firms to invest locally. Mechanism tests show that Fintech attracts nonlocal firms’ investment by reducing firms’ financing and business costs, while also improving cities’ innovation levels and entrepreneurial vitality. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the investment attraction effect of Fintech is more significant when the investment destination is a core city, has a high level of human capital, possesses high-speed rail connections, and is located in the same province as the firms’ registration. Additionally, if the firm’s CEO is from the investment destination, or if the firm has a higher level of diversification, the attraction of Fintech to the firm’s cross-regional investment is significantly enhanced. Further analysis demonstrates that after Fintech attracts investment from nonlocal firms, it not only enhances firms’ market value but also promotes income growth for local residents.

title: Reduction of Intestinal Redox Potential by Coated Ferulic Acid Accelerates Microbial Restoration and Restricts Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli Colonization in Weaned Piglets
summary: ABSTRACT Weaning stress induces redox perturbation and microbial dysbiosis in piglets, resulting in intestinal disorders and disease susceptibility. This study investigated the effects of coated ferulic acid (FA) on intestinal redox homeost
content: ABSTRACT Weaning stress induces redox perturbation and microbial dysbiosis in piglets, resulting in intestinal disorders and disease susceptibility. This study investigated the effects of coated ferulic acid (FA) on intestinal redox homeostasis, microbial restoration, and host responses during enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) infection. Results showed that coated FA supplementation accelerated the structural and functional recovery of the gut microbiota following weaning stress. Specifically, coated FA accelerated the restoration of ecological complexity and selectively enriched beneficial taxa. Following the ETEC challenge, a reduced redox potential facilitated the recolonization of advantageous taxa—including the genera Lactobacillus , Ligilactobacillus , Lachnospira , Roseburia , Lachnoclostridium , and Blautia— while suppressing E. coli ( p < 0.05). Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses under coated FA treatment indicated the induction of short‐chain fatty acids synthesis and the downregulation of inflammatory genes ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, genes involved in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation ( COX5B , COX6A1 , and COX7A2 ), antioxidant defense ( GPX4 , GPX7 , and GPX8 ), cytokines ( IL‐22 , IL‐17 ), as well as mucins ( MUC1 , MUC2 , and MUC13 ) showed strong association with these beneficial genera. These findings suggest that coated FA helps restore intestinal redox balance, supports the colonization of beneficial bacteria, and enhances host resistance, offering a promising nutritional strategy for swine production.

title: Weather–power mapping inference for wind power forecasting across heterogeneous sites
summary: Abstract Accurate wind power forecasting is critical for increasingly weather-sensitive power systems. Forecast accuracy depends on the meteorology–power mapping, which varies across farms and evolves with operating conditions. Existing app
content: Abstract Accurate wind power forecasting is critical for increasingly weather-sensitive power systems. Forecast accuracy depends on the meteorology–power mapping, which varies across farms and evolves with operating conditions. Existing approaches either fit site-specific mappings from limited local data, making them vulnerable to poorly represented operating conditions, or learn a shared mapping across farms and risk blurring local response differences. The challenge is to exploit cross-farm data while retaining mappings that adapt to local and evolving conditions. Here we develop UniWind, which infers target-specific mappings from a shared cross-farm prior rather than relearning each farm’s complete mapping. Using data from 576 wind farms spanning all nine wind-energy environments in China, UniWind learns a shared weather–power prior to reduce reliance on conditions represented at any single farm, and uses target-farm observations to infer local deviations, adapting this prior to the current site and operating regime. On the held-out test sets of these farms, UniWind achieves 82.98% mean accuracy, outperforming the strongest baseline by 1.28 percentage points. It further achieves 84.05% accuracy on 142 farms excluded from training. UniWind also improves forecasts of rare ramp and low-power events, reduces estimated upward-reserve requirements by 5.0 MW per 100 MW at 95% reliability, and cuts fleet-wide model-update computation by 96.7%.

title: Working towards new means for reconciling wind power and reindeer husbandry through collaboration in Northern Finland
source: Journal of Environmental Planning and Management
summary: As formal governance and planning processes struggle to address energy transition related conflicts, there is a growing need for approaches that help parties understand emerging tensions and identify mutually acceptable solutions. In this p
content: As formal governance and planning processes struggle to address energy transition related conflicts, there is a growing need for approaches that help parties understand emerging tensions and identify mutually acceptable solutions. In this paper, we present a case study from Finland where wind power developers and reindeer herders have established a collaborative arrangement to address conflicts and develop shared practices for communication and negotiation. Drawing on action research, we explore how the arrangement can enhance understanding of root causes of tensions and support reconciliation of competing land-uses. Our findings highlight the importance of neutral ground, addressing issues beyond individual projects, identifying drivers of conflict, developing practical solutions, and establishing arrangements for recurring interaction. We argue that while reconciling different needs is not always possible, collaborative arrangements can foster mutual learning, trust-building, and novel practices to balance competing land uses, thereby supporting the management of conflicts associated with the energy transition.

title: The spatiotemporal evolution mechanism of enterprise-led organic agriculture: Evidence from Shandong Province
summary: This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level citi
content: This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023, we combine spatial statistical analysis, Local Moran's I, two-way fixed-effects regression, and robustness checks. The results show that certified organic bases expanded substantially but became increasingly concentrated, forming a clear core-periphery structure centered on the Jiaodong Peninsula. Transportation infrastructure, e-commerce connectivity, and GI-protected agricultural products are positively associated with base expansion, while fiscal expenditure shows a negative association, possibly reflecting compensatory policy allocation to less-developed areas. Overall, the findings suggest that enterprise-led organic agriculture evolves through a layered "Pressure-Transformation-Support-Market" mechanism and provide evidence for promoting coordinated regional development in sustainable agriculture.

title: Climate-Driven Temperature Changes in the Future Impair China's Terrestrial Carbon Sink Capacity
summary: Abstract. The terrestrial carbon sink modulates the rise of atmospheric CO2, yet its long-term persistence under climate warming remains poorly constrained, largely due to nonlinear temperature responses of ecosystem carbon fluxes. Here we
content: Abstract. The terrestrial carbon sink modulates the rise of atmospheric CO2, yet its long-term persistence under climate warming remains poorly constrained, largely due to nonlinear temperature responses of ecosystem carbon fluxes. Here we integrate eddy-covariance observations, process-based simulations, and interpretable machine learning to quantify the nonlinear temperature dependence of China's net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and project changes in terrestrial carbon sinks to 2060 across shared socioeconomic pathways. Site-scale observations reveal vegetation-specific turning points in NEP–temperature relationships, yielding a broad range of NEP temperature thresholds spanning 15–25 °C. Aggregated to the national scale, NEP remains stable between 0 and 18 °C, peaks near 20 °C (18–22 °C), and declines beyond this optimum threshold, implying that sustained warming could weaken terrestrial carbon sequestration. A controlled sensitivity experiment with uniform 0.5 °C warming reduces national NEP by 0.17 PgC yr–1, corresponding to a 31 % loss of the terrestrial carbon sink. Extending this framework to 2060, our projections show national NEP reductions of 24 %, 27 %, and 56 % under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5, respectively. Across all three scenarios, grasslands exhibit the highest proportional vulnerability to warming, with NEP losses ranging from 44 % to 171 %, whereas forests show comparatively modest relative NEP declines (7–23%). While land-use and vegetation dynamics can partially offset these sink losses, such buffering effects remain localized and are overwhelmed by nationwide warming-driven carbon sink reduction. Our findings demonstrate that this warming-triggered NEP decline diminishes the capacity of terrestrial ecosystems to buffer atmospheric CO2 accumulation and mitigate climate change. This study illustrates how threshold-line nonlinear NEP-temperature responses weaken terrestrial carbon sink contributions toward China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals.

title: Influence of Multiple Recycling Processes on the Properties of MgO Derived from Magnesium Oxychloride (MOC)
summary: Magnesium oxychloride is gaining renewed attention in the scientific community as a light-weight and low-carbon mineral binder. However, primary production pathways are constrained by geographically concentrated availability of MgCO3 and it
content: Magnesium oxychloride is gaining renewed attention in the scientific community as a light-weight and low-carbon mineral binder. However, primary production pathways are constrained by geographically concentrated availability of MgCO3 and its energy-intensive calcination at temperatures up to 1000 °C. In this regard, reclaiming MgO from waste MOC through calcination at up to 1000 °C has been demonstrated to produce high quality MgO without decarbonation involved. In prior work by the authors, thermal recycling of MOC between 400 and 700 °C has been investigated and a lower temperature boundary of 550 °C has been established at which recycled MgO yielded highest reactivity and fully recycled MOC achieved 90% of the mechanical performance of the reference mix.

title: Agroforestry, Climate Resilience, and Land Degradation in OECD Economies: Roles of Innovation and Finance
summary: ABSTRACT Despite the growing prominence of agroforestry practices in environmental research, its specific impact on climate‐induced land vulnerability, land degradation, and territorial carbon dioxide emissions is insufficiently explored in
content: ABSTRACT Despite the growing prominence of agroforestry practices in environmental research, its specific impact on climate‐induced land vulnerability, land degradation, and territorial carbon dioxide emissions is insufficiently explored in OECD economies. This study investigates how nonlinear effects of agroforestry practices, financial markets, innovation, environmental taxes, along with final consumption expenditure, determine territory‐based carbon emissions in OECD countries over the period 1994–2021. This study applied the second‐generation Driscoll–Kraay technique to analyze the data, while quantile regression serves as a nonparametric approach as a robustness check. The results show that agroforestry has inverted‐U shaped curve underlying that agroforestry in the initial stages may cause land degradation while at the later stages, it supports the climate resilience practices and land restoration in OECD economies. Moreover, financial development exerts heterogeneous effects in both models, suggesting differing channels of support for financial development. Green innovation and environmental taxes significantly reduce territorial carbon emissions, while final consumption expenditure, as theoretically expected, increases it. The results show robustness through nonparametric quantile regression with the role of income. Policy implications emphasize the adaptive framework of financial mechanisms, innovation, and environmental taxation to support agroforestry practices in a customized yet constantly focused manner on the reduction of emissions while supporting the development of climate resilience strategies in OECD economies.

title: Financiamiento verde, crédito agrícola y cambio climático: conocimiento de los productores de Veraguas, Panamá
source: Revista Multidisciplinar Epistemología de las Ciencias
summary: This study aimed to analyze the green finance sources available to agricultural producers in Panama and to determine the extent to which producers in Veraguas are aware of them. From a pragmatic paradigm, a convergent mixed-methods design i
content: This study aimed to analyze the green finance sources available to agricultural producers in Panama and to determine the extent to which producers in Veraguas are aware of them. From a pragmatic paradigm, a convergent mixed-methods design integrated an integrative review of 22 sources with a self-administered survey of 30 producers from several districts of the province, contacted through a cooperative. An emerging but fragmented supply was identified. Between 90% and 93.3% of producers were unaware of each source (exact binomial test, p < 0.001), and awareness was concentrated among those who had applied for credit (3 of 6 vs. 0 of 24; Fisher’s exact test, p = 0.005). Overall, 96.7% expressed interest in learning about them and willingness to adopt sustainable practices. Capital availability does not equal access: the first barrier is informational and precedes the adoption of practices that could generate carbon credits.

title: Predicción de emisiones de CO2 en países de la OCDE mediante redes neuronales e indicadores demográficos, económicos y de economía circular
summary: Introduction: Mitigating climate change requires accurate monitoring and prediction of CO2 emissions, particularly in OECD countries, where industrialization and economic growth have historically driven high emission levels.Objective: To pr
content: Introduction: Mitigating climate change requires accurate monitoring and prediction of CO2 emissions, particularly in OECD countries, where industrialization and economic growth have historically driven high emission levels.Objective: To predict CO2 emissions in OECD countries using a neural network approach that incorporates demographic and economic indicators, circular economy legislation, and plastics trade data.Methods: A quantitative, longitudinal and predictive design was applied to a panel of 32 OECD countries (1960–2023; 2,048 country-year observations). GRU networks with one-, three- and five-year windows were optimized with Optuna, trained with a temporal split (training up to 2018, validation 2019–2021, test 2022–2023), and complemented by post-hoc calibration and Kernel SHAP. Results were compared with persistence, fixed-effects panel, Random Forest and LSTM benchmarks and checked across five random seeds.Results: Optimization and calibration raised the test R² from 0.053 for the non-optimized network to 0.968 for the calibrated three-step model (MAE = 83.7 MtCO2). This model was the most stable across seeds (MAE = 86.7 ± 4.3 MtCO2), and window length did not yield consistent differences. Simple benchmarks, however, achieved lower errors: persistence (MAE = 11.0) and Random Forest (MAE = 45.8). Plastics trade, likely acting as a proxy for economic size, and labor force were the most influential variables, whereas circular economy laws had the weakest contribution.Conclusions: Calibrated GRU networks provide an interpretable framework that links CO2 emissions to structural demographic, economic, trade and regulatory indicators without using past emissions as inputs. However, they do not outperform simple benchmarks for short-term forecasting. Their value lies in explanation and scenario analysis rather than in point prediction.

title: سياسات الحياد الكربوني العالمية ومستقبل جاذبية استثمارات النفط والغاز العربية: تحليل استراتيجي (SWOT): Global Carbon Neutrality Policies and the Future Attractiveness of Arab Oil and Gas Investments: A Strategic SWOT Analysis
summary: This study examines the gap between global climate commitments and rentier economic structures exploring strategic pathways to sustain the Arab oil barrel competitiveness using a descriptive-analytical approach and SWOT, based on A.M.F and
content: This study examines the gap between global climate commitments and rentier economic structures exploring strategic pathways to sustain the Arab oil barrel competitiveness using a descriptive-analytical approach and SWOT, based on A.M.F and IEA. Findings reveal high sensitivity of Arab budgets to emissions policies with oil dependency exceeding 89% in Kuwait and Iraq, and Bahrain structural dependency gap 49.7%. UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar maintain strong competitiveness due to low fiscal breakeven prices (under $55) and low carbon intensity positioning the Arab barrel as the "last barrel standing”. The study recommended expanding Carbon Capture technologies (especially in Iraq and Libya) and developing hydrogen industry to leverage Arab gas reserves (24% globally) ensuring regional leadership in clean energy by 2050.

title: Matrix-aware 2D field-effect biosensing of cardiac troponin I using complementary ion-sensitive transduction
summary: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for rapid, sensitive and reliable detection of cardiac injury at the point of care. Here, we develop a dual-sensor platform that combines an aptame
content: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for rapid, sensitive and reliable detection of cardiac injury at the point of care. Here, we develop a dual-sensor platform that combines an aptamer-functionalized molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) field-effect transistor (2D-FET) with a graphene-based ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) for the detection of cardiac troponin I (Trop-I) in complex biological matrices. The atomically thin MoS2 channel enables highly sensitive detection of Trop-I, achieving a limit of detection of 0.001 ng mL-1. However, the high ionic strength of serum substantially attenuates the field-effect response, resulting in approximately 80% degradation of the sensor response. To address this matrix effect, the ISFET is employed as a secondary sensor to characterize the ionic environment of the sample. Machine-learning-assisted integration of the 2D-FET and ISFET responses is investigated as a strategy for compensating serum-induced signal distortion and recovering key electrical figures of merit extracted from the 2D-FET transfer characteristics, including maximum on-state current (Ids_max), subthreshold slope (SS) and transconductance (gm). This dual-sensor architecture combines molecular recognition, high analytical sensitivity and matrix-aware electrical signal correction, providing a potential pathway towards more reliable FET-based biomarker detection in complex biological fluids. The approach may further enable multiplexed detection of cardiac biomarkers through incorporation of target-specific aptamers, offering potential for broader assessment of cardiac stress and myocardial injury risk.

title: The Dark Side of the Periodic Table: Theory and Signatures of Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
summary: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). Th
content: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). This framework offers a solution to the $matter~coincidence~problem$ ($Ω_{\rm DM}\simeq5Ω_b$), as the twin $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry can correlate the visible and DM mass scales and their number densities. We analyze twin nucleon freeze-out and the onset of twin Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) to estimate the total naDM abundance, and determine which elements in the dark periodic table could be populated. An appreciable but subdominant naDM component generally requires a fractional nucleon mass splitting near the percent level, with twin-BBN creating heavy elements up to twin carbon. Strong twin neutron-proton scattering allows nearly all of the dark matter, not only the atomic sub-component, to participate in $dark~acoustic~oscillations$ (DAO) at early times, giving rise to a characteristic two-stage DAO signature that may be detected with future cosmological probes. Interactions between the twin and visible sectors, including the irreducible Higgs portal, make this scenario a well-motivated target for future directional direct-detection searches, and the naDM sub-component is expected to exhibit highly exotic astrophysics. We outline a supersymmetric twin Froggatt-Nielsen realization in which spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ breaking in the flavon sector can generate the required fermion spectrum and Higgs potential.

title: Impurity turbulent transport and its role in driving zonal flows in tokamak plasmas
summary: The driving mechanisms of zonal flows (ZFs) in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas are investigated by using gyrokinetic theory and simulations. For deuterium plasmas containing either helium ash with a steep density gradient or lithium impur
content: The driving mechanisms of zonal flows (ZFs) in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas are investigated by using gyrokinetic theory and simulations. For deuterium plasmas containing either helium ash with a steep density gradient or lithium impurity at a high charge concentration, the magnitude of impurity turbulent energy flux (TEF) can be comparable to, or even stronger than, that of the main-ion TEF. Moreover, the impurity TEF significantly drives ZFs. Both the impurity and main-ion turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress (PRS) drives are significant for the case with a high lithium charge concentration. The shielding timescale of the turbulent PRS drive is found to be the damping time of geodesic acoustic mode, which is significantly shorter than one ion bounce period.

title: ESG and financial performance in public and private companies: evidence from Brazil
summary: Abstract Using detailed, questionnaire-based ESG data embedded in a broader corporate ranking for 156 public and 317 private Brazilian companies from 2017 to 2023, we examine the relationship between ownership structure, financial performan
content: Abstract Using detailed, questionnaire-based ESG data embedded in a broader corporate ranking for 156 public and 317 private Brazilian companies from 2017 to 2023, we examine the relationship between ownership structure, financial performance, and ESG performance. Panel regressions and propensity score matching reveal that public companies have lower ESG scores than private companies due to weaker governance. The gap is most pronounced among large companies with low leverage, high liquidity, and low capital intensity. Transitions from public to private ownership are associated with improved ESG scores. Prior profitability is positively linked to ESG scores, particularly in brown industries and among companies with weaker financial constraints, consistent with financial slack theory. Family ownership is positively associated with profitability, especially in private companies. A difference-in-differences design around an ESG disclosure regulation shows that ESG scores of public companies significantly increased after implementation. Our findings highlight the pivotal roles of ownership structure, financial slack, and disclosure mandates in shaping ESG performance in emerging markets, extending ESG analysis to private companies and identifying a family-ownership premium in profitability.

title: Strength and network evolution of waste glass powder activated by rice husk ash-derived sodium silicate
summary: Abstract Under the condition of an approximately constant NaO equivalent, with waste glass powder as the sole precursor, rice husk ash-based sodium silicate combined with NaOH was used to prepare rice husk ash-based sodium silicate-activate
content: Abstract Under the condition of an approximately constant NaO equivalent, with waste glass powder as the sole precursor, rice husk ash-based sodium silicate combined with NaOH was used to prepare rice husk ash-based sodium silicate-activated glass powder cementitious materials (RAGP) with moduli of 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0. Compressive strength, XRD, FTIR, and XPS analyses were performed to characterize the strength development and silicon-oxygen network evolution at 7 d and 28 d. The results show that the 7 d compressive strength decreased from 31.4 MPa to 29.6 MPa as the modulus increased; at 28 d, RAGP-1.5 achieved the highest compressive strength of 39.6 MPa, corresponding to an increase of 31.1%. Compared with the raw glass powder, the centroid of the amorphous diffuse peak of the hardened RAGP shifted toward higher angles by 2.13°–2.33°, while the centroid difference among the different mix proportions did not exceed 0.19°, indicating that alkali activation altered the amorphous scattering environment of the glass powder without inducing a resolvable crystalline phase transformation. The main Si-O-T band of all specimens was located at 973–981 cm and did not exhibit a consistent shift with curing age. In addition, the bridging oxygen ratio at 7 d decreased from 55.38% to 50.40% as the modulus increased; at 28 d, the bridging oxygen ratio of RAGP-1.5 reached 63.25%, an increase of 10.47% relative to 7 d, consistent with the ranking of compressive strength. A higher NaOH proportion was favorable for early-age depolymerization of the glass network, whereas the later-age strength depended on the balance between continued glass dissolution and polycondensation of soluble silicon; within the present mix design range, the activator composition with a modulus of 1.5 yielded the highest 28 d compressive strength and the largest increment in bridging oxygen.
