Nocturnal diastolic BP was lower at 2500 m (− 7.25 mmHg, p = 0.024), normetanephrine, metanephrine and angiotensin II were reduced at 2000 m (Ang II: −23.10 pg/mL, p = 0.011), and 8-iso-PGF2α was lower with higher total antioxidant capacity at both altitudes. None of these differences persisted at the fifth-week recovery assessment. A nocturnal pressurization intervention simulating descent to 2000 m was associated with improved nocturnal oxygenation and short-term reductions in neurohormonal and oxidative stress in male high-altitude workers. The changes were reversible and had disappeared one week after the intervention ceased; they should therefore not be interpreted as an improvement in long-term adaptation, and the study should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

title: Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa2O4
summary: Structure sensitivity limits the rational control of CO2 hydrogenation over oxide catalysts, yet how cation coordination governs product selectivity in spinel remains unclear. A synthesis-structure-mechanism framework for ZnGa2O4 is establi
content: Structure sensitivity limits the rational control of CO2 hydrogenation over oxide catalysts, yet how cation coordination governs product selectivity in spinel remains unclear. A synthesis-structure-mechanism framework for ZnGa2O4 is established by linking Ga coordination to methanol and CO production. Ammonia-mediated coprecipitation favors octahedrally coordinated Ga, whereas organic-assisted hydrothermal synthesis enriches tetrahedrally coordinated Ga. Catalytic measurements, structural characterization, in-situ spectroscopy and calculations show that Ga coordination is associated with reaction pathway selection, while surface area, crystallinity and oxygen vacancies also influence CO2 conversion. Octahedral Ga-rich surfaces readily form oxygen vacancies and expose Zn-containing sites, promoting the hydrogenation of formate intermediates to methanol. In contrast, tetrahedral Ga-rich surfaces suppress extensive vacancy formation and favor a carboxyl-mediated pathway to CO. This coordination-based framework links synthesis to operando active-site structure and product distribution, providing a general strategy for programming methanol/CO product distributions in Zn-based spinel catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation. Controlling whether carbon dioxide hydrogenation yields methanol or carbon monoxide remains challenging. This study shows that tuning gallium coordination in ZnGa₂O₄ directs distinct reaction pathways and product selectivity.

title: Bi-level multi-objective optimal scheduling and multi-mechanism interaction-effect evaluation for integrated energy systems with coordinated hydrogen utilization
summary: Integrated energy systems (IESs) often struggle to balance renewable energy integration, low-carbon operation, and coordinated multi-energy scheduling. Accordingly, this study proposes a bi-level multi-objective optimization method incorpor
content: Integrated energy systems (IESs) often struggle to balance renewable energy integration, low-carbon operation, and coordinated multi-energy scheduling. Accordingly, this study proposes a bi-level multi-objective optimization method incorporating integrated demand response, joint green certificate–carbon trading, and coordinated hydrogen utilization. First, an operator–user bi-level framework is established. The upper level optimizes energy prices and system dispatch to minimize operating cost, carbon emissions, and wind and photovoltaic curtailment. The lower level optimizes electricity, heat, and gas loads based on energy costs, utility, discomfort, and response compensation. Next, a joint trading mechanism is developed. Its green certificate price tracks net load, while its carbon offset coefficient responds to curtailment severity. A coordinated hydrogen utilization chain is constructed. It covers electrolysis, methanation, hydrogen fuel cells, hydrogen storage, and hydrogen blending in gas turbines and boilers. Hourly blending ratios are optimized with corrections for lower-heating-value differences and equivalent energy conversion. Finally, a multi-mechanism interaction-effect evaluation method based on independent re-optimization of each case is proposed. It quantifies each mechanism's individual effect and the conditional interaction effects among mechanisms. Together, these components coordinate market signals, user responses, and multi-energy conversion within a unified framework. The model is solved using a nested NSWOA–Gurobi framework, and TOPSIS identifies a compromise solution. Case studies show that the combined mechanisms reduce total social cost and carbon emissions by 6.18% and 20.41%, respectively, compared with the baseline. The wind and photovoltaic curtailment rate decreases from 25.13% to 11.37%. Joint green certificate–carbon trading and coordinated hydrogen utilization exhibit positive synergy. In contrast, integrated demand response and coordinated hydrogen utilization show marginal saturation.

title: Unveiling the Intrinsic Disparity of Ethylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate in Lithium Metal Battery Exceeding 600 Wh kg −1
summary: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg −1 . Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives p
content: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg −1 . Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives persistent electrolyte consumption and thereby rapid capacity degradation of LMBs. Here, it is disclosed that simply replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) significantly extends the lifetime of LMBs. Compared to LiPF 6 ‐EC based electrolyte, LiPF 6 ‐FEC based electrolyte enhances the cycling stability of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||Li LMBs and enables the 11.13 Ah LiNi 0.95 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 O 2 ||Li pouch cell to deliver 601.2 Wh kg −1 with stable cycling over 100 cycles. Yet, the intrinsic mechanism disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs remains unclear. Through correlated characterizations, we reveal that EC tends to generate highly soluble low‐molecular‐weight carbonate species, whereas FEC tends to form a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer containing high‐molecular‐weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode. Inspired by these polymers, we further construct artificial SEI layers by integrating rubber polymers with LiF to stabilize Li anode. This work elucidates the intrinsic disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs and highlights solvent engineering and artificial SEI layer construction as effective strategies toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

title: Stoichiometry‐Controlled Melamine Phosphites as a Synergist of Piperazine Pyrophosphate for Intumescent Flame Retardancy and Smoke Suppression in Polypropylene
summary: ABSTRACT Compared with the well‐studied and commercially established phosphate and hypophosphite flame retardants, the design, preparation and investigation of phosphite‐based flame retardants in diverse structural forms remain insufficient
content: ABSTRACT Compared with the well‐studied and commercially established phosphate and hypophosphite flame retardants, the design, preparation and investigation of phosphite‐based flame retardants in diverse structural forms remain insufficient. Herein, three melamine phosphites (MPIs) with controlled melamine/phosphorous acid molar ratios (2:1, 2:2 and 2:3) were synthesized via an acid‐base salt formation reaction and combined with piperazine pyrophosphate (PAPP) to flame‐retard polypropylene (PP) by melt blending. The MPIs exhibited high initial decomposition temperatures (268°C–297°C), well above the PP processing window. The 20% (7PAPP/3MPI)/PP composite achieved the best overall performance: a limiting oxygen index of 28.5%, UL94 V‐0 rating at 1.6 mm, an 87% reduction in the peak heat release rate (138 kW·m −2 ), and the lowest total smoke release (1292 m 2 ·m −2 ), outperforming the commercial counterparts in combustion behavior and smoke suppression. Meanwhile, the composite retained a high heat deflection temperature (131.8°C) and about 97% of the flexural strength of neat PP. The enhanced flame retardancy originates from a synergistic dual‐phase mechanism in the condensed and gas phases. This work demonstrates that tuning the stoichiometry of melamine phosphite is an effective strategy for designing efficient P/N synergists for PP.

title: Undercooled Liquid Metallic Core–Shell Particles Enabling Heatless Metal–Semiconductor Bonding for Micro-Transfer Printed GaN
summary: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of Gallium Nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) via micro-transfer printing (μTP) offers a scalable route to address critical thermal management and integration challenges for high-powe
content: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of Gallium Nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) via micro-transfer printing (μTP) offers a scalable route to address critical thermal management and integration challenges for high-power and high-frequency applications. However, traditional polymer adhesives used in the printing process create a thermal bottleneck due to their low thermal conductivity. This work introduces a room-temperature, heatless soldering mechanism at the device level utilizing undercooled liquid metallic core–shell (ULMCS) particles. Synthesized via the shearing liquids into complex particles (SLICE) method, these Field’s metal (Bi/In/Sn) particles are encapsulated in a self-limiting 10 nm oxide shell, maintaining a metastable liquid state until mechanical rupture triggers spontaneous solidification. To test this, GaN/AlGaN coupons were released from Qromis Substrate Technology wafers and printed onto silicon substrates using ULCMS particles. Printing parameters, including shear speed and shear distance, were optimized to ensure consistent adhesion. While initial μTP using compliant polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) stamps achieved high transfer yields, cross-sectional analysis revealed incomplete coalescence due to insufficient pressure applied by the stamp. To resolve this, a dual-stage integration framework was developed, incorporating a secondary rigid glass stamping step. This process successfully created a dense, metallic adhesion layer, providing a robust and cost-effective pathway for the integration of GaN devices for thermal management applications.

title: Spin State Regulation of Co Species for Controllable Product Selectivity in CO 2 Hydrogenation
summary: ABSTRACT Precise regulation of product selectivity remains a critical challenge in CO 2 hydrogenation. Herein, we report an atmosphere‐regulated pyrolysis strategy to tailor the spin state of Co species in Co 3 O 4 , thus realizing a dramat
content: ABSTRACT Precise regulation of product selectivity remains a critical challenge in CO 2 hydrogenation. Herein, we report an atmosphere‐regulated pyrolysis strategy to tailor the spin state of Co species in Co 3 O 4 , thus realizing a dramatic switch in catalytic selectivity for this reaction. Systematic studies reveal that the introduction of oxygen vacancies into Co 3 O 4 triggers a spin transition of Co sites from the low‐spin (LS) state ( d xy 2 d yz 2 d xz 2 ) to the intermediate‐spin (IS) state ( d xy 2 d yz(xz) 2 d xz(yz) 1 d z2 1 ). Across the temperature range of 200°C–350°C, LS‐Co 3 O 4 consistently favors CO production, reaching a selectivity of ∼83.3% at 350°C, whereas IS‐Co 3 O 4 selectively produces CH 4 with a selectivity of up to ∼91.1% at 350°C, accompanied by excellent long‐term stability. The antibonding states of (3 d z2 – 5 σ ) * and (3 d z2 – 1 s ) * in IS‐Co 3 O 4 ‐ * CO and IS‐Co 3 O 4 ‐ * H 2 show lower electron occupancy below the Fermi level ( E f ) compared with those in LS‐Co 3 O 4 ‐ * CO and LS‐Co 3 O 4 ‐ * H 2 , respectively. As a result, the weak interaction between Co sites in LS‐Co 3 O 4 and * CO/ * H 2 favors CO desorption. In contrast, the strengthened binding of these key intermediates to Co sites in IS‐Co 3 O 4 promotes the deep hydrogenation of * CO intermediates toward CH 4 . This work highlights spin‐state engineering as an effective approach for tuning product selectivity in CO 2 hydrogenation.

title: Integrated genomic, biochemical, and molecular dynamics analyses identify Chromohalobacter sp. D23 as a promising quorum-quenching probiotic for sustainable aquaculture
summary: Quorum sensing-driven biofilm formation is a key contributor to the persistence and multidrug resistance (MDR) of pathogenic bacteria, presenting a major challenge in combating infectious diseases. Probiotic quorum-quenching (QQ) bacteria r
content: Quorum sensing-driven biofilm formation is a key contributor to the persistence and multidrug resistance (MDR) of pathogenic bacteria, presenting a major challenge in combating infectious diseases. Probiotic quorum-quenching (QQ) bacteria represent a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics by suppressing quorum sensing-dependent virulence in MDR pathogens and simultaneously enhancing fish growth, immunity, and overall health. In this study, the probiotic and QQ attributes of Chromohalobacter sp. D23 were comprehensively investigated. The strain exhibited robust tolerance to gastrointestinal stress conditions, surviving bile salt (1.2%), phenol (0.75%), and acidic environments (pH 2.0–4.0). Additionally, it displayed pronounced antioxidant activity (> 69%), high auto-aggregation (72.0 ± 2.42%), and co-aggregation (> 73%) with fish pathogens, suggesting a high potential for gut colonization and pathogen exclusion. Genome mining also revealed presence of putative proteins involved in resistance to bile, phenol, acid, osmotic pressure along with adhesion and aggregation facilitating host gut colonization. Virtual screening of strain D23 also enabled to predict potential enzymes/proteins for biosynthesis of vitamins and amino acids. In spite of presence of very few antibiotic resistance genes, overall genome-wide analysis of the draft genome of strain D23 detected no putative virulence genes, plasmid, or transposable element-associated genes, suggesting a favorable safety profile. Whole-cell assay showed complete breakdown of synthetic N-acyl homoserine lactones (N-AHLs) as revealed by biosensor-based assay. Strain D23 also degraded natural N-AHLs of Aeromonas hydrophila within 12 h. Co-culture experiment revealed potent anti-biofilm activity against A. hydrophila ( p ≤ 0.0001). Genome mining identified putative metallo-beta lactamase enzyme (lactonase_D23) having conserved ‘ 66 HXHXDH 71 ’ motif. Molecular docking revealed moderate binding affinities of lactonase_D23 towards both C4-Homoserine lactone (C4-HSL) and C6-HSL, however, molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that the C4-HSL–lactonase_D23 complex exhibited greater conformational stability, indicating highly persistent protein–ligand interaction. Later, in silico mutant enzymes exhibited higher binding affinity than wild-type lactonase_D23 to C4-HSL. This pioneer, integrated study suggests potentiality of strain D23 as safe, beneficial, autochthonous QQ probiotic candidate in aquaculture to improve overall fish health.

title: Traffic congestion in Baghdad: a review of causes, impacts, challenges, and sustainable alleviation strategies
source: Muthanna Journal of Engineering and Technology
summary: The concurrent increase in population size and private vehicle ownership, coupled with limited public transport supply, outdated infrastructure, imbalanced land use along with inefficient traffic management have made dealing with traffic co
content: The concurrent increase in population size and private vehicle ownership, coupled with limited public transport supply, outdated infrastructure, imbalanced land use along with inefficient traffic management have made dealing with traffic congestion by far the most pressing transportation and urban-development challenge facing Baghdad. This review currently summarizes previous studies to determine the primary congestion causes and effects in Bagh-dad, while also evaluating traditional methods as well as new mitigation strategies. The Related literature revealed that congestion is observed at the major intersections on roads, at arterials and approaches to bridges and has a sig-nificant economic, environmental and social impact. Recent research also shows the possibility of intelligent trans-portation systems, adaptive signal control, data-driven traffic control and smart parking to enhance traffic manage-ment. There is some evidence that merely expanding infrastructure to relieve congestion provides only transient re-lief and does not solve the problem sustainably for Baghdad. An integrated approach is thus needed that includes an integrated public transportation, BRT, ITS, Traffic Demand Management, Parking Management and selective infra-structure improvements. For this reason, a methodical implementation strategy is recommended, beginning with op-erational improvement and the creation of traffic data intended to integrate public transportation and intelligent mo-bility for an inclusive and sustainable support of urban mobility in Baghdad. The review's contribution is an inte-grated framework linking congestion causes and impacts with coordinated mitigation strategies, including public transport improvement, intersection performance enhancement, and intelligent transportation systems, to support implementation priorities in Baghdad.

title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
summary: Colloidal nanoparticles can assemble into richly structured materials, yet the complex morphologies that emerge under non-equilibrium conditions are often viewed as irreproducible artifacts. Here we show that evaporating a lens-shaped collo
content: Colloidal nanoparticles can assemble into richly structured materials, yet the complex morphologies that emerge under non-equilibrium conditions are often viewed as irreproducible artifacts. Here we show that evaporating a lens-shaped colloidal suspension at a fluid–fluid interface produces a robust cascade of nanoparticle film morphologies, ranging from continuous monolayers to perforated films, ribbon networks, and isolated tiles. Using in situ confocal microscopy and ex situ electron microscopy together with coupled cross-scale simulations, we identify the physical principles that govern this sequence. A macroscopic transport model determines the deposition history imposed by evaporation, which drives a nanoscale kinetic Monte Carlo model capturing particle rearrangement and solvent-mediated kinetic arrest. A coarse-grained Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes framework rationalizes the observed mesoscale periodicity as a finite-wavelength instability of the evolving film. By tuning concentration and solvent volatility, we control the system’s trajectory through this dynamic phase space and establish a predictable framework for navigating non-equilibrium nanoparticle assembly. Nanoparticle assembly at fluid interfaces is often viewed as unpredictable and dominated by uncontrolled non-equilibrium effects. Here, the authors show that evaporation-driven nanoparticle assembly reveals predictable morphologies through multiscale modeling, linking transport dynamics and kinetic arrest.

title: Valorisation of Bos-indicus excreta biowaste into nanocellulose-reinforced PVA composite films for sustainable seed coating
summary: Abstract Agro-livestock nano-composite film enhance bio-degradable polymeric property and seed coating technology. Nanocellulose derived from bovine excreta (BNC) offer a promising strategy for sustainable crop production and storage. In th
content: Abstract Agro-livestock nano-composite film enhance bio-degradable polymeric property and seed coating technology. Nanocellulose derived from bovine excreta (BNC) offer a promising strategy for sustainable crop production and storage. In this study the optimized film was evaluated for dip seed coating i.e. mung bean (Vigna radiata). Nanocellulose-polyvinyl alcohol coated seeds showed significantly enhanced germination and seedling growth at 5% NC-PVA composite. After 6 days, root and shoot lengths reached 10.20 cm and 13.60 cm, respectively, compared with 6.95 and 9.85 cm for the H₂O control. The improved performance was attributed to the moisture-retaining and gas-permeable nanocellulose network which is suitable for storage application in packaging. In this study novelty lie in, nanocellulose extracted from Bos-indicus excreta through alkaline treatment and sulfuric acid hydrolysis with less percentage of NaOH as reported earlier. NC incorporation in different percentage into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) to fabricate biodegradable bio-nanocomposite films. Structural analyses ensured the successful elimination of hemicellulose and lignin components along with formation of cellulose I nanocrystals with nanoscale diameter 15.95 nm through TEM morphology. Among the prepared formulations (1–7 wt% nanocellulose), the 5 wt% NC-PVA film exhibited the optimum properties, including a crystallinity index of 79.14%, tensile strength of 31.76 MPa, and improved thermal stability attributed to strong nanocellulose-PVA interfacial hydrogen bonding through (251.4 °C to 362.8 °C). This study demonstrates an effective waste-valorisation approach for producing biodegradable seed-coating materials that improve germination efficiency and extended the period of storage of seed, support sustainable agricultural practices and reduction in white pollution.

title: CONSUMER ELECTRICITY CONSUMPTION BEHAVIOR IN SOLAR AND GRID SYSTEMS: TOWARD SDG-ALIGNED ENERGY CONSERVATION
summary: The global transition from fossil-fuel-based electricity systems to renewable energy sources is essential to achieving sustainable development and reducing grid dependency. This study investigates residential energy consumption behavior wit
content: The global transition from fossil-fuel-based electricity systems to renewable energy sources is essential to achieving sustainable development and reducing grid dependency. This study investigates residential energy consumption behavior within a solar-battery-grid architecture using the proposed GridSolarMatch framework. System monitoring data were obtained through a dedicated data logger operating with Module Version No.: LSWS_01_2421_SS_00_00.00.00.06, ensuring high-resolution and reliable time-series measurement of solar generation, battery operation, and grid interaction. GridSolarMatch employs a transparent, rule-based dispatch strategy that prioritizes solar energy utilization, regulates battery charging and discharging via explicit state-of-charge (SOC) dynamics, and uses the grid as a fallback resource during energy deficits. Time- of-Use electricity tariffs are incorporated to evaluate tariff-aware operational behavior without relying on forecasting or computationally intensive optimization solvers. The result demonstrates effective battery buffering, reduced grid dependency during peak tariff periods, and controlled SOC cycling that preserves battery longevity. Analysis of grid import behavior, battery state-of-charge profiles, and a cumulative sustainability-cost objective function confirms that the framework enhances renewable self-consumption while moderating long term grid reliance. Unlike conventional cost-driven approaches, the proposed model prioritizes sustainability and operational feasibility, aligning with Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). The findings highlight GridSolarMatch's sustainability as a practical, scalable, and deployable energy management solution for residential renewable energy systems

title: Nickel–Iron–Manganese Oxides Stabilize Oxygen Evolution in Seawater Electrolysis
summary: Chloride‐induced corrosion poses significant challenges for hydrogen production via seawater electrolysis. Herein, we synthesize a trimetallic oxide catalyst on Ni foam (denoted as NiFeMnO x @NF). The catalyst is fabricated by electrodeposi
content: Chloride‐induced corrosion poses significant challenges for hydrogen production via seawater electrolysis. Herein, we synthesize a trimetallic oxide catalyst on Ni foam (denoted as NiFeMnO x @NF). The catalyst is fabricated by electrodeposition to form a NiFeMnO x precursor, followed by annealing at 450 °C in air to form a protective layer composed of mixed metal oxides. The resulting catalyst exhibits an overpotential of 470 mV at a current density of 200 mA cm −2 and a Tafel slope of 93.6 mV dec −1 in simulated seawater. Notably, in a stability test at a high current density of 500 mA cm −2 for over 200 h, no significant corrosion is observed. We attribute this stability to the formation of mixed metal oxides (e.g., Fe 3 O 4 , NiMn 2 O 4 , and NiFe 2 O 4 ). This strategy offers a new design principle for chlorine‐corrosion‐resistant anodes in seawater electrolysis.

title: Hydroxy-Functionalized n-Type OMIECs as Multifunctional Conductive Biointerfaces for Simplified Biosensor Fabrication
summary: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing re
content: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing remains largely untapped, particularly for n-type systems. Here, we report a hydroxy-functionalized n-doped poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO-OH) that unifies efficient electron transport and enzyme immobilization within a single material platform. By introducing terminal hydroxy groups into the polymer backbone, PBFDO-OH enables the direct immobilization of glucose dehydrogenase through a simple one-pot strategy, eliminating the gold substrates, self-assembled monolayers, and multistep surface activation protocols that underpin conventional biosensor fabrication. This streamlined approach yields robust biofunctional electrodes with enhanced electrochemical performance while preserving enzyme activity and long-term stability. Integrated with additively manufactured electrodes, the resulting glucose biosensor demonstrates a high sensitivity of 17.4 μA L mmol-1, a low detection limit of 3.42 μmol L-1, excellent reproducibility (RSD = 5.35%), reliable quantification in human serum (RSD < 10%), and outstanding operational stability over three weeks (RSD < 3%). Beyond glucose sensing, this work establishes a general materials design strategy in which chemical functionalization transforms n-type OMIECs into conductive biointerfaces that simultaneously simplify device fabrication and provide stable bioreceptor integration for next-generation bioelectronic technologies.

title: Geotechnical properties of lateritic sandy soil: changes induced by oil contamination
source: Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment
summary: Soil contaminated with diesel oil and its chemical components is a significant environmental concern that affects soil properties and compromises its performance for geotechnical engineering purposes. This paper presents an experimental stu
content: Soil contaminated with diesel oil and its chemical components is a significant environmental concern that affects soil properties and compromises its performance for geotechnical engineering purposes. This paper presents an experimental study of lateritic sandy soil contamination using 2%, 4%, 6%, and 8% diesel oil to evaluate changes in geotechnical properties. Geotechnical characterization tests, ATR-FTIR spectrometry, X-ray diffraction (XRD), gas chromatography, mechanical tests, and scanning electron microscopy were conducted on uncontaminated and contaminated specimens. This study also addresses the gap in understanding the effect of oil contamination over time by conducting unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests at 7, 28, and 56 days of curing. Results have shown that UCS is affected by oil content and curing time. Regarding curing time, UCS decreased until 28 days, reaching a maximum reduction of 42% for 6% diesel oil. However, at 56 days of curing, the UCS reduction was not observed, and samples with 2%, 4%, and 8% showed a strength recovery. This recovery may be associated with oil evaporation, as verified by gas chromatography. These results can help interpret contaminated-soil behavior and select suitable remediation or stabilization activities.

title: Ethanol concentration impacts cannabinoid and flavor extraction in hemp-infused beer
summary: Industrial hemp has been considered as a substitute for hops in beer flavoring because the plants are botanical relatives and share aromatic compounds. Dry-hopping, the cold solid-liquid extraction of hop compounds into beer, transfers vola
content: Industrial hemp has been considered as a substitute for hops in beer flavoring because the plants are botanical relatives and share aromatic compounds. Dry-hopping, the cold solid-liquid extraction of hop compounds into beer, transfers volatile terpenes that contribute desirable aromas and sensory properties. Hemp inflorescences also contain cannabinoids, which may be restricted or subject to legal limits in foods and alcoholic beverages. Because cannabinoids have low water solubility but greater ethanol solubility, this study evaluated their extraction kinetics during hemp-based dry-hopping, which have not previously been reported. Beer ethanol content significantly affected cannabinoid extraction and volatile terpene profiles. Increasing ethanol from 0% to 9% (v/v) altered cannabinoid concentrations and the terpene groups detected in beer. Although trace tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) was present, cannabinoid concentrations remained below regulatory and physiological thresholds associated with health and safety effects. These findings indicate that hemp can provide beer aromas while maintaining cannabinoid exposure below limits. The results provide a foundation for further evaluation of hemp as a food ingredient and may assist regulators in assessing its lawful use in brewing. Further research should examine sensory acceptance, process optimization, product stability, and cannabinoid variability across hemp cultivars and brewing conditions under commercial production and storage conditions.

title: Design Blueprint: Ablative Heat-Shield Sizing for a Mars Direct-Entry Capsule: Heat Load, Ablator Mass and Margin Budgets
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Design blueprint derived from the source paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24229950): This paper presents a computed design study of a planetary entry system on a single stated operating principle: a phenolic-impregnated carbon ablator shield prote
content: Design blueprint derived from the source paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24229950): This paper presents a computed design study of a planetary entry system on a single stated operating principle: a phenolic-impregnated carbon ablator shield protects the capsule by sacrificing itself in a controlled way — its resin pyrolyzes, its char layer radiates and insulates, and the mass it loses carries heat away — and the shield is sized directly from the integrated heat load, so the sizing study, not the material, is the design product. The system is a 900 kilogram direct-entry Mars capsule of 3.5 metre diameter entering at 6.10 kilometres per second, with peak heating evaluated at a density of 0.0018 kilograms per cubic metre over a stated heating pulse, sized with a PICA-class ablator of stated effective ablation enthalpy. The design target is a complete shield sizing: peak heating rate, integrated heat load, required ablator areal mass including the structural floor allowance, shield mass and shield mass fraction, each computed and each carrying its margin policy openly. Peak deceleration is 13.1 Earth gravities, peak heating is 179 watts per square centimetre, the heat load is 113 megajoules per square metre, and the thermal protection mass is 114 kilograms, a fraction 0.127 of the entry mass. This work is a computed design study for civilian planetary science, with no targeting or weapon application. Its subject is the safe delivery of scientific payloads through a planetary atmosphere, and its numbers are simulated from stated assumptions rather than measured on hardware. Status: DESIGN BLUEPRINT — SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED — NOT BUILT. All numbers are simulated values from the source paper's computation, deposited with this blueprint as compute.py and results.json. The design is a civilian planetary-science atmospheric entry system and has no targeting or weapon application. AI-use disclosure: Dave, an AI research system, assisted with the computation and drafting under the author's direction; author of record William Alexander Aldred.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
summary: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nit
content: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Development of Halogen‐Free Flame Retardant PLA Filaments for 3D Printing: Role of Aluminum Hypophosphite, Nanoclay, and Structural Porosity
source: Journal of Vinyl and Additive Technology
summary: ABSTRACT In this study, halogen‐free flame‐retardant poly(lactic acid) (PLA) filaments are developed for fused filament fabrication (FFF) by incorporating aluminum hypophosphite (AHP) as the primary additive and nanoclay (NC) as a potential
content: ABSTRACT In this study, halogen‐free flame‐retardant poly(lactic acid) (PLA) filaments are developed for fused filament fabrication (FFF) by incorporating aluminum hypophosphite (AHP) as the primary additive and nanoclay (NC) as a potential adjuvant filler. The effects of AHP and NC contents, as well as the infill density (25%–100%), on thermal stability, combustion behavior, processability, morphology, and mechanical performance are systematically examined. Thermal analysis reveals that increasing the AHP amount reduces the initial degradation temperature while significantly increasing char yield. The peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat evolved (THE) values reduce with increasing AHP loading. AHP enhances limiting oxygen index (LOI) value and enables a V0 rating at high infill densities. The highest LOI value is achieved with the addition of 1 wt% NC; further increases in NC amount reduce the LOI value. The composite containing 5 wt% NC exhibits a deterioration in UL‐94 classification to V‐2 at 75% infill density. Infill density significantly influences time to ignition (TTI), pHRR, and THE values by altering fuel mass. Increased melt flow is observed with AHP incorporation. Mechanical properties decrease with increasing additive loading, with the ternary systems exhibiting the most brittle behavior. Micro‐CT and SEM analysis reveal generally homogeneous particle dispersion with localized micro‐clustering in the presence of NC. Overall, the composite containing 1 wt% NC offers a favorable balance of pHRR suppression and flammability performance, while mechanical penalties and the dependence of UL‐94 classification on infill density remain important design constraints. It enables potential applications in additive manufacturing for lightweight, customized functional parts requiring enhanced fire safety.

title: Flexural Behaviour and Ductility of High-Strength Concrete Beams Reinforced with Hybrid BFRP-Steel Bars
summary: This study investigates the flexural performance of high-strength concrete beams reinforced with hybrid basalt fibre-reinforced polymer (BFRP) and steel bars. Six beams were tested under four-point bending, including four with varying BFRP-
content: This study investigates the flexural performance of high-strength concrete beams reinforced with hybrid basalt fibre-reinforced polymer (BFRP) and steel bars. Six beams were tested under four-point bending, including four with varying BFRP-to-steel ratios and two reference beams reinforced solely with steel and BFRP, respectively. The main variable was the reinforcement proportion. The experimental program evaluated load-bearing capacity, midspan deflection, crack width, and ductility. Compared to the BFRP-only beam, hybrid specimens exhibited up to 16.2% higher ultimate load and 29% lower deflection, while ductility indices ranged from 1.62 to 2.71, depending on reinforcement configuration. Crack width and deflection predictions from ACI 440.1R-15, CSA S806-12, and the Bischoff model were found to overestimate experimental values by 20–35%, highlighting the need for refinement in existing models. Results confirm that hybrid reinforcement effectively enhances strength, deformation capacity, and serviceability, offering a viable approach to improving the ductility and crack control of high-strength concrete members

title: Cost and Environmental Protection Related to Procedure Room Surgery Versus Operating Room Surgery
source: Journal of Hand Surgery Global Online
summary: Purpose Climate change poses a significant public health threat, and the health care sector could contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Operating rooms (ORs) are highly energy-intensive and produce substantial waste, including di
content: Purpose Climate change poses a significant public health threat, and the health care sector could contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Operating rooms (ORs) are highly energy-intensive and produce substantial waste, including disposable products and anesthesia services. This study compares the environmental impact and cost-effectiveness of simple operative procedures like carpal tunnel release, ganglion excision, and trigger finger release performed in outpatient procedure rooms (PRs) versus ORs, hypothesizing that PRs are more sustainable and cost-effective. Methods This observational study was conducted at a level 2 trauma center in Saskatchewan, Canada. Institutional Research Ethics Board approval was obtained. A total of three OR and six PR surgeries performed by a single surgeon were observed. Data on procedural duration, resource utilization, waste generation, and associated direct costs were systematically collected. Carbon emissions in kilograms of CO 2 equivalents (kgCO 2 e) were estimated using standardized emission factors based on the processing of surgical waste and linens, as well as energy consumption from room lights, surgical lights, and central processing. Statistical analysis was conducted using the statistical software SAS 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc). Results A single PR procedure produced 1.05 kgCO 2 e, whereas an OR procedure produced 4.36 kgCO 2 e. OR procedures generated 18 times more surgical waste and used twice as many linens. Financially, a PR procedure costs $376.78, whereas an OR procedure costs $1,004.28. Conclusions Shifting simple operative procedures from ORs to PRs can significantly reduce environmental impact and costs. PR surgeries generated 76% less carbon emissions and 94.5% less surgical waste and were 62.5% less expensive. These findings suggest that outpatient PR settings offer a more sustainable and cost-effective alternative for many simple procedures, contributing to a greener and more economically efficient health care system. Type of study/level of evidence Economic/decision analysis IIb.

title: Enhancing nutrient use efficiency and productivity of field pea (Pisum sativum L.) through dual inoculation of Rhizobium and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi under reduced fertilization
summary: Improving nutrient use efficiency while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers is a major challenge in sustainable agriculture. This study evaluated the effects of single and dual inoculation with Rhizobium leguminosarum and arbuscular
content: Improving nutrient use efficiency while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers is a major challenge in sustainable agriculture. This study evaluated the effects of single and dual inoculation with Rhizobium leguminosarum and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on the growth, nutrient uptake, productivity, and economic returns of field pea (Pisum sativum L.) under reduced nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) fertilization. A field experiment was conducted using a randomized block design with seven treatments and three replications. Dual inoculation significantly improved plant growth, yield attributes, nutrient uptake, and nutrient use efficiency compared with sole fertilization and the control. The combined application of Rhizobium + AMF with 50% of the recommended N and P (treatment T 7) produced the highest grain yield (0.88–0.91 t ha −1), representing approximately an 85% increase over the control and exceeding the yield achieved with the full recommended fertilizer dose. Treatment T 7 also recorded the highest N uptake (18.29–22.34 kg ha −1), P uptake (1.92–2.02 kg ha −1), N use efficiency (∼75%), and P use efficiency (∼53%). Economic analysis showed the greatest net return and benefit–cost ratio with dual inoculation. Overall, dual inoculation sustained field pea productivity while reducing fertilizer inputs by 50% and improving economic returns, indicating its potential as a sustainable nutrient management strategy to reduce fertilizer dependence without compromising yield.

title: Recurrent features of stress response in the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium: intracellular inclusions and vacuoles forming upon UV
summary: The Zygnematophyceae, the closest algal relatives of land plants, many of which are unicellular, must manage environmental stress responses largely cell-autonomously, making them powerful models for dissecting the ancestral cellular toolkit
content: The Zygnematophyceae, the closest algal relatives of land plants, many of which are unicellular, must manage environmental stress responses largely cell-autonomously, making them powerful models for dissecting the ancestral cellular toolkit underlying plant terrestrialisation. In this brief report, we revisit UV-B time-course experiment data on the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium endlicherianum, in which UV-B irradiation triggered a significant accumulation of terminal vacuoles. We re-analysed the corresponding RNA-seq data with a new focus on genes associated with vacuolar biology and lipid metabolism. Within 2 h of UV-B onset, homologs of genes linked to vacuolar functions in land plants were differentially expressed: transcripts of putatively lytic enzymes (a papain-like cysteine protease and two GH38 alpha-mannosidases), of a metal tolerance protein and of two AHK1-like histidine kinases increased, whereas those of the tonoplast H⁺-pyrophosphatase AVP1, the Ca²⁺/H⁺ antiporter CAX5 and the phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate 5-kinase FAB1A decreased. Lipid-related transcripts indicated a shift from membrane lipid biosynthesis towards lipid turnover, including the induction of a SUGAR-DEPENDENT 1-like triacylglycerol lipase. Based on homology, we propose the working hypothesis that UV-B shifts the vacuole from a homeostatic towards a stress-adapted state with altered ion homeostasis and increased lytic capacity. Together with reports of stress-associated vacuoles in other zygnematophytes, our data are consistent with an ancient role of the vacuole in streptophyte stress responses.

title: Rigid–Flexible Interpenetrating Network and Bimodal Alumina Packing Strategy for Thermally Conductive, Mechanically Robust, and Electrically Insulating Adhesives
summary: ABSTRACT In new energy vehicles, the adhesive layers in power battery packs must simultaneously provide strong bonding, mechanical robustness, and efficient heat conduction—properties that are notoriously difficult to integrate into a singl
content: ABSTRACT In new energy vehicles, the adhesive layers in power battery packs must simultaneously provide strong bonding, mechanical robustness, and efficient heat conduction—properties that are notoriously difficult to integrate into a single material. In this work, a rigid‐flexible interpenetrating network (IPN) was constructed by blending silane‐terminated polyether (STPE) with epoxy (EP) at optimized mass ratios. The optimal SEA 1.6 formulation (mass ratio of STPE to EP = 1.6) exhibited a tensile strength of 13.22 MPa, an elongation at break of 660.73%, and a lap‐shear strength of 9.05 MPa, demonstrating a well‐balanced combination of mechanical robustness, ductility, and strong adhesion. Binary‐sized Al 2 O 3 fillers (45 and 5 μm) were further incorporated at an optimal coarse‐to‐fine mass ratio of 4:1 to construct densely packed thermal conduction pathways. At a total filler loading of 50 wt.%, the Al 2 O 3 /SEA 1.6 thermally conductive structural adhesive delivered a thermal conductivity of 0.79 W·m −1 ·K −1 , while retaining a lap‐shear strength of 9.47 MPa, an elongation at break of 228.77%, volume resistivity of 2.92 × 10 13 Ω·cm and breakdown strength of 19.16 kV/mm. Further increasing the loading to 70 wt.% boosted the thermal conductivity to 1.07 W·m −1 ·K −1 , a 494% enhancement over neat SEA 1.6 (0.18 W·m −1 ·K −1 ). By virtue of their moderate thermal conductivity, high bond strength, and good mechanical compliance, the fabricated thermally conductive structural adhesives emerge as attractive candidates for new energy vehicle and electronic applications.

title: Geological and fluid inclusion characteristics of quartz carbonate veins in the Tamar area of the North Singhbhum Mobile Belt, Eastern India
summary: Abstract The Tamar area of the western North Singhbhum Mobile Belt (NSMB) contains quartz and quartz carbonate veins hosted mainly by quartzite, carbonaceous phyllite, mica schist and amphibolite. This study documents the lithological and s
content: Abstract The Tamar area of the western North Singhbhum Mobile Belt (NSMB) contains quartz and quartz carbonate veins hosted mainly by quartzite, carbonaceous phyllite, mica schist and amphibolite. This study documents the lithological and structural setting of the vein system and evaluates its hydrothermal alteration and fluid characteristics using field observations, petrography, fluid inclusion microthermometry and Raman spectroscopy. Quartz carbonate veins are spatially associated with shear zones, fold hinges, lithological contacts and fracture intersections, but the present dataset does not by itself demonstrate that each structure genetically controlled gold deposition. The principal alteration assemblages are silicification, sericitization, chloritization, carbonatization and sulfide development. Pyrite, arsenopyrite and chalcopyrite are the principal opaque minerals documented in the investigated samples. Yellow reflective grains reported in some specimens as gold were not independently confirmed by SEM EDS or EPMA in the present dataset and are therefore treated as provisional gold identifications. Fluid inclusions include aqueous, carbonic and aqueous-carbonic populations. Corrected microthermometric treatment indicates very low NaCl equivalent salinity for the aqueous population, while salinity is not assigned to carbonic-bearing inclusions where clathrate effects were not independently constrained. Raman spectra indicate CO 2 and CH 4 and a broad H 2 O band. A weak feature in a single spectrum that may be attributable to H 2 S is treated only as a tentative assignment and is not used as evidence for the composition of the mineralising fluid. The available observations are compatible with a deformation-related hydrothermal system and with several characteristics commonly observed in orogenic gold systems; however, the timing of mineralisation, fluid provenance and deposit classification remain incompletely constrained.

title: Tackling urban heat: equity, resilience, and innovative finance
summary: Abstract Extreme urban heat, amplified by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, is a structural and recurring risk embedded within contemporary urban systems. Urban dwellers, especially those in low-income settings, outdoor workers, pregnant
content: Abstract Extreme urban heat, amplified by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, is a structural and recurring risk embedded within contemporary urban systems. Urban dwellers, especially those in low-income settings, outdoor workers, pregnant women, and other vulnerable groups, are disproportionately exposed to its health, economic, and social harms. These inequalities are rooted in historical land-use decisions, housing precarity, and chronic underinvestment in public infrastructure. Yet even where warning systems exist, policy, planning, finance, and data systems still often treat heat as a sporadic emergency rather than a predictable, institutionalized risk. In this commentary, we argue for reframing heat resilience through four interlinked and mutually reinforcing dimensions: governance, equity, open and interoperable data, and innovative finance that scales beyond pilots. These four dimensions are interdependent: governance without finance remains aspirational, finance without equity risks misallocation, and data without institutional uptake fails to translate evidence into action. Drawing on recent research, practitioner handbooks, and global initiatives, we propose recommendations to guide cities and governments: institutionalizing heat risk, integrating UHI mitigation into national cooling policies, leveraging blended finance, embedding community participation, and promoting global knowledge-sharing. Unless extreme heat is managed as a recurring and predictable element of urban life akin to floods and earthquakes in existing risk frameworks, cities risk failing those most vulnerable, undermining both public health and social justice.

title: Education on the Dangers of PM2.5 and Best Practices for Mask-Wearing among Students at SD Inpres BTN IKIP I Makassar
summary: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an air pollution issue that poses risks to respiratory health, including among school-aged children. Education regarding the dangers of PM2.5 and personal protective measures is essential for f
content: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is an air pollution issue that poses risks to respiratory health, including among school-aged children. Education regarding the dangers of PM2.5 and personal protective measures is essential for fostering environmental health awareness from an early age. This community service initiative aimed to provide students at SD Inpres BTN IKIP I Makassar with an understanding of the hazards of PM2.5 and the proper use of face masks. The implementation method included the presentation of educational material using visual aids, a demonstration of the steps for putting on and removing a mask, and an interactive quiz. The outcomes of the activity demonstrated that the education covered an introduction to PM2.5, sources of pollution, health impacts, personal protection measures—incorporating the "3L" concept—and the practical application of wearing a mask. This initiative served as an environmental health learning tool that combined information with hands-on practice. Similar educational efforts should be conducted on an ongoing basis, supported by more structured evaluation

title: An optimized multi objective simulated annealing approach for efficient drone based product delivery
summary: Abstract Drone technology has revolutionized e-commerce and logistics by enabling cost-effective product delivery and increased revenue. Optimizing drone scheduling and routing is challenging as delivery locations increase and the solution
content: Abstract Drone technology has revolutionized e-commerce and logistics by enabling cost-effective product delivery and increased revenue. Optimizing drone scheduling and routing is challenging as delivery locations increase and the solution space expands. The primary objective is to jointly optimize delivery scheduling and routing by proposing a Multi-Objective Simulated Annealing (MO-SA) approach that satisfies payload capacity and battery life constraints while using customer priority and delivery deadlines as urgency-based sequencing criteria. This research introduces a new scheduling and routing method by modifying a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm to optimize delivery sequences and routes. The method combines local search with the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm to generate initial neighbor sequences, refined by the SA process using Boltzmann distribution for acceptance probabilities. Across three 100-customer benchmark instances, MO-SA reduced mean delivery distance by 28.14–54.85% relative to the four evaluated baselines, with a mean runtime of 6.16 seconds on R101. Further experiments demonstrate reduced travel distances under weight constraints, a higher number of deliveries within the assumed battery threshold than the compared methods, and priority-based sequencing. A post-hoc graph-theoretic check confirms no customer duplication, consistent with Hamiltonian and Eulerian properties at the customer-sequence level. Overall, the proposed approach offers a constraint-aware solution with promising results at the tested problem scale, indicating potential for last-mile drone delivery applications pending explicit arrival-time modeling, scalability, and real-world validation.

title: Concentration variations and risk characteristics of volatile organic compounds and nitrochlorobenzenes in groundwater at a retired pesticide site under risk control
summary: Abstract Retired pesticide sites are an important category of contaminated land, and groundwater pollution at these sites remains a major environmental concern. Understanding groundwater pollution characteristics and the effectiveness of co
content: Abstract Retired pesticide sites are an important category of contaminated land, and groundwater pollution at these sites remains a major environmental concern. Understanding groundwater pollution characteristics and the effectiveness of containment measures is essential for site management and safe reuse. This study investigated a retired pesticide site under risk control in Jiangsu Province, China to characterize the spatio-temporal distribution patterns, source relationships, and ecological and human health risks of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and nitrochlorobenzenes (NCBs) in groundwater from 2019 to 2021. The results showed that chlorobenzene (CB) and NCBs were the dominant pollutants. Spatial distribution of pollutants exhibited marked heterogeneity, with two distinct contamination hotspots identified. Historical storage and handling facilities in the southern part of the site suggest potential localized sources of contamination. Time-series monitoring showed that groundwater pollutant concentrations fluctuated but declined overall after containment implementation. In particular, the mean concentration of ΣNCBs decreased sharply from 6846 μg/L in 2019 to 1025 μg/L in 2020, with a slight rebound to 1109 μg/L in 2021, indicating that the containment measures effectively reduced pollutant migration and the overall contamination level. Risk assessment results indicated that the target compounds posed high ecological (RQ T range: 140 ~ 219) and human health risks under conservative generic exposure scenarios, with CR T ranging from 2.80 × 10 –5 to 1.77 × 10 –1 and HQ T ranging from 5.15 × 10 –1 to 5.08 × 10 3 (i.e., 0.515 ~ 5080). However, site-specific actual risk evaluation under industrial land use showed that the groundwater risk outside the controlled zone was generally acceptable. These findings provide a scientific basis for evaluating risk-control effectiveness, supporting dynamic management, and informing safe land-reuse decisions for pesticide-contaminated sites.

title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
summary: Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring-opening transformations via reductive single-electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo-induced
content: Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring-opening transformations via reductive single-electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo-induced copper-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole-cored photocatalyst (Ph-BCBZ) and a hydrogen-bond-donor-coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph-BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition-metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen-bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β-scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ-amino and γ-keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral f-PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET-induced radical generation and outer-sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)-alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

title: Nano‐Scaffolding of Fibrous Skeletons for High‐Strength Icephobic Composites Integrating Wave‐Transparent Functionalization
summary: ABSTRACT The complex operating environments in aerospace engineering pose increasing demands for advanced composites with coupled icephobic‐electromagnetic‐mechanical performance. However, existing materials fail to integrate effective icep
content: ABSTRACT The complex operating environments in aerospace engineering pose increasing demands for advanced composites with coupled icephobic‐electromagnetic‐mechanical performance. However, existing materials fail to integrate effective icephobicity, high electromagnetic wave transmission, and practical mechanical strength. To solve the above challenge, a novel multifunctional composite design strategy is developed based on the proposal of nano‐scaffolding of fibrous skeletons (NSFS). By incorporating multiscale wave‐transparent fibers and icephobic polymer matrix, a high‐strength icephobic composite with electromagnetic wave transparency is engineered. The nano‐scaffolding of fibrous skeletons prompts significant mechanical enhancement, demonstrating a tensile strength reaching 30 MPa, which corresponds to an approximate 72% increase compared to microfiber‐only composites. Simultaneously, the multiscale modulus mismatch among microfibers, nanofibers, and polymer matrix induces enhanced interfacial elastic instability, enabling high efficiency in reducing the ice adhesion strength. Finite element simulations reveal the crucial role of the micro/nano multiscale structure in prompting higher stress concentration at the ice/solid interface and regulating the de‐icing efficiency. Furthermore, the materials retain excellent wave transparency, with the transmission efficiency in the X‐band remaining above 98%. The proposed NSFS strategy effectively breaks the bottleneck among mechanical properties, icephobic performance, and wave transparency of traditional materials, providing a novel design strategy for multifunctional composites.

title: HSSW Salinity Potentially Modulated by Summertime Preconditioning in Terra Nova Bay Polynya
summary: Abstract High Salinity Shelf Water (HSSW) in Terra Nova Bay, a key constituent of Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW), freshened from 1959 to 2014 before reversing in 2015. Variations in HSSW salinity influence AABW properties, global ocean heat
content: Abstract High Salinity Shelf Water (HSSW) in Terra Nova Bay, a key constituent of Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW), freshened from 1959 to 2014 before reversing in 2015. Variations in HSSW salinity influence AABW properties, global ocean heat and oxygen distribution. Yet, observations informing salinity trends are primarily collected during austral summer, months after HSSW is formed by wintertime brine rejection in Antarctic polynyas. We find that wintertime brine rejection only partly explains summertime HSSW salinity. Model simulations suggest that surface salinity in the preceding winter and HSSW residence time contribute to summertime salinity variability, while mooring and sea‐ice observations provide some evidence consistent with these mechanisms. This study highlights the importance of year‐round observations for improving our understanding of HSSW variability, temporal lags, and the future of AABW.

title: Influence of Hollow Glass Microspheres (HGM) on Thermo-Mechanical Properties of Composite Foam Panels
source: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
summary: Abstract The appropriateness of sandwich composite panels reinforced with glass fibre facesheets and hollow glass microsphere (HGM) foam cores for lightweight structural applications was assessed by experimentally and numerically examining
content: Abstract The appropriateness of sandwich composite panels reinforced with glass fibre facesheets and hollow glass microsphere (HGM) foam cores for lightweight structural applications was assessed by experimentally and numerically examining their mechanical and thermal characteristics. This paper investigates both thermo-mechanical properties of HGM-filled sandwich composite foam panels in a single study. This provides a more comprehensive assessment for structural applications. This combination is particularly relevant for lightweight construction and transportation applications. The sandwich structure’s stiffness and interfacial behaviour were considerably altered by the addition of HGMs to the foam core, improving its resistance to bending loads. The improved flexural strength and modulus are attributed to the high stiffness of the glass fibres in the facesheets, efficient stress transmission at the core–facesheet interface, and the microstructural capacity of HGMs to control core deformation during flexure of the panel which has no HGMs. There was 63.31, 22.54 and 32.26% improvement in tensile strength, flexural and impact strength Additionally, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) verified that the addition of HGMs enhanced the sandwich composites’ thermal stability by 67.50% because of the microspheres’ innate thermal resistance and inertness. Overall, sandwich panels containing HGM foam cores and glass fibre facesheets demonstrate superior bending resistance, reduced weight, and improved thermal stability, making them promising candidates for aerospace, marine, and high-performance engineering applications where stiffness-to-weight and thermal resistance are critical.

title: Local Configurational Metastability Accelerates Oxygen Exchange in High‐Entropy Perovskites
summary: ABSTRACT High‐entropy electrocatalysts are nominally randomized, but local atomic ordering can spontaneously emerge and diminish the actual high‐entropy effect. How this localized ordering governs reaction kinetics remains poorly understood
content: ABSTRACT High‐entropy electrocatalysts are nominally randomized, but local atomic ordering can spontaneously emerge and diminish the actual high‐entropy effect. How this localized ordering governs reaction kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we manipulate two local configurational states within a high‐entropy perovskite cobaltate: a kinetically trapped metastable state (MS) with a pseudo‐cubic framework and highly randomized local arrangement, and an equilibrium‐like state (ES) with enhanced lattice relaxation and cation/oxygen‐sublattice ordering. Multiscale structural analyses reveal that ES develops stronger medium‐range correlations, symmetry‐lowered R3c‐like octahedral distortions, heterogeneous local strain, and a more than twofold increase in average B‐site off‐centering displacement, together with a more electron‐deficient Co environment and a less oxygen‐vacancy‐rich sublattice. Remarkably, operando near‐ambient‐pressure X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that MS exhibits approximately 5‐ to 7.5‐fold higher oxygen‐exchange kinetics than ES under a range of chemical and electrochemical perturbations. Density functional theory calculations show that subsurface‐to‐surface oxygen migration is more favorable in MS, which has a lower forward barrier and a smaller energy increase between the initial and final states. In contrast, the lower reverse barrier in ES (0.850 vs 1.135 eV) favors the return of migrated oxygen to the subsurface, resulting in stronger oxygen retrapping and slower oxygen exchange.

title: Spiro-OMeTAD-Inspired Molecular Design: Electron Tunneling Meets Halogen Bonding for Robust Buried Interfaces
summary: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs) are limited by fragile buried interfaces and uncontrolled nucleation. These get exacerbated when conventional hole-transport materials such as spiro-OMeTAD are used with dopants, especially
content: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs) are limited by fragile buried interfaces and uncontrolled nucleation. These get exacerbated when conventional hole-transport materials such as spiro-OMeTAD are used with dopants, especially in inverted p–i–n devices, leading to accelerated ion migration and poor stability. To overcome these limitations, we introduce BDTP-4D, a spiro-OMeTAD-inspired bis-dithienopyrrole molecule designed to mimic its merits while avoiding dopant-induced instability. Applied as a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) atop NiOx, BDTP-4D was co-sensitized with triphenylamine derivatives possessing targeted functionalities (–Br, –SMe, –OMe), which modulated hole-transport-layer surface energy and directed perovskite nucleation and crystallization. This yielded pinhole-free films with large, homogeneous grains atop the co-sensitized electrodes. Mechanistic analysis revealed complementary buried-interfacial processes: NiOx–Br electronic coupling and halogen-bonding between Br and Sn perovskite (BDTP:Br), and sulfur-mediated passivation (BDTP:SMe). This mixed-SAM strategy reproduces the benefits of doped spiro-OMeTAD while eliminating interfacial instability, thereby defining a generalizable molecular design principle for robust buried interfaces across emerging photovoltaics.

title: Steering the Selectivity of Copper Nanoparticles through Imidazole and Benzimidazole Ligands in Coordination Polymers for CO2 Electroreduction
summary: Abstract Controlling catalyst reconstruction and product selectivity remains a major challenge for copper-based electrocatalysts during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Herein, we demonstrate a ligand-controlled and polym
content: Abstract Controlling catalyst reconstruction and product selectivity remains a major challenge for copper-based electrocatalysts during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Herein, we demonstrate a ligand-controlled and polymer-mediated strategy to regulate the catalytic behavior of precursor-derived copper coordination polymers through their coordination environment. Two copper-imidazole coordination polymers, [Cu(IMN)2]n and [Cu(BiZ)2]n, were synthesized and investigated as CO2RR electrocatalysts. Structural characterization confirmed the coordination of Cu2+ centers with imidazole-based ligands and the formation of well-defined coordination frameworks. Online electrochemical mass spectrometry combined with gas chromatography revealed distinct product distributions for the precursor-derived [Cu(IMN)2]n and [Cu(BiZ)2]n electrocatalysts. The [Cu(IMN)2]n-derived catalyst exhibited Faradaic efficiencies of 13.06% for CO at –0.9 V, 39.87% for CH4 at –1.2 V, and 8.54% for C2H4 at –1.1 V vs RHE, whereas the [Cu(BiZ)2]n-derived catalyst achieved 28.43, 22.25, and 31.98%, respectively. Electrochemical polarization generated Cu-derived nanoparticles with average diameters of 27.0 ± 2.6 nm for [Cu(IMN)2]n and 37.0 ± 4.1 nm for [Cu(BiZ)2]n, indicating that the ligand environment influences catalyst nanostructure and product selectivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) analyses further indicated electrochemical reconstruction toward reduced Cu-derived domains, while the initially present nitrogen-containing species may have contributed to nanoparticle stabilization and organization during reconstruction. The electrocatalytic performance was further validated in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzers under zero-gap conditions, where the selectivity trends observed in H-type cells were reproduced. The [Cu(BiZ)2]n-modified PTFE/C electrode achieved ∼42% Faradaic efficiency for C2H4 at 20–40 mA cm–2, compared with ∼35% for bare PTFE/Cu, whereas [Cu(IMN)2]n-modified PTFE/C increased CH4 selectivity from ∼5 to ∼15% at higher current densities. Together, these findings demonstrate that the precursor coordination environment influences copper reconstruction, Cu-derived nanostructure, and CO2RR product selectivity, while polymer-mediated interfacial modulation enables control of catalyst evolution under operating conditions. This coupled control of ligand-directed reconstruction and interfacial environment provides complementary design principles for selective Cu-based CO2RR.

title: Effect of oven drying duration on the structural and functional properties of green synthesized NiO and Co3O4 nanomaterials for oxygen evolution electrocatalysis and antibacterial applications
summary: Abstract Tailored NiO and Co 3 O 4 nanomaterials were successfully synthesized via a green solution combustion method using citric acid and dextrose as environmentally benign fuels. The influence of oven-drying duration on the structural, m
content: Abstract Tailored NiO and Co 3 O 4 nanomaterials were successfully synthesized via a green solution combustion method using citric acid and dextrose as environmentally benign fuels. The influence of oven-drying duration on the structural, morphological, electrochemical, and antibacterial properties was systematically investigated to establish the structure–property relationship. Among all the synthesized samples, Co-CA (16 h) exhibited the most favorable characteristics, including high crystallinity, a defect-rich porous morphology, and a high BET surface area and an accessible porous morphology, which collectively contributed to its superior oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance. Specifically, Co-CA (16 h) delivered a low overpotential of 0.463 V at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻ 2 , a Tafel slope of 210.9 mV dec⁻ 1 , and the lowest solution resistance of 1.681 Ω · cm 2 , together with excellent electrochemical stability during continuous cycling. In addition to its electrocatalytic performance, Co-CA (16 h) demonstrated significant antibacterial activity, producing inhibition zones of 12 ± 0.6 mm against Escherichia coli , 13 ± 0.5 mm against Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and 20 ± 0.7 mm against Staphylococcus aureus at a catalyst concentration of 20 µg, outperforming the corresponding Ni-CA and Co-Dex samples. The electrochemical energy-storage measurements are included only as supplementary information to provide additional insight into the electrochemical behavior of the synthesized materials and are not intended as the primary focus of this study. Overall, the present work demonstrates that the green-synthesized Co-CA (16 h) nanomaterial is a promising OER electrocatalyst with the added advantage of antibacterial activity, highlighting its potential for sustainable energy and environmental applications.

title: LED light specifications to reduce marine pollution, mitigate bycatch and increase target catch in pelagic longline fisheries
summary: Pelagic longline fisheries use millions of single-use chemical lightsticks each year. These contribute to plastic and toxic pollution and increase at-risk bycatch. We explored reusable light-emitting diode and phosphorescent lights as poten
content: Pelagic longline fisheries use millions of single-use chemical lightsticks each year. These contribute to plastic and toxic pollution and increase at-risk bycatch. We explored reusable light-emitting diode and phosphorescent lights as potential replacements. We evaluated candidate lights’ potential effects on economic viability, practicality, crew safety and at-risk bycatch rates. We measured light properties that are potentially informative predictors of catch rates of target and at-risk bycatch species, including peak wavelengths (λmax), wavelength range, flicker rate, flicker duration, light level (total radiant power and at λmax), diminution and directionality. We compiled and synthesized the sensitivities of species captured in longline fisheries to light spectral, temporal and intensity characteristics, which informed defining criteria predicted to increase commercial species’ and reduce at-risk bycatch species’ catch rates. For example, to include peak spectral sensitivities of pelagic longline target species while avoiding longer wavelength peak spectral sensitivities of marine turtles, pelagic sharks and possibly other marine megafauna visual predators, we shortlisted lights with λmax between 400-480 nm (violet to blue to humans) and with low or no radiant power at longer wavelengths. We assessed apparent (submerged) weight and activation mechanism, which are attributes that might affect seabird bycatch. Following demonstrations of short-listed lights in three longline fisheries, overall, captains preferred smaller and dimmer LED models, preferred water- or pressure-activation over manual activation, and were ambivalent on preferences for flickering versus constant lights. The study identified characteristics of lights that hold high promise for meeting objectives for commercial viability, bycatch mitigation, and reducing marine pollution.

title: Tri-level hybrid electric bus scheduling under time-of-use tariffs for cost-effective public transportation
summary: Abstract The deployment of electric buses requires coordinated fleet scheduling and charging management to maintain passenger services while controlling infrastructure and electricity costs. This study proposes a Tri-Level Hybrid Electric B
content: Abstract The deployment of electric buses requires coordinated fleet scheduling and charging management to maintain passenger services while controlling infrastructure and electricity costs. This study proposes a Tri-Level Hybrid Electric Bus Scheduling under Time-of-Use tariffs (TLH-EBS-TOU) framework that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for global exploration, Rule-Based Scoring Large Neighborhood Search (RBS-LNS) for schedule restructuring, and Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) for neighbourhood repair. A TOU-aware charging-time selection procedure coordinates charging expenditure with battery-energy requirements, compatible-charger availability, deadheading, and prescribed passenger departures. The framework is evaluated on a Madurai transportation network comprising 810 scheduled passenger trips per day and compared with standalone MILP, PSO, and RBS-LNS. The reported baseline solution uses 149 electric buses and 15 chargers, with an annualized total cost of ₹30.86 crore, representing a 4.85% reduction relative to standalone PSO. Bus capital, charger capital, electricity, and deadheading costs decrease by 5.77%, 4.81%, 3.54%, and 3.70%, respectively. Under the modelled conditions 48.00% of the required 37,885kWh per day charging capacity is allocated to the most economical time of day to charge. The results of these tests illustrate the possibilities of coordinated hybrid scheduling and tariff-aware charging for achieving operating economy while maintaining the prescribed passenger services.

title: Innovative design of a power transmission system for a multi-function machine tool
summary: This study presents the design, analysis, and validation of a compact power transmission system for a multifunctional tabletop CNC machine capable of performing turning, drilling, and milling operations using a single motor. Three distinct
content: This study presents the design, analysis, and validation of a compact power transmission system for a multifunctional tabletop CNC machine capable of performing turning, drilling, and milling operations using a single motor. Three distinct gear cases are used in this study and are clearly distinguished throughout: the proposed transmission design (pinion 18 teeth/gear 51 teeth, module 6 mm), a replicated reference case used solely to benchmark the contact-stress methodology (“Case B”: 20 teeth/20 teeth, module 4 mm), and a design-sizing calculation (23/92 teeth, module 3 mm) used to determine the module and face width of the actual gear train. Spur gear design for the proposed transmission was carried out using AGMA and Lewis equations and validated through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in ANSYS. The analytical bending stress of the pinion was 31.38 MPa, closely matching the FEA result of 31.11 MPa, while the gear exhibited analytical and FEA stresses of 23.51 MPa and 21.14 MPa, respectively.
