At a given accretion luminosity, molecular line luminosities are systematically lower in USco than in young disks, and the scaling relations with accretion luminosity differ between the two populations. Moreover, we find that about one-half of the older disks, preferentially the millimeter-faint and likely more compact disks, have observable mass ratios of C- to O-bearing molecules that are higher than the maximum values in the young sample. These results point to reduced inner-disk molecular gas masses, cooler emitting layers, and higher inner gas C/O ratios in older disks, the latter being consistent with pebble drift. Taken together, our findings provide evidence for chemical evolution of inner-disk gas from young to older systems, with important implications for the accretion of primordial planetary atmospheres.

title: Impact of repeated temperature cycling on the low-concentration CO2 adsorption capacity of grafted silica-amine
summary: The use of short-chain ethyleneimines (SCEI) and polyethyleneimines (PEI) as CO 2 sorbents has been extensively studied as a potential means of capturing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Previous work on such sorbents has focuse
content: The use of short-chain ethyleneimines (SCEI) and polyethyleneimines (PEI) as CO 2 sorbents has been extensively studied as a potential means of capturing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Previous work on such sorbents has focused on concentrated sources of CO 2 , such as found in combustion exhaust streams, as well as 400 μLL − 1 CO 2 concentrations more typical of the atmosphere. In this study, we examine changes in the adsorption properties and physical, chemical, and morphological changes induced in grafted SCEI, specifically diethyleneimine and triethyleneimine chains grafted onto two high surface- area silica supports, MCM-41 and SBA-15, when subjected to large numbers of thermal cycles in dry, CO 2 -free air. Emphasis is placed on the adsorption at 400 μLL − 1 CO 2 at 25 ◦C to study the potential suitability of similar grafted imine-containing systems for use as direct air capture (DAC) sorbents. For comparison, we also examine changes in the adsorption capacity at CO 2 concentrations of 50,000 μLL −1 , which are more typical of combustion exhaust. Notably, the low-concentration capacity is found to generally decrease faster than the capacity at the higher concentration with increased thermal cycling. All sorbents were found to decrease in adsorption capacity after a large number of cycles; however, DAS-derived sorbents were in general more robust. Moreover, the decrease in the CO 2 adsorption capacity at 25 ◦C before and after thermal cycling was found to vary significantly with the adsorptive concentration.

title: Learning from SILCS FragMaps: Combining Physics-Based Energies with Artificial Intelligence for Rapid Drug Permeability Prediction
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Abstract Prediction of drug passive permeability represents an important component of rational drug design, requiring continued development of methods to address this problem. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have long been shown to be
content: Abstract Prediction of drug passive permeability represents an important component of rational drug design, requiring continued development of methods to address this problem. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have long been shown to be of utility for prediction of compound permeability, though they are limited by the range of chemical space in the data sets used in the training of the models. To address this, in the present study, the site identification of ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) methodology is used to calculate free energy profiles for compounds across 3 model lipid bilayers: a POPC–cholesterol bilayer, a bilayer model mimicking parallel artificial membrane permeability assay (PAMPA) experiments, and a bilayer modeling the blood–brain barrier. We present a rapid workflow generating around 15,000 such profiles that accounts for the passive permeation of more than 2500 unique ligands for 3 different membranes. The free energy profiles, which account for all accessible protonation states of the compounds, are then used as features in a collection of AI models. As the physics-based free energy profiles are calculated based on the functional group types in the compounds combined with the SILCS FragMaps calculated for the bilayers, their use potentially improves model transferability by overcoming the limitation of the applicability of the AI models to the chemical space included in the training set, assuming the SILCS-based energies are representative of barriers to compound permeabilities. The resulting models are shown to be almost comparable with available passive permeability models reported in the literature while additionally offering energetic information about the contribution of functional groups to the permeation barriers that may be used for rational compound optimization. Limitations in the cell-based training data, including the presence of drug transporters, are discussed.

title: The antimicrobial potential of Exocarpos cupressiformis Labill. (Santalaceae): a bioassay-guided screening and fractionation of Australia’s ethnobotanically significant flora
summary: Australia’s First Peoples medicine practices were suppressed after colonisation, leading to their decline in use. The tree genus Exocarpos (ballarts) was used widely as a curative (styptic, poultice and astringent) and is still used in smok
content: Australia’s First Peoples medicine practices were suppressed after colonisation, leading to their decline in use. The tree genus Exocarpos (ballarts) was used widely as a curative (styptic, poultice and astringent) and is still used in smoking ceremonies for purification. The current study aims to use a bioassay-guided screening approach to evaluate 46 plant taxa of ethnobotanical interest and provide a candidate for follow up fractionation; use bioassay guided fractionation to purify the active compound; and elucidate the identity and measure the antimicrobial potential of the active component. Disc Diffusion Assays guided screening and fractionation, where 31 of 46 taxa demonstrated some antimicrobial activity. Exocarpos cupressiformis Labill. (cherry ballart) showed a particular propensity for activity and was chosen for further fractionation. TLC-bioautography was then used to inform column chromatography to purify the antimicrobial fraction. QQQ-MS was used in scan and product ion mode with NMR (1H, 13C, HMBC, HSQC, COSY, NOESY) to fully assign structure. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were measured by an agar dilution method. Ultimately, aromadendrin-(1→7)-α-L-rhamnopyranoside, a known antimicrobial flavonoid, was a key component responsible for the activity of the extract and was measured to have a MIC of 32 mg L–1 (Streptococcus pyogenes) and 64 mg L–1 (Streptococcus dysgalactiae). This provides a mechanism by which some of the medicinal uses of E. cupressiformis by Australian First Peoples can be explained.

title: Distributed curvature and spinorial holonomy in Yukawa-regularized disclinations: a finite-core model for graphene-like Dirac systems
summary: Abstract Conical geometries provide the standard description of disclinations, but they concentrate the curvature at a singular apex. We introduce a Yukawa-type regularization that replaces the apex singularity by a finite core with an inte
content: Abstract Conical geometries provide the standard description of disclinations, but they concentrate the curvature at a singular apex. We introduce a Yukawa-type regularization that replaces the apex singularity by a finite core with an integrable, logarithmically peaked curvature distribution, while preserving the asymptotic conical geometry and its deficit angle. The metric is continuous and locally Euclidean at the origin, although the Ricci scalar diverges logarithmically there. Exact expressions are obtained for the conformal factor, the curvature, and the curvature enclosed by a circle of radius $$\rho $$ ρ , which is scale dependent and reaches the topological value only asymptotically. The corresponding vector and spinorial holonomies are derived from the spin connection. For massless Dirac quasiparticles in a single valley, we show that the spin-connection term can be removed from the radial equations by a rescaling, so that the core acts only through the conformal factor, and that the far-field problem reproduces the standard Dirac equation on a cone. The model describes the geometric part of the disclination problem in graphene-like systems and does not include the valley-mixing gauge holonomy.

title: Dynamic Metal–Semiconductor Electrical Interfaces in Model Cu|ZnO Hydrogenation Catalyst Structures
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts are commonly used for methanol synthesis; yet, the chemical state of the Cu|ZnO interface remains debated. Recent studies have suggested that interfacial fields and junction effects could explain observed shi
content: Abstract Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts are commonly used for methanol synthesis; yet, the chemical state of the Cu|ZnO interface remains debated. Recent studies have suggested that interfacial fields and junction effects could explain observed shifts in binding energies of intermediates (e.g., CO2δ− and HCOO−) involved in the reduction of CO2 to methanol on Cu|ZnO. In this study, we probe Cu|ZnO interfacial chemistry by measuring junction electrical characteristics under N2, CO2, and H2 gas mixtures from 50 to 250 °C and up to 10 bar. The pristine interface behaves as a nonideal rectifying Schottky diode, and H2 exposure increases n-type donor density in the ZnO and lowers Schottky-barrier height, with full transition to an ohmic junction. These observations imply the electrostatic potential gradient at the putative active-catalyst interface could change under reaction conditions, depending on the precise composition of the oxide phase. H-doping of ZnO is reversed in a N2 or CO2 stream at 200 °C without any O2, inconsistent with proposed Cu–Zn alloying or oxygen-vacancy formation mechanisms suggested in studies of methanol synthesis on Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts, and instead suggests reversible hydrogen doping of ZnO. The addition of CO2 reduces the rate of H doping into ZnO, while water addition strongly suppresses it. The time scale for the H-doping of Cu|ZnO devices by H2 is much longer than that estimated for H diffusion in bulk ZnO, suggesting that H2 dissociation and/or H insertion into ZnO are the elementary steps governing the rate of H doping of the ZnO. Junction electrical measurements can thus inform how electro-active interfaces invoked in catalysis evolve under reaction conditions.

title: High‐Throughput DNA Sequence Space Exploration for Carbon Nanotube Biosensor Design
summary: ABSTRACT Fluorescent single‐walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) can be non‐covalently functionalized with biopolymers such as DNA to create biosensors. Noncovalent functionalization promises a vast design space, but synthesis is limited by low
content: ABSTRACT Fluorescent single‐walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) can be non‐covalently functionalized with biopolymers such as DNA to create biosensors. Noncovalent functionalization promises a vast design space, but synthesis is limited by low‐throughput dispersion steps. Here, we present a high‐throughput SWCNT‐based platform that utilizes covalent DNA‐anchor chemistry to recruit single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) recognition motifs via hybridization. The approach circumvents low‐throughput processing steps such as sonication or centrifugation. By integrating automated liquid handling and spectroscopy, we bypass traditional fabrication bottlenecks and synthesize 180 unique sensors and test 540 analyte/sensor conditions in less than three days. This accelerated workflow generates large datasets that are combined with an iterative machine learning (ML) pipeline. We demonstrate the versatility of this approach by evolving sensors with enhanced sensitivity for the neurotransmitter dopamine over common interfering molecules such as ascorbic acid in complex media. Through iterative rounds of ML‐driven prediction and synthesis, we establish a scalable framework for rapid synthesis of functional nanosensors and increase the sensitivity for dopamine in up to 89 % of the evolved sensors. This strategy bridges the gap between the vast DNA sequence space and the generation of sensor variants, offering a scalable path to next‐generation sensors.

title: Temporally Distinguishing Photocatalytic Dynamics
summary: Abstract Light can induce both photothermal and nonthermal catalytic activity in plasmonic nanoparticles, but the extent, timescale, and efficacy of these two mechanisms remain unresolved. Here, we introduce pump–pump photocatalysis, an ada
content: Abstract Light can induce both photothermal and nonthermal catalytic activity in plasmonic nanoparticles, but the extent, timescale, and efficacy of these two mechanisms remain unresolved. Here, we introduce pump–pump photocatalysis, an adaptation of ultrafast excitation correlation spectroscopy in which incident laser pulses are split into two spatially and energetically equivalent pulses separated by a variable time delay. For a given reaction and catalyst, time-sensitive nonlinear enhancements in photocatalytic activity may be distinguished from time-insensitive responses as a function of time delay, pulse power, excitation wavelength, applied temperature, reactant pressure, and pulse asymmetry. In this way, the timescales of photothermal and nonthermal activity of any photocatalyst may be monitored on sub-picosecond to nanosecond timescales, and the conditions for optimal chemical reactivity may be discovered. To illustrate this technique, we perform ultrafast measurements of the ammonia decomposition reaction using a Cu–Ru antenna-reactor photocatalyst. Photothermal contributions exhibit little sensitivity to pulse delay, while nonthermal contributions are most apparent at low excitation intensity, moderate temperatures, and sub-nanosecond timescales. Here, nonlinear, nonthermal mechanisms enhance H2 production by a factor of up to eleven compared to when pulses overlap. This technique may be used to provide insightful in operando diagnostics and control of any photocatalyst for any chemical reaction while revealing the optimal distribution of light to maximize photocatalytic activity.

title: Chiral discrimination and mechanistic study of enantiomers R-1,1′-Bi-2-naphthol and S-1,1′-Bi-2-naphthol in Briggs–Rauscher oscillatory chemical system
summary: Abstract A novel method for the qualitative discrimination of the axial enantiomers R-1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (R-BINOL) and S-1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (S-BINOL) was developed using the Briggs–Rauscher (B-R) oscillatory system catalyzed by [NiL](ClO₄)₂
content: Abstract A novel method for the qualitative discrimination of the axial enantiomers R-1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (R-BINOL) and S-1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (S-BINOL) was developed using the Briggs–Rauscher (B-R) oscillatory system catalyzed by [NiL](ClO₄)₂ (L = 5,7,7,12,14,14-hexamethyl-1,4,8,11-tetraazacyclotetradeca-4,11-diene). Addition of either enantiomer at identical concentrations temporarily inhibited the oscillations, yet produced distinctly different inhibition times (t_in). Over the concentration range 1.25 × 10⁻⁶ to 6.25 × 10⁻⁶ mol/L, R-BINOL consistently gave longer t_in values than S-BINOL (e.g., 255.6 s vs 183.5 s at 1.25 × 10⁻⁶ mol/L; 1538.4 s vs 1131.6 s at 6.25 × 10⁻⁶ mol/L), enabling clear qualitative discrimination. Cyclic voltammetry indicated that hydroperoxyl radicals (HOO•) participate in the oxidation of the phenolic hydroxyl groups. Infrared spectroscopy confirmed conversion of the hydroxyl groups into carbonyl functionalities. The different inhibitory behaviors are interpreted within the Free Radical Controlled Autoinhibition (FCA) framework, in which R-BINOL more effectively scavenges HOO•, thereby more strongly disrupting the radical balance required for sustained oscillation. The results demonstrate that B-R oscillatory systems can serve as simple, sensitive platforms for chiral discrimination.

title: Stellar Flares Rather than High T int as Possible Cause for the Missing Methane in Young Exoplanets: The Case Study of V1298 Tau b
summary: Abstract Recent observations of V1298 Tau b, a warm sub-Neptune ( R = 9.85 ± 0.3 R ⊕ , M = 13.1 ± 5.3 M ⊕ , T eq = 670 K) orbiting a young (10–30 Myr) K star, show depleted methane and surprising abundances of CO 2 in its atmosphere. This m
content: Abstract Recent observations of V1298 Tau b, a warm sub-Neptune ( R = 9.85 ± 0.3 R ⊕ , M = 13.1 ± 5.3 M ⊕ , T eq = 670 K) orbiting a young (10–30 Myr) K star, show depleted methane and surprising abundances of CO 2 in its atmosphere. This makes the planet an interesting target to study the “missing methane problem,” where Hubble Space Telescope, Spitzer, and JWST have revealed many sub-Jovian planets with effective temperatures cooler than 800 K to be depleted in methane compared to equilibrium chemistry predictions. On V1298 Tau b, an intrinsic temperature ( T int ) of 500 K is required to explain the methane depletion if strong mixing from a warm interior is the reason for the missing methane, but this T int is too large for a planet of its age and size according to standard interior structure evolution theories. Here, we show that stellar flares can result in methane depletion in a warm planet’s atmosphere with nominal T int ∼ 100 K. During a stellar flare, fast methane photolysis rates cannot be balanced by diffusion from below into the upper atmospheric layers probed by observations. Young active stars flare frequently, and we show that the timescale of diffusion for the methane to recover from a flare-induced depletion can be slow compared to the flare frequency. Over time, the atmosphere reaches a new steady state set by the average flare frequency and energy. This new steady state shows depleted methane in the 2 mbar region, and abundant CO, CO 2 , and HCN, which results in synthetic transmission spectra that reproduce the main features of the recent JWST observations of V1298 Tau b.

title: How robust are transcriptomics-based points of departure when translated to in vivo doses by kinetic-modeling? A case study with the herbicide pendimethalin using HepG2 and HepaRG cells
summary: Abstract Risk assessment of agrochemicals has traditionally relied on animal studies to derive points of departure (PODs) for the establishment of regulatory guidance values. More recently, new approach methodologies (NAMs) have been explor
content: Abstract Risk assessment of agrochemicals has traditionally relied on animal studies to derive points of departure (PODs) for the establishment of regulatory guidance values. More recently, new approach methodologies (NAMs) have been explored as a means to estimate protective exposure levels without generating new animal data. In the present case study, we evaluated whether a transcriptomics-based NAM workflow combined with physiologically-based kinetic (PBK) modeling can provide biologically plausible estimates of systemic toxicity thresholds for pendimethalin (PDM), an agrochemical with extensive toxicological and kinetic reference data. We compared two in vitro liver models and transcriptomic approaches: targeted TempO-Seq in HepG2 cells and untargeted RNA sequencing in HepaRG cells. After 48 h exposure to PDM in concentration ranges of 0.07–202 µM (HepaRG) and 0.8–56 µM (HepG2), gene expression changes were analyzed using benchmark-dose modeling in BMDExpress 3.0. Transcriptomic PODs (tPODs) were derived using gene- and distribution-based approaches and subsequently translated to external doses by in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) employing three rat PBK models. The resulting PODs were compared with regulatory in vivo PODs reported for PDM. In addition, a human population-based PBK model was used to derive an oral equivalent dose (OED) from the most sensitive transcriptomic POD. Across transcriptomic platforms, tPOD derivation methods, and PBK models, the resulting IVIVE-derived PODs generally fell within the range of regulatory in vivo PODs reported for PDM. The most sensitive prediction yielded a POD of 6.0 mg/kg bw/day for the rat, while human population-based modeling resulted in a 5th-percentile OED of 0.068 mg/kg bw/day, close to currently established regulatory guidance values. Notably, the variability introduced by the choice of toxicokinetic model was of a similar magnitude as the variability associated with transcriptomic POD derivation, indicating that uncertainty in IVIVE contributes at least as much to the final prediction as uncertainty in transcriptomic data analysis. Overall, this study supports the feasibility of combining in vitro transcriptomics with IVIVE to estimate systemic toxicity thresholds for an agrochemical compound. The results encourage further evaluation of transcriptomics-based NAM workflows and next-generation risk assessment of agrochemicals. Assessment of a broader range of agrochemicals, together with continued refinement of toxicokinetic modeling and in vitro dosimetry, will be required to establish their predictive performance and future regulatory applicability.

title: Alchemy: Bounded Enumeration and Interactive Exploration of Small-Molecule Radical Reaction Networks
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Abstract Automated construction of chemical reaction networks is limited by the combinatorial growth of possible molecules, intermediates, and formal transformations. We present alchemy, an open-source Python workflow for systematic enumera
content: Abstract Automated construction of chemical reaction networks is limited by the combinatorial growth of possible molecules, intermediates, and formal transformations. We present alchemy, an open-source Python workflow for systematic enumeration and interactive exploration of small-molecule radical reaction networks. Within an explicitly bounded graph space, alchemy generates connected, neutral C/N/H molecular graphs with single, double, or triple bonds and specified radical counts; RDKit sanitization and canonicalization then remove graph-invalid and duplicate records. Formal reaction candidates are constructed without learned reaction templates by combining bond-dissociation records into rearrangement and transfer stoichiometries. Parallel generation, persistent disk-backed storage, and Kuzu graph representation make the resulting formal network searchable. An independent brute-force control recovers exactly the same 416 neutral molecular graphs as alchemy in a three-heavy-atom C/N/H space. In a trimethylamine case study limited to at most five heavy atoms and one unpaired electron per reaction side, the workflow generated 41,735 unique molecular graphs and a seed-0 bounded sample of 60,035 first-generation reaction records. The reaction construction is not complete because high-frequency shared fragments are handled by a documented deterministic sampling cap. An optional PaiNN molecular-energy model is distributed with the software, but its closed-shell QM9 benchmark does not validate the open-shell species considered here, and its output is not used to rank, filter, or interpret the case-study records. Alchemy therefore, provides a reproducible route to bounded reaction-space construction and downstream graph inspection.

title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
summary: Relaxation of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions was followed by a global resurgence of respiratory infections, yet how accumulated population susceptibility interacts with environmental forcing and human mobility remains unclear. He
content: Relaxation of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions was followed by a global resurgence of respiratory infections, yet how accumulated population susceptibility interacts with environmental forcing and human mobility remains unclear. Here we analyse ~1.88 million clinical influenza tests from Macau (2010-2025) alongside meteorology, air quality, digital information-seeking, and independent surveillance and time-resolved viral genomes from Hong Kong, benchmarked against global surveillance data. Counterfactual inference indicates a post-pandemic excess in influenza activity consistent with immunity debt, mirroring global resurgence patterns, and an independently parameterised susceptible–exposed–infectious–recovered–susceptible model reproduces this excess (best-fit debt fraction 42%; approximate Bayesian computation posterior 58%, 95% uncertainty interval 32-77%). Susceptibility rises disproportionately in adults rather than children, whereas vaccination coverage in high-risk groups does not decline, arguing against reduced uptake as the driver. Time-varying models and convergent cross mapping reveal environmental decoupling, whereby high susceptibility weakens meteorological constraints and sustains influenza A transmission, and asymmetric suppression of influenza B. Spatiotemporal and phylogenetic evidence supports travel-linked reintroduction from ports of entry into dense neighbourhoods, and digital information-seeking shifts from lagging to leading clinical burden. These findings indicate a post-pandemic regime shift in influenza dynamics rather than a return to historical baselines, motivating adaptive, multi-source surveillance in high-density cities. Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

title: Safe-by-design algal extracellular polymeric substances-based zeolite/ZnO bio-nanocomposite for the removal of bisphenol-A
summary: The existence of endocrine disrupting chemical (EDCs), like bisphenol-A (BPA), creates a huge challenge for conventional wastewater treatment plants. The current study aimed to develop a hybrid adsorption-photocatalytic material for efficie
content: The existence of endocrine disrupting chemical (EDCs), like bisphenol-A (BPA), creates a huge challenge for conventional wastewater treatment plants. The current study aimed to develop a hybrid adsorption-photocatalytic material for efficient BPA removal under UV-A irradiation. The characterization of the bio-nanocomposite was performed using FE-SEM, EDX, FTIR, UV–Vis spectrophotometry and total organic carbon (TOC). Batch experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of concentration, catalyst dosage, pH and an optimal bio-nanocomposite was developed. The optimized zeolite:ZnO:EPS ratio of 1:1:0.5 achieved the highest BPA removal under UV-A irradiation. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging experiments identified superoxide radicals as the dominant oxidative species. Among the scavengers, p-benzoquinone was seen to reduce efficiency, along with isopropanol and sodium azide. In addition, degradation kinetics were determined to be pseudo-first-order kinetics. The TOC analysis further confirmed approximately 96% mineralization of BPA after UV-A irradiation. In addition, the bio-nanocomposite showed 54.74% effectiveness on its 6th cycle of usage. In real water matrices under optimized conditions, the bio-nanocomposite showed 82.9%, 79.4% and 78.4% removal efficiencies for tap water, seawater and lake water, respectively. For the biosafety assessments, Scenedesmus obliquus and Allium sativum were used as model organisms. The results indicate that the presence of EPS reduced oxidative stress and improved biological compatibility.

title: Composition-driven defect and interface engineering in Cu1−xZnxFe2O4 nano-interlayers for high-performance Cu/p-Si MIS Schottky ultraviolet photodiodes
summary: Abstract Engineering defect chemistry and interface quality in nano-interlayers is an effective strategy for improving carrier transport in metal–insulator–semiconductor (MIS) photodiodes; however, the influence of composition-controlled de
content: Abstract Engineering defect chemistry and interface quality in nano-interlayers is an effective strategy for improving carrier transport in metal–insulator–semiconductor (MIS) photodiodes; however, the influence of composition-controlled defect engineering in ferrite nano-interlayers remains insufficiently explored. In this work, Cu 1−x Zn x Fe 2 O 4 (x = 0.2–0.8) nano-interlayers were synthesized by chemical bath deposition and employed as interfacial insulating layers in Cu/p-Si MIS Schottky photodiodes. Zn substitution was utilized as a composition-driven defect and interface engineering approach to systematically tailor the structural, optical and electronic properties of the ferrite layer. Structural and morphological analyses reveal progressive crystallinity enhancement, grain growth and reduced lattice strain with increasing Zn concentration, while optical studies demonstrate band-gap narrowing from 3.68 to 3.50 eV, promoting enhanced ultraviolet light absorption. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirms oxygen-vacancy-related defect states and mixed valence species that facilitate charge transfer and improve interface quality. These interconnected structural and electronic modifications reduce carrier trapping and recombination, leading to lower ideality factors and enhanced barrier homogeneity. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ Cu 0.2 Zn 0.8 Fe 2 O 4 /p-Si photodiode exhibits a responsivity of 65.9 mA W⁻¹, quantum efficiency of 25.5% and detectivity of 2.41 × 10¹¹ Jones under ultraviolet illumination. The present work establishes a comprehensive structure–defect–interface–performance relationship, demonstrating that composition-controlled defect engineering offers a practical design strategy for high-performance ferrite-based silicon photodiodes and other optoelectronic devices.

title: Efficiency of photocatalytic ozonation process in the presence of CoFe₂O₄/ZnTiO₃/Ag nanocomposite for the removal of bisphenol a from aqueous solutions
summary: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting compound, persists in aquatic environments and resists conventional wastewater treatment, posing ecological and human health risks. In this study, a magnetic CoFe₂O₄/ZnTiO₃/Ag ternary nan
content: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting compound, persists in aquatic environments and resists conventional wastewater treatment, posing ecological and human health risks. In this study, a magnetic CoFe₂O₄/ZnTiO₃/Ag ternary nanocomposite was prepared by co-precipitation and calcination and tested as a heterogeneous catalyst for BPA removal by photocatalytic ozonation (6 W UV-C lamp, 0.2 g/h ozone) in a model aqueous system. XRD showed reflections of a spinel phase and metallic silver together with weak reflections attributed to ilmenite-type ZnTiO₃; however, the iron-rich EDX composition and an XRD pattern of the calcined core that includes reflections consistent with hematite show that the material is not phase-pure. Batch experiments (one run per condition) varied initial BPA concentration (10–50 mg/L), catalyst dosage (0.25–0.75 g/L), pH (4–10) and reaction time (up to 240 min). Under the best conditions tested (pH 7, 0.5 g/L catalyst, 10 mg/L BPA), BPA removal reached 91.30% and COD removal 82.5% after 240 min. Under the same conditions, removal was 76.09% for UV-C/O₃, 70.65% for O₃ alone, 9.78% for UV-C alone and 1.09% for the catalyst alone. The catalyst with UV-C but without ozone removed 85.87%, and the catalyst with ozone but without light removed 80.43%, so the composite acted both as a photocatalyst and as an ozonation catalyst. A 400 W metal halide lamp used as a simulated-sunlight source gave no improvement over the catalyst/O₃ system (80.65% versus 80.43%). The apparent rate constant of the three-component process was about 1.8 times the sum of those of the single processes but only about 1.25 times that of the best two-component process (catalyst/UV-C). Removal fell from 91.30% to 47.83% over seven reuse cycles, while the catalyst was easily recovered with a magnet. The proposed mechanism and degradation pathway are hypotheses based on the literature and on tentatively identified intermediates and were not tested directly. The results suggest that the system is a promising option for BPA removal in model water; regeneration, metal leaching, toxicity of the treated water and performance in real wastewater remain to be studied.

title: When Knowledge Institutions Pollute: Cultivated Meat, Science Communication, and Public Policy
summary: Using a press release on cultivated meat’s climate impact as a case study, this paper argues for reforming universities’ media policies. Drawing on a dataset of 491 media items across 2023–2025, it traces how the press release triggered a c
content: Using a press release on cultivated meat’s climate impact as a case study, this paper argues for reforming universities’ media policies. Drawing on a dataset of 491 media items across 2023–2025, it traces how the press release triggered a cascade of ‘churnalism,’ propelling the preprint into mainstream and international media, embedding its most extreme claims into background knowledge, and contributing to policy actions restricting a potentially promising alternative protein. Misinformation in this case did not originate from overt industry manipulation, but from an epistemically polluted ecosystem that blends the different vested interests of academics, press officers, universities, and journalists.

title: Fast and Furious—High-velocity Features of Ca and Si in the Spectra of Type Ia Supernovae*
summary: Abstract High-velocity absorption lines of Ca II and Si II (high-velocity features (HVFs)) are common in the early spectra of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), but their physical origin is still poorly understood. We used 181 optical spectra of
content: Abstract High-velocity absorption lines of Ca II and Si II (high-velocity features (HVFs)) are common in the early spectra of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), but their physical origin is still poorly understood. We used 181 optical spectra of 56 SNe Ia that show HVFs in at least the Ca II near-infrared (NIR) triplet to better understand the nature of HVFs. To model the profiles of HVFs we applied Gaussian fitting as well as spectrum synthesis modeling with the SYNOW code. We found that Gaussian fitting usually underestimates the velocity of HVFs compared to SYNOW, and derived a linear formula for correction. In accord with many previous studies, the observed properties of HVFs (velocity, strength, and duration) were found to correlate with the general observables of SNe Ia (decline rate and spectral subtype). Brighter, slow-declining supernovae usually exhibit stronger, higher-velocity HVFs, while fainter objects typically show weak, low-velocity HVFs. SNe Ia in early-type galaxies showed weaker and slower HVFs compared to events in late-type galaxies in our sample. Comparing these observational findings with theoretical predictions, we conclude that the overall physical picture of HVFs is quite complex, and could be explained by multiple models. A double-detonation explosion model is promising as it is inherently capable of explaining the creation of high-velocity shells that may produce HVFs, but an asymmetric delayed detonation model or interaction with circumstellar material cannot be ruled out.

title: Substituent effects on electronic properties and predicted acetylcholinesterase binding potential of donepezil analogues: a DFT, molecular docking, and ADMET study with dynamics assessment of the lead candidate
summary: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that is the leading cause of dementia in older people. Donepezil is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used for symptomatic management of AD. Due to its high effic
content: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that is the leading cause of dementia in older people. Donepezil is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used for symptomatic management of AD. Due to its high efficacy, low hepatic toxicity, prolonged half-life, and enhanced bioavailability, it was used as a reference. In this study, a series of donepezil derivatives (MH-1 to MH-5) were designed through structural modification at the benzyl moiety and systematically investigated along with the reference using density functional theory, time-dependent DFT, molecular docking, and in silico pharmacokinetics analysis. The geometry optimization and electronic structure calculations were performed using the B3LYP/6-311G (d, p) level. Frontier molecular orbital analysis indicated reduced energy in MH-1 and MH-2 , while the optical study shows that all derivatives (MH-1 to MH-5) demonstrate a bathochromic shift. The molecular docking of all derivatives and the reference against the acetylcholinesterase receptor 4EY7 indicates strong predicted affinities, where MH-1 , MH-2 , and MH-4 show binding energy equivalent to the reference (-12.2 kcal/mol). A 300 ns molecular dynamics simulation of the AChE MH-4 complex showed a stable trajectory, as indicated by RMSD/RMSF profiles. Binding free energy calculated using MM-GBSA combined with the Interaction Entropy approximation yielded ΔG = -13.04 ± 3.73 kcal/mol, confirming favourable and thermodynamically stable binding. Moreover, the results of the ADME analysis indicated good oral absorption and blood-brain barrier penetration. Toxicity assessment predicted favourable safety profiles for most of the derivatives, except for a few that show potential concerns. In summary, all these results indicate that MH-4 has an encouraging physicochemical and computationally predicted bioactive profile for anti-Alzheimer drug development.

title: Catalytic dehydration of fructose to 5- Hydroxymethylfurfural by a lignin-derived carbon solid acid catalyst modified by non-thermal plasma
summary: Abstract Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) as a critical biomass-derived platform chemical shows significant potential for synthesizing diverse value-added products. However, conventional 5-HMF preparation methods often suffer from inherent dra
content: Abstract Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) as a critical biomass-derived platform chemical shows significant potential for synthesizing diverse value-added products. However, conventional 5-HMF preparation methods often suffer from inherent drawbacks including high energy demand, environmental pollution, and high cost. A solid acid catalyst (LDSA-COOH) was prepared using solvent-extracted lignin as the carbon support and modified by non-thermal plasma grafting in an acrylic acid atmosphere. The structure and properties of the catalyst were comprehensively analyzed by various spectroscopies (FTIR, XPS) and SEM microscopy, and the porosity structure was detected by BET method. The catalytic performance of LDSA-COOH was systematically assessed through measurements of acidic group density and dehydration of fructose to 5-HMF. In a DMSO/water biphasic solvent system, high fructose conversion of 99.2% and 5-HMF yield of 85.7% was obtained at 180 ℃ and 30 min by LDSA-COOH. Notably, the LDSA-COOH catalyst also demonstrated excellent stability and reusability through five consecutive reuse cycles. This method offers advantages including shorter solid acid preparation time, lower energy consumption, lower environmental pollution, and higher catalytic stability, providing a promising strategy for the preparation of solid acid catalyst.

title: Cheap talkers or hard hitters? Political parties’ climate policy proposals
summary: Parties are central to climate politics, yet we have little knowledge of their climate policy preferences beyond salience or ‘pro’ or ‘anti’ positions. This study develops a new measure of parties’ climate policy preferences based on whethe
content: Parties are central to climate politics, yet we have little knowledge of their climate policy preferences beyond salience or ‘pro’ or ‘anti’ positions. This study develops a new measure of parties’ climate policy preferences based on whether they advance policy proposals, and the ‘soft’ and ‘hard’ quality of those proposals. It is argued that policy proposals are more ‘substantial’ than general climate-related content in political texts, and that ‘hard’ policies are more substantial than ‘soft’ policies as the former are less popular and therefore associated with higher political risks. The analysis of original data from 502 manifestos in 20 industrial democracies over four elections (2002–2022) finds that climate policy proposals – both pro- and anti-climate, and soft and hard – have become less prevalent. The study’s analysis of parties’ climate policy preferences shows that party ideology, size and incumbency help to explain variation in the prevalence of climate proposals.

title: Tailoring Gas Transport Properties in MOF-Based Mixed Matrix Membranes: The Role of Filler Morphology and Surface Functionalization
summary: Abstract The development of high-performance mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) for gas separations relies on precise control of filler morphology and optimized polymer–filler interactions. In this study, we elucidate how crystal size, morpholog
content: Abstract The development of high-performance mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) for gas separations relies on precise control of filler morphology and optimized polymer–filler interactions. In this study, we elucidate how crystal size, morphology, and surface functionalization of the perfluorinated metal–organic framework (MOF) F4_MIL-140A(Ce) influence the gas transport properties of MMMs based on Pebax 1657 and Matrimid 9725 matrices. Through systematic modulation of reaction conditions, we synthesized submicrometric F4_MIL-140A(Ce) particles with tailored size and aspect ratio, achieving improved dispersion and interfacial contact within the polymer phases. A postsynthetic grafting strategy using stearic acid further enhanced the compatibility of the MOF with the polymer matrix without altering crystallinity, pore accessibility, or CO2 adsorption behavior, as confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and sorption analyses. MMMs prepared with the surface-functionalized MOF displayed improved polymer–filler adhesion, minimized interfacial voids, and significantly enhanced gas transport properties. In particular, the Pebax 1657-based MMMs approached the 2008 Robeson upper bound for CO2/N2 separation, primarily driven by increased CO2 solubility, which increased the CO2 permeability by 62% (from 76 to 123 Barrer) and the CO2/N2 selectivity by 28% (from 58 to 74). In contrast, Matrimid 9725 MMMs exhibited substantial improvements in H2/N2 and O2/N2 selectivity (i.e., from 93 to 108 and from 6.6 to 7.7, respectively), because of enhanced diffusivity. The insights presented in this work provide a rational framework for engineering MOF–polymer interfaces and advancing membrane-based gas separation and CO2 capture technologies.

title: A Rapid Low Temperature Route to High‐Entropy Thiospinels for Efficient Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT High‐entropy thiospinels have emerged as promising candidates for magnetic and catalytic applications owing to their dual cationic sites and strong synergistic effects. However, their synthesis is challenging due to the high proces
content: ABSTRACT High‐entropy thiospinels have emerged as promising candidates for magnetic and catalytic applications owing to their dual cationic sites and strong synergistic effects. However, their synthesis is challenging due to the high processing temperature, complex chemistry, and post‐sulfurization treatments that are generally required to obtain single‐phase thiospinels. Herein, we report a low‐temperature synthesis of thiospinel high‐entropy sulfides (HESs, i.e. (NiCoFeInZn) 3 S 4 ) via simultaneous thermolysis of metal xanthate (M(S 2 COEt 2 ) x , where M = Ni 2+ , Co 3+ , Fe 3+ , In 3+ , and Zn 2+ , and x is the charge of the metal cation) precursors at 300°C. This method produced crystalline HESs with well‐defined thiospinel structure. Elemental mapping confirms a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Co, Fe, In, and Zn cations and anions in near‐stoichiometric proportions. These HESs demonstrate respectable electrocatalytic performance for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media, achieving a low overpotential of 168 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , significantly outperforming their binary and ternary counterparts. This approach offers a rapid and sustainable pathway toward high‐entropy thiospinels at relatively low synthetic temperatures.

title: Composition optimization and diffusion behavior of a cold rejuvenator in aged asphalt using molecular dynamics
summary: Abstract To address the challenges of low utilization efficiency and weak adhesion in the cold recycling of reclaimed asphalt pavement, this study developed a novel cold recycling rejuvenator (CRR) designed for ambient temperatures. Guided
content: Abstract To address the challenges of low utilization efficiency and weak adhesion in the cold recycling of reclaimed asphalt pavement, this study developed a novel cold recycling rejuvenator (CRR) designed for ambient temperatures. Guided by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the research screened penetrants using asphalt dissolution tests and determined the optimal CRR dosage and regeneration time via dynamic shear rheometry. Diffusion mechanisms were analyzed through MD-derived metrics, including diffusion coefficients and interaction energies, and further validated using fluorescence microscopy. Results indicate that CRR composition and dosage significantly impact diffusion behavior at 25 ℃, with limonene playing a dominant role in the process. Specifically, the RA3 formulation achieved optimal diffusion at a 12% dosage. The CRR effectively reduced interactions between asphaltene molecules, which enhanced molecular dispersion and partially restored the asphalt’s colloidal structure. Notably, after only 10 min of rejuvenation, the aged asphalt recovered 96% of the performance of virgin asphalt.

title: Electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia on black-phosphorus-type two-dimensional monochalcogenides
summary: The reduction of nitric oxide (NO) is a powerful method for eliminating the pollutant NO and a feasible route for synthesizing ammonia (NH 3 ) at ambient temperature, a promise to replace the energy-consuming Haber-Bosch process. However, t
content: The reduction of nitric oxide (NO) is a powerful method for eliminating the pollutant NO and a feasible route for synthesizing ammonia (NH 3 ) at ambient temperature, a promise to replace the energy-consuming Haber-Bosch process. However, the design of efficient catalysts with low cost and high activity to boost the complex electron transfer process is significantly challenging. Herein, we applied state-of-the-art density functional theory (DFT) calculations for the first time to investigate NO reduction on black-phosphorus-like two-dimensional monochalcogenides GeSe and SnSe, respectively. The strong bonding state between the catalyst and the adsorbate is attributed to the activation of NO, favouring NO-side adsorption and the substantial reduction to NH 3 . The catalysts are highly efficient for nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR), as evidenced by the low limiting potentials of −0.19 and −0.11 V, respectively. Moreover, the formation of by-products (N 2 O and N 2 ) and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are strongly suppressed, indicating the selective formation of NH 3 . This work is a promising strategy for designing practical and economical NORR electrocatalysts and an effective method to solve the problem of NO environmental pollution.

title: CPSF6 coordinates adipogenesis and metabolic homeostasis through alternative polyadenylation-mediated modulation of GSK3β
summary: Abstract Healthy expansion of white adipose tissue (WAT) depends on efficient adipogenesis to preserve systemic metabolic homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms of RNA 3'-end processing that govern adipogenesis remain incompletely charac
content: Abstract Healthy expansion of white adipose tissue (WAT) depends on efficient adipogenesis to preserve systemic metabolic homeostasis, yet the molecular mechanisms of RNA 3'-end processing that govern adipogenesis remain incompletely characterized. Through integration of human obesity transcriptomes with genome-wide alternative polyadenylation (APA) profiling, we identify CPSF6 (Cleavage and polyadenylation specific factor 6) as a critical regulator of adipocyte differentiation. In vivo conditional deletion of Cpsf6 in adipocyte progenitors results in WAT atrophy and impaired insulin sensitivity under physiological conditions, whereas deletion in mature adipocytes attenuates diet-induced weight gain and restricts adipose tissue expansion, revealing stage-dependent functions of CPSF6 in adipose tissue development and remodeling. Mechanistically, CPSF6 binds the Gsk3b 3'UTR and orchestrates APA-dependent isoform switching, thereby maintaining GSK3β protein abundance. Restoring GSK3β expression in Cpsf6-deficient cells partially rescues impaired adipogenesis. Furthermore, human genetic analyses support a role for CPSF6 in metabolic regulation. These findings reveal a CPSF6-Gsk3b APA axis that coordinates adipogenesis and systemic metabolic homeostasis.

title: Anion manipulation for breaking through 3.0 V of aluminium–graphite batteries
summary: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al2Cl7−([AlCl3–AlCl4]−) anions are in
content: Aluminium-graphite batteries offer low cost and intrinsic high safety. However, the voltage window mostly remains limited because conventional chloroaluminate ionic-liquid electrolytes with Lewis-acidic Al2Cl7−([AlCl3–AlCl4]−) anions are intrinsically moisture-sensitive and unstable beyond 2.5 V. To extend the voltage window, a polytetrafluoroethylene/AlF3 framework‑confined, fluorine-rich chloroaluminate ionic-liquid composite quasi-solid-state electrolyte cosolvated with 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl ether is designed for constructing stable aluminium-graphite batteries with a cut-off voltage of 3.0 V. With the presence of AlF3, the Al2Cl7− is regulated through AlF3-associated chloroaluminate interactions, which reduces its activity and suppresses its electrochemical decomposition in the range of 2.5–3.0 V. Meanwhile, the fluorinated ether coordinates with the AlCl3 units in Al2Cl7− and promotes the formation of a fluorine-rich artificial interface on the graphite, essentially improving the electrochemical stability via alleviating electrochemical decomposition of AlCl4− up to 3.0 V. Furthermore, ion transport channels could be well maintained during large mechanical deformation induced by anion-intercalation/deintercalation of graphite interlayer. Therefore, the Al|electrolyte|graphite cells deliver discharge capacity beyond 137 mAh g−1 up to 3.0 V (specific current: 5.0 A g−1) (compared to 64 mAh g−1, charged up to 2.5 V at 5.0 A g−1) along with stable cycles beyond 35,000, demonstrating long-term high-voltage operation in rechargeable aluminium–graphite batteries. Aluminium–graphite batteries are limited by electrolyte decomposition above 2.5 V. Here, authors regulate chloroaluminate anions with a fluorine-rich, framework-confined quasi-solid-state electrolyte, enabling stable 3.0 V operation for Al | |Graphite cells.

title: Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Efficiency and Responses of Recalcitrant Dissolved Organic Carbon Under Future Emissions Scenarios
source: Journal of Ocean University of China
summary: Abstract Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is increasingly regarded as a promising ocean-based carbon dioxide removal strategy because it can enhance oceanic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) uptake while alleviating ocean acidification. However, reg
content: Abstract Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is increasingly regarded as a promising ocean-based carbon dioxide removal strategy because it can enhance oceanic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) uptake while alleviating ocean acidification. However, regional differences in OAE efficiency and the associated responses of recalcitrant dissolved organic carbon (RDOC) remain poorly constrained. Here, we incorporate a microbial carbon pump (MCP) module into the carbon-centric Grid-Enabled Integrated Earth System Model (cGENIE) to assess the carbon sequestration potential of OAE and the RDOC response under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios SSP2-45 and SSP5-85 across different regional deployment configurations. By explicitly linking OAE with MCP-mediated RDOC dynamics, our study extends previous carbonate-chemistry-focused assessments to include long-term inorganic–organic carbon feedbacks. In idealized simulations with sustained OAE deployment beginning in 2030 CE, atmospheric CO 2 concentrations are (62–75)×10 −6 lower and global mean surface temperatures are 0.15–0.21 °C lower by 2100 CE than in the corresponding simulations without OAE. Alkalinity deployment in the Northwest Pacific yields the highest long-term efficiency and strongest local surface alkalinity enhancement among the configurations tested. OAE also induces distinct long-term responses among dissolved organic carbon (DOC) fractions. The RDOC response lags behind those of labile DOC and semilabile DOC and evolves more slowly over millennial timescales, with concentrations remaining relatively stable at 44–45 µmol/kg. These results underscore the coupled inorganic–organic feedbacks governing OAE efficiency and highlight the necessity of spatial and temporal optimization for maximizing long-term carbon sequestration.

title: Calcium Signaling Enhances Bostrycin Biosynthesis in Nigrospora sphaerica HCH285: Transcriptomic Insights into Metabolic Regulation
summary: Abstract Background: Bostrycin, an anthraquinone secondary metabolite produced by Nigrospora sphaerica , exhibits broad-spectrum antitumor and antimicrobial activities, but its low production limits further development and application. Calc
content: Abstract Background: Bostrycin, an anthraquinone secondary metabolite produced by Nigrospora sphaerica , exhibits broad-spectrum antitumor and antimicrobial activities, but its low production limits further development and application. Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) are important intracellular signaling molecules that regulate fungal physiology and secondary metabolism, but their role in bostrycin biosynthesis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effect of exogenous Ca 2+ on bostrycin production and to elucidate the underlying molecular response using transcriptomic analysis. Methods: Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, and K⁺ (supplemented as chloride salts) were screened for their ability to promote bostrycin production in N. sphaerica HCH285. The optimal Ca²⁺ concentration and addition time were determined by measuring bostrycin production using HPLC. Biomass accumulation, sporulation capacity, and extracellular nucleic acid and protein leakage were evaluated to characterize the physiological effects of Ca 2+ treatment.Control and Ca²⁺-treated cultures were subjected to transcriptome sequencing, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses and qRT-PCR validation. Results: Among all tested metal ions, Ca 2+ showed the strongest stimulatory effect on bostrycin biosynthesis, with 4 g/L Ca 2+ producing the highest yield of bostrycin with 63.6 ± 0.31 μg/mL, representing a 2.55-fold increase over the control. Ca 2+ supplementation also significantly increased fungal biomass and sporulation capacity, suggesting that enhanced growth contributed to the elevated metabolite production. Increased extracellular nucleic acid and protein contents indicated altered cell integrity or secretion activity following Ca 2+ treatment.Transcriptomic analysis identified DEGs most significantly enriched in metabolic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, while genes related to polyketide metabolism and ubiquinone biosynthesis were also annotated. Several genes associated with ion transport, energy metabolism, and secondary metabolite biosynthesis were significantly upregulated. Among them, wbpA, talA, cho1, and aroB were further validated by qRT-PCR, indicating that Ca²⁺ supplementation triggered broad metabolic reprogramming associated with bostrycin accumulation. Conclusions: Exogenous Ca 2+ effectively enhances bostrycin production in N. sphaerica HCH285 through coordinated physiological and transcriptional responses. Transcriptomic analysis suggests that Ca 2+ supplementation promotes energy metabolism, ion transport, and secondary metabolic processes associated with bostrycin biosynthesis. These findings provide new insights into calcium-mediated regulation of fungal secondary metabolism and offer a potential strategy for improving bostrycin production through fermentation optimization and metabolic engineering.

title: Improvement in stamping formability of Ti/Al multilayered composites via annealing-induced interface modification
summary: Abstract Ti/Al/Ti/Al/Ti layered metal composites (LMCs) were obtained via hot-pressing and hot-rolling, followed by annealing at 550 ℃ for different times to regulate the interface. The effect of Ti/Al interfacial evolution on the mechanica
content: Abstract Ti/Al/Ti/Al/Ti layered metal composites (LMCs) were obtained via hot-pressing and hot-rolling, followed by annealing at 550 ℃ for different times to regulate the interface. The effect of Ti/Al interfacial evolution on the mechanical behavior and stamping formability of the LMCs was investigated. As annealing proceeded, the Ti/Al interface bonding strength exhibited a rise followed by a decline, reaching a peak of 8.73 N/mm at an annealing duration of 1 h. The strength of the LMCs decreased, whereas elongation (EL) increased first and then decreased, reaching the maximum of 7.15% after 1 h of annealing, which was closely related to superior interfacial bonding. The enhanced interfacial bonding improved deformation compatibility among adjacent layers, thereby delaying premature failure of the less ductile Al layer and increasing the overall EL. The optimal stamping formability was obtained in the LMCs annealed for 1 h, as the weakened basal texture of the base metal induced a lower yield-to-tensile strength ratio (σs/σb) and a larger strain hardening exponent (n), endowing the LMCs with a longer uniform plastic deformation and higher strain hardening resistance. During stamping, localized and stable interfacial delamination promoted crack deflection and blunting and contributed to energy dissipation, thereby improving the stamping formability of the LMCs, whereas extensive and unstable wedge-shaped delamination provided a rapid interfacial crack-propagation path and accelerated failure.

title: The Welfare Effects of Price Shocks and Household Relief Packages: Evidence from an Energy Crisis
summary: Aggregate price shocks generate unequal welfare losses both across and within income groups.Policymakers face a trade-off: price subsidies direct more support to households facing larger losses, but create inefficiencies, while transfers ar
content: Aggregate price shocks generate unequal welfare losses both across and within income groups.Policymakers face a trade-off: price subsidies direct more support to households facing larger losses, but create inefficiencies, while transfers are less distortionary but harder to target.We develop and implement a framework to quantify this trade-off using rich panel data on households' energy spending and incomes, alongside price and policy variation from the 2022-23 European Energy Crisis.Absent policy intervention, average household welfare losses would have equalled 6% of income, with some households facing much larger losses.The combination of an energy-price subsidy and universal transfers reduced both the mean and dispersion of losses, but incurred efficiency costs equal to 12% of total relief-package revenue costs.Optimal policy entails a strictly positive price subsidy, though its level is lower when transfers can be targeted using income and prior energy usage.

title: Gradient‐Driven Spatial Relay in Titanium Oxynitride for Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to C 2 H 4 demands simultaneous management of light harvesting, proton supply, and C−C coupling, functions that are difficult to integrate on a single surface site. Here, we present a “surface‐subsurfa
content: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to C 2 H 4 demands simultaneous management of light harvesting, proton supply, and C−C coupling, functions that are difficult to integrate on a single surface site. Here, we present a “surface‐subsurface spatial relay” strategy to overcome this limitation using a gradient titanium oxynitride (G−TiNO) architecture that spatially partitions these steps, realizing CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 conversion without noble metal on Ti‐based catalysts. Operando spectroscopy and DFT reveal that the surface Ti−O layer captures CO 2 and dissociates water to supply *H, while a built‐in electric field drives linear intermediates into a subsurface N−Ti−O domain, where the barrier for *OCCO formation is markedly lowered. Crucially, operando XAFS spectroscopy unveils a reversible “breathing‐mode” adsorption of CO 2 within the gradient architecture, wherein the N−Ti−O lattice dynamically expands and contracts in response to interfacial charge accumulation, stabilizing key intermediates. The optimized G−TiNO−425 achieves a C 2 H 4 evolution rate of 73.34 µmol g −1 h −1 with 76.46% product selectivity and 93.14% electron selectivity. Comparative control experiments show that progressive removal of the TiNO interlayer shifts selectivity from C 2 H 4 to CO, establishing a causal link between the gradient interface and C−C coupling. This work provides a design principle for buried interfaces that exploit dynamic structural flexibility to direct complex multi‐electron photocatalysts.

title: Preparation of cerium oxide/graphene oxide composite aerogels and its photocatalytic activity for Congo red
summary: The CeO 2 /GO composite aerogels were fabricated through a straightforward one-step hydrothermal process, specifically designed for the photocatalytic breakdown of Congo red.
content: The CeO 2 /GO composite aerogels were fabricated through a straightforward one-step hydrothermal process, specifically designed for the photocatalytic breakdown of Congo red.

title: Synthesis Strategies and Photocatalytic Efficiency of Bi2O3 based Nanostructures: A Comprehensive Review on Recent Progress and Applications in Dye Degradation, CO2 Reduction and Hydrogen Generation
summary: Bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) based nanomaterials have emerged as promising visible light driven photocatalysts for different applications like wastewater treatment, CO2 reduction and hydrogen generation. This is possible due to their suitable band
content: Bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) based nanomaterials have emerged as promising visible light driven photocatalysts for different applications like wastewater treatment, CO2 reduction and hydrogen generation. This is possible due to their suitable band structure, strong visible light absorption and chemical stability. This review presents a critical assessment of recent advances in the synthesis, modification and photocatalytic applications of Bi2O3 nanostructures for the degradation of organic dyes, pharmaceutical residues and other emerging pollutants. Major synthesis routes, such as sol-gel, hydrothermal, solvothermal, chemical precipitation and green synthesis, are discussed in relation to their effects on crystal structure, morphology, surface properties and photocatalytic performance. Strategies to address the inherent limitations of pristine Bi2O3 are examined, with particular emphasis on elemental doping and heterojunction engineering. Recent developments in Bi2O3-based composites incorporating semiconductors such as TiO2, g-C3N4 and MoS2 are reviewed, with attention to interfacial charge transfer and improved charge-carrier separation. The fundamental aspects of photocatalysis, such as charge-carrier dynamics, reactive oxygen species formation and interfacial electron-transfer processes, are critically discussed. The scope of the review extends beyond pollutant degradation to the application of Bi2O3-based nanostructures in photocatalytic CO2 reduction and water splitting, with particular focus on solar-driven hydrogen generation, material modification and surface reaction pathways. The existing limitations in photocatalytic efficiency, structural stability and practical applicability are assessed, along with future research directions for the design of efficient, durable and scalable Bi2O3-based photocatalysts for environmental remediation and solar energy conversion.

title: Combined Saussurea costus and doxorubicin suppresses breast cancer cell migration and proliferation through MMP2/MMP9 downregulation: in vitro and molecular docking evidence
summary: Abstract Breast cancer (BC) is still a major cause of cancer-related death in women and requires new strategies for treatment. Saussurea costus (COS) has been reported to exhibit anticancer activity, and doxorubicin (DOX) is a commonly used
content: Abstract Breast cancer (BC) is still a major cause of cancer-related death in women and requires new strategies for treatment. Saussurea costus (COS) has been reported to exhibit anticancer activity, and doxorubicin (DOX) is a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent. The relationship between their roles and BC cell behavior and regulation remains unclear. 28 compounds were identified in the COS ethanolic extract by LC–ESI–MS/MS. The docking and dynamics study of major compounds with MMP2 and MMP9 was performed. The effects of COS, DOX, and their combination on MCF7 and MDA-MB-231 cells were assessed for cytotoxicity, proliferation, migration (wound healing and transwell), colony formation, apoptosis (annexin-V), cell cycle, and MMP2/MMP9 mRNA expression. The main compounds found were apigenin (12.99%), medioresinol (8.32%), and luteolin (8.12%). Luteolin had the most negative value for protein binding (MMP2: − 8.90 kcal/mol; MMP9: − 9.50 kcal/mol) and medioresinol for mRNA binding. COS demonstrated dose-dependent cytotoxicity (IC 50 : 106.8 ± 1.43 μg/mL for MCF7; 116.8 ± 5.66 μg/mL for MDA-MB-231). The COS + DOX combination significantly reduced proliferation, migration, and colony formation, and increased apoptosis (MCF7: 34.85 ± 1.84%, MDA-MB-231: 45.56 ± 7.74%), and induced G2/M arrest in MDA-MB-231 cells. The expression of MMP2 and MMP9 mRNA was significantly downregulated. The COS + DOX treatment had a combinatorial effect in suppressing BC cell growth and migration, which was associated with downregulation of MMP2/MMP9 and induction of apoptosis. While these findings suggest a potential mechanistic role for MMP2/MMP9 downregulation, future studies measuring protein expression and enzymatic activity are required to confirm functional inhibition. Given its potential therapeutic significance, further in vivo studies are warranted.

title: HUH-tag conjugation enables accessible, site-specific functionalization of DNA origami with signaling-competent proteins
summary: DNA origami enables precise nanometer scale control over the number, spacing, and geometry of biomolecules, making it a powerful tool for dissecting spatially organized biological processes such as receptor signaling. However, functionalizi
content: DNA origami enables precise nanometer scale control over the number, spacing, and geometry of biomolecules, making it a powerful tool for dissecting spatially organized biological processes such as receptor signaling. However, functionalizing origami with proteins remains a bottleneck restricting the technology to specialized laboratories. Here we show that viral-derived HUH endonuclease tags, small (~10 kDa) domains that form a covalent phosphotyrosine bond with short unmodified ssDNA, provide a simple and cost-effective route to decorating DNA origami with functional proteins. Using interleukin-1β (IL-1β) as a model ligand, we generated recombinant IL-1β-HUH, achieved efficient site-specific conjugation to unmodified ssDNA within minutes, and coupled the conjugates to a DNA origami pegboard with tunable stoichiometry. IL-1β-functionalized origami triggered ligand-dependent signalling in living cells and allowed visualization of the recruitment of downstream signaling molecules, confirming that HUH-tag conjugation preserves functionality. Because this strategy requires only standard molecular biology equipment and unmodified DNA, it lowers a technical and financial barrier to DNA origami-based experimentation, opening the approach to a broader range of biological questions and laboratories outside the DNA nanotechnology field.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Self-Sensing E-Gasket for Early Warning of Transportation Pipeline Leakage
summary: Abstract In advancing structural health monitoring (SHM) of industrial pipeline networks, the real-time assessment of bolt-gasket-flange connections (BGFCs) is crucial for preventing hazardous fluid leakage. The most critical indicator of s
content: Abstract In advancing structural health monitoring (SHM) of industrial pipeline networks, the real-time assessment of bolt-gasket-flange connections (BGFCs) is crucial for preventing hazardous fluid leakage. The most critical indicator of sealing integrity is the spatial distribution of contact pressure at the gasket-flange interface. However, conventional monitoring methods are inherently limited by environmental susceptibility, compromised mechanical sealing, and insufficient spatial resolution in contact pressure distribution. To address these limitations, this study presents a continuous self-sensing electronic gasket (e-gasket) based on a piezoresistive carbon black/nitrile butadiene rubber (CB/NBR) composite for the early warning of sealing failure. Featuring a uniform percolation network within a hyperelastic matrix, the e-gasket simultaneously performs structural load-bearing functions and enables spatial self-sensing of contact pressure. Systematic evaluations of sensing performance reveal that the composite achieves the highest sensitivity of −0.2185 MPa–1 within the range of 0–1.9 MPa. To overcome the ill-posed problem caused by the soft-field effect and crosstalk errors, a data-driven hybrid strategy is proposed. Utilizing a customized U-Net architecture and a validated finite element model, this methodology maps the resistance matrix to a high-resolution contact pressure distribution. In the application demonstrations involving single- and double-bolt loosening, the method achieves an image correlation coefficient (ICC) exceeding 0.97 and a relative image error (RIE) below 0.15. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the e-gasket in precisely localizing potential leakage pathways, enabling a reliable and noninvasive solution for comprehensive pipeline SHM.

title: Integrated Thermodynamic–Mechanical Analysis of a Combined ORC– VCC Refrigeration System Using an Expander–Compressor Unit-Based Piston for Waste-Heat Utilization
summary: Abstract This study presents a theoretical analysis of a directly coupled Organic Rankine Cycle–vapor-compression cycle (ORC–VCC), which is an alternative thermally driven refrigeration system. This system combines an ORC with a VCC via a f
content: Abstract This study presents a theoretical analysis of a directly coupled Organic Rankine Cycle–vapor-compression cycle (ORC–VCC), which is an alternative thermally driven refrigeration system. This system combines an ORC with a VCC via a free-piston expander-compressor unit (ECU). The ECU directly transfers mechanical work to a piston compressor without an intermediate generator, motor, or shaft train. A coupled thermodynamic–mechanical model is developed to assess piston force balance, swept volume, working-fluid mass flow rate, compressor work, cooling capacity, heat input, and system coefficient of performance (COP). Seven refrigerants, R134a, R22, R32, R410A, R1233zd(E), R1336mzz(E) and R1234yf are compared over generator temperatures of 60–90°C, condenser temperatures of 30–45°C, and evaporator temperatures of − 10 to 10°C. The results show that increasing generator or condenser temperature reduces COP, whereas increasing evaporator temperature and useful preheating improves COP. Mechanical parameters primarily scale cooling capacity because cooling output and required input increase in broadly similar proportions; consequently, they have little influence on COP under the idealized assumptions. R22 and R32 provide the highest calculated performance in most cases, while low-global-warming-potential fluids offer environmental advantages but lower predicted capacity under the investigated conditions. The findings establish design relationships for matching thermodynamic states to free-piston geometry and identify heat recovery, fluid selection, and operating temperatures as the principal levers for improving system-level efficiency.

title: Voltage-Gated Ionic Conductivity in Ultranarrow Confinement
summary: Abstract Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular d
content: Abstract Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.

title: Non-Targeted Quantitative Profiling of the Molecular Composition and Relative Distribution of Water-Soluble Organic Carbon from Biomass Pyrolysis Smoke Using GC×GC-TOF-MS
summary: Biomass pyrolysis produces abundant water-soluble organic carbons (WSOC) that influence the environmental behavior and utilization potential of pyrolysis products. However, the molecular-level formation mechanisms and physicochemical fracti
content: Biomass pyrolysis produces abundant water-soluble organic carbons (WSOC) that influence the environmental behavior and utilization potential of pyrolysis products. However, the molecular-level formation mechanisms and physicochemical fractionation processes of pyrolytic WSOC remain poorly understood. This study systematically characterized the molecular composition, redox properties, aromaticity and volatility distribution of WSOC generated during biomass pyrolysis to elucidate its formation pathways and aqueous-phase partitioning behavior. The results showed that among the 274 chromatographic peaks detected, 158 were tentatively assigned, with aromatic/phenolic compounds contributing the largest relative peak area (46.5%), followed by hydrocarbons (26.4%) and esters (16.9%). Aromatic/phenolic compounds were dominant, highlighting the important contribution of lignin-derived products, while the occurrence of diverse oxygenated compounds reflects the thermal transformation of cellulose and hemicellulose. Most WSOC molecules exhibited moderate molecular size and unsaturation, with carbon oxidation states (OS-C) ranging from -2 to 0, indicating predominantly reduced characteristics. Volatility analysis revealed a negative relationship between molecular weight and volatility, with volatility-dependent fractionation controlling WSOC enrichment in the aqueous phase. Highly volatile low-molecular-weight compounds were preferentially released into the gas phase, whereas intermediate-volatility polar compounds containing hydroxyl, carbonyl, and ester functionalities were efficiently condensed and retained in the aqueous phase. This study provides molecular-level insights into the coupling between pyrolysis pathways, molecular properties, and aqueous partitioning of WSOC, contributing to improved understanding of biomass pyrolysis-derived soluble organic matter and its potential toxicity and environmental implications.

title: Case Report: Running through transplant: preserved aerobic capacity in an elite endurance athlete after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation
summary: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) imposes profound hematologic, inflammatory, and immunologic stress, and survivors typically show reduced cardiorespiratory fitness that may be further compromised by chronic graft-versus-h
content: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) imposes profound hematologic, inflammatory, and immunologic stress, and survivors typically show reduced cardiorespiratory fitness that may be further compromised by chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGvHD) and corticosteroid therapy. Competitive, performance-oriented endurance training through these phases has not been described. We report the longitudinal clinical and training course of a 54-year-old elite endurance runner with previously treated Hodgkin lymphoma who resumed structured treadmill exercise on Day +1 after matched-sibling allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma transformed from follicular lymphoma. Daily physiologic training data were aligned with transplant milestones, donor chimerism, donor lymphocyte infusions (DLI), and immunosuppression, and serial cardiopulmonary exercise testing was performed before and after HCT. The patient exercised through marrow aplasia and progressed to timed running within 100 days; he recorded a 5K of 17:55 (Day +314) and a 10K of 41:00 (Day +340), both during active cGvHD on prednisone plus cyclosporine. Directly measured peak oxygen uptake (VO 2 peak) was 75.8 mL/kg/min before HCT and 71.5 mL/kg/min at 7 months post-HCT. Oxygen uptake (VO 2 ) at the first ventilatory threshold (VT1) was 53.0, 48.0, and 42.4 mL/kg/min before HCT and at 7 and 20 months post-HCT, respectively. VO 2 at the second ventilatory threshold (VT2) was 66.0 and 59.9 mL/kg/min before HCT and at 7 months post-HCT, respectively. The 20-month assessment was submaximal; therefore, VO 2 peak was not determined. This case illustrates that exceptional aerobic capacity and high-level endurance performance can be maintained during recovery from allogeneic HCT, including during corticosteroid-treated cGvHD, with continued structured training.
