title: Spin-Coating-Speed-Dependent Structural and Optical Properties of Open-Air-Processed MAPbI 3 Thin Films with Bandgap-Constrained SCAPS-1D Sensitivity Analysis
summary: Abstract Spin coating offers an accessible route for depositing metal-halide perovskite absorbers, but interactions among rotational speed, solvent removal and crystallization complicate ambient process optimization. This study examined the
content: Abstract Spin coating offers an accessible route for depositing metal-halide perovskite absorbers, but interactions among rotational speed, solvent removal and crystallization complicate ambient process optimization. This study examined the effects of spin-coating speed (2000–5000 rpm) on the structural and optical properties of open-air-processed methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI₃) films and used measured optical bandgaps to constrain SCAPS-1D simulations. Films were deposited from a 1.25 M precursor using ethyl acetate antisolvent treatment and annealed at 110°C for 10 min under controlled conditions of 24.4°C and 41.5% relative humidity. X-ray diffraction confirmed tetragonal MAPbI₃ with preferential (110) orientation and no detectable PbI₂ reflection. The structural response was non-monotonic. At 3000 rpm, the film exhibited the narrowest (110) peak (FWHM: 0.352°), largest Scherrer coherent-domain size (22.73 nm), lowest estimated microstrain (1.257 × 10⁻²) and lowest crystallographic dislocation-density parameter (1.936 × 10⁻³ nm⁻²). Thus, 3000 rpm produced the most favourable XRD-derived crystalline characteristics within the investigated range, although these metrics do not establish reduced electronic trap density, suppressed recombination or superior photovoltaic performance. Optical bandgaps ranged from 1.59–1.60 eV. In an otherwise fixed FTO/TiO₂/MAPbI₃/Spiro-OMeTAD/carbon model, the corresponding simulated efficiencies were 16.67% and 16.47%, respectively. Coordinated parameter optimization yielded a projected efficiency of 25.38%, with \(\:{V}_{oc}\) of 1.25 V, \(\:{J}_{sc}\) of 24.24 mA cm⁻² and fill factor of 83.61%. These results establish a process-specific structure–optical-property relationship, while the simulated outputs remain model-dependent projections requiring experimental device validation. The approach also illustrates how experimental measurements can inform device-level sensitivity analysis without overstating causal relationships.

title: Waste-to-zeolite pathways for industrial residue valorization, material flow integration, and end-of-waste considerations
source: Journal of Material Cycles and Waste Management
summary: Waste-derived zeolite synthesis is increasingly proposed as a route for converting large-scale residues into functional sorbents, ion exchangers, and catalysts. This review evaluates the conversion pathways as material-cycle processes rathe
content: Waste-derived zeolite synthesis is increasingly proposed as a route for converting large-scale residues into functional sorbents, ion exchangers, and catalysts. This review evaluates the conversion pathways as material-cycle processes rather than only as synthesis recipes. The literature is organised through a feedstock-synthesis-performance framework that links residue chemistry, mineralogy, reactive silicon and aluminium availability, impurity burden, conditioning route, zeolite framework outcome, application performance, and deployment constraints. The evidence shows that the bulk silicon and aluminium contents alone are insufficient predictors of zeolite formation, as reactive species may be locked in quartz, mullite, feldspar, talc, gehlenite, or calcium-bearing phases. Therefore, route selection must consider activation demand, alkali consumption, water use, solid-liquid separation, liquor recycle, residue fate, and product qualification. Quantitative comparisons showed that waste-derived zeolite routes can deliver useful adsorption, ion-exchange, and catalytic performance. However, sustainability claims depend on normalised inventories, product specifications, techno-economic analysis, life-cycle assessment, regeneration behaviour, and leachability. Future studies should prioritise pilot-scale mass balances, closed-loop reagent recovery, wastewater management, shaped-product performance, and application-specific release criteria.

title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole
summary: BACKGROUND: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg)
content: BACKGROUND: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged 'lake' at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. RESULTS: We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota, Thermoproteota, Planctomycetota, and Actinobacteriota. We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycling. We further supported these findings using the functional annotation of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and protein clusters showing enrichment of nitrification and halogen cycling genes, suggesting the presence of specialized degradation and biosynthetic pathways, directly connecting microbial metabolism to the observed geochemical conditions. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that the submerged acid lake contains specific microbially driven biogeochemical processes under acidified and low-oxygen conditions, providing a natural model for future extreme ocean acidification scenarios. With this multi‑omics approach, we were able to connect the microbial metabolism with this unique environment, thereby expanding our understanding of how both are interconnected. Video Abstract.

title: Poly(Glycolic Acid) and Copolymers of Glycolic Acid: Syntheses, Properties and Applications
summary: Abstract Poly(glycolic acid) (PGA) is one of the oldest synthetic biodegradable polyesters and has been produced on a technical scale since the mid-20th century. Its development was strongly driven by medical applications, particularly as a
content: Abstract Poly(glycolic acid) (PGA) is one of the oldest synthetic biodegradable polyesters and has been produced on a technical scale since the mid-20th century. Its development was strongly driven by medical applications, particularly as a resorbable surgical suture, leading to the commercialization of PGA-based products such as Dexon and Vicryl. PGA is primarily synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of glycolide, a method that provides high molecular weights and remains the dominant industrial route. Alternative synthetic approaches based on polycondensation have also been explored and are reviewed herein. Owing to its highly regular and polar structure, PGA exhibits exceptional properties, including high crystallinity, high melting temperature, excellent mechanical strength, and an outstanding barrier performance. However, its broader utilization is limited by challenges associated with monomer production costs, melt-processability, limited solubility, and rapid hydrolytic degradation. In addition to neat PGA, a wide range of glycolide-containing copolymers have attracted significant attention because their properties can be tailored for medical and pharmaceutical applications. This review summarizes the synthetic methods, structure−property relationships, and current as well as emerging applications of PGA and its copolymers from almost 300 references. Furthermore, the toxicity of the catalysts employed in the synthesis of PGA and its copolymers is discussed.

title: Lipase-rich fermented solids produced by wickerhamiella osmotolerans: direct application as biocatalysts for dairy wastewater treatment and integration with coagulation/flocculation/sedimentation
summary: Lipase-based bioprocesses are promising alternatives for the treatment of lipid-rich industrial effluents; however, enzyme recovery and purification steps may limit their practical application. In this study, lipase-rich fermented solids pr
content: Lipase-based bioprocesses are promising alternatives for the treatment of lipid-rich industrial effluents; however, enzyme recovery and purification steps may limit their practical application. In this study, lipase-rich fermented solids produced by Wickerhamiella osmotolerans under solid-state fermentation were evaluated as direct biocatalysts for dairy wastewater treatment. A total of 39 yeast isolates obtained from poultry slaughterhouse wastewater were screened for lipolytic activity. Five isolates with the highest enzymatic indices were selected for molecular identification and identified as Wickerhamiella osmotolerans based on sequencing of the D1/D2 region of the 26 S rDNA. Lipase production was evaluated through sequential experiments investigating particle size, substrate/support composition, moisture content, fermentation time, and inducer addition. Although 100% sunflower seed produced the highest lipolytic activity, the sunflower seed/rice husk mixture (1:1) was selected as a practical trade-off between enzyme production and the incorporation of an agro-industrial residue. Under the selected conditions of 60% initial moisture and 24 h of fermentation, this mixture reached 24.14 U g⁻¹ without external lipid inducers. The direct application of the fermented solid resulted in 65.4% apparent O&G removal but did not reduce turbidity. The subsequent C/F/S step reduced turbidity from 1190 to 693 NTU, corresponding to a stage-specific reduction of 41.8%, but did not provide additional O&G removal. These findings demonstrate a proof-of-concept strategy for simplifying lipase application by eliminating enzyme extraction steps and integrating microbial enzyme production with wastewater treatment.

title: Organizational strategies for ethical and sustainable AI implementation
summary: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified debate about its dual role as a driver of efficiency and a source of environmental, social, and ethical challenges. These challenges include the growing energy and water de
content: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified debate about its dual role as a driver of efficiency and a source of environmental, social, and ethical challenges. These challenges include the growing energy and water demands of data centers, hardware-related emissions and e-waste, data governance risks, workforce concerns, and increasing regulatory pressure. While prior research highlights AI’s sustainability potential, less is known about how organizations translate ethical and sustainability principles into concrete implementation strategies. This study examines responsible AI adoption under sustainability constraints, using the Technology-Organization-Environment framework extended with ESG and ethics considerations, and the Triple Bottom Line perspective to interpret outcomes. Empirical insights are based on five semi-structured expert interviews with senior executives, AI specialists, and sustainability professionals across industries and national contexts. The findings show that AI supports efficiency, predictive analytics, and sustainability monitoring, but responsible deployment depends on readiness, data quality, workforce capabilities, and governance structures.

title: Directional orthorhombic phase precipitation and coarsening enable strength-ductility synergy in compositionally modified Ti 2 AlNb-based alloys
summary: Ti2AlNb-based intermetallic alloys are promising candidates for aero-engine hot-end components, yet their intrinsic covalent bonding inevitably causes a strength-ductility trade-off that limits their engineering applications. Herein, a nove
content: Ti2AlNb-based intermetallic alloys are promising candidates for aero-engine hot-end components, yet their intrinsic covalent bonding inevitably causes a strength-ductility trade-off that limits their engineering applications. Herein, a novel strategy integrating directional O-phase precipitation and coarsening is proposed to achieve excellent strength-ductility synergy in newly designed Ti2AlNb-based alloys. Four alloys with reduced Al and Nb contents were designed, three of which were further modified with Zr and Mo. Among them, the as-cast Ti-20Al-21Nb-2Zr-0.5Mo (A2) alloy exhibited the most favorable tensile performance. Severe cold rolling coupled with short-term direct aging at 880 °C induces the directional precipitation of dense and fine lamellar O-phase. Dislocations and banded substructures provide abundant heterogeneous nucleation sites, while local stress fields and B2/β texture constrain lamellar growth to form a well-aligned microstructure. Prolonged aging primarily enlarges interlamellar spacing, accompanied by a slight decrease in the O-phase area fraction, whereas elevated aging temperatures lead to O-phase coarsening and partial dissolution. These unique microstructural evolutions effectively break the inherent performance bottleneck. The cold-rolled A2 alloy aged at 880 °C for 30 min exhibits superior comprehensive properties, with a room-temperature yield strength of 1,046 MPa, tensile strength of 1,223 MPa, elongation of 9.6%, and a high-temperature tensile strength of 943 MPa at 650 °C, outperforming most previously reported Ti2AlNb alloys. The coordinated deformation mechanisms stem from concentrated dislocations in B2/β channels and interfacial dislocation pile-ups ensuring high strength, while continuous B2/β channels accommodate plastic strain. This work provides a feasible guideline for composition optimization and short-process manufacturing of high-performance Ti2AlNb alloys.

title: Geochemical characteristics and origin of the oil residues in the fractured basement reservoir rocks in the Habban oilfield, Shabwah depression of Southeast Yemen
summary: Fractured basement rock, located in the Habban oilfield, Shabwah depression, is one of the major oil-bearing reservoir rocks made in recent years. However, the geochemical characteristics of the discovered oils from the fractured basement r
content: Fractured basement rock, located in the Habban oilfield, Shabwah depression, is one of the major oil-bearing reservoir rocks made in recent years. However, the geochemical characteristics of the discovered oils from the fractured basement reservoir, origin of organic matter (OM), depositional environment conditions, thermal maturity, and oil-source rock correlation remain unclear. This study presents the first comprehensive geochemical investigation of the oil filling the micro fractures of the basement reservoir rock in the Habban oilfield, integrating biomarker characterization of the oils, molecular structural data of their oil-asphaltene and 1-D basin modeling analysis of oil generation and expulsion histories. The studied oil residues from the host fractured basement rock is characterized by high total organic carbon (TOC) and free hydrocarbon (S 1 ) values up to 2.75 wt% and 5.17 mg HC/g rock, respectively, resulting in high oil saturation index (OSI) values of more than 40 mg HC/ g TOC and up to 188 mg HC/ g TOC. The elevated OSI and S 1 values indicate that the oil residues in the host fractured basement rock are migrated from mature source rock. Integrated biomarker data from the saturated fraction of the oil residues suggest that these oil residues originated from marine source rock that deposited under suboxic to anoxic conditions, and containing mixed planktonic and bacterial organic matter, reflecting mainly Type II kerogen. This finding of Type II kerogen input into marine source rock is supported by the molecular structure (MS) characteristics of the corresponding oil-asphaltene fraction. The geochemical signatures of the oil residues and molecular structure of their asphaltene are consistent with the oil-source rocks of the Lam and Meem succession. However, the maturity-biomarker indicators of the examined oil residues provide evidences of mature source rock, reaching mainly peak mature of the oil-generative window. 1D basin modeling shows that the Meem source rock is more mature than Lam source rock, reaching late mature of oil-generation phase, with Easy %Ro values of up to 1.10. The extensive maturity level of the Meem source rock results in an extensive kerogen conversion ratio (TR) of up to 78%, and high oil holding capacity, promoting the development of high pressure and create micro-fracture pores within the Meem source rock. The basin model results also show that the significant amounts of generated oil have been expelled from the Meem source rock since Late Cretaceous to Late Oligocene, and then moved and migrated downward from the overlying Meem source rock into the underlying porous basement reservoir through micro-fracture network system, and also vertically migrated along faults upward to shallow sandstone reservoir of the Lam Member. These findings reduce exploration risk and highlight that the mature Meem source rock in deeper stratigraphic levels is regarded as a main source rock for most of oil exploration and pro

title: Ultrahigh Energy Storage in Supramolecular Biomass‐Based Dielectrics
summary: ABSTRACT Biomass‐based polymer dielectrics exhibit considerable potential for sustainable capacitive energy storage applications. However, they are limited by a relatively small discharged energy density (<20 J cm −3 ) with low efficiency c
content: ABSTRACT Biomass‐based polymer dielectrics exhibit considerable potential for sustainable capacitive energy storage applications. However, they are limited by a relatively small discharged energy density (<20 J cm −3 ) with low efficiency compared to their state‐of‐the‐art petroleum‐derived counterparts. Herein, a green supramolecular architecture design is implemented by introducing poly (arylene ether urea) (PEEU) into a cyanoethyl cellulose (CEC) matrix. Hydrogen‐bond‐mediated PEEU supramolecular association is integrated with micrometer‐scale PEEU‐rich microdomains and abundant CEC/PEEU interfacial regions, collectively promoting structural densification and suppressing charge migration. Consequently, our supramolecular dielectric composites exhibit a remarkable breakdown strength of 758 MV m −1 and a superior discharged energy density of 36.4 J cm −3 with an efficiency of 76.9%, well surpassing currently existing biomass‐based counterparts. This work provides a rational supramolecular assembly framework to fabricate environmentally sustainable dielectrics featuring outstanding room‐temperature energy‐storage performance and self‐cealing capability for next‐generation capacitors.

title: Global wind farms are associated with land use dependent asymmetric warming and ecological changes
summary: Abstract Wind farms are crucial for decarbonization, but their effects on the atmosphere and ecosystems remain unclear. Here, we use explainable machine learning and structural equation modeling applied to decades of observations from tens
content: Abstract Wind farms are crucial for decarbonization, but their effects on the atmosphere and ecosystems remain unclear. Here, we use explainable machine learning and structural equation modeling applied to decades of observations from tens of thousands of wind farms worldwide. The findings show that global wind farms are associated with land-use-dependent asymmetric warming and ecological changes. Nighttime land surface temperature increases by 0.041–0.125 °C and tends to level off when installed capacity reaches approximately 300 megawatts under observational aggregation. Based on the quantitative comparison, wind farm areas show a mean reduction of 1.75 grams of carbon per square meter in Net Primary Productivity. These relationships vary by land use: wind farms in forests show reduced evapotranspiration and lower vegetation productivity, whereas croplands and barren lands manifest altered moisture fluxes and cooling-related associations. Structural equation modeling supports the hypothesized pathways linking wind farms, vegetation responses, evapotranspiration, and land use. These results highlight the potential value of land-use-specific siting for sustainable wind energy development.

title: Multiscale Study on the Bearing Performance and Failure of Interference‐Fit CFRP /Al Blind‐Riveted Joints
summary: ABSTRACT This study establishes a sequential multiscale numerical framework to investigate how interference affects the mechanical properties and damage behavior of single‐lap interference‐fit CFRP/Al blind‐riveted joints, with experimental
content: ABSTRACT This study establishes a sequential multiscale numerical framework to investigate how interference affects the mechanical properties and damage behavior of single‐lap interference‐fit CFRP/Al blind‐riveted joints, with experimental validation through quasi‐static tensile tests and SEM observations. First, representative volume elements (RVEs) are constructed at the microscale, and a bottom‐up homogenization scheme calibrates the macroscopic elastic moduli of the laminates. A refined finite element (FE) model is then developed at the macroscale to characterize the load–displacement responses of the joints under various interference fit levels. Subsequently, a top‐down sequential framework is adopted to map the macroscopic strain histories extracted from selected hole‐edge elements onto the stochastic RVE model, enabling the evaluation of progressive damage mechanisms. This strategy balances high computational efficiency and mechanistic analysis of constituent‐scale failure modes. Macroscopic results indicate that moderate interference enhances the ultimate strength of the joint, whereas excessive interference induces preexisting damage on the hole wall and thus impairs the load‐bearing capacity. Microscopic observations reveal that microcracks preferentially nucleate in fiber‐rich, resin‐poor microregions, and the dominant failure modes depend on the local loading orientation.

title: DIFFERENCES IN HEMOGLOBIN LEVELS BETWEEN FIRST- AND THIRD-TRIMESTER PREGNANT WOMEN AT PUBLIC HEALTH CENTER I EAST DENPASAR
summary: Hemoglobin levels in pregnant women may decrease with advancing gestational age due to a greater increase in plasma volume than in erythrocyte mass. Studies comparing changes in hemoglobin levels between the first and third trimesters in th
content: Hemoglobin levels in pregnant women may decrease with advancing gestational age due to a greater increase in plasma volume than in erythrocyte mass. Studies comparing changes in hemoglobin levels between the first and third trimesters in the same respondents remain limited. This study aimed to determine the difference in hemoglobin levels between the first and third trimesters among pregnant women at Public Health Center I East Denpasar. This quantitative study used an analytical observational design with a paired comparative longitudinal approach and was conducted in March 2026. The sample consisted of 30 pregnant women selected using accidental sampling. First-trimester data were obtained from medical records, whereas third-trimester data were obtained through venous blood examination using a Micros ES-60 Hematology Analyzer. Data were analyzed descriptively, tested for normality using the Shapiro–Wilk test, and subsequently analyzed using a paired-samples t-test. The mean hemoglobin level in the first trimester was 12.85 g/dL, and all respondents were classified as having normal hemoglobin levels. In the third trimester, the mean hemoglobin level was 10.38 g/dL; 23 respondents were classified as having low hemoglobin levels, while 7 respondents had normal levels. The mean decrease in hemoglobin level was 2.47 g/dL. The data were normally distributed with a p-value of 0.053, while the paired-samples t-test showed p < 0.001. There was a significant difference in hemoglobin levels between the first and third trimesters. Regular hemoglobin monitoring is recommended to support the prevention of anemia during pregnancy.

title: Gallium induces an RNR-associated nucleotide crisis and sensitizes osteosarcoma cells to cisplatin
summary: Abstract Gallium (Ga) exhibits antitumor activity, but the mechanisms underlying its cytotoxicity in osteosarcoma remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated gallium nitrate using LC–MS metabolomics, 13 C 2 -glutamine tracing, iron-r
content: Abstract Gallium (Ga) exhibits antitumor activity, but the mechanisms underlying its cytotoxicity in osteosarcoma remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated gallium nitrate using LC–MS metabolomics, 13 C 2 -glutamine tracing, iron-rescue experiments, DNA synthesis and damage assays, DepMap dependency analysis, and density functional theory (DFT) modelling. In MG-63 osteosarcoma cells, gallium depleted glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathway intermediates while increasing several ribonucleotide monophosphates and nucleosides and reducing dTTP, consistent with disrupted deoxynucleotide supply. DepMap analysis revealed broad RRM1 and RRM2 dependencies in osteosarcoma models. Gallium reduced EdU incorporation, increased DNA damage detected by alkaline comet assay, and expanded the low-DNA-content/sub-G1 population without clear phase-specific arrest. Iron supplementation rescued gallium-associated loss of viability, whereas cystine, selenium, and ferrostatin-1 did not, arguing against canonical ferroptosis as the dominant death mechanism under these conditions. 13 C 2 -glutamine tracing showed depletion of glutamine, glutamate, and glutathione, with an increased fractional contribution of labeled glutathione driven largely by loss of the unlabeled pool. DFT cluster modelling supported the geometric feasibility of Ga accommodation within an RNR R2-like metal centre. Finally, gallium enhanced cisplatin cytotoxicity within defined concentration ranges, and exogenous deoxynucleosides partially rescued the combination effect. Together, these findings identify an iron-dependent, RNR-associated nucleotide-metabolic vulnerability that links gallium exposure to impaired DNA synthesis and enhanced cisplatin sensitivity in osteosarcoma.

title: Impact of different surface conditioning protocols on fracture resistance of monolithic zirconia vonlay restorations
summary: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to evaluate and compare the influence of three different surface conditioning protocols on the fracture resistance of maxillary premolars restored with monolithic multilayer zirconia vonlay restorat
content: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to evaluate and compare the influence of three different surface conditioning protocols on the fracture resistance of maxillary premolars restored with monolithic multilayer zirconia vonlay restorations fabricated from two zirconia materials. METHODS: Forty-eight maxillary premolars were prepared for zirconia vonlay restorations and allocated to two groups (n = 24) according to zirconia type: Group I (C): Cercon xt ML, and Group II (K): KATANA YML. Each group was further divided into three subgroups (n = 8) based on surface treatment: subgroup (A): airborne particle abrasion; subgroup (L): Er: YAG laser; and subgroup (E): hot chemical etching. Following cementation, all specimens were subjected to 10,000 thermocycles. Axial loading was applied using a universal testing machine. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA and Bonferroni's post-hoc test, with one-way ANOVA conducted for each factor. RESULTS: Two-way ANOVA demonstrated that the surface treatment had a significant effect on fracture resistance (P < 0.0001), whereas the main effect of zirconia material was not statistically significant (P = 0.229). The hot chemical etching KATANA YML subgroup recorded the highest mean values, 1476.25 (177.33) N, while the airborne particle abrasion and Cercon xt ML subgroup showed the lowest mean values, 1053.33 (172.78) N. CONCLUSION: The fracture resistance values of both zirconia materials were within the accepted range for clinical application. Hot chemical etching resulted in significantly higher fracture resistance than airborne particle abrasion and Er: YAG laser treatment, while no significant difference was found between the two zirconia materials.

title: ZnCl2-Catalyzed Acylation of Dextrose: Process Optimization, Kinetic Modelling and Pharmaceutical Prospects
summary: Acylation of dextrose (D-glucose) provides a reversible strategy for modulating sugar solubility by converting the highly hydrophilic polyhydroxyl molecule into a lipophilic, water-insoluble peracetate that can be readily regenerated to the
content: Acylation of dextrose (D-glucose) provides a reversible strategy for modulating sugar solubility by converting the highly hydrophilic polyhydroxyl molecule into a lipophilic, water-insoluble peracetate that can be readily regenerated to the parent sugar through deacylation. This reversible acylation-deacylation approach is attractive for carbohydrate processing and serves as a versatile synthetic platform for the preparation of glycoconjugate prodrugs with improved pharmaceutical properties. In the present study, the acylation of dextrose with acetic anhydride was investigated using zinc chloride as a Lewis acid catalyst. The effects of catalyst loading (0.05-1.0 g), reaction time (5-60 min) and temperature (30-90 ºC) were independently evaluated, while dextrose conversion and α/β-D-glucose 2,3,4,5,6-pentaacetate selectivity were quantified by GC-MS. A comparative screening of four Lewis acid catalysts (AlCl3, CuCl2, FeCl3 and ZnCl2) revealed that ZnCl2 gave the best performance. Under optimized conditions it achieved 86.05% dextrose conversion with 95.57% selectivity towards the desired α-anomer. The kinetic analysis revealed that the reaction follows a second-order rate law (R2 = 0.9544) with an apparent rate constant of (3.0 ± 0.2) × 10–3 L mol–1 min–1, which is consistent with a bimolecular Lewis acid-catalyzed acylation mechanism. The progressive conversion of the kinetically favoured β-anomer towards the thermodynamically more stable α-anomer supports the role of Lewis acid catalysis in promoting anomeric equilibration.

title: Arrhenius-Based Capacity and Dispatch Optimization of a Wind–Photovoltaic–Storage Microgrid Using Task-Preserving, Degradation-Aware Refinement
summary: Abstract Feasibility repair can change the state-of-charge (SOC) trajectory used to evaluate battery degradation. We develop a cost–carbon–degradation model for a grid-connected wind–photovoltaic–storage microgrid. After correcting each sch
content: Abstract Feasibility repair can change the state-of-charge (SOC) trajectory used to evaluate battery degradation. We develop a cost–carbon–degradation model for a grid-connected wind–photovoltaic–storage microgrid. After correcting each schedule to meet a common daily terminal SOC, a degradation-aware refinement shifts charging and discharging between admissible hours while preserving their respective daily energy totals. An improved nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) combining differential evolution, adaptive variation and structured local search uses 24,000 objective evaluations in each of 12 independent runs. Across the 12 runs, the improved NSGA-II achieved a mean inverted generational distance (IGD) of 0.02840 ± 0.00168 and a normalized hypervolume (HV) of 0.84665 ± 0.00444. The corresponding mean values for standard NSGA-II were 0.08489 and 0.72758. The representative solution from the run closest to the median IGD is rated at 40.49 MW/114.97 MWh. Across 12 candidate pairs with matched ratings and daily charge and discharge totals, refinement reduces modeled first-year capacity loss by 10.70% ± 1.11% on average. Fixed-trajectory sensitivity across 17 degradation-model settings gives mean reductions in modeled first-year loss of 0.39% to 16.19%; two candidates instead show increased loss in the anchored linear case. These results show that the degradation benefit of temporal redistribution depends on the assumed aging model and that feasibility-repair choices can affect degradation assessment.

title: Dual Molecular Confinement Engineering of Graphene Oxide‐Based Monovalent Cation‐Selective Membrane for Osmotic Energy Harvesting and Chlor‐Alkali Process
summary: ABSTRACT Ion‐selective membranes are widely employed to extract energy and resources from seawater, yet their performance is significantly compromised by divalent ions present in natural seawater. Here, we present a graphene oxide‐based mon
content: ABSTRACT Ion‐selective membranes are widely employed to extract energy and resources from seawater, yet their performance is significantly compromised by divalent ions present in natural seawater. Here, we present a graphene oxide‐based monovalent cation‐selective membrane with high ion selectivity and permeability that can reject divalent ions by leveraging steric exclusion within nanoconfined interlayers. The graphene oxide nanochannels are dual‐confined with charged small molecules tannic acid and the amphiphilic molecule through cross‐linking and electrostatic modulation, respectively. The obtained membrane achieves ion selectivity ratios of 87 for K + /Mg 2+ , 74 for Na + /Mg 2+ , and 67 for Li + /Mg 2+ . The output power density can reach 30.2 W m −2 under a 50‐fold salinity gradient in osmotic energy harvesting, with a conversion efficiency of 43.8%. Furthermore, the membrane can be used in the chlor‐alkali process, enabling the production of high‐purity sodium hydroxide with brine containing divalent ions. This study provides a novel perspective for the development of next‐generation ion‐selective membranes, with potential applications in advanced resource and energy recovery technologies.

title: An eco-friendly glucose-based dust suppressant for heavy-duty haul roads in open-pit coal mines during high-temperature seasons
summary: Abstract Dust from heavy-duty haul roads in open-pit coal mines poses a serious environmental challenge, particularly under high-temperature summer conditions. In this study, an eco-friendly dust suppressant was developed based on physicoch
content: Abstract Dust from heavy-duty haul roads in open-pit coal mines poses a serious environmental challenge, particularly under high-temperature summer conditions. In this study, an eco-friendly dust suppressant was developed based on physicochemical characterization of three representative dust types (coal, loess, and rock-soil) from the Haerwusu Mine. Wettability and chemical analyses revealed that coal dust exhibited the poorest wettability, whereas loess and rock-soil dusts exhibited superior wetting behavior. A formulation comprising industrial-grade glucose as the base material, SDBS as the surfactant, and glycerol/NaCl as moisture-regulating agents was optimized via single-component and orthogonal experiments. The optimal composition was determined as 30% glucose, 0.05% SDBS, 2% glycerol, and 2% NaCl. Molecular dynamics simulations elucidated the adsorption configurations and wetting mechanisms of the suppressant on quartz and coal surfaces. Field validation under actual summer conditions demonstrated that a single suppressant application at 1 L/m 2 maintained a noticeable dust suppression effect for approximately 5 h at temperatures up to 54 °C under normal truck operations during this field test, and the effect could last up to three days when combined with reduced routine watering. This work presents a sustainable, cost-effective, and operationally viable strategy for dust mitigation on haul roads in open-pit coal mines during high-temperature seasons.

title: Oxygen-Vacancy Engineering Coupled with In Situ Spinel Reconstruction Enables Fast Electronic and Ionic Transport in Li-Rich Layered Cathodes
summary: Lithium-rich Mn-based cathodes possess exceptionally high energy-storage potential but suffer from severe voltage decay, sluggish reaction kinetics, and structural instability associated with lattice oxygen loss. Herein, a malic-acid-assist
content: Lithium-rich Mn-based cathodes possess exceptionally high energy-storage potential but suffer from severe voltage decay, sluggish reaction kinetics, and structural instability associated with lattice oxygen loss. Herein, a malic-acid-assisted surface engineering strategy is developed to simultaneously induce oxygen vacancies and an in-situ spinel reconstruction layer on Li 1.2 Mn 0.54 Ni 0.13 Co 0.13 O 2 . Under optimized treatment conditions (pH = 2.5), a uniform ~ 30 nm spinel shell is formed, providing fast three-dimensional Li-ion transport channels and enhanced interfacial stability. Combined experimental investigations and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies not only facilitate the formation of the spinel phase but also trigger electronic structure reconfiguration. The introduced vacancies increase the electronic states near the Fermi level, eliminate the band gap, and promote metallic-like conductivity. Moreover, the Li-ion migration barrier is significantly reduced from 0.67 to 0.38 eV. COHP analysis demonstrates that this kinetic enhancement originates from the suppression of Li–O antibonding interactions and stabilization of the migration transition state. Owing to the synergistic effects of surface reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering, the optimized LMR-2.5@1 cathode delivers 290.7 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.1 C and retains 85.7% of its capacity after 600 cycles at 1 C. This work provides an effective route for developing durable, high-performance Li-rich cathodes through coupled structural and electronic regulation.

title: Decoding the Stacking and Arrangement of Aromatic Structures in Liptinite Macerals from Low-Rank Coal Utilizing HRTEM and 13C NMR
summary: Abstract The arrangement and differences of aromatic clusters of liptinite macerals in low-rank coal are considered as essential foundations for exploring their thermal conversion behavior and enabling clean utilization. Density gradient ce
content: Abstract The arrangement and differences of aromatic clusters of liptinite macerals in low-rank coal are considered as essential foundations for exploring their thermal conversion behavior and enabling clean utilization. Density gradient centrifugation was used to enrich liptinite macerals (cutinite, sporinite, barkinite, and resinite) in four low-rank coals (Ro,max = 0.52–0.67%), and the purity of liptinite macerals could reach over 90%. The aromatic clusters and carbon skeleton structure of liptinite macerals were evaluated using a high resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) and nuclear magnetic resonance (13C NMR) to reveal chemical structural and aggregated structural differentiation. The results of 13C NMR showed that the relative content of aliphatic carbon was approximately 56.60–77.59%, among which the resinite was the highest and the sporinite was the lowest. The aromatic carbon and oxygen-substituted aromatic carbon showed the opposite trend. The bridgehead carbon index (χb) of the liptinite macerals was between 0 and 0.25, indicating that the aromatic structures were mainly composed of benzene and naphthalene. The HRTEM results showed significant differences in the length, orientation, tortuosity, and stacking pattern of the aromatic layers for the liptinite macerals. The size of the aromatic layers in the sporinite was relatively long with an average of 0.502 nm, good orientation, low curvature, and abundant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The aromatic layers were mainly composed of screw dislocation geometry and T-shaped structures. The aromatic layers of cutinite had a medium size (0.443 nm) with a mixed feature of local order and overall disorder. The resinite had the shortest aromatic layers (0.380 nm), random orientation, and disordered stacking. Overall, the resinite and cutinite had hydrogen-rich and oxygen-poor characteristics, while sporinite had a relatively developed aromatic ring structure, and barkinite was in between the cutinite and sporinite.

title: Arabidopsis TRB Proteins Promote ROS Detoxification for Ethanol-Enhanced Salt Stress Tolerance
summary: Soil salinization is a major threat to global agricultural productivity. Developing strategies to alleviate the effects of soil salinization is essential for maintaining stable and sustainable food production under climate change conditions
content: Soil salinization is a major threat to global agricultural productivity. Developing strategies to alleviate the effects of soil salinization is essential for maintaining stable and sustainable food production under climate change conditions. We previously showed that ethanol enhances Arabidopsis salt stress tolerance by promoting reactive oxygen species (ROS) detoxification through ASCORBATE PEROXIDASE (AtAPX1/2) activation. However, ethanol induces the expression of many genes beyond AtAPX1/2. Moreover, the transcriptional mechanisms underlying ethanol-mediated stress tolerance remain unclear. In this study, we identified TELOMERE REPEAT BINDING (TRB) proteins as regulators of ethanol-enhanced salt stress tolerance. Transcriptome and qRT-PCR analyses showed that TRBs regulate the expression of AtCSD1, AtCSD2, and AtCCS, which encode Cu/ZnSODs and a copper chaperone. Ethanol increased Cu/ZnSOD activity, whereas csd1 and ccs mutants were sensitive to salt stress and accumulated superoxide, even after ethanol treatment. Thus, Cu/ZnSOD-mediated detoxification contributes to ethanol-induced stress tolerance. ChIP assays showed that AtTRB3 associates with AtCSD1, AtCSD2, and AtCCS, and that ethanol treatment enhanced H4K5 acetylation at these loci. Ethanol also increased global H4 acetylation levels, suggesting that ethanol metabolism may contribute to histone acetylation. Accordingly, AtTRB proteins likely promote Cu/ZnSOD-dependent ROS detoxification through chromatin-associated gene activation, thereby contributing to ethanol-mediated salinity tolerance in Arabidopsis seedlings.

title: Cosmic-ray B/C, B/O, and C/O flux ratios from a decade of DAMPE data with machine learning
summary: Accurate measurements of secondary cosmic-ray (CR) fluxes offer essential information about how high-energy particles propagate and interact throughout the Galaxy. Primary CR species, notably carbon and oxygen nuclei, undergo spallation rea
content: Accurate measurements of secondary cosmic-ray (CR) fluxes offer essential information about how high-energy particles propagate and interact throughout the Galaxy. Primary CR species, notably carbon and oxygen nuclei, undergo spallation reactions with the interstellar medium and produce lighter secondary nuclei. Among these secondaries, boron stands out for its relative abundance, and its energy spectrum is a valuable probe for studying CR propagation and interaction processes. The DArk Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE) has been in orbit since December 2015 and operates the deepest calorimeter currently deployed in space for CR studies, allowing direct spectral measurements up to hundreds of TeV. In this work, the boron-to-carbon, boron-to-oxygen and carbon-to-oxygen ratios measured from a decade of DAMPE activity are presented. In particular, the usage of machine-learning techniques over traditional methods for tracking and energy reconstruction enhances the accuracy and precision at the highest energies.

title: El fin de la hora dorada: un algoritmo desarrollado con inteligencia artificial para la descontaminación gastrointestinal tardía
source: Revista de Educaci�n e Investigaci�n en Emergencias
summary: Introducción: Cualquier tóxico en la luz gastrointestinal puede eliminarse mediante técnicas de descontaminación; sin embargo, el momento óptimo para ello sigue siendo motivo de debate.Objetivo: Proponer un algoritmo desarrollado con inteli
content: Introducción: Cualquier tóxico en la luz gastrointestinal puede eliminarse mediante técnicas de descontaminación; sin embargo, el momento óptimo para ello sigue siendo motivo de debate.Objetivo: Proponer un algoritmo desarrollado con inteligencia artificial para orientar sobre la aplicación tardía de estas técnicas.Material y métodos: Se utilizaron las IA generativas ChatGPT y Gemini, a las que se pidió que ponderaran los factores que influyen en el tiempo de vaciamiento gástrico.Posteriormente, se descartaron las variables con escasa evidencia, subjetivas o difíciles de evaluar.A continuación, se les pidió que desarrollaran un algoritmo cuya suma diera como resultado el tiempo en minutos necesario para realizar la descontaminación.Resultados: Se obtuvo un algoritmo con siete variables ponderadas con valores que oscilaban entre 0 y 120 minutos, lo que dio como resultado un tiempo mínimo de descontaminación de 120 minutos y un máximo de 660 (11 horas).El uso tardío de técnicas de descontaminación (> 2 horas) podría beneficiar a los pacientes que ingirieron fármacos de liberación prolongada, formadores de bezoares, anticolinérgicos, opiáceos o que promueven el espasmo pilórico.Conclusiones: Si bien las técnicas de descontaminación pueden provocar complicaciones y la información sobre su efectividad es insuficiente, podrían beneficiar a pacientes seleccionados.El algoritmo busca guiar a los médicos en urgencias, aunque antes de convertirse en una herramienta confiable debe ser validado mediante su aplicación clínica.Mientras ello ocurre, es necesario preguntarse si el paciente se beneficia más de la hora dorada o del algoritmo.

title: Biotechnological enhancement of l-asparaginase production by mutant Aspergillus flavus against MCF-7 breast cancer cells

content: This study aimed to concentrated on isolating the best fungal strain with the highest l -ASNase activity; strain l -ASNase-4 recorded 296.68 U/mg, was sequenced the genomic region/gene used for molecular identification, identified as Aspergillus flavus AFK3 using PCR and ITS region gene sequencing and submitted into NCBI accession no. OK086056. Sequential mutation induction using Acridin Orange (AO) and Ethidium Bromide (EtBr) were used in successive mutagenesis to increase strain A. flavus AFK3 l -ASNase production. The most successful mutant that produced l -ASNase was A. flavus AO-22, which showed l -ASNase activity two times (622.47 U/mg) over the wild type strain A. flavus AFK3. This study aimed to enhance enzyme production by employing a two-phase optimization strategy. The initial phase employed the One Factor at a Time (OFAT) approach to identify key process parameters (different carbon and nitrogen sources) influencing enzyme activity. OFAT analysis revealed that the best carbon and nitrogen source showed the highest levels of l -ASNase activity in the medium containing glucose and malt extract. In the subsequent phase, Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used for further optimization, involving 30 experiments to assess the combined effects of multiple factors. The Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used to identify the ideal conditions for l -ASNase expression. With a pH of 7, 1.5% glucose (a carbon source), 1.5% malt extract (a nitrogen source), and 3 days of incubation, the maximum l -ASNase activity for mutant A. flavus AO-22 was 1923.04 U/mg. Ammonium sulfate precipitation (35–75%), DEAE-cellulose ion exchange chromatography, and Sephadex G100 gel filtration were used to completely purify l -ASNase for the wild type A. flavus AFK3 and its mutant A. flavus AO-22.The purification process raised the purification fold of the purified l -ASNase by 12.79 and 13.09 times, resulting in protein yields of 34.70 and 36.26%; respectively, for the wild type A. flavus AFK3 and its mutant A. flavus AO-22. title: The Influence of Ammonia Port Injection on Combustion Dynamics and Particulate Matter Properties in a Gasoline Direct Injection Engine
summary: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising zero-carbon fuel for decarbonising transport, although its low reactivity limits its direct use. This study investigated the combustion and emission characteristics of an NH 3 -gasoline dual-fuel high-compress
content: Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a promising zero-carbon fuel for decarbonising transport, although its low reactivity limits its direct use. This study investigated the combustion and emission characteristics of an NH 3 -gasoline dual-fuel high-compression gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine. Gaseous NH 3 was port-injected up to a 30% energy ratio (AER), with gasoline direct-injected as a high-reactivity combustion promoter. Testing across various indicated loads revealed that uncalibrated NH 3 addition severely retarded combustion phasing and suppressed peak cylinder pressures. Applying the maximum brake torque (MBT) spark advance successfully recovered the optimal mass fraction burned phasing and indicated thermal efficiency. However, this necessary calibration exposes a critical emission. Although increasing the AER proportionally reduced engine-out CO 2 and soot particulates, the MBT advance required for combustion stability resulted in higher emissions through thermal and fuel-bound mechanisms. Furthermore, extended late-stage combustion durations indicate a potential unburned NH 3 slip. These findings demonstrate that although NH3 port injection is a viable GDI decarbonisation strategy, dynamic spark calibration is essential. Consequently, balancing thermodynamic efficiency with emission and particulate compliance will necessitate an advanced, combined aftertreatment system

title: Stevia Sweetened Golden Berry and Strawberry Wine as a Low Sugar Option with Antioxidant Activity and Good Sensory Acceptance for Diabetes Conscious Consumers
summary: Abstract Conventional fruit wines typically retain residual sugars that pose glycaemic risks for people living with diabetes, and co-fermenting underutilised fruits such as golden berry ( Physalis peruviana ) and strawberry ( Fragaria × ana
content: Abstract Conventional fruit wines typically retain residual sugars that pose glycaemic risks for people living with diabetes, and co-fermenting underutilised fruits such as golden berry ( Physalis peruviana ) and strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa ) to reduce sugar remains poorly documented. This study developed and evaluated a low-sugar, diabetic-friendly wine produced by co-fermenting golden berry and strawberry juices and sweetening the fermented product with stevia. Golden berry and strawberry juices were blended at three ratios—Blend A (40:60), Blend B (50:50) and Blend C (60:40, golden berry: strawberry)—pasteurised, inoculated with Saccharomyces cerevisiae , and fermented to dryness over 21 days before stabilisation with potassium metabisulfite and post-fermentation sweetening with stevia (4–6 g/L). Final pH, total soluble solids (°Brix), alcohol content, titratable acidity, antioxidant activity, and sensory acceptability (15 untrained panelists, 5-point hedonic scale) were assessed. Final pH values were 3.52 ± 0.02, 3.30 ± 0.02 and 3.29 ± 0.02 for Blends A, B and C, respectively, with corresponding °Brix of 0.50 ± 0.07, 0.30 ± 0.06 and 0.20 ± 0.05. Blend B (equal-ratio) recorded 10.05 ± 0.07% ABV and titratable acidity of 6.1 ± 0.07 g/L, and received the highest sensory scores for appearance (4.6 ± 0.3), taste (4.4 ± 0.3), flavour (4.5 ± 0.2), aroma (4.3 ± 0.3) and overall acceptability (4.6 ± 0.3). Antioxidant activity increased with golden berry proportion (Blend A 0.82, Blend B 0.95, Blend C 1.02 absorbance units). The equal-ratio formulation (Blend B) was the most acceptable prototype, combining a balanced acid–sweetness profile, moderate alcohol content, and antioxidant capacity. These findings indicate that stevia-sweetened golden berry–strawberry co-fermentation can yield a visually appealing, low-residual-sugar wine with functional potential for diabetes-conscious consumers, although the product should be regarded as an experimental prototype rather than a clinically validated diabetic beverage.

title: Selective, Simultaneous, and Sequential Deconstruction Strategies for Isocyanate Regeneration from Polyureas, Polyurethanes, and Their Mixtures
summary: Abstract Isocyanate recovery from end-of-life polyureas (PUEs), polyurethanes (PUs), and polyurethane-ureas (PUUEs) offers a potential route to valuable chemical feedstocks and reduced reliance on hazardous, economically burdensome, phosgen
content: Abstract Isocyanate recovery from end-of-life polyureas (PUEs), polyurethanes (PUs), and polyurethane-ureas (PUUEs) offers a potential route to valuable chemical feedstocks and reduced reliance on hazardous, economically burdensome, phosgene-based manufacturing. Herein, we report a deconstruction platform that regenerates isocyanates from PUEs/PUs/PUUEs under mild conditions (60 °C, 1 atm). Our approach leverages a Lewis-acid-driven deconstruction strategy in which thionyl chloride and B-chlorocatecholborane selectively cleave urea and urethane linkages, respectively, to regenerate isocyanates. Through this methodology, we demonstrate three deconstruction modes: (i) selective isocyanate regeneration from PUEs or PUs, (ii) simultaneous deconstruction of PUUEs and PUE/PU mixtures, and (iii) sequential reagent addition and deconstruction that directs isocyanate regeneration from urea or urethane linkages within mixed polymer streams. Recovered isocyanates were used to prepare second-generation PUEs and PUUEs with molecular weights and thermal properties comparable to the virgin counterparts. Overall, this work presents a deconstruction framework with controlled access to isocyanates and provides a foundation for future recycling strategies for PUEs, PUs, and PUUEs.

title: Confidence-Weighted Explainable Learning for Vessel Fuel-Consumption Analysis: A Multi-Model Comparative Framework
summary: Abstract Improving vessel energy efficiency is essential for reducing fuel consumption, greenhouse-gas emissions, and operating costs while supporting maritime decarbonisation objectives. Although advances in maritime analytics and machine
content: Abstract Improving vessel energy efficiency is essential for reducing fuel consumption, greenhouse-gas emissions, and operating costs while supporting maritime decarbonisation objectives. Although advances in maritime analytics and machine learning have improved vessel monitoring and fuel-consumption prediction, existing studies focus mainly on predictive accuracy and offer limited insight into the engineering, operational, and reliability factors that are associated with vessel energy demand. In addition, confidence-aware learning, uncertainty quantification, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and comparative evaluation of machine-learning models remain underexplored within maritime energy-intelligence research. This paper presents a confidence-weighted explainable learning framework for vessel fuel-consumption analysis and conducts a systematic comparison of five model families, namely Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Bayesian Ridge Regression (BRR), and Elastic Net, within a unified confidence-aware, explainable, and uncertainty-aware analytical architecture. Confidence integration is formulated as a reliability-weighted signal-fusion problem in which vessel-level confidence scores derived from heterogeneous data sources are incorporated directly into model learning. The Vessel Energy Efficiency Intelligence (VEEI) combines statistical driver analysis, duty-cycle intelligence, explainable machine learning, and uncertainty quantification to generate interpretable vessel-level energy intelligence. Experiments use a tidal River Thames inland-waterway dataset comprising 26 representative vessels and 131 engineering, operational, propulsion, fuel-consumption, and confidence-related attributes. Spearman rank correlation analysis identifies operating hours ($OH$) and installed engine power ($EP$) as the only statistically significant direct fuel-consumption drivers ($p<0.05$), while medium-cruise operation exhibits the strongest significant duty-cycle association with fuel demand. Among the evaluated models, Bayesian Ridge Regression achieves the highest predictive performance with an MAE of 41.23~L, an RMSE of 59.87~L, and an $R^{2}$ of 0.881, followed by XGBoost ($R^{2}=0.876$) and Random Forest ($R^{2}=0.873$). Confidence-weighted learning consistently improves predictive performance across all model families relative to their unweighted counterparts. Cross-model SHAP analysis identifies vessel draft and duty-cycle behaviour as the dominant explanatory factors, while uncertainty analysis consistently highlights vessels with elevated predictive uncertainty. The results show that operational utilisation, propulsion characteristics, vessel geometry, duty-cycle behaviour, and data reliability jointly influence vessel fuel consumption.
