title: Detection and classification of failed fiber reinforced polymer composite samples under mechanical loading using YOLO11 on microscopic SEM images
summary: The fracture surfaces of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and are slow to conduct. The fracture surfaces of FRP composit
content: The fracture surfaces of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and are slow to conduct. The fracture surfaces of FRP composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and slow to conduct. This proof-of-concept study compares an anchor-free single-stage detector, YOLO11n, to localize and classify six fractographic features: fiber breakage, fiber pull-out, fiber–matrix debonding, delamination, voids and matrix debris, in SEM images of carbon- and glass-fiber/epoxy specimens failed in tension, three-point bending and short-beam shear. The data consists of 125 images with 37 specimens, with 1318 labelled boxes following written labelling criteria. The weights for the model were initialized from COCO and were updated using the Adam optimizer. YOLO11n was able to obtain mAP@0.5 = 0.821 with 6.5 ms per image on a preliminary image-level split, but the number of images per subset is not consistent with 125 images and the results may be optimistic due to the fact that images from one specimen can be split into multiple subsets. Multiple seeds, a controlled comparison between it and YOLOv5n, YOLOv8n and YOLOv9t, per-class ablations and an error analysis were performed at the level of the specimen and the groups. The study shows that it is possible to apply the method of detector-assisted laboratory fractography. It does not provide any structural-health-monitoring or safety-critical capability, and is not tested on other material systems or imaging conditions.

title: Interphase‐controlled crystallization and Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization in hybrid polyether ether ketone–carbon fibre–TiB 2 composites
summary: Abstract Hybrid polyether ether ketone–carbon fibre–TiB 2 (PEEK–CF–TiB 2 ) composites were investigated to elucidate the coupled influence of TiB 2 loading (0–3 wt%) and melt‐mixing duration (30 and 40 min) on crystallization, microstructur
content: Abstract Hybrid polyether ether ketone–carbon fibre–TiB 2 (PEEK–CF–TiB 2 ) composites were investigated to elucidate the coupled influence of TiB 2 loading (0–3 wt%) and melt‐mixing duration (30 and 40 min) on crystallization, microstructural evolution and dielectric response. In the K30 series, TiB 2 promoted heterogeneous nucleation, increasing the crystallization temperature from 273.3 to 281.2 °C at K30‐2, while the crystalline fraction increased from 40.4% to a maximum of 49.9% at K30‐3. Prolonged mixing produced a distinct thermal response in the K40 series, characterized by a progressive increase in glass transition temperature from 155 to 174 °C and a non‐monotonic evolution of crystallinity. Field‐emission scanning electron microscopy revealed a finer and more spatially distributed particulate morphology after prolonged mixing, while X‐ray diffraction confirmed retention of the characteristic crystalline phases and processing‐dependent variation in PEEK crystalline ordering. Isothermal thermogravimetric analysis established high mass retention throughout the processing‐relevant thermal exposure. Dielectric spectroscopy showed an increase in dielectric constant from 487 to 836 at 1 kHz across the K40 series, accompanied by controlled loss‐tangent values and frequency‐dependent conductivity characteristic of an interfacial‐polarization‐dominated electrical regime. The combined thermal, morphological, crystallographic and dielectric results demonstrate that melt‐mixing duration regulates the balance between heterogeneous nucleation, segmental constraint and Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization in hybrid PEEK–CF–TiB 2 composites. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Economic Legal Instruments for Indonesia’s Green Economy Transition: Carbon Taxes, Energy Subsidies, and Green Investment Incentives
summary: Climate change and environmental degradation have prompted Indonesia’s green economy transition. This study evaluates carbon taxation, energy subsidy reform, and green investment incentives through a structured qualitative narrative-concept
content: Climate change and environmental degradation have prompted Indonesia’s green economy transition. This study evaluates carbon taxation, energy subsidy reform, and green investment incentives through a structured qualitative narrative-conceptual review of scholarly publications, policy reports, and institutional documents. Carbon taxation can support emissions control and clean-technology innovation, depending on policy design, institutional coordination, and emissions-reporting capacity. Energy subsidy reform can correct price distortions and create fiscal space for cleaner energy, provided distributional impacts are addressed through social protection. Green investment incentives may support low-carbon investment, although effectiveness depends on regulatory certainty, transparent governance, additionality, and measurable environmental outcomes. Aviation implications include sustainable aviation fuel, airport renewable energy and efficiency investments, and coordination with the International Civil Aviation Organization’s Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation. These are policy implications, not measured sectoral effects. Stronger legal frameworks, coherent green fiscal policies, and institutional capacity are needed to support an equitable transition.

title: Cement production and respiratory health in emerging and advanced economies within the sustainable development framework
summary: This study examines the sector-specific effects of cement production on chronic respiratory disease (CRD) mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) across emerging and advanced economies. The analysis incorporates particulate mat
content: This study examines the sector-specific effects of cement production on chronic respiratory disease (CRD) mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) across emerging and advanced economies. The analysis incorporates particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), carbon emissions, health expenditure, government effectiveness, urbanization, and economic complexity as conditioning macro factors. A balanced panel dataset from 2000 to 2022 is analysed using Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) to reveal distributional heterogeneity. Nonparametric kernel regression and panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE) are employed as complementary robustness checks. The empirical results reveal that cement production is significantly associated with Chronic respiratory disease (CRD) mortality and Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in emerging economies, with elasticities intensifying at higher disease-burden quantiles. In contrast, advanced economies show a weaker association between cement production and respiratory health outcomes, alongside a protective association with government effectiveness, particularly for CRD mortality. Based on these findings, the study proposes targeted regulatory modernisation and health-system strengthening to achieve sustainable industrial transition. By quantifying the sector-specific health costs of cement-driven industrialisation, the study contributes evidence directly relevant to the Sustainable Development Goals, notably SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

title: Education, public expenditure and carbon emission in Ghana: the moderating role of the Kyoto Protocol
summary: Purpose Education and government expenditure are increasingly recognized as key variables for climate policy. However, their effectiveness in African contexts as shaped by the Kyoto Protocol remains limited. This study addresses this gap by
content: Purpose Education and government expenditure are increasingly recognized as key variables for climate policy. However, their effectiveness in African contexts as shaped by the Kyoto Protocol remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the moderating role of the Kyoto Protocol on government expenditure impacts on carbon emissions in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach Employing the Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence and Technology framework, we analyse 32 years of time-series data (1990–2022) using fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) and autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) cointegration techniques. Findings From the FMOLS results, a 1% increase in education and government expenditure significantly reduces carbon emissions in Ghana by 0.0007% and 0.68%, respectively. The study further shows that the Kyoto Protocol negatively moderates the effect of government expenditure on carbon emissions. Other results show that industrialization, mineral rent and urbanization significantly and positively impact carbon emissions in Ghana. Practical implications The study recommends that Ghana should expand renewable energy education in primary curricula. This will minimize the benefit of renewable energy consumption knowledge deficit. Moreover, the government should increase green infrastructure expenditure to leverage Kyoto-driven efficiencies which align fiscal policy and Nationally Determined Contribution. This will potentially accelerate achievement of 2030 emissions targets. Originality/value This study examines the effect of education, government expenditure and Kyoto Protocol moderation in an African country, revealing country-specific policy pathways that panel studies obscure. This is justified because existing literature on the continent has shown the standalone effects of education and government expenditure on carbon emissions across sub-Saharan Africa, without the interaction effect of the Kyoto Protocol. The study fills this identified gap and demonstrates that international agreements reshape domestic policy effectiveness, a mechanism overlooked in existing literature.

title: Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Energy Management in Smart Renewable Microgrids
source: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
summary: The high penetration rates of renewable energy sources (RES) calls for more advanced and novel‌ technologies for The high penetration rates of renewable energy sources (RES) calls for more advanced and novel technologies for effective manag
content: The high penetration rates of renewable energy sources (RES) calls for more advanced and novel‌ technologies for The high penetration rates of renewable energy sources (RES) calls for more advanced and novel technologies for effective management of RES intermittency and variability․ Smart renewable microgrids have emerged as a potential solution for local controllable grids for distributed generation and grid resilience enhancement․ Hence‚ for successful operation‚ smart renewable microgrid systems require effective Real-Time Energy Management (R-TEM) strategies which can account for uncertainties introduced by renewable generation‚ variable load demand and operational constraints․ This paper provides the state-of-the-art review and proposes a Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence (MA-AI) based R-TEM solution for smart renewable microgrids․ We presents a system architecture of MA-AI‚ showing the profiles and interactions of specific agents‚ such as the Distributed Generator Agent‚ Energy Storage Agent‚ Load Agent‚ and Coordinator Agent․ In this paper‚ we define R-TEM problem with both cost minimizing and emission minimizing objective functions and operational constraints and then propose a MA-AI framework for implementing autonomous and adaptive decision-making based on Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient(MADDPG) model with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) / Transformers forecasting models and improved coordination strategies․ The system was implemented in Python-based simulation environment. The MARL algorithms were implemented using the OpenAI Gym framework‚ alongside the interaction of the code with the energy system models․ Simulations show that this approach improves considerably on rule-based strategies‚ yielding 22.8% cost savings cost savings‚ 17․3% more renewables penetration the grid operate independently and reliably with a 24․8% improvement as well as lowered the total carbon emissions by 18․5% by prioritizing renewable energy․ The paper provides insights on scalability‚ cyber-security‚ explainable AI (XAI)‚ and future work in agentic artificial intelligence‚ quantum AI and hybridizing agents with multi-energy systems (for example‚ electricity and heat)․ This reveals the promise of MA-AI technology for efficient‚ strong‚ and sustainable power management in the emerging ecosystem of smart renewable microgrids.

title: Translating Scope 3 Carbon Accounting Into Climate Disclosure in Maritime‐Port Ecosystems: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: ABSTRACT Maritime‐port ecosystems pose distinctive challenges for credible Scope 3 carbon accounting and climate disclosure because emissions, data and responsibilities are distributed across organizational boundaries. This study systematic
content: ABSTRACT Maritime‐port ecosystems pose distinctive challenges for credible Scope 3 carbon accounting and climate disclosure because emissions, data and responsibilities are distributed across organizational boundaries. This study systematically reviews 114 peer‐reviewed journal articles (84 from Scopus database and 30 supplementary studies identified through Google Scholar), combining bibliometric mapping with qualitative content analysis. The synthesis identifies three interconnected research areas: Scope 3 accounting and boundary‐setting; climate disclosure and accountability; and digital infrastructures and traceability. While existing research prioritizes emissions measurement, monitoring and decarbonization, less attention has been paid to disclosure credibility and distributed accountability. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes the transition from Scope 3 accounting to climate disclosure as a governance‐dependent translation process shaped by boundary‐setting and commensuration, data governance, verification and assurance and responsibility allocation. This study proposes a theory‐informed framework and a Theory, Context, Characteristics and Methodology (TCCM)–based agenda for future empirical research in fragmented value‐chain ecosystems.

title: Secondary Steel Producers in India and Draft National Steel Policy 2047 - Role and Challenges
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: India’s draft National Steel Policy (NSP) – Vision 2047 targets 604 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) of crude steel capacity and a fall in average emission intensity from 2.54 to 1.54 tCO₂ per tonne of crude steel. Roughly 2,200–2,550 second
content: India’s draft National Steel Policy (NSP) – Vision 2047 targets 604 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) of crude steel capacity and a fall in average emission intensity from 2.54 to 1.54 tCO₂ per tonne of crude steel. Roughly 2,200–2,550 secondary steel units, mostly induction-furnace (IF), electric-arc-furnace (EAF), sponge-iron (DRI) and re-rolling enterprises, account for about 47% of installed capacity and more than 60% of long products, yet they are the least capitalized and most fragmented part of the industry. This paper examines the role these producers must play in the NSP and the challenges that could prevent the targets from being met. Using document analysis, secondary industry and think-tank evidence, and first-order calculations, we show that (i) if the secondary share is held at 47%, secondary capacity must roughly triple to about 284 Mtpa; (ii) the policy’s own scrap and DRI projections imply that coal-based DRI remains structurally important to 2047; (iii) meeting the sector target would require coal-DRI-based producers to cut intensity by roughly one-third to one-half; and (iv) the proposed ₹5,000 crore support scheme equals only about ₹1.5 crore per unit. We identify twelve interlinked risks in raw materials, technology, finance, energy cost, quality perception, trade, carbon regulation, skills and data, and propose a differentiated three-tier pathway and eight policy recommendations.

title: IoT-Based Real-Time Air Quality Surveillance System using Arduino Uno
source: Journal of Methodical Computing and Communications
summary: Recently, air pollution has become a critical environmental concern globally as a result of rapid population growth, increasing vehicle emissions, industrialization, and urbanization. They are all factors that can negatively impact human he
content: Recently, air pollution has become a critical environmental concern globally as a result of rapid population growth, increasing vehicle emissions, industrialization, and urbanization. They are all factors that can negatively impact human health and the respiratory system. Consequently, this study presents a low-cost, Internet of Things (IoT)-based air quality monitoring system designed to provide real-time local and remote assessments of air pollution levels. The proposed system integrates an Arduino Uno microcontroller, an MQ135 gas sensor, and a NodeMCU ESP8266 Wi-Fi module for data collection, processing, and wireless transmission. The MQ135 sensor is used to monitor changes associated with different kinds of gaseous pollutants such as carbon dioxide, smoke, alcohol vapors, benzene, and ammonia. The MQ135 sensor data are processed by the Arduino Uno and displayed on an LCD screen as indicative air quality values. In addition, the air quality level is assessed according to predefined pollution thresholds. When the measured pollutant concentration exceeds a predefined safe limit, the system triggers an alert to indicate unsafe air pollution conditions. Besides that, the collected data is sent to the ThingSpeak cloud platform, where it is stored, analyzed, and displayed graphically as time-sequence graphs via a web interface. This allows users to remotely monitor air quality in real time using a computer or mobile device with an internet connection. Overall, the proposed system offers a simple, cost-effective, and accessible IoT-based solution for continuous air quality monitoring and early detection of potentially hazardous pollution.

summary: This dataset supports the research examining the effects of board characteristics and audit committees on carbon emission disclosure, with Environmental Management System (EMS) as a mediating variable, among companies listed on the Indonesi
content: This dataset supports the research examining the effects of board characteristics and audit committees on carbon emission disclosure, with Environmental Management System (EMS) as a mediating variable, among companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2021–2025 period. The dataset comprises 806 firm year observations from 162 companies operating in carbon intensive sectors, including energy, manufacturing, construction, and transportation. The dataset includes information on board size, board independence, board gender diversity, board nationality diversity, audit committee characteristics, Environmental Management System (EMS) adoption proxied by ISO certification, and Carbon Emission Disclosure (CED) measured using an 18-item disclosure index. The dataset is provided to support transparency, facilitate further academic research, and enable the replication of the empirical analysis presented in the associated research article. The accompanying documentation provides descriptions of the variables, measurement procedures, and dataset structure.

title: CO2 sorption-driven interpolyelectrolyte complexes of poly(allylammonium) bicarbonate and sodium alginate with dissociation-based recyclability
summary: To introduce a new strategy for replacing water-insoluble, non-biodegradable synthetic plastics with dissociation-based recyclable interpolyelectrolyte complexes (IPCs), this study demonstrates sustainable closed-loop recycling of IPCs form
content: To introduce a new strategy for replacing water-insoluble, non-biodegradable synthetic plastics with dissociation-based recyclable interpolyelectrolyte complexes (IPCs), this study demonstrates sustainable closed-loop recycling of IPCs formed through CO 2 sorption-driven complexation between a synthetic non-biodegradable polyelectrolyte and a natural biodegradable polysaccharide. Water-soluble poly(allylammonium) bicarbonate (PALm-BC), derived from synthetic poly(allylamine) (PAL) through the capture of CO 2 as carbonic acid, formed water-insoluble IPCs with sodium alginate (Alg-Na) in aqueous solution. The complexes exhibited various morphologies depending on temperature, concentration, stoichiometry, and the molecular weight of PALm. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis revealed that ammonium–carboxylate ion pairs were preferentially located on the surfaces of the complexes after isolation from the solution. Molecular modeling using GROMACS and HGS revealed​ that low-molecular-weight PALm formed ladder-like linear complexes that aggregated intermolecularly into thick nanofibers. In contrast, high-molecular-weight PALm formed incomplete ladder-like structures, resulting in insufficient precipitation and the formation of thin nanofibers. The complexes completely dissociated into PAL and Alg-Na upon basification with NaOH; however, these water-soluble components re-formed the complexes upon reintroduction of CO 2 through the recapture of carbonic acid by PAL, enabling sustainable closed-loop recycling of the IPCs through reversible CO 2 sorption. These findings provide a strategy for reducing the use of non-biodegradable plastics by replacing them with dissociation-based recyclable IPC materials.

title: Data-driven analysis of barriers to net zero practices in the UK construction sector: a multidisciplinary approach using clustering and topic modelling
summary: The construction industry is falling behind in achieving the net-zero targets established under the Paris Agreement. As such, this study investigates barriers to net-zero adoption from the perspectives of interdisciplinary construction prof
content: The construction industry is falling behind in achieving the net-zero targets established under the Paris Agreement. As such, this study investigates barriers to net-zero adoption from the perspectives of interdisciplinary construction professionals. An exploratory qualitative research approach was adopted, using semi-structured interviews to collect data. Interview transcripts were analysed through thematic analysis, supported by K-means clustering and Latent-Dirichlet-Allocation topic modelling. The analysis identified five barrier themes: financial and economic constraints; technological and expertise challenges; regulatory and policy limitations; industry practices and cultural resistance; and supply chain and operational difficulties. The findings reveal that net-zero construction is widely perceived as costly, highlighting the need for government financial support and incentives to encourage adoption. The study provides insights into challenges hindering net-zero implementation and offers practical implications for policymakers and industry stakeholders in developing targeted interventions, supportive policies, and an enabling environment to accelerate the construction industry’s transition towards net-zero emissions.

title: Trace-metal responses to enhanced rock weathering with basalt in agricultural and riparian soils
summary: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a promising carbon dioxide removal strategy, but its field deployment requires careful evaluation of metal-related risks. Crushed, low-Ni basalt (20 t ha−1) was surface-applied in June 2023 to hayfield and
content: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a promising carbon dioxide removal strategy, but its field deployment requires careful evaluation of metal-related risks. Crushed, low-Ni basalt (20 t ha−1) was surface-applied in June 2023 to hayfield and pasture soils in a working Vermont dairy agroecosystem, and an adjacent hydrologically connected riparian corridor was monitored for downstream changes in extractable soil metals and Ca:Al ratios. Agricultural surface soils (0–15 cm) were sampled twice before application (fall 2022 and spring 2023) and four times afterward (fall 2023; spring 2024; fall 2024; spring 2025), and central riparian corridor soils were sampled once before application and during four post-treatment campaigns. Forage biomass and tissue metal concentrations (Ni, Cu, Zn, Mn) were measured at first cut in spring 2023 (pre-treatment) and spring 2024 (one-year post-treatment). Extractable soil metals were quantified using the Modified Morgan extractant. In agricultural plots, extractable Ni, Cr, Pb, Al, Mn, Zn, Cu, and Cd showed no sustained or systematic increases relative to controls, and forage biomass and tissue metal concentrations did not differ between treatments. Across plots, extractable Ni, Al, and Pb covaried most strongly (inversely) with soil pH. Downslope riparian soils showed large declines in extractable Ni, Al, and Pb (58–79% in arithmetic campaign means), with mixed-effects models indicating statistically significant departures from baseline. These declines coincided with an increase in extractable Ca:Al ratios (charge-equivalent basis), consistent with pH-driven reductions in metal lability, particularly for metals exhibiting strong hydrolysis and sorption behavior. The soil, forage, riparian, and groundwater observations indicate that agronomic-rate application of this low-Ni basalt did not create detectable metal-mobilization concerns in treated fields and coincided with reduced extractable metal concentrations in hydrologically connected riparian soils. Effective ERW monitoring should therefore consider hydrologic connectivity and track soil pH and extractable Ca:Al ratios as additional useful indicators of Ca–Al balance alongside direct measurements of metals of concern.

title: Modelling the drivers of modular construction adoption in Australia: a hybrid interpretive and classification approach
summary: Modular construction (MC) is increasingly promoted in Australia as a pathway toward more sustainable and efficient building delivery; however, adoption remains limited because the conditions shaping implementation are not yet fully understo
content: Modular construction (MC) is increasingly promoted in Australia as a pathway toward more sustainable and efficient building delivery; however, adoption remains limited because the conditions shaping implementation are not yet fully understood. Existing studies largely identify or rank adoption drivers independently, with limited integration of hierarchical structural modelling and data-driven classification in the Australian context. This study investigates drivers of MC uptake through a mixed-method approach integrating qualitative evidence with quantitative modelling. A targeted literature scan and semi-structured interviews with 15 professionals, 11 based in Australia and four New Zealand-based comparative experts produced and refined an inventory of 79 drivers. Interview-occurrence analysis and category-specific Pareto evaluation prioritised the drivers; TISM-MICMAC modelled relationships among eight categories; and an ANN assessed how consistently occurrence and structural attributes reproduced the Pareto-defined classification. Social, technological, and supply-chain considerations occupied the strongest structural positions. A five-member content-review panel drawn from the remaining survey volunteer pool provided favourable ratings on 27 of 30 item responses (90%), with item-level favourable proportions of 60–100%. This supports face and content credibility only. Because the framework was developed from one small purposive dataset and the classifier target was occurrence-derived, the computational results remain internal-consistency evidence rather than independent causal or predictive validation.

title: Carbon fluxes in rhodoliths, coraliths and artificial substrates on tropical reefs
summary: Abstract Understanding how calcifying benthic systems contribute to short-term carbon dynamics helps assess their role in shallow tropical ecosystems under environmental change. We compared day-to-night relative patterns of net organic carb
content: Abstract Understanding how calcifying benthic systems contribute to short-term carbon dynamics helps assess their role in shallow tropical ecosystems under environmental change. We compared day-to-night relative patterns of net organic carbon production and net calcification in three contrasting functional units from the Colombian Caribbean: rhodoliths, spherical free-living colonies (coraliths) of the coral Siderastrea radians , and colonized artificial substrates mimicking the rhodolith shape. In situ incubations were conducted during morning, afternoon, and nighttime periods under natural environmental conditions. We observed significant variation among incubation periods and across all functional units, with higher daytime net organic carbon production and calcification and reduced or negative nighttime values. Rhodoliths exhibited the highest daytime rates of both net organic carbon production and net calcification and the greatest morning-to-night contrast in net calcification (11.6-fold). Colonized artificial substrates showed the greatest contrast in net organic carbon production (5.37-fold) and consistent nighttime net CaCO₃ dissolution, whereas corals exhibited comparatively lower daytime rates and more moderate contrasts. Morning-to-night metabolic ratios revealed marked differences among functional units in the relative magnitude of daytime net organic carbon production and the measured nighttime respiratory rate, as well as in the relative magnitude of light and dark calcification rates. Daytime net organic carbon production and light calcification showed contrasting relationships among systems. Corals exhibited proportionally higher net organic carbon production relative to calcification than rhodoliths and colonized artificial substrates. Calcifying benthic systems differ not only in metabolic magnitude but also in the temporal expression of organic and inorganic carbon processes. In addition, the artificial substrates provide a potentially scalable experimental platform for exploring short-term metabolic and carbonate dynamics associated with colonized structures in reef-associated environments. Biological organization and substrate identity influence fine-scale carbonate chemistry variability in shallow tropical ecosystems, with implications for understanding benthic carbon cycling and the ecological functioning of natural and artificial reef-associated habitats.

title: Beyond the Exchange Picture of Singlet–Triplet Gaps
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Abstract Molecules with inverted singlet–triplet gaps are promising candidates for next-generation organic light-emitting diode emitters, but identifying general principles that explain and guide singlet–triplet inversion remains challengin
content: Abstract Molecules with inverted singlet–triplet gaps are promising candidates for next-generation organic light-emitting diode emitters, but identifying general principles that explain and guide singlet–triplet inversion remains challenging. Here, we investigate substituted heptazines, vibrational ensembles of azupyrene and isopyrene, and a chemically diverse molecular set using CIS, EOM-CCSD, and wave function-based state matching. The CIS analysis reveals an intermediate level of electronic response between direct exchange and correlation: state-specific configuration relaxation redistributes the gap among exchange, orbital-energy, and electron–hole Coulomb contributions. Correlation beyond CIS generally lowers the gap, with a larger reduction associated with greater relative double-excitation character in the singlet. However, the final gap also depends on the positive CIS baseline, so similar doubles content can occur in systems with either positive or negative gaps. Within related molecular data sets, a larger CIS baseline is accompanied by a stronger correlation-driven reduction, but this relationship does not hold across chemically diverse molecules. These findings establish the importance of balancing the full state-specific singles baseline against correlation-driven gap reduction when interpreting and designing singlet–triplet energetics.

title: Plastic matters: it drives soil aggregation, carbon retention, nutrient cycling, and microbial communities dependent on its degradability
summary: Microplastics (MPs) have shown different effects on soil physical structure, chemistry, and microbial communities. As soils are known to differ in their potential to develop structure, the observed variability in MP effects may be strongly
content: Microplastics (MPs) have shown different effects on soil physical structure, chemistry, and microbial communities. As soils are known to differ in their potential to develop structure, the observed variability in MP effects may be strongly attributed to MPs impact on soil aggregation. Hence, we here address the impact of different MPs on soil aggregation and associated soil functions such as water, carbon, and nutrient storage, and microbial habitat in soils differing in texture and soil organic matter (SOM). We hypothesized that conventional MPs hinder soil aggregation, speeding up the turnover of soil inherent OM, and reducing soil water holding capacity (WHC), while degradable MPs represent substrates altering soil microbial community composition, and directly promoting microbial activity and nutrient turnover. To address this, Zea mays was planted in a greenhouse with silty loam and sandy loam soil and spiked with polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), or biodegradable polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT), varied by concentration (0%, 0.1%, 1% w/w) and size (200–400, 75–200, <75 µm). Soil aggregate fractions and stability, WHC, 15 N-ammonium-nitrate and 13 C-yeast as models for soil N and C cycling, available P and K, as well as plant growth, and microbiota within aggregate fractions were analyzed. Overall, MP addition led to a decrease in more stable, occluded soil microaggregates, and a respective increase in free aggregates, while macroaggregate fractions remained unaffected. For both soils and across all MPs, soil C retention was reduced about 50%. Soil texture dominated the response of soil to MP addition: finer-textured soils lost more microaggregates, around 25% greater SOM turnover, and 33% lower WHC. As this was independent of polymer size and type, we relate this to physical MP effects. An MP-specific biochemical effect was observed for biodegradable PBAT tending to increase soil microaggregate formation, stability, and WHC. It led to 15 N immobilization in soil and increased plant uptake and significantly altered soil prokaryotic communities in aggregate fractions. Here, microbial taxa involved in reductive nitrogen cycling, depletion of N-fixing Azospirillum spp., and enrichment of the potentially plant-pathogenic Xylophilus spp. was observed. We reveal that MPs exert fundamentally bidirectional effects on soils. Biodegradable MPs enhance beneficial properties such as aggregation and water retention yet concurrently disrupt key microbiome functions. Across all polymer types, MPs accelerate soil C turnover, underscoring the need to resolve their net impact on critical soil functions in a soil- and polymer-specific context.

title: SUN'IY INTELLEKTNING YASHIL IQTISODIYOTGA TA'SIRI: ENERGIYA SAMARADORLIGI VA UGLEROD EMISSIYALARINING SABABIY TAHLILI
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Mazkur tadqiqot sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarining yashil iqtisodiyotga ta'sirini energiya samaradorligi, qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalari, raqamli infratuzilma va uglerod emissiyalari o'rtasidagi o'zaro bog'liqlik asosida o'rgan
content: Mazkur tadqiqot sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarining yashil iqtisodiyotga ta'sirini energiya samaradorligi, qayta tiklanuvchi energiya manbalari, raqamli infratuzilma va uglerod emissiyalari o'rtasidagi o'zaro bog'liqlik asosida o'rganishga qaratilgan. Tadqiqotning asosiy muammosi shundan iboratki, sun'iy intellekt bir tomondan elektr energiyasini ishlab chiqarish va taqsimlashni optimallashtirish, sanoat jarayonlarida energiya sarfini kamaytirish hamda resurslardan foydalanish samaradorligini oshirish imkonini beradi. Boshqa tomondan, SI modellarini o'qitish va ishlatish uchun zarur bo'lgan ma'lumotlar markazlari, yuqori unumdor hisoblash tizimlari va sovitish infratuzilmasi elektr energiyasiga bo'lgan talabni oshirishi mumkin. Xalqaro energetika agentligining 2025-yilgi baholashiga ko'ra, ma'lumotlar markazlarining elektr energiyasi iste'moli 2024-yilda taxminan 415 TWh ni tashkil etgan va asosiy ssenariy bo'yicha 2030-yilga kelib qariyb 945 TWh ga yetishi kutilgan. Tadqiqotda Janubiy Koreya, Germaniya va AQSh tajribasi asosida mamlakatlararo panel ma'lumotlardan foydalanish, dinamik bog'liqliklarni System-GMM orqali baholash va emissiyalar taqsimotidagi geterogen ta'sirlarni panel kvantil regressiyasi — MMQR yordamida aniqlash taklif etiladi. Endogenlik muammosi kechiktirilgan o'zgaruvchilar, muqobil SI indikatorlari, instrumentlar va qo'shimcha robustlik testlari orqali tekshiriladi. Shuningdek, qayta tiklanuvchi energiya ulushi, elektr energiyasining uglerod intensivligi va ilmiy-tadqiqot xarajatlarining SI–emissiya munosabatiga ta'siri tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqotning kutilayotgan ilmiy hissasi SI ta'sirining shartli va geterogen xususiyatlarini aniqlash hamda O'zbekiston uchun raqamli infratuzilma va energiya siyosatini uyg'unlashtirishga qaratilgan dalillarga asoslangan tavsiyalar ishlab chiqishdan iborat.

title: Ionised Mass and Free-Free Emission Budget of the Young Nebula NGC 7027
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper computes a self-contained budget for NGC 7027 from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. NGC 7027 is a young, carbon-rich and exceptionally dense planetary nebula
content: This paper computes a self-contained budget for NGC 7027 from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. NGC 7027 is a young, carbon-rich and exceptionally dense planetary nebula whose radio continuum is bright enough to serve as a flux-density calibrator. Because it is compact and dense, its ionised mass is sensitive to the distinction between the local electron density measured from line ratios and the root-mean-square density implied by the emission measure. The ratio of those two densities gives the volume filling factor directly, and the filling factor in turn controls whether the ionised mass is a few hundredths or a few tenths of a solar mass. The headline results are: R_pc = 0.045; local_density_cm3 = 6e+04; filling_factor = 0.3; rms_density_cm3 = 3.29e+04; ionised_mass_Msun = 0.199; recombination_time_yr = 2.11; emission_measure_pc_cm6 = 9.72e+07; electron_temperature_K = 1.05e+04. The filling factor is well below unity, so the nebula is clumped rather than uniformly filled. Even with that correction the ionised mass remains modest, which means most of the ejected envelope in this young object is still neutral or molecular rather than ionised. The free-free budget is consistent with the observed radio brightness only when the clumping is included; a uniform-density model overpredicts the mass at fixed emission measure. The calculation is presented with its inputs, relations and sensitivities stated openly, so that any revised distance, density or stellar parameter can be substituted and the verdict recomputed directly.

title: Divergent biophysical controls on the complementary dimensions of global diurnal photosynthesis
summary: Vegetation photosynthesis exhibits pronounced diurnal variations that reflect rapid physiological responses to environmental change. However, a global understanding of these diurnal dynamics and their biophysical controls remains elusive. H
content: Vegetation photosynthesis exhibits pronounced diurnal variations that reflect rapid physiological responses to environmental change. However, a global understanding of these diurnal dynamics and their biophysical controls remains elusive. Here we use emerging global hourly gross primary production (GPP) datasets to characterize the asymmetry, magnitude, and midday depression of the diurnal GPP cycle. These complementary characteristics exhibit distinct global patterns and seasonal dynamics. Vapor pressure deficit (VPD) primarily regulates diurnal asymmetry, vegetation greenness and temperature dominate the magnitude, while VPD together with temperature controls midday depression, with these biophysical controls varying substantially across seasons. Current Earth system models generally capture the magnitude of diurnal GPP cycle and its biophysical controls but fail to reproduce its asymmetry and midday depression. Our study advances the understanding of vegetation photosynthetic dynamics at the sub-daily scale, laying the foundation for subsequent efforts to unravel plant adaptive strategies and refine next-generation ecosystem models. Global vegetation photosynthesis shows distinct diurnal asymmetry, magnitude, and midday depression governed by seasonally varying biophysical controls that Earth system models only partly capture, based on global hourly gross primary production datasets.

title: Omani 10th Grade Students’ Conceptual Understanding of Material Recycling and Environmental Waste Management
summary: Abstract This study examined Omani 10th grade students’ conceptual understanding of material recycling and environmental waste management, including their ability to apply this understanding through design, explanation, interdisciplinary co
content: Abstract This study examined Omani 10th grade students’ conceptual understanding of material recycling and environmental waste management, including their ability to apply this understanding through design, explanation, interdisciplinary connections, and the incorporation of entrepreneurial features into proposed recycling solutions. A task-based assessment was administered to 453 students from eight schools in two educational governorates in the Sultanate of Oman. The instrument assessed three dimensions: design and drawing, description and interpretation, and linking ideas with different fields. Descriptive statistics and multivariate analysis of variance were used to examine students’ performance and differences associated with gender and prior participation in environmental activities. Students demonstrated relatively strong performance in both description and interpretation and design and drawing, whereas their ability to link recycling ideas with different disciplinary fields was substantially weaker. Multivariate analyses indicated significant differences associated with gender, prior environmental-activity participation, and their interaction. Follow-up analyses showed gender differences in design and drawing and in linking ideas with different fields, while prior environmental-activity participation was associated only with linking ideas with different fields. Across the four recycling tasks, the proportion of students demonstrating innovative entrepreneurial features ranged from 41.8% to 62.7%, indicating variation across task contexts. The findings highlight the value of connecting recycling concepts with authentic design tasks, interdisciplinary learning, and environmental entrepreneurship. The study recommends strengthening practical, context-based sustainability learning and supporting teachers in integrating such experiences into school science and environmental education.

title: Dust Mass and Gas Budget of the Post-Asymptotic-Giant-Branch Nebula Frosty Leo
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This paper computes a self-contained budget for IRAS 09371+1212 (Frosty Leo) from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. Frosty Leo is a bipolar post-asymptotic-giant-branch n
content: This paper computes a self-contained budget for IRAS 09371+1212 (Frosty Leo) from published observational values, with every derived number produced by the deposited computation script. Frosty Leo is a bipolar post-asymptotic-giant-branch nebula famous for its strong ice absorption features and its bright reflection lobes. It has not yet formed a fully developed ionised planetary nebula, so its gas budget must be framed carefully: the dust mass from the infrared emission is comparatively secure, while the gas mass is traced by molecular and scattered light rather than by a bright ionised shell. The dust-to-gas comparison in such an object measures the conditions in the envelope during the brief transition off the asymptotic giant branch. The headline results are: dust_mass_Msun = 0.006; gas_mass_Msun = 0.045; dust_to_gas_ratio = 0.133; ratio_to_ISM_0p01 = 13.3; total_dust_plus_gas_Msun = 0.051; dust_temperature_K = 80. The dust mass is substantial for so compact an envelope, indicating efficient condensation during the final superwind phase. The inferred ratio is consistent with an oxygen-rich chemistry in which silicate and ice mantles carry much of the solid mass, in contrast to the carbon-rich case treated elsewhere in this set of objects. Because the object is still in transition, its budget is a snapshot of envelope assembly rather than of nebular dispersal, and the paper keeps that distinction explicit throughout. The calculation is presented with its inputs, relations and sensitivities stated openly, so that any revised distance, density or stellar parameter can be substituted and the verdict recomputed directly.

title: Naïve Bayes integration with Markov chain and cellular automata for modelling urban land use change
source: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: Abstract Away from the conventional Logistic Regression (LR) technique, this study presents a novel Naïve Bayes (NB) integration with Markov Chain (MC) and Cellular Automata (CA) for modelling urban land use change. Although NB is a simple
content: Abstract Away from the conventional Logistic Regression (LR) technique, this study presents a novel Naïve Bayes (NB) integration with Markov Chain (MC) and Cellular Automata (CA) for modelling urban land use change. Although NB is a simple parametric algorithm similar to the Logistic Regression (LR), previous studies have shown that it can outperform the LR when the features are independent, and the dataset is small and highly dimensional, such as land use datasets. In this experiment, NB was used to classify land use into urban and non-urban classes. The training data, test data, and validation data were extracted from the land use data. The training and test datasets were used to train and evaluate the NB; while the validation data was used to validate the CA prediction. The NB probabilities, transition probabilities from the MC model, neighbourhood interaction, and transition rule from the CA model were combined to determine the evolution of each cell in the prediction. Land use drivers were derived from Landsat-5 Thematic Mapper (TM, 1984), Landsat-7 Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus (ETM+, 2000), and Landsat-8 Operational Land Imager/Thermal Infrared Sensor (OLI/TIRS, 2020) imageries. Binary urban scenarios (urban and nonurban cells) were modelled using twelve salient urban land use drivers. Urban transitions from 1984–2000 to 2000–2020 were used to predict the urban state in 2060. The Model validation techniques employed were McNemar’s test and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves. The computed mean Area Under the Curve (AUC) for 1984–2000 and 2000–2020 were 0.7969 ± 0.0842 and 0.8357 ± 0.0613 respectively; which indicated that the predicted maps aligned closely with the validation data. We discussed the advantages and limitations of the NB algorithm relative to nonparametric algorithms for predicting urban land use change. We compared the results from NB and LR, and NB emerged a slightly better algorithm for the prediction. The resulting maps demonstrated the robust predictive power of the NB model.

title: Emergent-constrained future aridity and drought changes under low-to-moderate emission scenarios with explicit external forcings
summary: Drought is projected to intensify under greenhouse gas (GHG)-induced warming, yet uncertainties persist. To avoid spurious correlations from internal variability in conventional emergent constraint (EC) approaches, we construct a physically
content: Drought is projected to intensify under greenhouse gas (GHG)-induced warming, yet uncertainties persist. To avoid spurious correlations from internal variability in conventional emergent constraint (EC) approaches, we construct a physically robust EC framework separating external forcings to calibrate future aridity and drought projections under low-to-moderate emission scenarios. Utilizing self-calibrated Palmer Drought Severity Index with Penman-Monteith potential evapotranspiration (scPDSIpm) from phase 5 and 6 of Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5 and CMIP6) models, we extract historical forced signals driven by GHG only and combined with volcanic/anthropogenic aerosols (VA/AA). Raw projections underestimate future (from 1950-2024 to 2025-2099) aridity and drought changes. GHG-forced constraints reduce global-mean scPDSIpm by 0.39 (CMIP5) and 0.55 (CMIP6), increase drought frequency by 18% and 19%, and extend drought duration by 1.2 and 1.6 months, with uncertainty reductions of 20-62% and 25-55%, respectively. GHG + VA/AA-forced constraints yield weaker calibrations with scPDSIpm decreases by 0.16 and 0.35, drought frequency increases by 9% and 12%, and limited uncertainty reductions (12-16% and 11-25%), because historical aerosol emissions differ from future scenarios. Regionally, constraints amplify drying over southern Europe, central/southern Africa, and Canada, while reducing overestimated drying over northern Europe, the contiguous United States, northern Australia, the Tibetan Plateau, and central Asia.

title: EUBURN: The southern Europe biomass burning programme
source: Journal of the European Meteorological Society.
summary: Southern Europe is experiencing a shift towards a new wildfire regime, characterised by larger and more intense fires, and an extension of the fire season beyond the traditional summer months. Climate projections indicate that the occurrenc
content: Southern Europe is experiencing a shift towards a new wildfire regime, characterised by larger and more intense fires, and an extension of the fire season beyond the traditional summer months. Climate projections indicate that the occurrence and severity of fwildfires will increase faster than the global average due to an increased risk of heatwaves and droughts. These conditions are expected to reduce fuel moisture, extend the fire season and increase the likelihood of large and severe wildfires. At the same time, changes in fire regimes may alter vegetation composition and ecosystem structure, potentially favouring fire-adapted species while threatening species that are less resilient to increasingly frequent or severe fires. Addressing these emerging challenges require new tools and technologies needed to implement comprehensive fire management approaches. The community still faces challenges in predicting which wildfires may escalate into extreme events, and the environmental, climate and health impacts of the associated smoke remain poorly understood. The southern Europe biomass BURNing (EUBURN) programme was developed in response to the need to improve the prevention, monitoring and prediction of wildfire risks in southern Europe. EUBURN integrates multi-year, multi-scale field campaigns, laboratory studies, satellite remote sensing and advanced modelling to establish the research foundations for understanding the complex interactions between wildfires and the atmosphere. Based on this fundamental research, the programme aims to support fire responders, ecosystems and air quality management, while addressing specific climate research requirements by developing new or enhanced operational products, tools and services for predicting and monitoring wildfires and their associated smoke plumes. This article provides an overview of EUBURN, including its motivation and design. It also describes the measurements and modelling strategy that will be employed to fulfil the programme's scientific objectives.

title: Impact of heterogeneity on CO₂-enhanced oil recovery in extra-ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs at ultra-high water cut
source: Journal of Petroleum Exploration and Production Technology
summary: Prolonged waterflooding of China''s extra-ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs produces water cuts above 95%, while more than 70% of the original oil remains in place. How pore-throat heterogeneity controls carbon dioxide (CO₂) displ
content: Prolonged waterflooding of China''s extra-ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs produces water cuts above 95%, while more than 70% of the original oil remains in place. How pore-throat heterogeneity controls carbon dioxide (CO₂) displacement under these conditions remains unquantified, limiting interval selection. This study combines multiscale characterization with compositional simulation of five years of waterflooding followed by ten years of CO₂ flooding. Characterization included petrophysical measurements on 207 core plugs, field emission scanning electron microscopy, automated mineral analysis, and mercury injection capillary pressure testing. Six rock types (RT I–VI) span permeabilities of 0.015–8.5 mD and characteristic pore-throat radii at 40% mercury saturation (R₄₀) of 0.015–2.8 μm. A threshold of R₄₀ = 0.081 μm separates convection-influenced from diffusion-dominated transport. Recovery contributions increase by 2.4–3.6 percentage points in convection-dominated RT I–II and 2.1–3.6 percentage points in transitional RT III–IV. The largest relative improvement occurs in RT III (71.9%). In diffusion-dominated RT V–VI, pressure recovers uniformly, whereas oil saturation remains heterogeneous and gas–oil ratios remain lower than those in RT I–IV. This pressure–composition decoupling is consistent with diffusion-limited CO₂ penetration and potential retention. Overall recovery increases from 27.4% to 40.6%, a gain of 13.2 percentage points. Unlike previous single-scale studies, this work uses one pore-throat parameter to link pore-scale structure with reservoir-scale CO₂-enhanced oil recovery. The framework distinguishes convection-accessible production zones from diffusion-dominated potential storage intervals, but the threshold requires site-specific recalibration.

title: Contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts
source: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behaviour & Research
summary: Purpose This study explores the dual influence of contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Gender is applied as a critical lens to theorise entrepreneurship and its constraints (Ghouse and McElwee,
content: Purpose This study explores the dual influence of contextual institutional constraints and gender entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Gender is applied as a critical lens to theorise entrepreneurship and its constraints (Ghouse and McElwee, 2026) in the gendered context (Welter, 2020) of rural family businesses. Design/methodology/approach From a dataset capturing the life stories of 30 entrepreneurs engaged in 22 rural family businesses, this work applies a gender lens and focuses on the life stories of 4 couples (men and women) owning and managing family businesses in rural Sweden. Following Larty and Hamilton (2011), the analysis structures the narratives of entrepreneurs in rural family businesses (cf. Alkhaled and Berglund, 2018) with the emerging themes of emancipation, empowerment and family business as an emancipatory space emerging as significant recurring themes in the stories of all four couples. Findings The findings reveal that rural family businesses provide women with a secure space that empowers and emancipates them to pursue entrepreneurial activities. Fathers play an important role in how daughters challenge traditional rural social norms, while contextual informal institutional constraints (i.e. traditional norms) hinder entrepreneurship in rural contexts. Here, the community acts as a vital stakeholder. Research limitations/implications This study challenges the assumptions of the heroic entrepreneur and the taken-for-granted agency of men. As such, in rural contexts, men act as co-agents to women entrepreneurs in pursuing entrepreneurship and emancipation. By including the voices of both women and men, this study responds to calls by scholars in the gender entrepreneurship literature (Smith, 2022; Hytti et al., 2024). Though empirical context is limited to Småland in this study, the dimensions of gender and rural might be taken into consideration for the generalisability of the findings. For example, Småland exists as part of a largely gender progressive country, and cultural norms present both within and outside of rural communities may be mirrored in other regions, extending beyond Sweden to other Nordic countries which share similar entrepreneurial contextual constraints (Munch Haagensen, 2013). Future research could seek to incorporate the perspective of couples owning and managing businesses in urban areas as a comparison to rural entrepreneurs in order to better highlight contextual institutional constraints, which would also benefit the generalisability of the research findings. Practical implications Overcoming contemporary challenges in mitigating and reducing gender inequality in Sweden and globally demands more than placing entrepreneurship at the heart of regional policy development. To develop and implement effective policies, local governments must be attentive to the specific differences in each (rural) setting's economic, social and institutional conditions. title: What drives the carbon dynamics under different urban expansion patterns in rapidly urbanizing regions? Long-term evidence from Jiangsu Province, China
summary: Urban expansion is one of the most direct drivers of changes in global carbon dynamics. It typically reduces ecosystem carbon sinks (CS) while increasing carbon emissions (CE). However, the impacts of different urban expansion patterns (UEP
content: Urban expansion is one of the most direct drivers of changes in global carbon dynamics. It typically reduces ecosystem carbon sinks (CS) while increasing carbon emissions (CE). However, the impacts of different urban expansion patterns (UEPs) on carbon dynamics vary substantially, and their associated social–ecological characteristics are highly heterogeneous. To address this issue, this study developed a theoretical framework linking UEPs to carbon dynamic responses. The Multi-order Adjacency Index (MAI) was employed to identify UEPs. We then systematically examined the spatiotemporal evolution of UEPs, CE, and CS in Jiangsu Province from 1985 to 2020. Furthermore, the XGBoost–SHAP model was applied to quantify differences in carbon effects among UEPs and to identify the contributions of key social–ecological factors. The results show that urban expansion in rapidly urbanizing areas was dominated by fringe expansion that primarily encroached upon farmland. Urban expansion exerted direct negative effects on both CE and CS. Nevertheless, Infill and fringe expansion patterns were found to partially mitigate some of the adverse impacts associated with urbanization. Across different UEPs, socioeconomic factors were the primary contributors to CE predictions. In contrast, CS predictions were more strongly associated with natural ecological factors. The contribution structures of these factors differed markedly among UEPs. This study reveals the heterogeneous responses of carbon dynamics to different UEPs. The findings suggest that optimizing the composition of UEPs may be more effective than simply limiting the scale of urban growth for balancing urban development with regional carbon reduction goals. These results provide new scientific evidence to support low-carbon transitions in rapidly urbanizing regions.

title: Green Consumer Values and Willingness to Pay for Sustainable Pork Attributes: Evidence From Germany
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines German consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) for sustainability attributes of pork products, with particular attention to animal husbandry standards under the planned but not yet implemented “Tierhaltungskennzeich
content: ABSTRACT This study examines German consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) for sustainability attributes of pork products, with particular attention to animal husbandry standards under the planned but not yet implemented “Tierhaltungskennzeichen,” regional origin, and carbon footprint. Using data from a discrete choice experiment (DCE) and Mixed Logit models, we estimate consumer preferences and explore the influence of green consumer values and conversational agent design. The results indicate strong preferences for higher animal welfare standards and regional production, while reductions in carbon footprint generate comparatively modest premiums. We also identify substantial preference heterogeneity across consumers. Consumers with stronger green consumer values generally exhibit higher WTP for improved husbandry conditions and regional origin, while differences in WTP for carbon footprint reductions are less pronounced. In contrast, the degree of conversational agent anthropomorphism has little effect on consumers' marginal WTP. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for value‐based heterogeneity when designing sustainability labels and food policies and highlight the relevance of green consumer values for understanding differences in consumer preferences for sustainable pork attributes.

title: Geopolitics of the Global Green Transition: Rethinking Azerbaijan's Energy Security
summary: The accelerating global transition toward renewable energy frameworks and comprehensive decarbonization is structurally reconfiguring the international political economy. While shifting away from fossil fuels mitigates historical macroecono
content: The accelerating global transition toward renewable energy frameworks and comprehensive decarbonization is structurally reconfiguring the international political economy. While shifting away from fossil fuels mitigates historical macroeconomic risks associated with hydrocarbon supply volatility and cartel-driven market manipulations, it simultaneously introduces novel structural vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities manifest within the global energy architecture as nations transition from a reliance on liquid resource extraction to a dependency on rigid industrial supply chains, advanced technology, and geographically concentrated raw materials. This study aims to analytically deconstruct the structural transformation of the global energy security paradigm, critically evaluate the geopolitical implications of critical raw material monopolies, examine the rise of geo-economic protectionism, and comprehensively assess the strategic positioning of Azerbaijan as an emerging transnational green energy hub and corridor. A multidimensional analytical framework combining systemic economic analysis, comparative geo-economics, and institutional theory was employed. Empirical indicators and global energy supply chain data spanning from 2015 to 2026—sourced from the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA)—were synthesized alongside the national strategic roadmaps and legislative frameworks of the Republic of Azerbaijan. The research demonstrates that the green transition systematically redistributes geopolitical leverage away from traditional oil and gas producers toward states that control the refining of critical minerals (such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earth elements) and the manufacture of clean technologies, where a single nation (China) commands a 60% to 90% market share. In response, major Western economic blocs are deploying aggressive "green protectionism" mechanisms, such as the US Inflation Reduction Act and the EU's Critical Raw Materials Act, effectively fragmenting international trade into regional alignment blocs. Concurrently, Azerbaijan is successfully leveraging its 157 GW Caspian offshore wind potential, transitioning from a classic hydrocarbon supplier to a pivotal green electricity hub via the implementation of the Black Sea Green Energy Cable. Although the global green transition successfully reduces carbon dependence, it fundamentally destabilizes traditional energy geopolitics by establishing mineral-centric monopolies and techno-nationalist trade barriers. For transitioning economies like Azerbaijan, strategic reorientation toward transnational green corridors and renewable electricity export is essential to maintain geopolitical relevance, hedge against long-term fossil-fuel demand destruction, and ensure domestic macroeconomic stability.

title: GC–MS metabolite profiling, elemental composition, and molecular docking analysis of camel milk extracts: insights into antioxidant and antibacterial activities
summary: Despite its rich nutritional value and diverse therapeutic properties, camel milk remains poorly studied in Ethiopia. Therefore, this study investigated the chemical profile, elemental composition, ATR-FTIR characteristics, antioxidant and
content: Despite its rich nutritional value and diverse therapeutic properties, camel milk remains poorly studied in Ethiopia. Therefore, this study investigated the chemical profile, elemental composition, ATR-FTIR characteristics, antioxidant and antibacterial activities, and molecular docking interactions of lyophilized camel milk extracts. GC–MS metabolite profiling of camel milk revealed solvent-dependent variations in chemical composition, with cholesterol (32.4–40.92%), palmitic acid (24.53–30.91%), and stearic acid (12.69–18.84%) as the major constituents of the n -hexane, chloroform, and ethyl acetate extracts, whereas the methanol extract was enriched in palmitoleic acid (40.22%), elaidic acid (27.38%), and heptadecanoic acid (14.59%). The DPPH radical scavenging assay revealed strong antioxidant activity for the methanol extract (IC 50 = 3.54 µg/mL) and lyophilized camel milk (IC 50 = 2.33 µg/mL), showing activities comparable to ascorbic acid (IC 50 = 1.25 µg/mL). The n -hexane and CHCl 3 extracts exhibited the highest antibacterial activity against Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus with MIC values of 2.5 mg/mL, whereas the methanol extract and crude lyophilized camel milk were most active against Escherichia coli at the same MIC value. ATR-FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates in lyophilized camel milk, indicating preservation of major bioactive constituents after lyophilization. Elemental analysis using MP-AES revealed the presence of essential macro- and microelements with varying concentrations. Potassium (2237.45 ± 22.10 mg/L) was the most abundant element, followed by calcium (1507.71 ± 26.54 mg/L), phosphorus (757.09 ± 28.02 mg/L), and sodium (714.80 ± 3.19 mg/L). Toxic heavy metals, including Pb, Cd, Cr, Ni, Co, and Mo, were below detectable limits. Molecular docking analysis showed that major camel milk phytochemicals exhibited notable binding affinities against key targets. Palmitoleic acid showed slightly higher predicted binding affinity (− 4.3 kcal/mol) than ascorbic acid (− 4.2 kcal/mol) against Human Peroxiredoxin 5 (PDB ID: 1HD2). Cholesterol demonstrated a strongest predictable binding affinity against S. aureus topoisomerase IV subunit A (− 7.1 kcal/mol; PDB ID: 2INR) and L. monocytogenes InlA protein (− 8.8 kcal/mol; PDB ID: 1O6T), with higher affinity than ciprofloxacin. These findings suggest that camel milk is a promising source of bioactive compounds, and the analyzed milk samples are safe for consumption due to the absence of harmful heavy metals.

title: On the Interference of Niobium Precipitation and Recrystallization During Austenite Conditioning of HSLA Steel
summary: Abstract The interplay between niobium precipitation and static recrystallization in austenite governs the microstructure and grain size obtained during thermomechanical processing of HSLA steels. This study examines microstructural evoluti
content: Abstract The interplay between niobium precipitation and static recrystallization in austenite governs the microstructure and grain size obtained during thermomechanical processing of HSLA steels. This study examines microstructural evolution in a 0.04 wt pct Nb microalloyed steel through double-hit compression tests at 975 °C with strains of 0.15 to 0.4 and holding times of 5 to 4000 seconds. Elaborate microstructural characterization combined deep learning segmentation of prior austenite grains, machine-learning quantification of Nb(C,N) on carbon extraction replicas, and matrix dissolution to normalize precipitate volume fractions. The techniques and their peculiarities are discussed in detail, and a method to filter out contributions by copper sulfide particles is proposed. Intermediate strains of 0.2 and 0.3 triggered a recrystallization stasis once the Zener pinning force reached ~ 0.01 MPa, at roughly 5 pct of total niobium precipitated—three times the 5 pct equilibrium precipitation proposed in earlier work—while the same fraction at strain 0.4 produced no stasis. This work shows that the onset of the stasis cannot be described by a fixed precipitation level, but depends on the combined kinetics of nucleation, growth and coarsening given by dislocation density and temperature. Grain size continued to evolve during the stasis as precipitates coarsened, challenging the constant grain size assumption of current models.

title: Does Climate Legislation Reduce Emissions in Developing Asia? Legislative Decoupling, Governance, and Carbon Intensity
summary: This study tests whether climate legislative intensity is associated with lower carbon emissions in developing Asia, contrasting the instrumental expectation that laws reduce emissions with the institutional decoupling expectation that form
content: This study tests whether climate legislative intensity is associated with lower carbon emissions in developing Asia, contrasting the instrumental expectation that laws reduce emissions with the institutional decoupling expectation that formal adoption leaves outcomes unchanged. Using panel data for 32 countries over 2010–2023, we estimate fixed effects models for CO 2 emissions per capita and CO 2 intensity of GDP, including lags of up to five years, and apply equivalence tests anchored to the effect sizes reported for global samples. The cumulative count of climate laws shows no statistically significant association with either outcome, and equivalence tests bound the per capita association below the global benchmark. Governance quality, by contrast, is associated with lower carbon intensity but not with lower per capita emissions. These results support the decoupling expectation in a developing region and suggest that climate accountability frameworks should track implementation capacity and carbon efficiency rather than legislative counts.

title: Due Diligence in Agribusiness, Natural Resource Governance, and Trade: Rethinking Voluntary Standards Under Sustainability Regulations
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines how sustainability due diligence is reshaping market access, private governance, and natural resource governance in agri‐food supply chains. It focuses on the EU Regulation on Deforestation‐Free Products (EUDR
content: ABSTRACT This article examines how sustainability due diligence is reshaping market access, private governance, and natural resource governance in agri‐food supply chains. It focuses on the EU Regulation on Deforestation‐Free Products (EUDR), which conditions market access on traceability and plot‐level geolocation, and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D), which strengthens firm‐level obligations to identify and manage environmental and human rights risks across value chains. The study draws on qualitative analysis of WTO Technical Barriers to Trade Committee discussions and 64 interviews with producers, cooperatives, exporters, NGOs, and public officials in Costa Rica's coffee and palm oil sectors. Findings highlight that due diligence requirements reallocate evidentiary responsibilities and associated costs upstream, where participation increasingly depends on digital infrastructure, administrative capacity, and access to finance. Voluntary Sustainability Standards remain relevant as a business‐to‐business language of sustainability and may continue to provide consumer‐facing information, but they are being repositioned as auxiliary tools for risk documentation. The article asserts that sustainability markets are moving toward a new generation of criteria rooted in risk‐based traceability, documented environmental and social production conditions, and credible evidence of risk management. These dynamics risk creating “passporting” effects, whereby evidentiary capacity becomes a condition for market participation, with uneven consequences for producers, suppliers, and natural resource governance.

title: Green Economic Convergence
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Green Economic Convergence establishes an empirical and policy framework demonstrating that economic catch-up and environmental sustainability are reinforcing complements rather than competing objectives. Rather than replicating the coal- a
content: Green Economic Convergence establishes an empirical and policy framework demonstrating that economic catch-up and environmental sustainability are reinforcing complements rather than competing objectives. Rather than replicating the coal- and carbon-intensive industrialization pathways of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries under delayed Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) assumptions, emerging and developing economies (EMDEs) can capture a clean latecomer advantage—narrowing disparities in income, productive capabilities, technological advancement, and living standards through green technology diffusion, sustainable industrialization, clean infrastructure, and institutional capacity building. Synthesizing a 184-economy PPP CO2/GDP panel (2000–2022), Malmquist–Luenberger green total-factor productivity (GTFP) club analysis, Kaya identity decomposition, IRENA hardware learning curves (2010–2025), IEA World Energy Investment and Cost of Capital Observatory benchmarks, and World Bank/ESMAP/WHO Tracking SDG 7metrics, the report advances five central findings: Relative Decoupling Is Broadly Underway, Yet Scale Still Drives Emissions: Carbon intensity per PPP dollar of GDP fell in 124 of 184 economies between 2000 and 2022 (global median drop of 21%), though rapid EMDE GDP scale expansion (+68%) outpaced energy efficiency (-24%) and clean fuel substitution (-11%). Convergence Is Conditional, Not Automatic: Economies sort into distinct Malmquist–Luenberger convergence clubs governed by institutional quality, utility bankability, STEM skills, and technological absorption capacity. Hardware Economics Favor Leapfrogging: Between 2010 and 2024, utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell 90% to $44/MWh and utility battery storage (BESS) installed costs dropped 93% to ~$192/kWh (with further ~30% declines in 2025), placing firm solar-plus-storage at $54–$82/MWh—below new coal or imported LNG across major emerging corridors. Capital-Market Asymmetries—Not Technology Costs—Block Catch-Up: Clean-to-fossil investment stands at 12:1 in advanced economies and 6:1 in China versus 2:1 in other EMDEs, where borrowing costs (11.7% average clean WACC vs. ~4.6% OECD baseline) erase natural renewable cost advantages. Human Inclusion Anchors Convergence Legitimacy: Closing Sub-Saharan Africa’s 970 million clean-cooking deficit (within a 2.0–2.1 billion global deficit) and electrification gap alongside foreign-exchange guarantees, digital grid modernization, and green industrial value-chain upgrading can lift aggregate EMDE per-capita income toward 50.3% of the OECD average by 2040 while avoiding $4.3 trillion in stranded fossil assets.

title: Impact of continuous low-pH acidification on nitrogen retention and gaseous emissions from raw and separated pig slurry
summary: Livestock manure management is a major source of N H 3 and greenhouse gas emissions, representing a critical environmental challenge for intensive animal production systems. Although slurry acidification is a well-established technique for
content: Livestock manure management is a major source of N H 3 and greenhouse gas emissions, representing a critical environmental challenge for intensive animal production systems. Although slurry acidification is a well-established technique for reducing gaseous emissions, most studies have focused on one-time applications targeting pH values between 5.0 and 6.0. In contrast, the effectiveness and acid requirements of continuous acidification at low pH throughout storage have not been comprehensively evaluated. The aim of this work is to evaluate the effectiveness of a continuous acidification strategy -maintaining a target pH of 5.0- combined with solid-liquid separation, and to assess its effects on slurry physicochemical composition, gaseous emissions, and acid consumption. A controlled experiment was conducted with raw and separated slurry samples where sulphuric acid was applied with weekly adjustments to maintain the target pH. Gaseous emissions were quantified using open dynamic ( N H 3 and C O 2 ) and closed static chamber ( C H 4 ) techniques. Results demonstrated that the adopted approach achieved a near-complete abatement of N H 3 emissions (97%–100%) and full suppression of C H 4 emissions. C O 2 emissions were significantly reduced by 36%–80% depending on slurry type and experimental week. Furthermore, the treatment enhanced nitrogen retention, preventing a 40%–44% loss of total ammoniacal nitrogen and total Kjeldahl nitrogen observed in the non-acidified slurry, while organic matter degradation was inhibited. These findings identify continuous low-pH acidification as a promising approach that warrants further investigation in both controlled environments and real-farm conditions to fully assess its effectiveness and evaluate its technical and economic feasibility.

title: Spatial mismatch of territorial carbon balance and supply-chain carbon flow: regional carbon compensation in China
