title: Ammonia from Seawater and Air as a Marine Fuel: Port-Side Production with the Arbok-Lacmus Platform
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Shipping burns about 300 million tonnes of fuel a year, at a cost of about USD 200 billion, and emits more than 700 million tonnes of CO₂. Ammonia is a carbon-free candidate for marine fuel, but today it is made from natural gas, in central
content: Shipping burns about 300 million tonnes of fuel a year, at a cost of about USD 200 billion, and emits more than 700 million tonnes of CO₂. Ammonia is a carbon-free candidate for marine fuel, but today it is made from natural gas, in centralized plants operating at 150–300 bar and 400–500°C, at USD 300–600 per tonne with price swings between USD 200 and USD 1,000. Green ammonia from electrolysis costs USD 600–1,000 per tonne. This paper describes the use of the Arbok-Lacmus platform, which produces ammonia from seawater and atmospheric air with an energy intensity below 4 MWh per tonne and a production cost of USD 120–180 per tonne, as a port-side marine fuel source. We present the module and cluster architecture (1–10 tonnes per day per module, 50–200 tonnes per day per cluster), the quay layout for direct bunkering, and an economic model for a 16 MW tanker. At production cost, the fuel bill of such a ship falls from about USD 33 thousand to USD 14–21 thousand per day, a saving of USD 4–6 million per year per ship. Because ammonia also serves the fertilizer market of USD 70–90 billion per year, a port cluster is not dependent on a single buyer and pays back in 2–4 years. Keywords: ammonia, marine fuel, seawater, decentralized production, port bunkering, decarbonization, fertilizer, Arbok-Lacmus

title: Do Biodiversity Disclosures Translate Into Corporate Green Excellence? Exploring From CEO Global Experience Within Sustainable‐Oriented Agreement
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Referring to the IPBES Global Assessment on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services report, global companies have been challenged by calls for global protection of biodiversity and nature. Companies play a crucial role in communicating
content: ABSTRACT Referring to the IPBES Global Assessment on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services report, global companies have been challenged by calls for global protection of biodiversity and nature. Companies play a crucial role in communicating their protection activities. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effect of biodiversity disclosure on corporate green excellence by considering the moderating role of CEO global exposure. To test empirically, this study used a sample of 26,232 firm‐year observations from the Top World's Most Sustainable Companies for the period 2018–2023, using a panel data regression approach. This study found that companies that practice biodiversity disclosure are associated with higher corporate green excellence. In addition, the moderating role of CEO global exposure also strengthens the influence of biodiversity disclosure practices on corporate green excellence. This study is expected to contribute practically and theoretically to the development of literature and governance. Companies are also expected to provide best‐practice guidelines related to biodiversity practices, thus positively influencing the sustainability ecosystem and green excellence.

title: Iridium Extraction and Recovery from Primary Ores and Secondary Materials: Process Chemistry, Metallurgical Routes, Selectivity, and Industrial Scale-Up—A Critical Review
source: Journal International Review of Research Studies
summary: Iridium is recovered mainly through platinum-group-metal production and specialized secondary-processing circuits, yet its chemical resistance, heterogeneous occurrence, and difficult separation from associated noble metals complicate proce
content: Iridium is recovered mainly through platinum-group-metal production and specialized secondary-processing circuits, yet its chemical resistance, heterogeneous occurrence, and difficult separation from associated noble metals complicate process selection. This critical review compares primary concentrates, refinery intermediates, industrial catalyst scrap, and end-of-life proton-exchange-membrane electrolyzer components across mineralogical characterization, thermal activation, dissolution chemistry, selective refining, and industrial integration. A structured bibliography covering 1960–2026 contrasts process mechanisms and evidence quality, without interpreting isolated laboratory dissolution as industrial recovery. The synthesis identifies mineral deportment, feed-specific oxidation requirements, chloride-complex speciation, separation from rhodium and ruthenium, and complete-circuit material accounting as decisive variables. Thermochemical and electrochemical strategies offer different trade-offs in selectivity, corrosion, safety, energy intensity, and reagent recirculation. Product specifications, secondary-residue handling, and functional recovery yields must be considered jointly, not inferred from leachate concentration alone. The review proposes a feedstock-first decision framework and reporting criteria to compare routes and identify where independent scale-up evidence remains insufficient.

title: Integrating ESG Data into Management Accounting for Corporate Risk Management: Evidence from Kazakhstan
summary: The scale of ESG reporting is expanding more rapidly than the internal application of such data for management accounting and financial risk assessment, particularly in emerging markets. This study examines the relationship between ESG metr
content: The scale of ESG reporting is expanding more rapidly than the internal application of such data for management accounting and financial risk assessment, particularly in emerging markets. This study examines the relationship between ESG metrics and corporate financial risk, drawing on balanced panel data from six major Kazakhstani companies for the period 2017–2024. Financial risk is assessed as a multidimensional category through two channels: debt burden (financial leverage) and the ability to generate cash (free cash flow, or FCF, margin). Panel modeling of normalized ESG metrics reveals that these metrics vary in their significance regarding financial risk, with specific connections emerging between individual ESG factors and financial risk. Carbon intensity shows a significant positive correlation with financial leverage, indicating that debt-related risk is closely tied to environmental factors. Employee turnover exhibits a significant negative correlation with the FCF margin – a consistent pattern across both models – underscoring how personnel instability affects a company’s ability to generate cash flows. Meanwhile, the proportion of independent directors shows negative, yet statistically insignificant, coefficients in both models. These findings provide a foundation for risk-oriented ESG analysis, in which the importance of specific metrics is determined by the particular financial risk channel they influence, rather than through their mechanical aggregation into a single, unified index. The study broadens the analytical scope of managerial accounting, demonstrating that ESG data can be transformed from mere reporting information into a tool for the differentiated assessment of corporate risks. The results point to an association – rather than a direct causal relationship – between ESG factors and financial risk. These findings pave the way for the further evolution of ESG analytics, shifting from generalized assessments toward empirically grounded models. This approach makes it possible to account for the heterogeneity of ESG factors and the mechanisms through which they relate to various components of corporate financial risk.

title: Advancing the study of economic exploitation and inequality: introducing a new scholarly forum
source: The Journal of Economic Exploitation and Inequality
summary: Purpose This inaugural editorial introduces the Journal of Economic Exploitation and Inequality (JOEEI), outlining its intellectual foundations, scholarly objectives and commitment to advancing understanding of economic exploitation and ine
content: Purpose This inaugural editorial introduces the Journal of Economic Exploitation and Inequality (JOEEI), outlining its intellectual foundations, scholarly objectives and commitment to advancing understanding of economic exploitation and inequality. It establishes 10 priority research agendas addressing conceptual, methodological, technological, institutional and structural challenges, alongside questions concerning the effectiveness of policy and institutional interventions. The editorial also introduces the six articles published in the inaugural issue, situating them within contemporary theoretical, empirical and interdisciplinary debates. Design/methodology/approach The editorial adopts a conceptual and integrative approach, drawing on established academic scholarship and the six articles published in the inaugural issue. It engages with different theoretical traditions and methodological perspectives to examine how economic exploitation and inequality are understood and investigated. Through a critical synthesis of these contributions, the editorial considers their intellectual connections, differences and collective significance for advancing scholarship across economic and institutional contexts. Findings The editorial highlights the importance of examining economic exploitation and inequality through the interaction of structural conditions, institutional arrangements and individual behaviour. It illustrates how access to economic opportunities and formal protections may coexist with persistent disadvantages and exploitative practices. The analysis also indicates that different manifestations of exploitation may involve distinct mechanisms whose significance depends on particular economic and social contexts. These insights reinforce the importance of distinguishing unequal economic outcomes from exploitative relationships and recognising the limitations of explanations that overlook the complexity of economic power and institutional practices. Research limitations/implications The editorial provides a foundation for future scholarship that combines conceptual clarity, methodological rigour and openness to competing theoretical perspectives. It encourages research capable of identifying exploitative relationships, examining their underlying mechanisms and evaluating the consequences of economic and institutional arrangements. Particular importance is attached to interdisciplinary and international collaboration, critical interpretation of empirical evidence and engagement with diverse forms of knowledge. These considerations can contribute to more context-sensitive explanations and strengthen the theoretical and empirical foundations of research on economic exploitation and inequality. Social implications The editorial emphasises the potential contribution of rigorous economic research to public understanding and informed policy debate. It highlights the importance of examining how economic and organisational arrangements influence the exp

title: Ethical Business Governance for Viksit Bharat 2047: Lessons From the Arthashastra
summary: ABSTRACT This study explores the relevance of Kautilya's Arthashastra as a source of ethical guidance for modern business governance in India. Using a conceptual and comparative analytical approach, this study examines the convergence betwe
content: ABSTRACT This study explores the relevance of Kautilya's Arthashastra as a source of ethical guidance for modern business governance in India. Using a conceptual and comparative analytical approach, this study examines the convergence between Kautilyan governance principles and contemporary ESG (environmental, social, and governance)/CSR (corporate social responsibility) frameworks. As the nation strives towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, economic development must be anchored in ethical, sustainable, and socially inclusive practices. A qualitative, interpretive, and conceptual approach underpins the analysis, which draws on thematic examination of Kautilyan governance principles and comparative mapping with contemporary business governance frameworks and selected Indian corporate practices. Building on these insights, the study proposes an Indic Ethical Governance Framework (IEGF) that operationalizes ancient wisdom in contemporary corporate settings through six interrelated pillars—truth and transparency, justice and fairness, duty and responsibility, protection from harm, welfare orientation, and environmental harmony. Each pillar is linked to concrete implementation mechanisms and evaluation indicators and supported by a staged adoption model to facilitate practical application. The findings suggest that leveraging India's indigenous knowledge traditions can strengthen institutional integrity, enhance stakeholder trust, and support sustainable development, thereby contributing meaningfully to India's journey towards a developed, inclusive, and ethically grounded nation by 2047.

title: Evaluating biochemical traits and genetic parameters as selection criteria for salinity tolerance in Nigella sativa L.
summary: The present investigation was conducted to assess the performance of a high-yielding line (AN-1) of Nigella sativa under six NaCl levels (0, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 mM) over two crop seasons. Data were recorded for seed yield and eight contr
content: The present investigation was conducted to assess the performance of a high-yielding line (AN-1) of Nigella sativa under six NaCl levels (0, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 mM) over two crop seasons. Data were recorded for seed yield and eight contributing traits, viz., chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids, phenolics, flavonoids, protein content, catalase, and peroxidase activity. Fundamental statistical measures, including mean, standard error, variance, and coefficient of variation, were investigated along with broad-sense heritability and genetic advance. The data were also analyzed using principal component analysis (PCA), correlation analysis, and path coefficient analysis. Seed yield increased at 10 mM salt concentration and was 26% higher than the control, but thereafter decreased. Protein content increased by 23% at 100 mM. At 50mM, peroxidase (maximum: +47.78%) reached a peak; catalase increased till 50mM but decreased at 100mM. The top two PCs explained > 73% of the variance, with the variance dominated by peroxidase/flavonoids (+) and chlorophyll a/carotenoids (−). The genotypic coefficient of variation (GCV) and genetic advance were highest in peroxidase, catalase, and seed yield, while broad-sense heritability was high across all traits. Chlorophyll b was the only pigment that showed high GCV, heritability, and genetic advance, along with a significant positive correlation with yield. Path analysis indicated that the direct positive contributions came from flavonoids, catalase, and chlorophyll b. Catalase, peroxidase, and chlorophyll b exhibited high GCV, heritability, and genetic advance in both experimental years, which indicated that these traits are under genotypic control and should be utilized in selection programs to enhance yield on soils with low to moderate salinity.

title: Dataset- and Endpoint-Guided Co-Evolutionary Feature Engineering of Molecular Descriptor Spaces: Benchmarking on 14 Datasets and DILI Prediction
summary: Abstract Feature engineering remains a central challenge in Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, as the quality and relevance of molecular descriptors (MDs) directly determine predictive performance. Traditional app
content: Abstract Feature engineering remains a central challenge in Quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, as the quality and relevance of molecular descriptors (MDs) directly determine predictive performance. Traditional approaches rely on the overproduction and subsequent selection of descriptors, a paradigm that often leads to redundancy and suboptimal representations. This limitation motivates the development of approaches that directly optimize descriptor representations rather than relying on post hoc selection. In this study, we introduce a cooperative coevolutionary extension of the Algorithm to explore and optimize descriptor configuration spaces (AExOp-DCS), termed C-AExOp-DCS, which explores multiple MD configuration spaces (DCSs) while evaluating descriptors in a cross-DCS cooperative context. The method combines supervised and unsupervised relevance criteria through the Choquet integral and introduces context-dependent descriptor evaluation by recalculating mean decrease impurity (MDI) in the presence of collaborators from other DCS populations. The proposed approach was validated on 14 benchmark data sets covering pharmacological and ecotoxicological end points, where it generally achieved improved or comparable predictive performance relative to the original noncooperative AExOp-DCS, while remaining competitive with previously reported state-of-the-art QSAR models. Statistical analysis indicated a higher probability of improved generalization performance. Furthermore, C-AExOp-DCS-derived models matched or outperformed advanced machine-learning and deep-learning approaches for DILI prediction across heterogeneous external validation sets. SHAP and LIME analyses revealed a stable recurrent explanatory signature across the top-performing random forest models, comprising a five-member dominant and a nine-member extended QuBiLS-MAS descriptor core, with highly consistent global SHAP-importance profiles (Pearson r = 0.978–0.992; Spearman ρ = 0.921–0.934). Structural interpretation revealed complementary molecular representations consistent with physicochemical and structural determinants previously associated with DILI. Overall, these results support cooperative optimization of MD configuration spaces as an effective strategy for identifying informative and complementary molecular representations with strong predictive utility and interpretability in complex QSAR and predictive toxicology applications.

title: From Commercial to Residential: Exploring a Circular Economy Approach to Light Steel Framing Reuse Potential in Auckland
summary: Housing affordability and construction-related carbon emissions pose dual challenges for New Zealand’s built environment. Reusing light steel framing (LSF) could address both by lowering project costs and embodied carbon, yet little researc
content: Housing affordability and construction-related carbon emissions pose dual challenges for New Zealand’s built environment. Reusing light steel framing (LSF) could address both by lowering project costs and embodied carbon, yet little research has examined its feasibility in the New Zealand context. This study investigates barriers to LSF reuse, identifies potential sources of reusable inventory, proposes a non-destructive disassembly method aligned with the New Zealand Building Code, and applies these findings through a case study of H&M Commercial Bay in Auckland to quantify recoverable LSF and evaluate its reuse potential. A mixed-methods approach combined a structured narrative literature review, an assessment of the local building materials market, and a simulated deconstruction of the case study building. Results indicate that most LSF dimensions used in H&M Commercial Bay meet New Zealand residential structural framing requirements. Simulated deconstruction identified an estimated 18.09 tonnes of potentially recoverable LSF, which is a significant material resource for affordable housing. Successful reuse requires careful non-destructive disassembly, including screw-removal and reverse construction techniques, to minimise LSF building component damage, alongside complete component documentation and dimensional matching to residential framing requirements. The findings offer a replicable framework for incorporating reused LSF into affordable housing and support New Zealand’s transition toward a more sustainable and circular built environment.

title: Turning Silver into Green: How Rural Population Aging Drives Agricultural Green Development
summary: Abstract Amid the global transition toward greener agriculture and rapid demographic restructuring in rural China, the role of rural population aging in agricultural green development remains contested. Using provincial panel data for 30 Ch
content: Abstract Amid the global transition toward greener agriculture and rapid demographic restructuring in rural China, the role of rural population aging in agricultural green development remains contested. Using provincial panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2011–2024, this study develops an entropy-weighted composite index to quantify agricultural green development. To mitigate endogeneity concerns, we construct a Bartik (shift–share) instrumental variable based on historical ethnic composition from the 1982 Population Census, which allows us to causally estimate the impact of rural aging. The results indicate that rural population aging significantly enhances agricultural green development. Mechanism analysis shows that agricultural socialized services play a central mediating role by facilitating the adoption and diffusion of greener production practices. Heterogeneity tests further reveal that the positive effect is concentrated in the dimensions of output efficiency and green supply, and is stronger in regions with lower economic development and weaker socialized service capacity. These findings clarify how demographic pressure can be transformed into a source of green momentum, and they underscore the policy value of cultivating socialized service markets and designing differentiated regional interventions.

title: Houses of pain: Paying the energy poverty premium for energy inefficiency and inequity in Hungary
summary: This article utilizes the energy affordability ratio and the energy equity threshold to quantify the energy poverty premium in the Hungarian household sector. The focus on equity meets a call to tailor policy solutions to individual needs,
content: This article utilizes the energy affordability ratio and the energy equity threshold to quantify the energy poverty premium in the Hungarian household sector. The focus on equity meets a call to tailor policy solutions to individual needs, in a similar manner to other sectors, such as health, education, and the environment. The novel arrangement of these quantitative methods enables the identification of households that do and do not pay an equitable amount for energy services. The calculations are based on required energy expenditures according to the energy rating of the buildings, instead of the actual energy expenditures. It can be stated that despite regulated and highly subsidized energy prices in Hungary, which are applied uniformly across all households, they generate unequal financial burdens due to the poor energy efficiency of the building stock and low disposable income. There is persistent and onerous energy inequity for almost all Hungarian households. While the median energy affordability ratio is 4.33%, the ratio varies widely across households, with a maximum of 107.27%. The energy equity threshold is 270 kWh/m 2 a, above which energy poverty is significantly present. Five particularly vulnerable social groups were identified in our study: 1) single person households with at least one dependent child, 2) other single person, 3) pensioner, 4) unemployed, and 5) other economically inactive households. We can conclude that assessing differences in energy affordability across population groups in Hungary requires a new set of indicators. The Hungarian utility cost reduction program needs immediate reforms including more bands for the block pricing system, introduction of a social energy tariff, time of use pilot projects, and greater investment into energy efficiency.

title: Limonene: A potent biostimulant for improving the drought tolerance in industrial hemp
summary: Drought can significantly impact fiber crop cultivation due to the plants specific water requirements and its extended vegetative period. The objective of the research is to investigate the impact of various levels of foliar applied limonen
content: Drought can significantly impact fiber crop cultivation due to the plants specific water requirements and its extended vegetative period. The objective of the research is to investigate the impact of various levels of foliar applied limonene for improving the drought stress tolerance in hemp. To evaluate the mechanism of drought tolerance in hemp, a pot trial was conducted under greenhouse conditions comprising of two factors drought stress i.e., control = 75%–100% field capacity, moderate drought stress = 50%–60% field capacity and severe drought stress = 30–40% field capacity and various treatments of foliar applied limonene (L 0 = control; L 1 = 0.01%; L 2 = 0.03%; L 3 = 0.05%). The findings revealed that drought stress had negative effect on hemp growth at various growth stages, biomass (above and below ground), photosynthesis and gas exchange traits under various severity levels of the drought. Severe drought stress significantly decreased the leaf greenness value (27.73%), lipid peroxidation (108.96%) and modulated the activities of antioxidant enzymes in the hemp plants. The optimal level of limonene (L 2 treatment group) showed significant improvement in biomass, photosynthetic and osmolyte traits relative to untreated control treatments. Furthermore, the multivariate analyses confirmed that exogenous limonene application at an optimal rate coordinates physiological and biochemical responses to mitigate drought stress. Overall, it was concluded that limonene application at an optimal rate (0.03%) was beneficial in mitigating the adverse effects of drought by maintaining their growth and antioxidant enzymes activity. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding the mechanism by which limonene application mitigates the drought stress. This finding may have significant implications for farmers, as it provides a potential solution to mitigate the negative effects of water stress on fiber crop productivity.

title: Grass Jelly Species (Platostoma palustre, Premna trichostoma, and Cyclea barbata): Phytochemistry, Pharmacology, and Translational Potential—A Review
summary: Grass jelly, a traditional Southeast Asian dessert, comes from three plants: Platostoma palustre, Premna trichostoma, and Cyclea barbata. Despite over a century of lab studies, no clinical therapeutic use exists. Recent genomics identified
content: Grass jelly, a traditional Southeast Asian dessert, comes from three plants: Platostoma palustre, Premna trichostoma, and Cyclea barbata. Despite over a century of lab studies, no clinical therapeutic use exists. Recent genomics identified 1,228 metabolites in P. palustre and key flavonoid/polysaccharide pathways, but most compounds remain uncharacterized. Preclinical data show antioxidant (IC₅₀ = 2.512 ppm), antidiabetic (37.1% glucose reduction), antihypertensive (36.25% ACE inhibition), and anticancer (57% tumor reduction) effects—yet nearly all studies use crude extracts or multi‑herb mixes, making it impossible to attribute benefits specifically to grass jelly. Veterinary uses include improved sperm cryopreservation (80% vs. 63.3% conception) and 43.7% lower ammonia in poultry waste, but again with mixed formulations. Only one registered clinical trial exists (NCT02875275), and none tests grass jelly as a drug. We identify seven systemic gaps (e.g., extract‑based research, attribution confusion, missing pharmacokinetics) and propose a five‑phase framework to shift from descriptive work to mechanistic pharmacology—aiming to turn grass jelly into a model for phytochemical discovery and real‑world application.

title: Analysis of Long-term Investment Decision-making Problems of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China
source: Journal of Historical Cultural and Social Sciences
summary: This paper takes Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC) as the case company and analyzes the long-term investment decision-making and financial management issues of commercial banks. Based on the case materials concerning IC
content: This paper takes Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC) as the case company and analyzes the long-term investment decision-making and financial management issues of commercial banks. Based on the case materials concerning ICBC’s investments in technology finance, green finance, inclusive finance, pension finance, and digital financial infrastructure, the paper organizes indicators including the scale of long-term investment, the proportion of financial-asset investment, return on investment, investment payback period, net present value, and internal rate of return from 2022 to 2024. It further evaluates the actual effects of long-term investment decision-making from the perspectives of changes in investment scale, investment structure, return levels, cash-flow recovery, and risk management. The study finds that ICBC’s long-term investment is characterized by relatively strong strategic alignment, broad investment coverage, significant digital empowerment, and a solid risk-control foundation. However, the growth of long-term investment has not been accompanied by a corresponding improvement in investment efficiency: ROI, NPV, and IRR have all declined; the proportion of financial-asset investment remains relatively high; new investment projects do not sufficiently consider micro-level variables such as cross-border regulation, peer competition, and transaction volume; and some projects face prolonged cash-flow recovery periods and insufficient post-investment management. In response, this paper proposes optimizing the structure of financial and non-financial investments, improving a multidimensional investment evaluation system, strengthening cash-flow budgeting and maturity matching, and establishing dynamic risk-warning and post-investment evaluation mechanisms. By incorporating strategic objectives, financial indicators, cash-flow management, and risk control into a unified decision-making framework, commercial banks can further improve the efficiency of long-term fund allocation and achieve a better balance between returns and risks in a complex operating environment.

title: From Wholesale Fuel Shock to Network-and-Tax Wedge: Industrial Electricity Tariff Component Dispersion and Manufacturing Output in Europe
summary: When wholesale natural gas and power markets retreat from an acute supply shock, cross-country industrial electricity cost divergence persists as dispersion rotates from traded generation prices toward regulated grid charges and national fi
content: When wholesale natural gas and power markets retreat from an acute supply shock, cross-country industrial electricity cost divergence persists as dispersion rotates from traded generation prices toward regulated grid charges and national fiscal wedges. Applying an exact variance–covariance decomposition across all 27 European Union Member States from 2017 to 2025, with semi-annual tax-wedge tracking through the first half of 2026, we document a structural reconfiguration of non-household tariff dispersion across three audited price definitions. In the benchmark medium-scale industrial consumption band (500 to 1,999 MWh annually), the share of cross-country tariff variance attributable to energy and supply costs fell from 57.26% in 2023 to 33.85% in 2025, whereas the regulated network variance share doubled from 6.54% to 13.03% and the net non-recoverable tax variance share reached 22.55%. Across 25 paired Member States in 2025, medium-consumption facilities faced unit network charges 21.85 EUR/MWh above large electro-intensive users alongside an additional 10.98 EUR/MWh net fiscal differential. Combining predetermined 2017–2019 sectoral electricity and gas intensities with a mutually exclusive panel of eight manufacturing divisions across 20 Member States (N = 1,182, 2017–2025) under country-by-sector, country-by-year, and sector-by-year fixed effects, we find a negative conditional association between electricity intensity interacted with regulated network charges and real manufacturing output (-0.00191; wild cluster bootstrap p = 0.0130; Holm family-wise p = 0.0390 across three electricity components), which strengthens on the strictly post-base-period 2020–2025 panel (-0.00283, bootstrap p = 0.0177, N = 783), under a five-country technological benchmark (-0.00259, bootstrap p = 0.0298), and with sector linear trends (-0.00213, bootstrap p = 0.0348), while attenuated first-difference horizons and a negative extended pre-crisis lead (-0.00588, bootstrap p = 0.0290) highlight bidirectional revenue-cap denominator feedback.

title: Mechanical and early age performance of CO2 mineralized recycled fines from real waste stream sources compared to low calcium blends with traditional SCMs
summary: Abstract The declining availability of traditional supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) has increased interest in alternative low-carbon binder constituents. This study evaluates CO 2 -mineralized recycled fines obtained from three c
content: Abstract The declining availability of traditional supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) has increased interest in alternative low-carbon binder constituents. This study evaluates CO 2 -mineralized recycled fines obtained from three construction and demolition waste streams as clinker replacement in binders containing 30% Portland cement and 70% SCMs. Mineralization increased calcium carbonate content and improved the reactivity of the recycled fines. The materials were investigated using calorimetry, thermogravimetric analysis, porosity measurements, and compressive strength testing on mortar bars. Compared with untreated recycled fines, mineralized materials showed greater early-age reactivity, resulting in higher heat release and calcium hydroxide consumption after calorimetry. They also refined pore structure by reducing threshold pore size. Mortars containing 70% mineralized recycled concrete fines achieved higher 28-day strength than blends containing natural pozzolan with limestone and performed similarly to limestone-calcined clay systems with the same clinker content. Environmental assessment indicated a favorable balance between strength and carbon emissions, particularly when accounting for carbon dioxide uptake during mineralization.

title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
summary: Cracking of polyolefins is a prerequisite for their selective conversion over microporous zeolites to value-added small molecules such as monocyclic aromatics. However, cracking and aromatization often proceed concurrently, creating an intr
content: Cracking of polyolefins is a prerequisite for their selective conversion over microporous zeolites to value-added small molecules such as monocyclic aromatics. However, cracking and aromatization often proceed concurrently, creating an intrinsic accessibility-selectivity conflict that limits aromatic yield and productivity. This paper describes a strategy that temporally decouples polyolefin cracking from selective aromatization in one-pot with tandem catalysts. This strategy delivers an aromatic yield of ca. 60.3 wt% within 0.5 h at 380 °C from postconsumer polyolefins over 40 consecutive cycles, corresponding to an aromatic space-time yield of 11 g gcat−1 h−1, more than twofold higher than reported values of ≤ 5 g gcat−1 h−1. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal that self-pillared pentasil zeolite rapidly and processively cracks polyolefins to small olefinic intermediates below 320 °C, enabling temporal decoupling of low-temperature cracking from higher-temperature aromatization through distinct dominant kinetic windows. Process modeling further suggests favorable economic potential and life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions 26% lower than fossil-based aromatics production and 66% lower than incineration. This work establishes temporal decoupling as a reaction-engineering strategy for reconciling polymer accessibility with micropore-controlled selectivity in plastic upcycling. Turning plastic waste into useful chemicals is limited because breaking polymer chains and controlling products need conflicting conditions. This study separates these steps in time, enabling fast, durable aromatic production with lower emissions.

title: Sorting the Eco-Citizen: Household Waste and Governmentality in Singapore
summary: This article examines how ecological citizenship is differentially enacted by residents in Singapore through everyday waste practices. It argues that household waste management is a key site through which the state governs environmental con
content: This article examines how ecological citizenship is differentially enacted by residents in Singapore through everyday waste practices. It argues that household waste management is a key site through which the state governs environmental conduct by framing waste routines as civic responsibility and mobilising residents to sustain a highly engineered sociotechnical regime. Drawing on a stratified household survey of 672 respondents conducted between December 2024 and January 2025, complemented by interviews with residents, the study develops an Ecological Citizenship Index (ECI) based on waste-related behaviours, perceived responsibility and environmental awareness. It shows that ecological citizenship is shaped less by ethnicity or income than by unequal capacities linked to education, gendered domestic labour, work constraints, housing conditions and neighbourhood infrastructure. The Singaporean eco-citizen thus emerges as a socially differentiated subject. More broadly, the article contributes to debates on environmental governmentality and post-political environmentalism by highlighting how responsibilisation sustains urban order.

title: A Luciferase Reporter of Ester Prodrug Delivery to the Cytosol of Intracellular Mycobacteria
summary: The bacterial cell envelope restricts access to cytoplasmic targets and is a principal reason that otherwise potent antibacterial compounds fail in cells. Masking an anionic carboxylic acid as an ester is a common way to cross that barrier,
content: The bacterial cell envelope restricts access to cytoplasmic targets and is a principal reason that otherwise potent antibacterial compounds fail in cells. Masking an anionic carboxylic acid as an ester is a common way to cross that barrier, but the strategy succeeds only if the target organism also hydrolyzes the ester once the compound arrives. These two requirements, permeation and intracellular unmasking, are rarely measured together in live bacterial cells, and existing reporters cannot specify where unmasking occurred. Here we describe a bioluminescent platform that resolves both steps in real time in live mycobacteria using carboxylate esters of D-luciferin. Luciferase requires that an ester both reach the bacterial cytoplasm and be hydrolyzed there, which makes light a compartment-specific readout of productive delivery. Across a series of alkyl esters in Mycobacterium smegmatis, chain length governed permeation while branching adjacent to the carbonyl governed esterase processing, indicating that the two parameters can be tuned independently. The n-butyl ester gave the strongest signal in broth, in infected macrophages, and in the pathogen Mycobacterium avium, whereas the tert-butyl ester was inert in Mycobacterium avium and unmasking of the whole series was attenuated at phagosomal pH. Ester activation is therefore both species- and compartment-dependent, and masking groups are best selected in the organism and environment in which they must act.

title: Integration vs. Segregation: Can Autochthonous Silvopastoral Systems Enhance Economic Viability and Ecological Functionality of the Brazilian Cerrado?
summary: Abstract The Brazilian Cerrado, a global biodiversity hotspot, faces severe threats from agricultural and livestock expansion. This study explores autochthonous silvopastoral systems (SPS) as a strategy to enhance ecosystem services (ES) in
content: Abstract The Brazilian Cerrado, a global biodiversity hotspot, faces severe threats from agricultural and livestock expansion. This study explores autochthonous silvopastoral systems (SPS) as a strategy to enhance ecosystem services (ES) in the Cerrado landscape. We mapped the potential for expanding SPS and compared the Potential for Conservationist Use (PCU) scenario to a Business-as-Usual (BaU) scenario in the Upper Pardo River basin, Brazil. Overall, soil and slope conditions are favorable, whereas low annual water yield limits productive land use in 23.9% of the land. Results confirm that SPS adoption in high-suitability land cover types – such as savanna formations, perennial crops, and forest plantations – is a viable strategy to enhance ES and promote sustainable land use. Under the BaU scenario, native vegetation covered 66.1% of the study area and 89.5% of total economic output (~ USD 1.46 billion/year) was derived from ES provision. SPS expansion in the PCU scenario reduced native vegetation cover to 40.8%, yielding higher economic output (~ USD 1.53 billion/year), with ES accounting for 81.2% of the total. These results demonstrate that SPS can enhance multifunctionality and economic output when targeted to suitable landscapes, underscoring the importance of spatial planning and supporting public policies, such as payment for ES.

title: Symbiotic Strategy and Organizational Growth in Complex Business Ecosystems
summary: This book addresses the growth ceiling confronting incumbent firms mired in stock-market saturation and technological disruption and explores how to pivot from a “zero-sum competitive logic” to a “logic of ecological co-growth.” Its distinc
content: This book addresses the growth ceiling confronting incumbent firms mired in stock-market saturation and technological disruption and explores how to pivot from a “zero-sum competitive logic” to a “logic of ecological co-growth.” Its distinctiveness lies in moving beyond conventional strategic frameworks: it reconceives the external environment as a three-dimensional ecological space defined by reach, richness, and rejuvenation; sets out three basic types of symbiotic strategy and four modes of implementation; and introduces an original value co-creation formula incorporating symbiotic emergent value (Ω), a VCEE four-dimensional model, and an AI-native pathway for the evolution of human-machine organizations—offering a new theoretical paradigm for commercial civilization in the digital-intelligent and AI era. The book serves both scholars and doctoral students in strategic management seeking to extend the research frontier and executives and practitioners navigating transformation. Readers gain not only an ecological worldview that breaks cognitive boundaries but also a practical toolkit comprising the “five core capabilities” and the “ecological-niche potential scorecard,” equipping organizations to transcend involution and achieve adaptive, exponential carbon-silicon growth.

title: No Silver Bullet for Digital Transformation: The Role of Managerial Ambidexterity and International Context
summary: Abstract Background/Purpose This study examines the role of managerial ambidexterity in enabling digital transformation within diverse national cultural contexts. It advances a more nuanced understanding of digital transformation as a manag
content: Abstract Background/Purpose This study examines the role of managerial ambidexterity in enabling digital transformation within diverse national cultural contexts. It advances a more nuanced understanding of digital transformation as a managerially guided, culturally grounded process rather than a universally applicable technological solution. Methods An integrative literature review was conducted, combining bibliometric analysis and qualitative thematic synthesis. Data were collected from publications indexed in the Web of Science database between January 2020 and January 2026. VOSviewer software was used to identify publication trends, geographical distribution, keyword co-occurrence, and authorship network. Following the bibliometric analysis, 30 studies were purposively selected for in-depth synthesis. Results Study findings confirm that managerial ambidexterity plays a central role in navigating the exploration–exploitation paradox during digital transformation. Its effectiveness is shaped by national culture characteristics and managerial practices, highlighting the importance of contextual factors in shaping transformation outcomes. Conclusion The study highlights the need to develop more adaptive, dynamic ambidextrous capabilities that align digital transformation initiatives with diverse national cultural contexts. It contributes to the growing literature on digital transformation by proposing an integrative framework that conceptualizes managerial ambidexterity as a context-dependent micro-foundational mechanism through which digital transformation is enacted and shaped across diverse national cultural environments.

title: Building collaboration in FMCG supply chains: a time-based perspective
source: Supply Chain Management An International Journal
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how supply chain collaboration (SCC) initiatives in logistics develop and are sustained over time. While SCC is widely discussed in the literature, existing research predominantly adopts static perspective
content: Purpose This study aims to examine how supply chain collaboration (SCC) initiatives in logistics develop and are sustained over time. While SCC is widely discussed in the literature, existing research predominantly adopts static perspectives, treating collaboration mechanisms as stable configurations rather than temporally evolving practices. This study addresses this gap by adopting a temporal, process-oriented perspective on SCC development. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative multiple-case research design, analysing 15 collaboration initiatives across nine companies, comprising major food retailers and multinational producers, operating in the Italian Fast-Moving Consumer Goods sector. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, pre-interview questionnaires and company documentation and analysed through within-case and cross-case analysis. Findings The findings show that collaboration mechanisms do not function uniformly across the lifecycle of an initiative: their role and relevance shift as partnerships mature. The cross-case analysis identifies two additional empirical insights: collaborative function autonomy, the degree of operational independence enjoyed by logistics teams in driving collaboration, and the dual role of time, both as an operational resource and as a relational enabler of trust. Building on these insights, the study proposes a time-based framework mapping how mechanisms are introduced, adapted and sustained across four phases: inception, development, execution and evolution. Practical implications The framework provides managers with a phased roadmap for designing and managing collaborative initiatives, supporting more realistic expectations about the pace of collaboration and the investments required at each stage. It also functions as a diagnostic tool, enabling organisations to identify gaps in their collaborative capabilities and plan targeted interventions. Originality/value The study’s central theoretical contribution is the concept of collaborative timing: the strategic alignment of mechanism introduction with the relational and operational maturity of the partnership. This concept is grounded in two supporting empirical contributions: first, evidence that established SCC mechanisms acquire different roles depending on the phase of an initiative; and second, a time-based framework that distinguishes phase-specific from continuous mechanisms across four phases (inception, development, execution, evolution).

title: Challenges to Adopting Eco-Friendly Maritime Solutions: Barriers and Perceived Impacts of Green Shipping Among Malaysian Maritime Stakeholders
summary: The transition to lower-emission shipping requires coordinated investment in vessel technology, alternative-fuel supply chains, port infrastructure, workforce capability, and regulatory implementation. This study examines the perceived barr
content: The transition to lower-emission shipping requires coordinated investment in vessel technology, alternative-fuel supply chains, port infrastructure, workforce capability, and regulatory implementation. This study examines the perceived barriers to green shipping adoption and the anticipated or experienced impacts among Malaysian maritime stakeholders. An exploratory questionnaire-based assessment was interpreted using the Relative Importance Index (RII) alongside a contextual review of maritime decarbonisation literature and policy. Six adoption barriers and six reported impact indicators were compared descriptively. Implementation and maintenance costs were the highest-rated obstacle (RII = 0.80), followed by alternative-fuel and infrastructure availability (0.74), technological readiness (0.68), market cost pressure (0.64), regulatory harmonisation (0.62), and workforce capability (0.62). Among perceived impacts, digital emissions monitoring scored highest (0.78), followed by fuel efficiency and alternative-fuel integration (0.70 each); reported greenhouse-gas reduction (0.60) and operational cost savings (0.54) were comparatively lower. These indices represent respondent perceptions, not verified emissions or financial savings. The findings favour a phased transition strategy combining financing support, safe fuel infrastructure, technical capability-building, performance measurement, and public–private cooperation. Interpretation is exploratory because respondent-level observations, a definitive achieved sample count, and inferential model outputs were not available for independent analysis.

title: Heat Resilience of Hospitals: Identification of Key Resilience Dimensions and Development of a Conceptual Structure Model : An Exploratory Study Based on Literature Analysis and Expert Interviews = Hitzeresilienz von Krankenhäusern: Identifikation zentraler Resilienzdimensionen und Entwicklung eines konzeptionellen Strukturmodells : Eine explorative Untersuchung mittels Literaturanalyse und Experteninterviews
summary: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense due to climate change, creating growing challenges for hospitals that must maintain essential healthcare services while coping with increased thermal stress.Despite the increasing relevance o
content: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense due to climate change, creating growing challenges for hospitals that must maintain essential healthcare services while coping with increased thermal stress.Despite the increasing relevance of climate adaptation in healthcare, a conceptual framework for understanding heat resilience at the hospital level remains largely underdeveloped.This working paper develops a conceptual structure model of hospital heat resilience by combining an exploratory literature review with qualitative expert interviews conducted in the German hospital sector.The analysis identifies four core internal dimensions of hospital heat resilience: governance and management, buildings and technical infrastructure, patient care and clinical processes, and workforce.Findings suggest that resilience emerges not from isolated measures within these domains but from their interaction and mutual dependence.In addition, financing and investment capacity as well as external cooperation and networking are identified as overarching contextual factors shaping the implementation and effectiveness of adaptation measures to reach heat resilience in individual hospitals.The resulting structure model provides a systematic framework for understanding hospital heat resilience and highlights the distinction between internal resilience dimensions and external enabling conditions.While the findings are exploratory and based on a limited number of expert interviews, the model offers a foundation for future empirical validation and the development of indicator-based assessment, self-evaluation, and decision-support tools for hospital climate adaptation.Kurzzusammenfassung: Der Klimawandel führt zu einer zunehmenden Häufigkeit und Intensität von Hitzewellen, wodurch Krankenhäuser vor die Herausforderung gestellt werden, ihre Versorgungs-und Betriebsfähigkeit auch unter steigenden thermischen Belastungen aufrechtzuerhalten.Auf Grundlage einer explorativen Literaturauswertung und qualitativer Experteninterviews wird ein konzeptionelles Strukturmodell der Hitzeresilienz von Krankenhäusern entwickelt.Die Analyse identifiziert vier organisationsinterne Resilienzdimensionen: Organisation und Steuerung, Gebäude und technische Infrastruktur, Patientenversorgung und klinische Prozesse sowie Personal.Ergänzend werden Finanzierung und Investitionsfähigkeit sowie externe Kooperation und Vernetzung als übergreifende Rahmenbedingungen identifiziert.Das entwickelte Strukturmodell bietet einen systematischen Bezugsrahmen für die Analyse von Hitzeresilienz und kann als Grundlage für zukünftige indikatorbasierte Bewertungs-und Entscheidungsunterstützungsinstrumente dienen.

title: Aloe vera-mediated green-synthesized silver nanoparticles enhance physiological performance and yield in bread wheat
summary: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (GS-AgNPs) have emerged as promising nano-biostimulant for improving crop productivity; however, their physiological effects under field conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study synthesi
content: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (GS-AgNPs) have emerged as promising nano-biostimulant for improving crop productivity; however, their physiological effects under field conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study synthesized Aloe vera-mediated GS-AgNPs and characterized them using UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, DLS, zeta potential, XRD, SEM, and EDX analyses. The synthesized GS-AgNPs exhibited concentration-dependent antioxidants, antifungal, antihemolytic, and phytostimulatory activities. Their agronomic potential was evaluated through foliar application at 5, 10, and 15 ppm to four bread wheat cultivars under field conditions. GS-AgNP application significantly enhanced growth, photosynthetic pigments, antioxidant defense, nitrogen metabolism, nutrient accumulation, grain nutritional quality, and yield in a cultivar-dependent manner. The 15 ppm treatment produced the greatest responses for several measured traits, although some trait-specific maxima occurred at 10 ppm. Grain yield in Borlaug-16 increased from 2.35 ± 0.11 to 6.93 ± 1.10 g plant −1 , corresponding to a 194.9% increase, while biological yield in Wafaq-23 increased by 94.25%, chlorophyll a in Zincol-16 by 216.4%, carotenoids in Wafaq-23 by 274.3%, urease activity in Zincol-16 by 169.3%, protein content in Borlaug-16 by 63.1%, and stem phosphorus in Wafaq-23 by 222.5%. Malondialdehyde, hydrogen peroxide, proline, and electrolyte leakage were reduced by 50.0%, 33.0%, 50.7%, and 26.6%, respectively. Multivariate analyses revealed strong associations among physiological, biochemical, nutritional, and yield-related traits. Collectively, low-dose Aloe vera-mediated GS-AgNPs improved wheat performance with no apparent phytotoxic effects under the tested conditions and concentrations, highlighting their potential as nano-biostimulant for wheat production.

title: Managing Tourism Impacts: A Comprehensive Practical Guide for Destination Managers, Policymakers, Researchers, Practitioners, and Tourism Stakeholders
summary: Managing Tourism Impacts offers a practical, data-driven framework that helps destinations understand, measure, and manage the full spectrum of tourism impacts to support resilient, community-centred, sustainable development. This book prov
content: Managing Tourism Impacts offers a practical, data-driven framework that helps destinations understand, measure, and manage the full spectrum of tourism impacts to support resilient, community-centred, sustainable development. This book provides actionable tools, metrics, governance models, and management strategies that move beyond growth indicators to focus on real impacts on residents’ wellbeing, health, and long-term resilience. Grounded in global empirical evidence, original measurement models, and applied case studies, it shows how destinations can anticipate, monitor, and mitigate negative impacts while amplifying positive outcomes. By translating advanced research into clear practical guidance, it provides a comprehensive system linking impact measurement to policy design, destination governance, monitoring frameworks, and community-centred tourism strategies. This text is designed for DMOs, policymakers, government agencies, tourism boards, international organizations, consultants, tourism providers, and community leaders seeking practical evidence-based approaches to managing tourism impacts. It is equally valuable for academics, researchers, and postgraduate students looking for an applied governance-focused framework for sustainable and resilient tourism development.

title: Soil Moisture Regimes Alter Growth-Stage-Specific Relationships between Growth Characteristics and Storage Root Yield in Sweet Potato
summary: Soil moisture availability is a major environmental factor affecting sweet potato growth and storage root yields, particularly under increasingly variable drought and excessive rainfall conditions.This study evaluated the growth-stage-speci
content: Soil moisture availability is a major environmental factor affecting sweet potato growth and storage root yields, particularly under increasingly variable drought and excessive rainfall conditions.This study evaluated the growth-stage-specific responses of sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam.cv.Jinyulmi) to contrasting soil moisture regimes over three consecutive years (2023-2025) under rain-shelter greenhouse conditions.Three moisture treatments-severe drought (DD), optimal moisture (N), and excessively wet soil conditions (WW)-were evaluated in 2023, and five treatments-DD, drought (D), N, wet soil conditions (W), and WW-were evaluated in 2024 and 2025.Stem length, stem diameter, and the SPAD value were measured at the storage root initiation, bulking, and pre-harvest stages, and their relationships with storage root weight were analyzed.Soil moisture treatments were clearly differentiated, with the mean volumetric soil water content in the N treatment maintained at 31.3-33.6%.The N treatment generally maintained relatively high SPAD values during the bulking and pre-harvest stages and produced the highest storage root yield in all three years, reaching 31, 49, and 37 Mg ha -1 in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively.Correlation patterns varied with the growth stage and soil moisture regime.Under the optimal moisture condition, the SPAD value and/or stem growth were positively associated with the storage root weight across growth stages, whereas drought and excessive soil moisture altered these relationships.Storage root yield was substantially reduced under both water-deficit and excessively wet conditions.These results demonstrate that the soil moisture regime modifies the relationships among shoot growth, leaf greenness, and storage root development, suggesting that maintaining soil moisture near the range associated with the highest observed storage root yield under the conditions in this study is important for stable sweet potato production under variable water conditions.

title: The Twinning Power of Data : Understanding How Data Drive Digital and Sustainable Transformation
summary: Societal disruptions have grown in intensity, frequency, and mutual entanglement, converging into a polycrisis that confronts organizations with unprecedented structural pressures. Digital technologies play an ambivalent role in this contex
content: Societal disruptions have grown in intensity, frequency, and mutual entanglement, converging into a polycrisis that confronts organizations with unprecedented structural pressures. Digital technologies play an ambivalent role in this context: they enable new forms of coordination and value creation, yet also risk reinforcing the unsustainable patterns they could help overcome. How digitalization can move from part of the problem to part of the solution has therefore become a defining question for information systems (IS) research - one increasingly addressed through the interplay of digital transformation and sustainability transformation. Recent debates on twin transformation conceptualize these two agendas as mutually reinforcing, yet how such reinforcement is enacted in organizational practice remains insufficiently understood. This dissertation argues that sustainability-related data constitute the connective resource through which digital and sustainability transformation become linked: digital technologies generate and process the data that make sustainability-related phenomena visible and actionable, while sustainability objectives determine which data matter and how they should be governed within digital systems and decision processes. Building on this argument, the dissertation addresses the overarching research question: How do data drive digital and sustainability transformation to become mutually reinforcing? Drawing on nine research papers, the dissertation develops a cumulative sociotechnical perspective on data-based twin transformation, structured around two reciprocal directions. The first is the enabling direction, in which digital transformation creates the data foundations and organizational capabilities that make sustainability-related phenomena manageable in the first place - for instance by conceptualizing ESG data as heterogeneous, purpose-bound objects and by specifying maturity pathways for sustainability data management and industrial decarbonization. The second is the guiding direction, in which sustainability transformation shapes what digital systems measure, optimize, and make credible, as illustrated through studies on carbon-aware energy management, sustainable mobility, and digitally verifiable carbon information. The dissertation then brings both directions together, showing how sustainability-related data are mobilized for strategic value within an interorganizational network and how enabling and guiding capabilities jointly shape the reciprocal relationship between the two transformations. Theoretically, the dissertation contributes to Green IS research by developing a data perspective on the mutual reinforcement of digital and sustainability transformation. It refines the emerging theory of twin transformation by showing that this relationship is neither automatic nor unidirectional: sustainability-related data become valuable only through organizational capabilities that make them usable, just as sustainabil

title: Accelerating Renewables Without Sacrificing Justice: Institutional Pathways to Sustainable Development in Europe
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether renewable energy project delivery across the European Union can be accelerated without weakening institutional legitimacy and procedural justice, focusing on permitting design, grid connection governance
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether renewable energy project delivery across the European Union can be accelerated without weakening institutional legitimacy and procedural justice, focusing on permitting design, grid connection governance, public‐sector policy capacity and justice and participation quality as the institutional conditions that shape delivery outcomes. A balanced country‐year panel of 275 observations for 25 European Union countries during 2015–2025 is constructed from ENTSO‐E, ACER, V‐Dem and World Bank sources, and the resulting Permitting Design Index, Grid Connection Bottleneck Index, policy‐capacity measure, and Justice and Participation Quality index are analysed using fixed‐effects, dynamic‐panel system‐GMM, instrumental‐variable, bootstrap mediation and moderation models. Stronger permitting design is associated with a lower share of projects scheduled beyond 2030, and this association operates partly through grid connection governance and public‐sector policy capacity, while strengthening further where procedural justice and participation mechanisms are more developed. These patterns indicate that administrative acceleration advances climate and clean‐energy objectives only when it is embedded in capable, coordinated and legitimate institutions, which challenges the assumption that participatory safeguards necessarily slow renewable deployment. The study identifies the institutional pathways linking formal climate‐policy ambition to implementation outcomes, and the findings imply that progress towards SDGs 7 and 13 should be pursued together with the participatory and accountable institutions embodied in SDG 16, with permitting deadlines combined with transparent queue management, adequately resourced administrations and early, fair participation.

title: The role of rubber and label disruptors in the re-processing of polyester from PET-rich textile Wastes
summary: From a global perspective, the share of post-consumer textile waste subjected to recycling amounts to a mere 0.5 %, whereas most textile waste ends up in landfills or incineration. Often this is the consequence of apparel being composed of
content: From a global perspective, the share of post-consumer textile waste subjected to recycling amounts to a mere 0.5 %, whereas most textile waste ends up in landfills or incineration. Often this is the consequence of apparel being composed of fiber blends, e.g. cotton/polyester. Recycling of such mixed textile waste at their end-of-life is challenging because of elementary differences in the structure and chemical properties of the constituents. Moreover, small fractions of impurities and contaminants as well as residues from the other fiber type(s), have commonly to be accepted to some extent. In particular, minor elements of apparel, for instance labels or rubber bands, can usually not be completely removed with reasonable effort because of chemical similarities with the main textile fibers. Consequently, during re-processing and compounding of recovered polymers, such elements and disruptors are inevitably present and are hypothesized to play a major role in the mechanical performance of recycled polymers. In this study the impact of potential disruptors commonly present in mixed fiber waste, in particular labels and rubber bands, on the mechanical performance of recovered polymers was investigated. Model formulations of polyester obtained from PET-rich waste streams with known fractions of disruptors were thermo-mechanically re-processed on a conical, co-rotating laboratory scale twin screw extruder and their mechanical properties characterized. Whereas labels had only a small impact on the mechanical performance of recovered polyester, rubber present during extrusion caused a decrease in tensile strength by more than 40 % from 63 to 36 MPa. This was assigned to degradation processes taking place in-situ at processing temperatures, resulting in chain scission and influencing the crystallization behavior.

title: Large-scale, low-cost, and low-pollution separation of end-of-life silicon photovoltaic modules via a combined mechanical peeling and pyrolysis strategy
source: Waste Management & Research The Journal for a Sustainable Circular Economy
summary: Developing an eco-friendly route for resource recovery from end-of-life (EOL) crystalline silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules is in high demand. Herein, an automated pilot-scale disassembly line was constructed to mechanically separate backsh
content: Developing an eco-friendly route for resource recovery from end-of-life (EOL) crystalline silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules is in high demand. Herein, an automated pilot-scale disassembly line was constructed to mechanically separate backsheets, glass, and ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulant with embedded silicon cells and solder ribbons from EOL PV modules. This prevents backsheets and glass from entering subsequent pyrolysis, inhibits fluorinated gas generation, and reduces energy consumption. The thermal behavior of EVA was analyzed by TG-DSC in air. Subsequently, approximately 2 kg of peeled EVA encapsulant was pyrolyzed in a pilot-scale furnace under different airflow rates to achieve complete removal of the encapsulant, yielding clean and bright crushed silicon cells and solder ribbons. Scanning electron microscope and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analyses show that airflow rate significantly impacts residual carbon content on silicon cell surfaces; surface carbon content drops from 18.59 wt% to 4.92 wt% when airflow rate increases from 10 to 40 L/min. The results verify that the integrated mechanical peeling-pyrolysis process is promising for large-scale green recycling of EOL PV modules.

title: DESIGN AND APPLICATION OF A COMPREHENSIVE SUPERVISION PLATFORM FOR OCEAN PASTURES BASED ON THE INTERNET OF THINGS: A CASE STUDY OF DONGCHANG BAY, XUWEN COUNTY, ZHANJIANG CITY, GUANGDONG PROVINCE
summary: Ocean pastures are the core carrier for restoring offshore ecosystems and conserving fishery resources, and an important lever for advancing the building of the “Blue Granary”. At the grassroots level in China, however, ocean pastures gener
content: Ocean pastures are the core carrier for restoring offshore ecosystems and conserving fishery resources, and an important lever for advancing the building of the “Blue Granary”. At the grassroots level in China, however, ocean pastures generally suffer from practical weaknesses such as low coverage of intelligent equipment, weak capacity for environmental risk early warning and short industrial chains for the integration of the primary, secondary and tertiary industries. Taking the ocean pasture in Dongchang Bay, Xuwen County, Zhanjiang City, Guangdong Province as the research object, this study conducted water quality monitoring in the spring and autumn seasons of 2019 and 2021 and combined the results with 372 valid questionnaires answered by aquaculture practitioners to establish the environmental baseline characteristics of the sea area and the needs of practitioners, and on this basis constructed a four-layer comprehensive supervision platform covering “perception–transmission–decision–application”. The platform comprises four modules: intelligent environmental monitoring, intelligent aquaculture management, risk early warning and emergency response, and resource and market matching. Benefit estimation draws on validation data for the intelligent precision feeding system for fish developed by Huazhong Agricultural University in land-based recirculating aquaculture and pond modes (a 10%–15% reduction in the feed conversion ratio) and on survival-rate data for the local “land–sea relay” mode in Zhanjiang (above 95%). Combined with the actual feed and labor expenditure of farmers in Dongchang Bay, it is estimated that after platform deployment feed waste can be reduced by 10%–15% and the aquaculture survival rate can be raised by 5%–8%.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
summary: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures inte
content: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Towards a climate-resilient strategy for sustainable livelihoods in rural communities of Patagonian rangelands
