title: The material flow analysis model REMIND-MFA: Global demand scenarios and circular flows for plastics, steel, and cement
summary: Abstract Plastics, steel, and cement production are responsible for roughly one-fifth of global greenhouse gas emissions, and demand for these materials is rising rapidly. Low-emission production technologies remain costly, resource-constra
content: Abstract Plastics, steel, and cement production are responsible for roughly one-fifth of global greenhouse gas emissions, and demand for these materials is rising rapidly. Low-emission production technologies remain costly, resource-constrained, and slow to scale. Circular economy measures are needed to reduce virgin material production. Robust demand modeling is a prerequisite for assessing both supply-side mitigation and demand-side circular economy strategies. We present REMIND-MFA, a global, top-down, economy-wide, stock-driven, prospective material flow analysis model for plastics, steel, and cement. We publish it here as a fourfold contribution of methods, open-source code, results, and a comprehensive data set of prospective stocks and flows. To our knowledge, it is the first material flow analysis which combines all of these characteristics while covering all three materials at country-level resolution. The main methodological innovations and distinguishing contributions are: a three-step stock extrapolation algorithm that derives consistent regional demand scenarios directly from gross domestic product and population trajectories of the shared socioeconomic pathways with minimal regional assumptions; a trade extrapolation method accounting for shifting patterns; recent historical data through at least 2022, capturing the globally significant peaks in China’s steel and cement demand and the onset of their decline; and a modular, automated codebase built for coupling with models like the integrated assessment model REMIND. We show baseline and illustrative circular economy scenario results, displaying strong demand growth under current policies and the potential for circularity to reduce virgin production.

title: Does Trade Uncertainty Shake Sustainability? Insights From the ESG ‐Based Sustainability Uncertainty Index ( ESGUI ) Using Wavelet Tools
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the scale‐dependent association between trade policy uncertainty (TPU) and ESG‐based sustainability uncertainty (ESGUI) at the global, US, and China levels. Monthly data from November 2002 to June 2025 are analy
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the scale‐dependent association between trade policy uncertainty (TPU) and ESG‐based sustainability uncertainty (ESGUI) at the global, US, and China levels. Monthly data from November 2002 to June 2025 are analyzed with continuous, multiple, and partial wavelet methods, while the CASS Shipments Index captures freight activity. The results reveal heterogeneous conditional coherence rather than a uniform crisis effect: the global, US, and China panels display different timing and persistence patterns. In lag‐only models that control for global economic policy uncertainty, market volatility, geopolitical risk, freight activity, and crisis episodes, lagged TPU remains jointly associated with global ESGUI but not China ESGUI. Baltic Dry Index substitution and wavelet‐specification checks preserve the broad time–frequency structure. The evidence supports a conditional and temporally ordered association, not causal transmission. The study clarifies the distinct constructs, tests common‐shock explanations, and identifies institutionally heterogeneous sustainability‐risk horizons.

title: Scales to measure the perceived beneficence and non-maleficence of generative artificial intelligence systems
source: Journal of Information Communication and Ethics in Society
summary: Purpose The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) offers significant opportunities but also raises ethical concerns. Across institutional guidelines and theoretical frameworks in the field of AI ethics, two principles –
content: Purpose The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) offers significant opportunities but also raises ethical concerns. Across institutional guidelines and theoretical frameworks in the field of AI ethics, two principles – beneficence and non-maleficence – aim to direct the development and use of GAI to ensure maximum value and minimum harm. However, understanding how the general population perceives these principles in the context of GAI remains limited. This study aims to develop and validate scales for two new constructs in the context of GAI: perceived beneficence and perceived non-maleficence of GAI systems. Design/methodology/approach The authors propose items for two scales. Two independent samples were used for scale development. The first group comprised young adults from the general population and was analysed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). The second group comprised used adults residing in the European Union and was analysed using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Findings EFA revealed a two-factor solution, explaining approximately 64 % of the total variance. CFA confirmed the expected two-factor structure, with all standardised loadings exceeding 0.70. Originality/value The proposed scales provide a practical and research-relevant means for further behavioural analysis within structural models to address various contexts of GAI use. The proposed scales can help policymakers better understand GAI user perceptions, thereby enabling more robust policies to govern the development and use of GAI.

title: THE CHINESE BUSINESS MODEL AND ITS IMPACT ON INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC RELATIONS
summary: This paper examines the main characteristics of the Chinese business model and its impact on international economic relations. The study analyzes China's economic development strategy, the specifics of interaction between the state and the
content: This paper examines the main characteristics of the Chinese business model and its impact on international economic relations. The study analyzes China's economic development strategy, the specifics of interaction between the state and the private sector, China's growing role in international trade, and the infrastructure initiative "One Belt, One Road" (Belt and Road Initiative). The paper also assesses China's influence on global investment processes, supply chains, and modern forms of international economic cooperation. The research findings show that the Chinese business model represents a unique system of economic development that combines centralized state governance with market economy mechanisms. This model significantly influences international economic processes, strengthens global trade and investment, and at the same time creates new economic and geopolitical challenges.

title: Project selection methods used in operations improvement practice: a challenge to the binary objective–subjective perspective
source: International Journal of Lean Six Sigma
summary: Purpose This study aims to expand the body of empirical knowledge through the identification and objective analysis of project selection methods used in operations improvement practice. Design/methodology/approach Conducted over two years,
content: Purpose This study aims to expand the body of empirical knowledge through the identification and objective analysis of project selection methods used in operations improvement practice. Design/methodology/approach Conducted over two years, this research followed a multiphase mixed method approach of expert interviews (n = 10), a survey (n = 181), Delphi-method iterations (n = 5), validation interviews (n = 8) and a hybrid fuzzy logic multicriteria analysis of the identified project selection methods, validated against TOPSIS, Entropy weighting and expert intuition. Findings This research identified 50 project selection methods confirmed to be used in operations improvement practice, while also identifying a conflation of project identification and selection. In addition, this sample of 50 methods showed a 25% overlap with a scoping sample of 32 methods favored by academia, indicating a potential research-to-practice gap within this domain. An analysis of the 50 methods indicates that most methods lean toward semi-objectivity, offering a nuanced alternative to traditional binary classifications in literature. This research postulates that subjectivity often arises from how methods are implemented rather than the structural design of the methods themselves, calling for a multidisciplinary, system-thinking perspective in future project selection research. Originality/value The novelty/contribution of this research lies in: the research design, the more than doubling of the combined list of methods published through empirical research to date, and the more nuanced view of the objectivity of methods, constituting a departure from current literature on the topic. The research-to-practice gap presents a call to action for academia, whereas the subjectivity postulation shifts the focus of managers and researchers from refining the methods to the strengthening the user and system.

title: Climate-smart dairy technology adoption profiles and multidimensional food security among smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia
summary: This study examines associations between climate-smart dairy technologies and practices (CSDTPs) adoption profiles and multidimensional food security (MDFS) among 734 smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia using cross-sectional
content: This study examines associations between climate-smart dairy technologies and practices (CSDTPs) adoption profiles and multidimensional food security (MDFS) among 734 smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia using cross-sectional survey design. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified three profiles: selective (19.5%), intermediate (45.9%), and intensive-diversified adoption (34.6%). Augmented-inverse probability weighting (AIPW) estimated the adjusted counterfactual contrast, with inverse-probability weighting regression adjustment (IPWRA) and inverse-probability weighting (IPW) estimators as a robustness checks. Compared with selective adoption, both adoption profiles had lower food insecurity deprivation scores across the four MDFS dimensions. The intensive-diversified adoption generally showed larger estimated differences relative to the selective profile mean: 23.46% for quantity, 10.35% for quantity, 27.22% for acceptability, and 16.62% for stability. Sensitivity analysis broadly supported the findings, although the quality contrast of intermediate profile was not robust to kebele-clustered standard errors. For binary MDFS, compared to selective adoption, intermediate and intensive-diversified adoption profiles were associated with 11.70% and 12.20% lower probabilities of food insecurity, respectively; their difference however, was not statistically significant. These findings highlight the relevance of context-specific combinations of CSDTPs in relation to MDFS. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to establish causal effects and investigate underlying mechanisms.

title: AIRPORTS AS TOURISM GATEWAYS: PASSENGER PERCEPTIONS AND COMMERCIAL REVENUE AT BUCHAREST HENRI COANDĂ INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT
summary: Airports have evolved from simple transit points into complex tourism gateways that shape the travel experience and generate significant non-aeronautical revenues. This study provides an innovative perspective by highlighting how each airpo
content: Airports have evolved from simple transit points into complex tourism gateways that shape the travel experience and generate significant non-aeronautical revenues. This study provides an innovative perspective by highlighting how each airport’s unique operating context affects the strategies available to airport managers for increasing non-aeronautical revenues while enhancing passenger satisfaction. The paper presents an empirical, passengerbased analysis by examining how passenger perceptions of terminal commercial offerings, perceived dwell time, travel frequency, airline type, and demographic factors influence commercial spending behavior at Bucharest Henri Coandă International Airport (OTP). A structured questionnaire based on the ACI Airport Service Quality (ASQ) framework was administered to 315 passengers, and the data were analyzed using Spearman correlations, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, binary logistic regression, and MANOVA. The results show that perceptions of commercial space attractiveness correlate positively with overall airport experience valuation (ρ = 0.247, p < 0.001), confirming the strategic importance of retail environments in airport tourism appeal. A counterintuitive finding indicates that passengers who perceive more available time after security are less likely to make purchases, suggesting that time pressure may trigger impulse buying at this airport. Travel frequency is the only globally significant predictor of post-security purchasing (p = 0.011), with occasional travelers showing a higher spending propensity than frequent flyers. Airline type (low-cost vs. full-service) has no statistically significant influence on purchasing behavior. The logistic regression model achieves an overall accuracy of 65.7%, demonstrating that perceptual and situational variables outweigh traditional traveler profile indicators in explaining airport consumer behavior. These findings have direct implications for airport managers, tourism planners, and commercial concessionaires seeking to optimize non-aeronautical revenue streams while enhancing the tourist passenger experience.

title: A Multi-Level Teleconnection and Dynamic Coupling Diagnostic Framework: Decoupling Stratospheric Wave Geometry and Eurasian Blocking via the SDI–BI–CI–EI Suite (1940–2026)
summary: Classical univariate teleconnection metrics frequently fail to capture the non-linear, vertical, and sub-seasonal coupling between middle-stratospheric momentum deposition and lower-tropospheric boundary conditions across the Euro- Mediterr
content: Classical univariate teleconnection metrics frequently fail to capture the non-linear, vertical, and sub-seasonal coupling between middle-stratospheric momentum deposition and lower-tropospheric boundary conditions across the Euro- Mediterranean domain. This paper presents the comprehensive formulation, epistemological justification, and physical validation of the SDI–BI–CI–EI Suite, an integrated multi-level diagnostic system standardized on a continuous, dimensionless metric spanning from minus four to plus four and verified across an uninterrupted historical matrix of 1,041 empirical records derived from ECMWF ERA5 reanalyses and global observational archives between January 1, 1940, and September 15, 2026, with an operative diagnostic baseline verified on Thursday, September 17, 2026, at 09:15 IST. The suite systematically decouples middle-stratospheric wave interference from near-surface continental advection by establishing four distinct diagnostic axes: the Split-Displacement Index at 10 hPa, which discriminates between Wave-1 off-pole displacements and Wave-2 resonant bifurcations; the Buran Index across 850 hPa and surface levels, which evaluates the structural continuity of the Voejkov Bridge, continental source reservoir charging, and Mediterranean cyclonic draw; the Christmas Index, which resolves sub-seasonal wave-preconditioning during the late-December festive window; and the Easter Index, which integrates an astronomical insolation correction derived from Gregorian Computus algorithms to evaluate late-season Arctic or continental outbreaks against vernal radiative dissipation. By testing the framework against eighty-six years of atmospheric data, this study demonstrates that the suite resolves fundamental dynamical paradoxes, explaining why extreme stratospheric warmings can paradoxically trigger mild European zonal flows, why historic continental freezes can emerge from off-pole displacements without circumpolar wind reversal, and how festive and vernal phenology metrics resolve critical time-lag discrepancies that conventional monthly means invariably smooth away.

title: Integrating rigorous techno‐economic analysis into generative process synthesis for economic optimization
summary: Abstract This study presents a fully automated dual‐loop framework integrating detailed techno‐economic analysis (TEA) into generative process synthesis. A trained generative model proposes process topologies, while an inner loop combines A
content: Abstract This study presents a fully automated dual‐loop framework integrating detailed techno‐economic analysis (TEA) into generative process synthesis. A trained generative model proposes process topologies, while an inner loop combines Aspen Plus equation‐oriented initialization with trust‐region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) of an external simulation–TEA evaluation. This evaluation includes discrete equipment‐sizing and utility‐selection decisions. Case studies on cyclohexane and ethylene glycol production show how particle swarm optimization (PSO) uses the resulting economic feedback to improve on the best randomly sampled designs. Relative to the best randomly sampled designs, annualized profit increases by 12.2% for cyclohexane, while the annualized deficit decreases by 30.6% for ethylene glycol. These results demonstrate the integration of topology generation, rigorous simulation, and economic evaluation in an automated design workflow.

title: Building rural economic growth through MSME digitalization: a society 5.0 perspective
source: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
summary: The Society 5.0 paradigm presents a strategic opportunity to bridge the digital divide and drive rural economic transformation. This study examines the role and impact of digitizing Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in stimulatin
content: The Society 5.0 paradigm presents a strategic opportunity to bridge the digital divide and drive rural economic transformation. This study examines the role and impact of digitizing Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in stimulating rural economic growth in Enrekang Regency, South Sulawesi Province, Indonesia. Employing a Participatory Action Research (PAR) methodology, the study directly involved local MSME actors throughout the data collection process, which encompassed field observations, in-depth interviews, and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs). The gathered data were then critically evaluated using a qualitative descriptive analysis approach. The findings indicate that the targeted adoption of digital technologies specifically through e-commerce integration, the implementation of the Internet of Things (IoT), and financial technology (Fintech) solutions significantly enhances operational efficiency, expands market reach beyond local boundaries, boosts household incomes, and creates local employment opportunities. However, the scope of this digital transformation remains constrained by critical structural barriers, notably low digital literacy, suboptimal technological infrastructure, and limited access to capital. To address these challenges, the study proposes a digital integration model that is tailored and adaptive to local conditions, aligning technological tools with the socio-economic context of rural communities. These findings offer actionable insights and a practical strategic framework for policymakers and development practitioners striving to build an inclusive, resilient, and sustainable rural economy in the Society 5.0 era.

title: Development of Unmanned Surface Vehicle, including hull, energy, propulsion, and intelligence: A review
summary: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) are gaining growing importance in marine‑related military and economic applications. Existing review studies on USVs tend to focus on individual technical dimensions such as hull design or autonomous algorit
content: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) are gaining growing importance in marine‑related military and economic applications. Existing review studies on USVs tend to focus on individual technical dimensions such as hull design or autonomous algorithms, while few reviews provide a holistic examination that integrates platform hardware, energy, propulsion and intelligent systems, together with large‑scale analysis of real‑world academic and industrial prototypes. In this paper, nearly one‑hundred USV products (77 of which are statistically counted) from both academia and industry are surveyed. Representative vessel configurations are covered, including monohulls, catamarans, trimarans, sailboats and wave gliders. Four core technical dimensions of USVs are systematically reviewed: hull design, energy systems, propulsion mechanisms, and autonomous intelligence systems. Conventional hull forms, sailboats and wave‑glider‑type platforms are analyzed for hull‑related research. For energy systems, renewable‑energy solutions including solar, wind and wave power are discussed with emphasis on their practical constraints. Propulsion approaches are further summarized, covering propeller‑based propulsion, water‑jet propulsion and bionic propulsion. For the autonomous intelligence module, we adopt a perception‑localization‑navigation‑control framework inspired by automotive ADAS, rather than the traditional aerospace‑oriented GNC architecture, to adapt to complex marine environments subject to wind, wave and spray disturbances. This paper summarizes the dominant features and inherent limitations of state‑of‑the‑art USVs, identifies key technical bottlenecks, and outlines promising future research directions. It is expected to offer references for subsequent USV hardware development and autonomous system research.

title: Hybrid Forecasting Model for Carbon Price: Integrating Chronological and Weekday‐Structured Temporal Representations
summary: ABSTRACT Accurate carbon price forecasts support allowance trading, compliance planning and market supervision. This study examines whether two temporal representations of the same carbon price series—the original chronological sequence (ho
content: ABSTRACT Accurate carbon price forecasts support allowance trading, compliance planning and market supervision. This study examines whether two temporal representations of the same carbon price series—the original chronological sequence (horizontal dimension) and five weekday‐structured subsequences (vertical dimension) obtained by regrouping Monday‐to‐Friday observations—contain complementary predictive information. Both representations are modeled within a common decomposition‐reconstruction‐forecasting framework: Dynamic time warping (DTW) diagnoses the correspondence between them, complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) and sample entropy (SE) decompose and reconstruct each series, and a leaky‐integrator echo state network (LiESN) generates the forecasts. The weekday‐specific forecasts are restored to chronological order and fused with the horizontal forecast by least squares (LS), and kernel density estimation (KDE) is used to construct prediction intervals. In the Hubei carbon market, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 0.365, a MAPE of 0.800%, an RMSE of 0.538 and an R 2 of 0.949 in the test period, reducing the MAE, MAPE, and RMSE of the chronological‐only benchmark by 2.41%, 2.20%, and 2.89%, respectively, and the Wilcoxon signed‐rank test indicates that its improvements over all benchmark models are significant at the 5% level. The model also attains the highest or tied‐highest interval coverage and the highest composite interval score. Additional experiments on the Shenzhen and Chongqing carbon markets show that the incremental gain is modest, and its statistical significance is market‐dependent: It is significant in Chongqing but not in Shenzhen. These results support the view that weekday‐structured forecasts can provide complementary predictive information beyond adjacent‐day chronological dependence, without treating the weekday sequences as independent multivariate variables or claiming a newly discovered weekday anomaly.

title: Peri-urban environmental degradation and the urbanisation of the Bamako District, Mali: the case of the rural commune of Sanankoroba
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: For several decades, the growth of the Bamako District has spilled over its administrative boundaries into neighbouring rural communes. This study examines the environmental effects of that urban spillover on the rural commune of Sanankorob
content: For several decades, the growth of the Bamako District has spilled over its administrative boundaries into neighbouring rural communes. This study examines the environmental effects of that urban spillover on the rural commune of Sanankoroba, located about 35 km south of the capital. The approach combines a questionnaire survey of 100 respondents with semi-structured interviews of five administrative and customary leaders. All respondents consider that the urbanisation of Bamako affects their commune. The interviews highlight five main effects: the conversion of farmland into housing plots and industrial sites, the decline of vegetation cover, the scarcity of wildlife, pollution of water, air and soil, and excavations that weaken soils. These are accompanied by social tensions, a perceived rise in insecurity and growing pressure on basic services. The three initial hypotheses, concerning vegetation, wildlife and land, are supported by the perceptions collected, although they have yet to be measured with biophysical indicators. The study calls for inter-municipal planning at the scale of Greater Bamako, the protection of farmland and the monitoring of vegetation cover through remote sensing.

title: Behavioural Diversity and Ecology of Cleaning Mutualisms in a Changing Ocean
summary: ABSTRACT One of the most pressing challenges confronting the scientific community today is understanding the consequences of global change on ecological communities and mitigating their impacts. Cleaning mutualisms are essential to the heal
content: ABSTRACT One of the most pressing challenges confronting the scientific community today is understanding the consequences of global change on ecological communities and mitigating their impacts. Cleaning mutualisms are essential to the health and stability of coral reef ecosystems, influencing individual fitness, parasite dynamics, and community composition. However, these interactions are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures. This review describes the behavioural diversity and ecology of dedicated cleaners, ranging from cognitively sophisticated wrasses and efficient, low‐conflict gobies to visually signalling shrimps. We then review how the intricate interactions between cleaners and clients respond to environmental change, including chronic stressors (e.g., acidification), extreme events (e.g., marine heatwaves), and direct anthropogenic disturbances (e.g., underwater noise). Mounting evidence demonstrates that such stressors can disrupt cleaner and client dynamics, diminishing interaction motivation and quality, and altering underlying neurobiological mechanisms. Despite recent advances, significant gaps remain in our understanding of the long‐term resilience and recovery of cleaning mutualisms across ecological, behavioural, cognitive and physiological pathways. As ocean climate‐related drivers of change intensify and increasingly co‐occur, it becomes urgent to investigate whether cleaners can continue to fulfil their ecological roles, or if reefs will face a future with compromised mutualistic services.

title: Artificial Flowering Induction Practices in Pineapple (cv. Sugarloaf) Production in Southern Benin: Comparative Analysis of Effectiveness of Induction Agents and Effects on Fruit Quality
summary: Flowering Induction Treatment (FIT) is an essential component of the commercial fresh pineapple production system. In Benin Republic and despite the efforts of the government, FIT is still carried out using calcium carbide, which is harmful
content: Flowering Induction Treatment (FIT) is an essential component of the commercial fresh pineapple production system. In Benin Republic and despite the efforts of the government, FIT is still carried out using calcium carbide, which is harmful to human health and the environment. To provide fresh pineapple producers with an eco-friendly FIT, we assessed the effect of 18 FITs on the flowering emergence and fruit quality parameters of cv. Sugarloaf. FITs consisted of zero application, calcium carbide 1%: 22 kg/ha (widely used), activated charcoal enriched with Ethylene (promoted by the government for organic pineapple production), reduced doses of calcium carbide by 25%-50% plus activated charcoal, fine clay or/and petroleum, and reduced doses of Ethrel plus urea and/or sodium bicarbonate or activated charcoal, and activated charcoal enriched with ethylene. Two experiments were carried out in southern Benin using a randomized complete block design with four repetitions. Results showed that treatments including calcium carbide mixed with activated carbon and clay, and Ethrel mixed with urea and/or bicarbonate, induced flowering in more than 95% of cv. Sugarloaf pineapple plants. With these treatments, the length and weight of pineapple fruit, infructescence, and crown, as well as pH and total soluble solids content, were significantly affected. The number of planting materials was also significantly affected by the FITs. Results indicated that treatments with "Calcium carbide 0.75% + Activated carbon 0.5%" and "Ethrel 200ppm + Urea 4% + Sodium bicarbonate 0.4%" offer interesting prospects for conventional cv. Sugarloaf, in terms of flowering incidence, days to flower, and fruit quality, with potential minimal risks for producers and the environment. The potential implications for producer health, environmental safety, and economic benefits were not directly assessed in this study and should be explored through further investigation.

title: Spin‐Selective Transport in Chiral 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Superlattices: Mechanisms and Device Applications
summary: The chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, enabling efficient spin polarization without external magnetic fields, has positioned chiral two-dimensional (2D) materials as promising platforms for next-generation spintronics, quantum t
content: The chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, enabling efficient spin polarization without external magnetic fields, has positioned chiral two-dimensional (2D) materials as promising platforms for next-generation spintronics, quantum technologies, and spin-dependent catalysis. Among these, 2D transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) superlattices offer a uniquely tunable platform, where molecular chirality incorporated into inorganic frameworks enables precise control over spin polarization through tailored chiral-host interactions. Despite significant progress, a critical gap remains in understanding how chirality transfers from intercalated molecules to TMD host lattices and bridges fundamental CISS mechanisms with device-ready performance. This review addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive and critical assessment of chiral TMD superlattices formed through molecular intercalation. We discuss proposed CISS mechanisms, including spin-orbit coupling and spinterface effects, and critically evaluate experimental and theoretical characterization techniques. We then present advances in synthetic strategies that enable precise control over chiral architectures, offering insights pivotal for designing high-performance spin-based devices. Building on these foundations, we explore emerging applications in spin optoelectronics, spin electrocatalysis, and chiral sensing, while offering critical analysis of the underlying mechanisms driving their enhanced performance. Finally, we identify key challenges and propose a roadmap for future research and innovation in this dynamic field.

title: The nitrate paradox: integrating environmental, nutritional and physiological perspectives on nitrate and human health
source: Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition
summary: Inorganic nitrate (NO3−) is a key intermediate in the global nitrogen cycle and essential for agricultural productivity. However, anthropogenic disruption of the nitrogen cycle over the last century has substantially increased NO3− accumula
content: Inorganic nitrate (NO3−) is a key intermediate in the global nitrogen cycle and essential for agricultural productivity. However, anthropogenic disruption of the nitrogen cycle over the last century has substantially increased NO3− accumulation in ecosystems, leading to widespread environmental and public health concerns. Consequently, regulatory policies have primarily focused on limiting NO3− exposure through drinking water, vegetables and processed foods. However, emerging evidence indicates that dietary NO3−, especially from vegetables, can exert important physiological benefits through its reduction to nitrite and nitric oxide and prebiotic effects. This apparent contradiction has created a “nitrate paradox,” contributing to ongoing debate and confusion regarding the role of NO3− in human health. This review critically examines NO3− across environmental, agricultural, nutritional, and physiological dimensions. We discuss how intensive use of nitrogen fertilizers has altered global NO3− accumulation in ecosystems. We further assess evidence linking nitrate exposure from drinking water and vegetables with health outcomes. Finally, we propose a more integrated framework for NO3− regulation that considers dietary and environmental considerations, and links nitrogen management to human health.

title: Shifting Sands: A Review of Decarbonization's Ripple Effects from Qatar, UAE and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Migrant Workers' Homeland
source: William & Mary School of Arts & Sciences
summary: This study examines the economic and social implications of decarbonization in three Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries—Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia—focusing on how changes in remittance patterns affect the econom
content: This study examines the economic and social implications of decarbonization in three Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries—Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia—focusing on how changes in remittance patterns affect the economies of migrant-sending countries in South Asia and Africa. Using a scenario-based approach, we model various post-carbon futures to estimate the effects of decarbonization strategies on labor markets and remittance flows. The analysis includes labor profile characteristics within and outside the hydrocarbon industry and evaluates potential shifts in employment and economic structures. Key findings suggest that decarbonization will significantly alter labor market dynamics, potentially reducing reliance on migrant labor in the fossil fuel sector and necessitating substantial investment in green technologies and re-skilling programs. The study underscores the need for policy designs that mitigate employment and income volatility for migrant workers and stabilize remittance flows, given the transnational exposure of sending countries to GCC labor-market adjustment. Policy implications highlight the urgency for GCC nations to plan their green transitions to balance economic growth, labor market stability, and global sustainability goals.

title: HOW GREEN BANKING PRACTICES INFLUENCE CUSTOMER SATISFACTION: A FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BANKING
summary: The emerging and rapidly growing trend of the banking industry is the adoption of green banking practices. It is a critical module of the transformation to a more environmentally sustainable future. The innovative strategies and initiatives
content: The emerging and rapidly growing trend of the banking industry is the adoption of green banking practices. It is a critical module of the transformation to a more environmentally sustainable future. The innovative strategies and initiatives of green banking can promote sustainable and environmental–friendly practices which contributes in the reduction of carbon footprints from banking related activities. Going green is the indispensable need of the present times. Therefore, the main aim of conducting this study is to evaluate the impact of green banking practices on the satisfaction level of customers with mediating variable of privacy and moderates the relationship with government support and trust in digital banking services. This study used purposive sampling technique and collected data from specifically those respondents who use bank mobile apps for their banking transactions. The sample size is 350 respondents of multiple banks in Pakistan.

title: Does Local Environmental Information Transparency Affect the Cost of Corporate Debt? Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT Using the policy pilot of China's Ambient Air Quality Standards , we constructed a triple‐differences model to explore the impact of environmental information transparency on the debt costs of high‐polluting enterprises. The baseli
content: ABSTRACT Using the policy pilot of China's Ambient Air Quality Standards , we constructed a triple‐differences model to explore the impact of environmental information transparency on the debt costs of high‐polluting enterprises. The baseline results show that the improvement of local environmental information transparency has pushed up the corporate bond spreads of high‐polluting enterprises. A series of robustness tests have confirmed the robustness of these baseline results. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that for high‐polluting enterprises with higher financing constraints, higher public attention, and those located in regions with a lower degree of marketization, the effect of increased debt costs caused by improved environmental information transparency is more significant. The results of mechanism tests show that the improvement of environmental information transparency can increase corporate bond spreads through two channels: increasing the credit default risk of high‐polluting enterprises and reducing their operating profits. Finally, based on the conclusions of this paper, we put forward some policy recommendations to promote the green transformation of financial markets.

title: Translating Organizational Capabilities into Sustainable Blue Economy Outcomes: The Roles of Operational Efficiency, Decarbonization Performance and Green Technology Absorptive Capacity in Pakistan
summary: The sustainable blue economy depends not only on the availability of financial, institutional and technological resources, but also on the organizational processes through which these resources are converted into operational and environment
content: The sustainable blue economy depends not only on the availability of financial, institutional and technological resources, but also on the organizational processes through which these resources are converted into operational and environmental outcomes. Yet empirical evidence on these conversion processes remains limited in emerging maritime economies. This study examines the relationships between economic capacity, institutional and governance capacity, technological and infrastructure capacity, operational efficiency and resource utilisation, decarbonization performance, and sustainable blue economy development in Pakistan. Drawing on the resource-based and dynamic capabilities perspectives, institutional theory, the absorptive capacity perspective, and the triple bottom line as an outcome framework, the study uses cross-sectional survey data from 179 senior management respondents in maritime, port-related, shipping, regulatory, educational, and renewable-energy organizations. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to assess the measurement and structural models. The results indicate positive associations between economic, institutional and technological capacities and operational efficiency and decarbonization performance. Technological and infrastructure capacity has the largest reported path to decarbonization performance (β = 0.373, p < 0.001). Operational efficiency (β = 0.287, p < 0.001) and decarbonization performance (β = 0.338, p < 0.001) are positively associated with sustainable blue economy development. Six specific indirect relationships are statistically significant; however, the current model does not include the direct capacity-to-outcome paths needed to determine the mediation form. The reported second-stage interaction estimates also require re-estimation and robustness checks before substantive interpretation. The model reports an R² of 0.429 for sustainable blue economy development. The study offers an emerging-economy perspective on how organizational capacities and performance processes relate to blue-economy outcomes, while identifying the need for stronger measurement, model specification and objective sector-level validation.

title: Beyond Chemical Purity: Optical Quality, Particle Morphology, Surface Modification, and Scale-Up of High-Whiteness Aluminum Hydroxide—A Critical Review
source: Journal International Review of Research Studies
summary: High-whiteness aluminum hydroxide, principally gibbsite-based alumina trihydrate (ATH), is commonly specified using bulk impurity concentrations, although visual appearance also depends on chromophore speciation, particle architecture, aggl
content: High-whiteness aluminum hydroxide, principally gibbsite-based alumina trihydrate (ATH), is commonly specified using bulk impurity concentrations, although visual appearance also depends on chromophore speciation, particle architecture, agglomeration, sample preparation, and matrix interactions. This structured critical narrative review critically appraises 151 bibliographic records (147 from 2020–2026, two foundational studies from 2013 and 2018, and two colorimetry standards published or reaffirmed in 2019 and 2025). It distinguishes direct process and optical evidence from mechanistic, functional, and contextual evidence across Bayer-liquor purification, seeded precipitation, finishing, surface modification, qualification, and scale-up. A Whiteness-by-Design framework links impurity transport and aluminum recovery with particle properties, standardized CIELAB coordinates, spectral reflectance, qualified-product yield, and end-use evaluation. The evidence does not justify equating chemical purity, precipitation yield, high L*, whiteness index, or matrix-level visual acceptance. Future industrial comparisons require paired mass balances and optical measurements under traceable specimen and application protocols.

title: Corporate Biodiversity Governance and Firm Environmental Performance: The Roles of Biodiversity Disclosure, CSR-Linked Executive Compensation, and Environmental Innovation
source: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
summary: Whether corporate environmental performance reflects what firms disclose, how executives are rewarded or the capabilities firms build remains an open empirical question. Drawing on stakeholder theory, this study examines the joint associati
content: Whether corporate environmental performance reflects what firms disclose, how executives are rewarded or the capabilities firms build remains an open empirical question. Drawing on stakeholder theory, this study examines the joint association of biodiversity disclosure (an information mechanism), CSR-linked executive compensation (an incentive mechanism) and environmental innovation (a capability mechanism) with the environmental pillar score of 664 firms from 20 countries and economies over 2015–2025. Pooled, random-effects and firm fixed-effects estimates show positive associations for all three variables. Within firms, biodiversity disclosure is associated with a 5.743-point higher score and CSR-linked compensation with a 2.781-point higher score, while a one-standard-deviation increase in environmental innovation corresponds to a 14.0-point higher score (0.60 standard deviations). Innovation is the most robust association, remaining stable when year effects are introduced, whereas the disclosure and compensation associations are sensitive to common time trends. All estimates are conditional associations. The findings imply that boards and investors should give weight to innovation capability and complement disclosure and pay-linkage practices with measurable targets and verification, while regulators should specify the content and quality of biodiversity disclosure. title: INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT
summary: This book discusses investment management. It covers the basic concepts and scope of investment management, the investment decision-making process, risk and return analysis in investments, investment instruments in financial markets, the ro
content: This book discusses investment management. It covers the basic concepts and scope of investment management, the investment decision-making process, risk and return analysis in investments, investment instruments in financial markets, the role of fundamental analysis in investment decisions, and the role of technical analysis in investment planning. Investment is a crucial activity in financial management because investment decisions determine how available resources are allocated to generate future economic benefits. From a management perspective, investment is more than simply purchasing stocks, bonds, mutual funds, or other assets. It is a process that includes goal setting, identifying needs and constraints, analyzing opportunities, measuring risk and return, forming a portfolio, implementing, monitoring, evaluating, and continuously adjusting decisions. Developments in financial markets have expanded investment options for individuals and organizations. Investors now have access to a variety of asset classes, capital market instruments, collectiveinvestment products, and technology-based strategies. In Indonesia,developments in investment management have also been accompanied by a strengthening of the regulatory framework. In 2025, the Financial Services Authority (OJK) emphasized the development and strengthening of investment management in the capital market, while the 2025 Capital Market Pocket Book updated its material with market developments through 2025, including carbon trading and financial derivatives with underlying securities (OJK, 2025; OJK, 2026). In addition to technical and financial aspects, this subchapter also highlights the role of management accounting information in providing relevant differential data and sensitizing readers to the influence of behavioral finance, which often traps investors in decision-making. By understanding all elements of this process,readers are expected to be able not only to make more rational and measured investment decisions but also to develop a disciplined and adaptive mindset to the ever-changing dynamics of the capital market.

title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
summary: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equ
content: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.

title: Ensemble forecasting of ERCOT efficiency and residual price variability using GFDL-CM4 climate projections
summary: This paper investigates the climate-induced reliability issues within the Texas ERCOT grid by developing a multi-phase ensemble learning forecasting infrastructure. Meteorological variable forecasts from the CMIP6 GFDL-CM4 climate model wer
content: This paper investigates the climate-induced reliability issues within the Texas ERCOT grid by developing a multi-phase ensemble learning forecasting infrastructure. Meteorological variable forecasts from the CMIP6 GFDL-CM4 climate model were synthesized to project operational efficiency and residual price variability (deviations of residential prices from an inflation-adjusted baseline attributable to projected efficiency) from 2025 to 2050. Random forest regression and a hybrid SARIMA–XGBoost structure were used to estimate power plant generation and corresponding fuel consumption across seven major energy sources, achieving tolerance accuracies up to 93.7%. Renewables were projected with the most severe efficiency deficits, with wind and solar averaging 8.14% and 12.44% per month, respectively, over the forecasting range. A supporting Gaussian process model was directly trained on the projected efficiencies and estimated long-term losses of $29.8 billion for residential consumers and $31.4 billion for retail energy providers under moderate conditions. Risk analysis identified key vulnerable climate zones and dominant predictive weather variables, namely heat-related metrics. Mitigation recommendations were developed based on model outputs, including the deployment of resilient technologies (e.g., anti-icing systems and perovskite PVs), integrated energy storage, and time-of-use pricing mechanisms.

title: Alternating Methods for Large-Scale AC Optimal Power Flow with Unit Commitment
summary: Security-constrained unit commitment with alternating current optimal power flow (SCUC-ACOPF) is a central problem in power grid operations that optimizes commitment and dispatch of generators under a physically accurate power transmission
content: Security-constrained unit commitment with alternating current optimal power flow (SCUC-ACOPF) is a central problem in power grid operations that optimizes commitment and dispatch of generators under a physically accurate power transmission model while encouraging robustness against component failures. SCUC-ACOPF requires solving large-scale problems that involve multiple time periods and networks with thousands of buses within strict time limits. In this work, we study a detailed SCUC-ACOPF model with a rich set of features of modern power grids, including price-sensitive load, reserve products, transformer controls, and energy-limited devices. We propose a decomposition scheme and a penalty alternating direction method to find high-quality solutions to this model. Our methodology leverages spatial and temporal decomposition, separating the problem into a set of mixed-integer linear programs for each bus and a set of continuous nonlinear programs for each time period. To improve the performance of the algorithm, we introduce a variety of heuristics, including restrictions of temporal linking constraints, a second-order cone relaxation, and a contingency screening algorithm. We quantify the quality of feasible solutions through a dual bound from a second-order cone program. To evaluate our algorithm, we use large-scale test cases from Challenge 3 of the U.S. Department of Energy s Grid Optimization Competition that resemble real power grid data under a variety of operating conditions and decision horizons. The experiments yield feasible solutions with an average optimality gap of 1.33%, demonstrating that this approach generates near-optimal solutions within stringent time limits.

title: Inside the battery box: a cross-technology assessment of PFAS uses, functions, and substitution potential
summary: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 56
content: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 5600 submissions to the Annex XV public consultation on the proposed universal PFAS restriction in the European Union and extracted information reporting use, associated substance(s), and stated function(s) of PFASs in batteries. 341 records were compiled into a database using our structured Battery Use & Function Framework that incorporates the Functional Substitution Framework. Among these records, 78 contained sufficient information to qualify as a potential PFAS use and were organized into 36 potential PFAS uses, accounting for overlaps. Each potential PFAS use was evaluated using supporting evidence from previous use-mapping studies, input from battery stakeholders, teardown-analysis studies, and other targeted academic literature. Across all lines of evidence, two PFAS uses in batteries were contradicted, indicating already large-scale availability of PFAS-free alternatives, while 16 PFAS uses were confirmed, primarily in cathode components across several battery technologies and chemistries. PFAS-free alternatives were identified for 13 PFAS uses across battery applications, with an additional five uses showing PFAS-free options for certain applications within the broader use category. The findings indicate that few technical barriers remain for substituting PFASs in most battery components. Our mapping provides a detailed foundation for future alternatives assessments, supports essential-use evaluations, and highlights opportunities and challenges relevant to monitoring and recycling.

title: Participation, procedural fairness and policy acceptability: A quasi-experimental field study of workplace travel planning
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: Parking restrictions are among the most effective tools available to organisations and local authorities seeking to manage transport demand and reduce commuting emissions. Yet their implementation often fails when commuters question their l
content: Parking restrictions are among the most effective tools available to organisations and local authorities seeking to manage transport demand and reduce commuting emissions. Yet their implementation often fails when commuters question their legitimacy, highlighting the need to better understand the conditions under which such measures gain acceptability during the development stage. This study examines whether involving commuters in the development of restrictive travel measures increases their acceptability, applying policy acceptance and deliberative democracy literatures to an organisational transport context for the first time. Using a quasi-experimental field design embedded in a travel plan development process at a UK university (N = 486, data collected between 15/09/2025 and 05/12/2025), we compare standard consultation via a travel survey with enhanced involvement via deliberative workshops. Mediation analysis shows that workshop participation increased perceived procedural fairness, which in turn increased policy acceptability, replicating and extending Liu et al.’s (2020) participation–fairness–acceptability pathway to an organisational setting. A significant negative direct effect indicates that deliberation simultaneously raised critical scrutiny, producing inconsistent mediation. Trust in the organisation emerged as a precondition of participation: deliberative engagement increased acceptability among those who already trusted the institution. For local authorities and organisations developing restrictive travel policies, these findings suggest that deliberative involvement can build the legitimacy necessary for effective implementation where institutional trust has already been established, and where the process is designed to be genuinely fair and inclusive.

title: Sorbates from 1,1-Dialkylsubstituted Alkenes and 3-Haloacrylic Esters via Pd(II)-Isohypsic Catalysis: Focus on Terpenes
summary: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C-H/C-X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples).
content: Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C-H/C-X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples). This coupling, unknown to date for the synthesis of 1,3-dienes, follows a mechanism distinct from the well-known Mizoroki-Heck, and works where the Mizoroki-Heck fails. Density functional theory (DFT) computations allowed to propose a plausible mechanism for this transformation.

title: Soil and host-tree associations with Tuber aestivum's ITS abundance in productive Istrian oak forests
summary: Abstract Understanding the ecological drivers of Tuber aestivum productivity in natural oak forests remains limited despite the species’ broad ecological niche and rising economic value. We characterised 65 productive plots of T. aestivum a
content: Abstract Understanding the ecological drivers of Tuber aestivum productivity in natural oak forests remains limited despite the species’ broad ecological niche and rising economic value. We characterised 65 productive plots of T. aestivum associated with Quercus pubescens and Q. cerris in forest stands of the Istrian peninsula, Croatia. At each plot, we applied a paired sampling design consisting of two systematically collected soil samples: one taken beneath the harvested ascocarp and the other taken 5 m outside the visible brûlé or tree crown area, yielding a total of 130 samples. We quantified soil physical–chemical properties (pH and texture), macronutrients (C, Ca, K, N and P), and mycelial abundance by qPCR (ITS2 copies g⁻¹ soil). Across the study area, a positive relationship between clay content and mycelial abundance emerged as the most consistent, highlighting the importance of soil water retention in T. aestivum mycelial development. In contrast, higher N levels and imbalanced K: Ca ratios were associated with lower mycelial abundance, particularly in Q. pubescens stands, whereas P showed a marginal, host‑dependent positive trend detectable only in Q. pubescens . Trends of increasing and decreasing median pH and nutrient values were detected between paired samples, with these patterns differing between host tree species. Altogether, our results indicate that T. aestivum mycelial development is promoted by clay-rich soils in oak forests and demonstrate the value of paired sampling for disentangling host- and soil‑driven processes in wild T. aestivum ecosystems.

title: The primary energy fallacy in energy transitions
summary: Abstract The global energy system remains dominated by fossil fuels, often cited as evidence that replacing them with renewables is unrealistic. Here we show that this view rests on a systematic misinterpretation of energy system size - the
content: Abstract The global energy system remains dominated by fossil fuels, often cited as evidence that replacing them with renewables is unrealistic. Here we show that this view rests on a systematic misinterpretation of energy system size - the primary energy fallacy - that arises when energy systems are compared using primary energy inputs rather than delivered energy services. Using global energy flow analysis grounded in the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory World Energy Flow framework and IEA energy balances, we compare today’s fossil-fuel-based system with a stylised highly electrified scenario delivering the same level of useful energy services. We find that system-wide losses (rejected energy) fall by 61%, while the contribution of ambient environmental heat captured by heat pumps rises approximately twentyfold; under conventional energy-balance conventions this corresponds to a fall in primary energy inputs of nearly half. Our results show that primary energy metrics increasingly misrepresent system scale as electrification advances, with important implications for energy system analysis and policy. We recommend that energy-system analysis and policy lead with system-loss and useful-energy indicators while continuing to report primary energy as a translation for readers anchored in conventional accounting.

title: Effect of Foeniculum vulgare seed phenolic extract as a natural additive on the physicochemical, microbiological, antioxidant, and organoleptic quality of traditional Algerian J’ben cheese during storage
summary: Abstract Chemical additives widely used in the agri-food industry have raised increasing concerns because of their potential adverse effects on human health. Thus, there is growing interest in replacing synthetic additives with natural alte
content: Abstract Chemical additives widely used in the agri-food industry have raised increasing concerns because of their potential adverse effects on human health. Thus, there is growing interest in replacing synthetic additives with natural alternatives capable of preserving food quality and safety. In this context, the present study aimed to evaluate the effect of incorporating a phenolic extract from fennel ( Foeniculum vulgare ) seeds as a natural food additive on the quality of J'ben, a traditional Algerian cheese, during 15 days of refrigerated storage at 4°C. J'ben cheese, produced by mixed coagulation, was supplemented with a phenolic extract of fennel seeds obtained by hydroethanolic maceration (80:20, ethanol/water, v/v). The extract was incorporated into the cheese at concentrations of 0% (control), 1%, 2%, and 3% (w/w), and the resulting products were evaluated during 15 days of refrigerated storage at 4°C. Physicochemical, microbiological, and sensory analyses were performed on both the experimental cheeses and the fennel seed extract. The results demonstrated that the hydroethanolic extract of Foeniculum vulgare exhibited strong antioxidant activity, attributable to its high content of total phenolic compounds (9.2 mg GAE/mL extract) and flavonoids (0.68 mg QE/mL extract). Microbiological analyses further revealed that the extract possessed antimicrobial activity against several pathogenic and spoilage microorganisms while simultaneously promoting the growth of beneficial lactic acid bacteria, highlighting its potential prebiotic effect. Physicochemical parameters, including moisture content, fat content, dry matter, pH, and acidity, exhibited variations among the experimental cheeses during storage. However, the most significant finding of this study was the substantial reduction in malondialdehyde (MDA) levels observed in cheeses supplemented with 3% fennel extract compared with the control. This decrease can be attributed to the strong antioxidant activity of the extract, as demonstrated by the DPPH and FRAP assays. Furthermore, sensory evaluation revealed that the incorporation of fennel seed phenolic compounds positively influenced the freshness, aroma, and colour of the cheeses.

title: Structural Reorganisation and Reduced In Vitro Digestibility of Jackfruit Seed Starch Induced by Sequential Hydrogen Peroxide Oxidation and Heat–Moisture Treatment
summary: Abstract Hydrogen peroxide oxidation and heat–moisture treatment (HMT) modify starch through distinct mechanisms, yet little is known about how their sequential application affects starch structure and digestibility. This study evaluated th
content: Abstract Hydrogen peroxide oxidation and heat–moisture treatment (HMT) modify starch through distinct mechanisms, yet little is known about how their sequential application affects starch structure and digestibility. This study evaluated the structural reorganisation and in vitro digestibility of jackfruit seed starch subjected to hydrogen peroxide oxidation followed by HMT. Oxidation resulted in a degree of oxidation of 1.26% and slightly disrupted the ordered structure, reducing relative crystallinity from 18.4% to 16.8% and the A 1047 /A 1022 ratio from 0.684 to 0.666. In contrast, subsequent HMT promoted structural reorganisation and granule aggregation, increasing relative crystallinity to 23.4% and the A 1047 /A 1022 ratio to 0.709. These structural changes were accompanied by a marked shift in digestibility: rapidly digestible starch decreased from 68.5% in native starch to 18.8% after sequential treatment, while resistant starch increased from 15.7% to 55.6%. Correspondingly, the hydrolysis index decreased from 70.76 to 17.81, with the predicted glycaemic index decreasing from 78.56 to 49.49. Together, these findings suggest that HMT-induced structural reorganisation following oxidation is closely associated with reduced enzymatic susceptibility in jackfruit seed starch, providing a useful dual-modification approach for tailoring starch structure and digestibility.

title: Groundwater Management: Combating the Sinking Feeling
source: Notices of the American Mathematical Society
summary: Management mechanisms have been adopted to track and regulate groundwater usage. Market-driven frameworks, essential to navigate the decades-old legal governance intricacies, are a major part of these solutions. This article surveys the nex
content: Management mechanisms have been adopted to track and regulate groundwater usage. Market-driven frameworks, essential to navigate the decades-old legal governance intricacies, are a major part of these solutions. This article surveys the nexus of emergent mathematical and statistical research themes linked to this topic.

title: Advancements in Fused Deposition Modeling: Materials, Processes, and Emerging Trends in Polymer Additive Manufacturing
source: Journal of Research and Applications in Mechanical Engineering
summary: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) has become a leading technology in polymer additive manufacturing due to its versatility, cost effectiveness, and accessibility. This review explores the current advancements, material innovations, and emergi
content: Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) has become a leading technology in polymer additive manufacturing due to its versatility, cost effectiveness, and accessibility. This review explores the current advancements, material innovations, and emerging trends within FDM, particularly focusing on high performance polymers and composite materials. Key materials like PEEK (Polyetheretherketone), PEI (Polyetherimide), and PPSU (Polyphenylsulfone) are discussed in terms of their mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, as well as their applications across industries such as aerospace, automotive, and medical devices. The incorporation of fiber and particle reinforced composites has significantly enhanced FDM capabilities, offering improved strength, rigidity, and thermal resistance for demanding applications. Moreover, the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to revolutionize the FDM process by enabling predictive maintenance, and real time monitoring. However, challenges such as printability, cost, and material limitations continue to hinder broader adoption, especially for high performance composites and advanced materials. The review concludes by highlighting areas for future research, and material development, which are essential for unlocking the full potential of FDM in both prototyping and end use production.

title: School Meals as Climate Policy: “As Long as It Tastes Good”
summary: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food consumption requires dietary changes, yet policies supporting such changes remain limited. Nevertheless, measures to reduce the carbon footprint of school meals are being implemented in several co
content: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions from food consumption requires dietary changes, yet policies supporting such changes remain limited. Nevertheless, measures to reduce the carbon footprint of school meals are being implemented in several countries. This thesis examines the potential of school meals to foster low-carbon food consumption, within and beyond school, focusing on policy outcomes, policy conditions and policy design.Two of the four papers draw on a controlled intervention in six Swedish schools, four of which introduced dishes with less red meat and other high-emission ingredients (low-carbon recipes). One analyses effects on food taken, plate waste and meal satisfaction; the other examines students’ perceptions of low-carbon recipes and of all-vegetarian days. The remaining two draw on a survey of public acceptability of such measures in France, Poland and Sweden, and interviews on the design of school meal climate policies with officials responsible for school meals in Swedish municipalities.In the intervention, low-carbon recipes reduced the carbon footprint of the menu by 20% without significant negative effects on these outcomes. Although students recognised that red meat has a higher carbon footprint than vegetarian food, they described their food choices as guided primarily by taste, satiety and familiarity, and expressed slightly stronger support for low-carbon recipes than for all-vegetarian days. Public support for such measures was around neutral: significantly higher than for a tax on high-emission foods, but lower than for subsidies and labelling. Municipal strategies primarily sought to reduce emissions by changing meal composition and presentation. Their main potential beyond school therefore appears to lie in repeated exposure to low-carbon meals, which may build familiarity, habits and norms.Overall, the thesis shows that school meal climate policies can reduce the carbon footprint of public meals without significantly undermining student acceptance, particularly when changes fit students’ expectations of an acceptable meal. The findings raise questions about how quickly and visibly changes should be introduced, and whether targets should consider consumption outside school. School meals may contribute to wider shifts towards low-carbon food consumption alongside other policies, but how school meal climate policies can best be designed for this remains to be examined.

title: Production Cost Efficiency, Profit Maximization, and Input Substitution in the Manufacturing Industry: A Narrative Review
summary: Global manufacturing industries face profound structural transformations driven by robotic automation, relative factor-price volatility, rising product-market markups, and stringent decarbonization mandates. Although extensive empirical and
content: Global manufacturing industries face profound structural transformations driven by robotic automation, relative factor-price volatility, rising product-market markups, and stringent decarbonization mandates. Although extensive empirical and theoretical literatures have investigated production cost efficiency, profit maximization, and input substitution individually, these research streams remain largely fragmented across industrial organization, macroeconomics, and productivity econometrics. This article presents a comprehensive narrative review synthesizing foundational duality axioms and recent empirical breakthroughs published between 2014 and 2026 across Capital–Labor–Energy–Materials (KLEM) manufacturing systems. Following a structured narrative review protocol, we critically evaluate four thematic domains: the shift from Cobb–Douglas and symmetric Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) functions to flexible translog and task-based automation architectures; micro-versus-macro empirical estimates of input substitution elasticities (where plant-level capital–labor complementarity, 0.40 ≤ σ ≤ 0.50, coexists with higher industry reallocation elasticities, σ ≈ 0.70); stochastic frontier decompositions of technical and shadow-price allocative cost inefficiency; and the divergence between cost minimization and variable profit maximization under rising market power and financial frictions. We conclude with an integrative methodological synthesis and a future research agenda for industrial economists.

title: Giải pháp thúc đẩy chuyển đổi kép tại Việt Nam
source: Tạp chí Kinh tế và Phát triển
summary: Chuyển đổi kép, với sự kết hợp giữa chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, đang trở thành xu hướng phát triển chiến lược của nhiều quốc gia trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và quá trình số hóa nền kinh tế diễn ra ngày càng sâu rộng. Nhiều quốc gi
content: Chuyển đổi kép, với sự kết hợp giữa chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, đang trở thành xu hướng phát triển chiến lược của nhiều quốc gia trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và quá trình số hóa nền kinh tế diễn ra ngày càng sâu rộng. Nhiều quốc gia và tổ chức quốc tế đã coi chuyển đổi kép là nền tảng của mô hình tăng trưởng bền vững, trong đó chuyển đổi xanh đóng vai trò định hướng nhằm giảm phát thải carbon, sử dụng hiệu quả tài nguyên và thúc đẩy phát triển kinh tế tuần hoàn, còn chuyển đổi số đóng vai trò công cụ quan trọng giúp tối ưu hóa quản lý tài nguyên, nâng cao hiệu quả sản xuất và thúc đẩy đổi mới sáng tạo. Tại Việt Nam, chuyển đổi xanh và chuyển đổi số là hai trong bốn chuyển đổi đóng vai trò trung tâm trong quá trình chuyển đổi mô hình tăng trưởng, và đang được thúc đẩy mạnh mẽ thông qua các chiến lược quốc gia về chuyển đổi số và tăng trưởng xanh. Nghiên cứu dưới đây sử dụng kết hợp phương pháp định tính và định lượng, gồm tổng quan tài liệu, phân tích kinh nghiệm quốc tế, khảo sát thực tế doanh nghiệp và tham vấn chuyên gia để đánh giá quá trình thực hiện chuyển đổi kép tại Việt Nam. Kết quả cho thấy Việt Nam đã đạt được một số kết quả tích cực trong từng quá trình chuyển đổi số và chuyển đổi xanh, song mức độ gắn kết giữa hai quá trình còn hạn chế; do đó, cần tăng cường tích hợp theo hướng chuyển đổi kép nhằm phát huy hiệu ứng cộng hưởng trong nâng cao năng suất, giảm phát thải và đổi mới mô hình tăng trưởng.

title: Biogenic Carboxylation of Granular Activated Carbon via Citrus aurantiifolia Juice for Fluoride Removal
summary: Abstract Excess fluoride (F⁻) in potable water matrices poses a critical global public health threat, including endemic dental and skeletal fluorosis across vulnerable populations. Conventional defluoridation techniques like electrocoagulat
content: Abstract Excess fluoride (F⁻) in potable water matrices poses a critical global public health threat, including endemic dental and skeletal fluorosis across vulnerable populations. Conventional defluoridation techniques like electrocoagulation and ion exchange are frequently constrained by prohibitive operational cost, complex synthesis protocols, and infrastructure limitations in decentralized settings. Herein, we demonstrate a surface functionalization approach for granular activated carbon (GAC) using raw Citrus aurantiifolia (lime) juice as a naturally derived, citric-acid-rich modifying agent. The procedure employs food-grade, non-hazardous materials as an alternative to conventional analytical-grade chemical reagents. Following modification, surface carboxyl-group concentrations increased from 1.26 mmol/g for GAC to 1.98 mmol/g for lime-modified GAC (LGAC) and 1.85 mmol/g for citric acid modified GAC (CAGAC). XPS showed a corresponding increase in surface oxygen content, from 5.92 at% (GAC) to 12.29 at% (CAGAC) and 21.28 at% (LGAC), with distinct C–O and O–C = O contributions on LGAC. Despite a 47% reduction in BET surface area, LGAC exhibited an empirical maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (q max ) of 1.63 mg/g, making its thermodynamic performance statistically identical ( p > 0.05) to CAGAC (1.65 mg/g) and yielding > 85% enhancement over unmodified GAC (0.88 mg/g). Geochemical speciation modeling (PHREEQC) further elucidated a possible immobilization pathway in LGAC via localized aqueous metal-F⁻ complexation dynamics, which were absent in synthetic CAGAC systems. Robust sorption kinetics were maintained across environmentally pertinent pH range (pH 4.0–8.0) and under competitive ionic strength conditions with co-existing groundwater anions. Fixed-bed continuous-flow experiments with multicomponent synthetic groundwater showed that LGAC’s column capacity was 26% higher than that of GAC and ~ 89% of that of CAGAC. These findings validate Citrus aurantiifolia juice as a food-grade, bio-derived modifier, thereby lowering synthesis barriers and offering a practical approach for point-of-use (POU) defluoridation in resource-constrained settings.

title: Modular engineering of aromatic metabolism in Corynebacterium glutamicum enables protocatechuic acid and gallic acid production
summary: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmac
content: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. However, the industrial production of these compounds remains limited by the insufficient performance of current microbial cell factories, resulting in low productivity and high manufacturing costs. Here, an efficient biosynthetic platform based on Corynebacterium glutamicum was systematically established for the production of PCA and GA. Through reconstruction of the PCA biosynthetic pathway, elimination of competing branches in the shikimate pathway, enhancement of the key rate-limiting enzyme, and modulation of the glucose uptake system to increase phosphoenolpyruvate supply, metabolic flux was effectively redirected toward PCA accumulation, resulting in the engineered strain PCA16 achieving a PCA titer of 19.8 g/L in shake-flask fermentation. Building on this platform, GA biosynthesis was established by introducing a mutant pobA from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and further strengthening the shikimate pathway, enabling strain GA06 to produce 7.86 g/L GA in shake-flask fermentation.
